abstract: Background Achieving early glycemic control in adolescents with diabetes is associated with improved short- and long-term health outcomes. The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between eating attitudes and glycemic control, as well as the factors associated with eating attitudes and glycemic control, in adolescents with diabetes. Methods This descriptive cross-sectional study included 143 adolescents with diabetes, aged 10-19 years, who attended a research hospital between February and April 2024. The data were collected using a Descriptive Information Form, Eating Attitudes Test (EAT) and an information form questioning the values of some metabolic variables. Results The mean age of the participants was 14 ± 2.3 years and 49.7% had diabetes between 1-5 years. The mean total score of the EAT scale was 16.62 ± 8.30. The mean score of the "Dieting" subscale of the EAT scale was 10.39 ± 5.58, the mean score of the "Bulimia food preoccupation" subscale was 2.33 ± 3.03 and the mean score of the "Oral Control" subscale was 3.79 ± 3.08. There was no significant difference between the mean EAT total score and glycemic control. Conclusions The mean EAT-26 total score was below the commonly used cutoff score, and no significant association was found between EAT-26 scores and HbA1c. Differences in EAT-26 total and subscale scores were observed according to selected demographic and clinical characteristics, including BMI, treatment modality, and treatment adherence. These findings describe self-reported eating attitudes in the study sample and support the inclusion of eating-related assessment within the holistic care of adolescents with Type 1 DM.

abstract: The rupture of an intracranial aneurysm (IA) has been linked to local hemodynamic environments, but it remains unclear how transient physiological states such as elevated heart rate modulate those environments, and whether different aneurysm geometries respond similarly. Here, we used volumetric particle tracking velocimetry (PTV) to measure 3D velocity fields in two patient-specific IA phantoms, a right middle cerebral artery (MCA) aneurysm and a left vertebral artery (LVA) aneurysm, under three heart rates representative of rest (60 bpm), active movement (100 bpm), and exercise (137 bpm). From these measurements, we quantified coherent structures, turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), wall shear stress (WSS), and oscillatory shear index (OSI). Increasing heart rate did not simply increase peak inflow; it altered the temporal organization of the flow. In the MCA aneurysm, higher heart rates produced a stronger, more anchored intra-saccular vortex and elevated coherent-structure strength and TKE that persisted into mid- and end-diastole, along with broader spatial coverage of elevated WSS that remained high beyond peak systole. The LVA aneurysm exhibited a more muted response, with minimal changes in streamline topology and WSS across heart rates. These results show that heart rate can drive prolonged high-shear, high-energy loading within the cardiac cycle, but that this amplification is morphology-dependent and non-monotonic rather than universal.

abstract: Background Appropriate complementary feeding is essential for children's growth and cognitive development. However, these practices remain inadequate in the study area. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the effect of nutrition counseling on complementary feeding practices among mothers with children aged 6-23 months in West Gojjam Zone, Northwest Ethiopia. Methods A two-arm, parallel, cluster-randomized controlled trial was conducted from June 2023 to December 2024 in rural districts of West Gojjam Zone. Thirty clusters (15 per arm) were assigned to either an intervention group (n = 401), which received Health Belief Model-based nutrition counseling by Women's Development Army leaders, or to a control group (n = 401), which received routine education. The intervention was delivered monthly for nine months from infant age 6-8 months. The primary outcome was appropriate complementary feeding practices. Secondary outcomes included minimum dietary diversity, meal frequency, acceptable diet, and egg/flesh food consumption. Data were collected via interviewer-administered questionnaires. The intervention effect was analyzed using Generalized Estimating Equations with adjustment for potential confounders. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results The difference-in-differences in appropriate complementary feeding practices between groups was 13.2 percentage points. After adjustment, mothers in the intervention group were nearly 2.5 times more likely to practice appropriate complementary feeding than controls [AOR = 2.49, 95% CI: (1.40, 4.42)]. Children of counseled mothers were also more likely to achieve minimum dietary diversity [AOR = 1.75, 95% CI: (1.04, 2.93)], minimum meal frequency [AOR = 1.62, 95% CI: (1.01, 2.61)], and minimum acceptable diet [AOR = 2.13, 95% CI: (1.26, 3.59)] compared with controls. Conclusion Health Belief Model-based nutrition counseling was positively associated with improvements in appropriate complementary feeding practices, minimum dietary diversity, meal frequency, and acceptable diet. Integrating such counseling into routine maternal and child health services may strengthen child nutrition programs in similar rural settings. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05871346).

abstract: Objective Enfortumab vedotin (EV) and cisplatin (CDDP) are central treatments for advanced urothelial carcinoma, yet the influence of prior CDDP exposure on subsequent EV efficacy remains unclear. In this report, we characterized EV-related drug responses in a CDDP-resistant bladder cancer subline. Methods A CDDP-resistant subline (HT1376-CR) was generated from parental bladder cancer cell (HT1376/P) through continuous exposure to CDDP. Sensitivities to CDDP, EV, and the EV payload monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) were compared between HT1376-CR and HT1376/P. Nectin-4 expression, EV binding, and drug-resistance-related gene expression were evaluated. The effect of ABCB1 silencing on drug response was also examined. In vivo EV responses were explored using xenograft models. Results HT1376-CR cells showed increased sensitivity to EV in vitro and in vivo. HT1376-CR cells were more sensitive to MMAE and showed greater G2/M accumulation after MMAE exposure. In contrast, cell-surface nectin-4 expression and EV binding were reduced. ABCB1 was markedly upregulated in HT1376-CR, and ABCB1 silencing increased sensitivity to CDDP, MMAE, and EV within the resistant subline. Conclusion The CDDP-resistant HT1376 subline showed enhanced sensitivity to EV, and ABCB1 suppression further increased EV sensitivity within this resistant subline.

abstract: Background Patching has been the mainstay of unilateral amblyopia treatment, but adherence is challenging. Digital binocular therapies have emerged as a novel approach; however, evidence in treatment-naive children remains limited, as existing studies have predominantly included previously treated children. Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of digital binocular therapies versus patching for improving visual acuity in treatment-naive children aged 3-13 years with unilateral amblyopia following refractive adaptation. Design A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261278100). Comprehensive literature searches were conducted from January 2000 to December 2025. Two independent reviewers screened and selected studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. The primary outcome was change in best-corrected visual acuity. Data were pooled using a random-effects model. The GRADE approach was used to rate the certainty of evidence. Results Five RCTs (n = 225) were included in the primary analysis. Digital binocular therapies showed no statistically significant difference in visual acuity compared with patching using a random-effects model (MD 0.00 logMAR, 95% CI -0.09 to 0.10; I2 = 50.2%). Sensitivity analysis including two additional RCTs judged to be at high risk of bias, one of which compared digital binocular therapy plus spectacles with spectacles alone (7 RCTs; n = 292), yielded similar results (MD 0.04 logMAR, 95% CI -0.03 to 0.10; I2 = 75.2%). The certainty of evidence for visual acuity was moderate, downgraded for inconsistency. Conclusion Digital binocular therapies may serve as adjunctive treatment options when adherence to patching is challenging. However, current evidence does not demonstrate superiority over patching in treatment-naive children with unilateral amblyopia. The evidence remains limited by the small number of RCTs and modest sample sizes. Registration This systematic review and meta-analysis was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) under registration number CRD420261278100 on 4 January 2026.

abstract: Object This study aimed to explore the experiences and perceived changes in self-management behaviors among older patients with a permanent stoma during adaptation, providing insights for the development of targeted supportive interventions. Methods Semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with 13 older colorectal cancer patients with a permanent stoma. All interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. The data were analyzed and thematically refined using Colaizzi's seven-step method. Results Three overarching themes and several sub-themes were identified. Theme one, decision-making dilemmas and uncertainty, included insufficient and poorly tailored decision support resources and challenges in processing complex self-management information. Theme two, reconstructing daily life and identity after stoma formation, encompassed disruptions in body image and daily routines, emotional struggles between rejection and acceptance, and the development of a new normal in living with a stoma. Theme three, developing resilience through accumulated experience and self-management practice, involved learning through repeated self-adjustment, drawing on previous life experiences as coping resources, and redefining life priorities after illness. Conclusion The findings suggest that older patients living with a permanent stoma experience self-management as an ongoing process involving decisional challenges, psychological adjustment, and the gradual reconstruction of resilience. Healthcare professionals should provide continuous decision support, psychological care, and family-inclusive interventions while adopting a strength-based approach that recognizes patients' existing abilities and lived experiences. Supporting patients in reflecting on their adaptation experiences and accumulated coping strategies may enhance self-efficacy and facilitate sustained self-management.

title: Explainable machine learning framework with Granger-based temporal predictive validation for monitoring fiscal risk in national health insurance expenditure.

author_details.name: Gwangsu Lee
author_details.affiliation: School of Computer Software, Daegu Catholic University, Gyeongsangbuk-do, South Korea.

affiliation_resolution.input: School of Computer Software, Daegu Catholic University, Gyeongsangbuk-do, South Korea.

abstract: Rising health insurance expenditure (HIE) poses fiscal risks and challenges to the sustainability of public insurance systems. Despite growing interest in data-driven analysis, empirical evidence on the associations between macroeconomic, social, and financial conditions and national HIE remains limited, particularly across provider types. This study introduces an explainable machine-learning framework with temporal predictive validation to analyze and forecast HIE using 60 macro-financial and socioeconomic indicators. The framework is applied to three monthly expenditure series from Korea's National Health Insurance system (2000-2023). Predictive performance and interpretability are assessed using two univariate autoregressive baselines, three regularized linear indicator-based benchmarks, and six nonlinear indicator-based ensemble models. LightGBM serves as the primary explanatory model, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) quantifies indicator contributions and captures autoregressive persistence. Beyond associational insights, temporal predictive validation using lagged regression and Granger-type temporal predictive tests examines, within a prespecified exploratory lag window, whether SHAP-identified indicators show statistically supported exploratory lagged monitoring relevance. These results are interpreted as hypothesis-generating temporal monitoring evidence rather than as evidence of structural causal effects. Although persistence-based baselines achieved the strongest short-term forecasting accuracy, indicator-based models provided model-conditional explanatory information beyond autoregressive controls. The results indicate that shared macroeconomic pressures and provider-specific factors are associated with HIE predictions. The cost-of-living index is consistently associated with expenditure patterns across categories, whereas domestic demand and external conditions indicate provider-specific associations for medical institutions and pharmacies. Only a subset of predictors retained exploratory lagged monitoring support, underscoring the distinction between model-based predictive importance and hypothesis-generating monitoring signals. This integrated framework may inform transparent fiscal risk monitoring hypotheses and contextual review of public HIE.

abstract: Background Understanding factors influencing specialty choice is essential for workforce planning and curriculum development. Recruitment into diagnostic radiology remains challenging in several regions, particularly in low- and middle-income settings. This study aimed to identify factors associated with Palestinian medical students' consideration of diagnostic radiology as a future specialty, with particular emphasis on educational exposure, perceptions of artificial intelligence (AI), and cognitive influences. Methods A multi-institutional cross-sectional study was conducted to evaluate factors influencing the choice of diagnostic radiology as a future specialty among Palestinian medical students between 2 November 2025 and 5 February 2026. Data were collected using a previously validated questionnaire adapted from Almuhanna et al. Descriptive statistics were performed, followed by bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors of considering radiology as a future specialty. Adjusted odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported. Results A total of 427 students participated (56.7% female; mean age 21.75 ± 2.1 years). Among 300 valid responses regarding radiology intention, 102 students (34.0%) reported considering radiology as a future specialty. In multivariable analysis, lack of exposure to radiology research (OR = 0.14, 95% CI 0.06-0.34, p < 0.001) and lack of preclinical radiology teaching (OR = 0.26, 95% CI 0.12-0.54, p < 0.001) were independently associated with a lower likelihood of considering radiology. Enjoyment of diagnostic problem-solving tasks (OR = 3.35, 95% CI 1.39-8.09, p = 0.007) and exposure to tele-radiology (OR = 3.96, 95% CI 1.72-9.12, p = 0.001) were independently associated with higher likelihood. Lifestyle, impact on patient care, and work environment were the most frequently reported motivating factors. Conclusions Palestinian medical students' interest in radiology is strongly associated with modifiable educational exposures, cognitive engagement in diagnostic reasoning, and perceptions of evolving technological practice. These findings support the potential value of structured undergraduate radiology exposure, research opportunities, and mentorship initiatives to improve awareness and interest in radiology.

abstract: Objective To identify patient-, clinical-, and system-level factors associated with loss to follow-up after point-of-care diabetic retinopathy examination (DRE). Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults ≥18 years undergoing DREs at 75 primary care clinics in Pennsylvania, USA (2017-2019), restricted to examinations with recommended follow-up. The unit of analysis was the DRE. Electronic medical records were used to obtain six-month follow‑up outcomes and patient-, clinical-, and system-level variables. Loss to follow-up was defined as failure to attend an eye care visit within 180 days of DRE. Examinations with duplicate results, those from patients who died within six months, or from sites where the program was discontinued were excluded. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models with random intercepts for patient and clinic were used. Analyses were conducted in the full cohort and separately for gradable and indeterminate exams (ungradable/no image). Results Among 3,121 DREs from 2,959 patients, 32.3% completed follow-up. In the full cohort, higher odds of loss to follow-up were associated with increasing age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=1.02, 95% confidence interval [95%CI]=1.00-1.03, p = 0.019), not being married (aOR=1.36, 95%CI = 1.04-1.77, p = 0.03), findings suggestive of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) on DRE (aOR=1.80, 95%CI = 1.14-2.85, p = 0.012), and higher no-show rates (aOR=1.04, 95%CI = 1.02-1.05, p < 0.0001). History of eye disease (aOR=0.50, 95%CI = 0.37-0.69, p < 0.0001) and patient contact within 30 days (e.g., same/next day: aOR=0.37, 95%CI = 0.20-0.67, p = 0.001) were associated with lower odds of loss to follow-up; contact at 31-60 days was not significantly associated. Findings were consistent across full and gradable models; only no-show rate remained significant in the indeterminate model. Socioeconomic variables, comorbidities, and diabetic retinopathy severity were not independently associated with loss to follow-up after adjustment. Conclusions Adherence was associated with patient (sociodemographic: age, marital status), clinical (AMD on DRE, prior eye disease), and system-level factors (no-show rates, patient contact within 30 days), supporting targeted, multifactorial interventions.

abstract: This paper proposes a Meta-Transformer model for few-shot accurate lane-changing intention recognition in connected vehicle environment. Given the velocity, acceleration, distance headway, time headway and time to collision of a vehicle at past time steps, a transformer model is developed to recognize the lane changing intention of the vehicle at the current time step. The multi-head attention layer of the Transformer model is capable of effectively extracting features from the multivariate time serie input. This enhances the accuracy of lane-changing intention recognition. The Transformer model is combined with a model -agnostic meta-learning (MAML) algorithm to be able to perform well with small amount of training data. The meta-learning consists of meta-training and meta-testing. During the meta-training, a task is sampled from the distribution over tasks. The tasks include recognition of intention of lane-keeping, lane-changing to left lane, and lane-changing to right lane. The model is trained with few samples and feedback from the loss function defined on the tasks. The loss function is defined as the categorical cross entropy of the errors between the labels and the results generated by the proposed model. During the meta-testing, the model is tested on new data from the distribution of the transition from a feature and the label to another feature. The model is trained by minimizing the test error. Experimental results show that the proposed model can achieve 8.7 percentage points higher accuracy than a transformer model.

abstract: Subgrade compaction is a critical procedure in highway construction. To elucidate the dynamic characteristics and energy transfer mechanisms throughout the entire compaction process, this study utilized four test lanes to conduct field experiments on highway subgrade under varying numbers of rolling passes. Comprehensive measurements and analyses were performed regarding the dynamic characteristics of vibration waves, energy distribution, and the evolution of soil compactness during operation. Furthermore, the compaction efficiency and energy transfer within the subgrade were quantitatively evaluated. The results indicate that the dynamic behavior of subgrade materials varies significantly across different compaction stages, which are consequently categorized into three distinct phases: loose, optimal compaction, and over-compaction. In this experiment, the third rolling pass represented the optimal compaction state, characterized by distinct resonance peaks, a regular frequency spectrum, and highly efficient energy transfer. As compactness increases, the horizontal propagation of vibration waves strengthens, whereas vertical attenuation accelerates, causing energy to concentrate beneath the vibration source. Additionally, the proposed method for evaluating compaction efficiency based on the energy transfer coefficient corroborates the three-stage evolution of the process, offering a direct, quantitative indicator for real-time quality assessment and endpoint determination. These findings provide new theoretical insights and empirical data to support intelligent and refined process control in subgrade compaction.

abstract: Legumes are a vital source of plant-based protein and bioactive compounds, yet their consumption is often limited by the development of undesirable off-flavors during processing. This study investigated how germination and milling influence the volatile organic compound (VOC) profiles of three Phaseolus vulgaris cultivars. VOCs from both unsprouted and sprouted seeds, as well as their corresponding flours, were analyzed using headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. In total, 79 VOCs were identified in the seeds and 57 VOCs in the flours. These compounds were classified into seven major chemical groups, including terpene- and non-terpene-derived constituents. The results revealed that germination significantly altered the VOC profile, notably increasing non-terpene derivatives, especially aldehydes, while reducing terpene-based compounds, indicating intensified lipid oxidation. Milling further modified the aroma composition by increasing monoterpene hydrocarbons and decreasing certain non-terpene compounds. Multivariate analyses, including principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering, effectively differentiated the bean cultivars and processing treatments, and identified key marker compounds responsible for these variations. These findings provide a chemical characterization of VOC changes induced by germination and milling in Phaseolus vulgaris, contributing to the development of processing strategies aimed at optimizing the sensory quality and consumer acceptability of legume-based products.

abstract: The valorization of organic waste is still one of the challenges in the path towards environmental sustainability and a circular bioeconomy. This research aimed at assessing the ability of three substrates of organic residues (olive pomace, potato peels and the green seaweed Ulva lactuca) to be used as alternative culture media for filamentous fungi. Mycelial growth on these media was compared with the conventional Potato Dextrose Agar (PDA) and Sabouraud media using three fungal species namely Fusarium oxysporum (F1), Fusarium solani (F2) and Alternaria alternata (N2) as biological models. The alternative media were made from waste materials, supplemented or not with glucose, and sterilized prior to the use. The measurements of mycelial growth were taken every day for 8 days and the data analyzed by multi-factorial ANOVA. Mycelial growth in all the waste-based media was found to be comparable to commercial media. Highest overall growth was seen in commercial PDA and Sabouraud media (19.9% and 19.3%) respectively. The glucose enriched formulations showed 13.2% (olive pomace) and 11.0% (potato peel) rich media with the remaining media showing less. The percentages of olive pomace, potato peels and U. lactuca were 12.9%, 9.3% and 1.2%, respectively, without the addition of glucose. Growth was significantly higher with glucose supplementation, showing the beneficial effect of the exogenous C supply and intrinsic nutritional value of the substrates. ANOVA revealed that incubation time and medium type significantly influenced mycelial growth across all three strains (p < 2.2 × 10-16), with significant interactions between medium and time (F1: F = 3.91, p = 6.08 × 10-10, F2: F = 163.31, p < 2 × 10-16, N2: F = 44.30, p < 2 × 10-16). The overall analysis of the three strains also indicated highly significant main effect for strain (F = 645.22) and incubation time (F = 391.95) as well as highly significant main effect for culture medium (F = 44.18) (all p < 2.2 × 10-16). Variations in texture and color that can be seen in the different media, however, may influence the macroscopic appearance of the mycelium and identification. Hence, these alternative media are recommended for post identification, subculture and preservation of fungal strains especially.

abstract: The study of the ecological interactions within microbial communities is crucial for gaining deeper insights into community ensemble and evolution, enabling targeted modification of the community's functionality. Many inference approaches have been developed to derive ecological associations. Here, we focus on co-occurrence computational methods, in which associations are inferred from metagenomic abundance data by measuring the statistical dependence between species counts across different sampled populations. The limitations in culture-based experiments have hindered the ability to assess these methods' validity, leading to scarce application in metagenomics studies. To provide a comprehensive assessment of network inference method performance, we benchmark 18 different computational approaches across a broad spectrum of experimental scenarios. We use synthetic 16S rDNA-seq count data generated from known underlying interaction networks, enabling systematic and controlled evaluation. The benchmark spans scenarios varying in numbers of species and samples, sample richness, sequencing depth, and interaction network structure. We evaluated the performance of the methods both in terms of accuracy of the inferred network, using various metrics from binary classification theory and metrics coming from network science, and in terms of computational burden. We found that methods have valid results only in a restricted, and often unrealistic, field of application, whereas their effectiveness diminishes with more realistic simulation parameters. Our findings highlight the limits of the co-occurrence-based approach and the need for further development in microbial ecological association inference.

abstract: The study of evolution in organisms with high mutation rates requires detailed data on the genomic composition of the population. Here we report on an innovative use of high-throughput sequencing technology combined with rapid experimental evolution that allowed us to follow the genetic diversification of four independent bacteriophage populations for 412 generations in extraordinary detail. One of our goals was to assess phylodynamic methods that use genetic information to infer key parameters of the population history. Because phylodynamic methods assume neutral evolution, we did not actively impose any selection pressures in our evolution experiment (in addition to those inherent in the bacterial cell environment). Tracing over 80'000 bacteriophage genomes, representing 884 distinct genotypes, we find that the patterns of viral diversification result in largely non-congruent genotype distributions, but also document multiple instances of parallel evolution. Unlike previous observations of parallelism in viral evolution, we do not just see the parallel evolution of mutations at single sites, but on the level of full-length genomes. Computer simulations that recapitulate our experiments in great detail show that this degree of parallelism is inconsistent with neutral evolution. We further show that the observed extent of parallel evolution biases phylodynamic analysis of migration rates, and wrongly estimates significant migration between the independent evolution lines. Our approach is applicable to many other viruses and paves the way to advanced population genetic investigations that aim to shed light on phenomena that relate to genetic linkage across the genome.

abstract: Dissecting the genetic basis of genotype × environment interaction (G × E) is important for breeding crops with stable or responsive performance across production environments. Using previously published seed-yield data from 107 Egyptian fenugreek accessions evaluated under two contrasting field environments, we investigated whether yield potential and environmental responsiveness share a common genetic basis. Seed yield per plant was measured in Giza (SYP_G; reference environment) and Wadi El-Natrun (SYP_W; contrasting environment). Nine derived indices were calculated to characterize environmental responsiveness, productivity, and stability: relative performance index (RPI), yield plasticity index (YPI), stress tolerance index (STI), log response ratio (LRR), mean productivity (MP), harmonic mean (HM), tolerance index (TOL), stress susceptibility index (SSI), and AMMI stability value (ASV). The near-zero correlation between SYP_G and SYP_W (r = 0.107) indicated substantial genotype reranking across environments, while several response indices were closely related to SYP_W and therefore predominantly reflected environment-dependent yield expression. Phenotypic analyses also identified contrasting performance strategies, ranging from highly responsive accessions, such as G15 (RPI = 3.629), to highly stable accessions, such as G41 (YPI = 0.001). These phenotypes were integrated with 38,142 SNPs using univariate association-mapping approaches. In addition, SYP_G and SYP_W were subjected to multivariate association-mapping. Association mapping identified one genome-wide-significant SNP for STI and several suggestive loci showed concordant associations across mapping methods. Within the current panel, marker coverage, and significance thresholds, most adaptation-index associations did not overlap previously reported yield loci; however, dDocent_Contig_39939_66, previously associated with seed yield in this panel, also showed cross-method suggestive associations with RPI and TOL. Comparative genomic analysis of three legume reference genomes supported two gene-linked candidate loci associated with STI: a cation/H⁺ antiporter and an importin subunit beta-1. The same analysis classified two of the strongest statistical signals, including the sole genome-wide-significant locus, as repetitive or transposable-element sequences rather than single-copy genes. These findings demonstrate that statistical association strength does not necessarily establish a coding-gene basis for loci identified using reference-free ddRAD markers. Within the current population size and marker coverage, environmental responsiveness and productivity appeared partially distinct but biologically connected components of environment-dependent yield performance. The results provide a genomic and phenotypic framework for prioritizing fenugreek germplasm for further evaluation while emphasizing the need for independent-population, multi-season, and functional validation of the identified candidate loci.

abstract: Background Cancer-related adverse-event reports are difficult to interpret because statistical disproportionality, stimulated reporting, and background disease burden are distinct phenomena. To address this, we formalized a two-dimensional prioritization framework that combines FAERS signal credibility with independent GBD burden context. Because the FAERS dataset is overwhelmingly of US origin, we utilized China exclusively as a prespecified macro-epidemiological GBD comparator, strictly avoiding cross-national pharmacovigilance extrapolations. Methods We analyzed FAERS reports (2004-2023) and female GBD 2023 estimates for China and the United States. Four disproportionality algorithms (ROR, PRR, IC, and EBGM) were evaluated for 150 high-frequency primary-suspect drug-event pairs (50 per cancer group). We report any-algorithm positivity and four-algorithm concordance alongside case-definition sensitivity analyses. GBD trends, age-period-cohort models, and exploratory projections to 2053 were integrated to provide population-level context, explicitly not as exposure denominators or for causal validation. Results FAERS cohorts yielded 19,717 cancer-associated report records. Among 150 high-frequency candidate pairs, 42 met all four algorithmic thresholds. The top-50 candidate screen captured approximately 72.8%-75.8% of primary-suspect records, serving as a variance-reduction step rather than a complete all-drug screen. Drugs like ranitidine and talc demonstrated marked disproportionality but also exhibited reporter and temporal features heavily compatible with stimulated reporting. Time-to-onset distributions reflected recorded administrative reporting intervals rather than biological carcinogenesis. GBD estimates revealed divergent China-US trajectories, notably a rising baseline for US uterine cancer. Conclusions The formalized F × G framework operates as a transparent triage tool, not a causal classifier. FAERS disproportionality generates hypotheses; GBD trajectories indicate potential public-health priority. All prioritized signals-particularly those involving consumer products or immunosuppressants-require formal causal evaluation in longitudinal exposure-denominator datasets.

abstract: Background Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a common head and neck cancer, and radiotherapy is its main treatment. Recurrence and metastasis are the main causes of treatment failure. Although immunotherapy can prolong patient survival, the molecular mechanisms underlying NPC development and progression remain unclear. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) and their target genes are abnormally expressed in many tumors and are closely involved in tumor development. Therefore, this study aimed to identify key miRNAs and immune-related target genes in NPC, construct miRNA-mRNA regulatory networks, and screen for and validate core immune genes to identify prognostic molecular biomarkers for NPC. Methods We downloaded NPC-related miRNA (GSE32960) and mRNA (GSE12452, GSE13597, GSE64634) microarray datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and identified differentially expressed miRNAs (DEMs) and mRNAs (DEGs) using R. Target genes of DEMs were predicted with TargetScan, miRDB, and miRWalk, and then intersected with DEGs to identify core genes. A miRNA-mRNA regulatory network was constructed in Cytoscape. The core genes were further overlapped with immune-related gene sets, followed by functional enrichment analysis. A prognostic risk model was established using LASSO-Cox regression, and immune cell infiltration was evaluated with CIBERSORT. Model validation, immunohistochemical analysis, and drug-gene interaction analysis were also performed. In vitro, RT-qPCR was conducted in C666-1 and NP69 cell lines to verify the expression of key genes. Results We identified 213 potential target genes of key miRNAs. Three miRNAs (hsa-miR-30e-5p, hsa-miR-30a-5p, and hsa-miR-20a-5p) were associated with NPC prognosis, and 17 core immune-related genes were enriched in cytokine-mediated signaling, chemokine response, and JAK-STAT pathways. Five genes (CXCL11, SOCS1, ROBO1, LGR5, and RORB) showed promising diagnostic value for NPC; their expression was positively correlated (P < 0.05) with CD8 ⁺ T-cell, macrophage, and neutrophil infiltration. Drug-gene analysis predicted that 5-fluorouracil targeted LGR5 and aldesleukin targeted SOCS1. RT-qPCR demonstrated that SOCS1 was upregulated approximately 3.7-fold in NPC cells (P < 0.01). Conclusion This study identified potential novel key genes in nasopharyngeal carcinoma, providing new therapeutic targets for the treatment of this disease.

abstract: Long-cable PWM-driven induction motor electric submersible pump (ESP) systems suffer from significant voltage reflection issues caused by distributed parameter effects, leading to transient overvoltages at the motor terminals that can reach several times the DC bus voltage. This severely threatens system stability and motor insulation integrity, and traditional control methods prove inadequate for effective suppression. To address this challenge, the paper proposes an improved model predictive current control (MPCC) strategy for induction motor ESP systems, which integrates overvoltage suppression and equivalent switching frequency reduction for long-cable PWM-driven applications. The reflection overvoltage mechanism is thoroughly analyzed through mathematical modeling of the motor and long-cable transmission line, and the applicability of predictive current control in such systems is investigated. The core improvement lies in a circular boundary constrained MPCC combined with a dynamic transition voltage vector selection mechanism, which enables dual-mode optimization based on current error boundary conditions: the normal cost function is applied within the circular boundary to jointly optimize voltage tracking, switching frequency, and dv/dt; while the backup cost function is activated outside the boundary to prioritize current error minimization. This effectively optimizes the voltage switching strategy, reducing both switching frequency and dv/dt, thereby preventing overvoltage excitation caused by abrupt voltage vector steps in PWM-driven systems. Simulation models under different cable configurations (1 km with RLC filter and 110 m without RLC filter) and an experimental platform based on a neutral-point-clamped three-level inverter (NPC-TLI) topology are established, with the 110 m no-filter configuration serving as a direct cross-validation baseline. Comparative simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly reduces the duration of motor terminal overvoltage while maintaining excellent system dynamic performance. Moreover, the improved MPCC effectively suppresses overvoltage and reduces equivalent switching frequency without requiring hardware filter redesign, while the RLC filter remains necessary for full insulation safety compliance under more demanding long-cable conditions, substantially mitigating the risk of motor insulation breakdown.

abstract: Municipal sewage sludge typically has high moisture and organic matter contents, which exert a significant influence on mechanical strength, dewatering and resource recovery. Organic soil specimens with varying water contents were prepared by mixing raw sewage sludge (RSS) with dry soil powder (DSP), humus, and quartz sand tailings (QST). Unconfined compressive strength (UCS) tests were conducted to investigate the effect of water content on the UCS. Results show that the UCS decreases with normalized water content (w₀/wL) following a power-law relationship, and a quantitative formula is established. Specimens with different organic contents were fabricated by blending DSP into RSS. Unconsolidated undrained triaxial tests were performed to assess strength evolution with organic content. For organic high-liquid-limit silt, the angle of internal friction changes slightly with organic content (wu), maintaining a low value of 1-3°. Cohesion decreases gradually when wu < 17%, drops sharply when 17% < wu < 21%, and stabilizes at around 6 kPa when wu > 21%. An organic content of 17-21% serves as a possible transition interval for sludge structure and strength degradation. Mechanism analysis reveals that the contribution of organic matter to soil strength is predominantly governed by cementation, with negligible influence on the internal friction angle. The reduction in cohesion is primarily attributed to the decrease in dry unit weight, degradation of mineral skeleton, a predominance of the soft organic matrix, and increased plastic deformation.

abstract: Aerial perception and dispatch scheduling in unmanned aerial vehicle emergency response are commonly arranged as a one-directional pipeline, and the contribution of closing the loop between them has not been measured under controlled conditions. This study evaluates a framework in which a YOLOv8 scene classifier gates task discovery, a Disaster Situation State Matrix aggregates spatially indexed detection outputs under exponential temporal decay, and a proximal policy optimization scheduler acts on that matrix. Evaluation used a 32 × 32 grid testbed with four vehicles, ten training seeds per configuration, and one hundred frozen evaluation scenarios per seed, with a complete two-by-two ablation separating policy access to the state matrix from the rate at which the matrix is refreshed. Runtime perception updating raised task completion from 0.4971 to 0.5859 relative to an initial-snapshot policy, a gain of 8.87 percentage points (95% CI 7.26 to 10.32, Holm-adjusted p = 0.0078). Policy access to the state matrix carried a main effect of 36.42 percentage points (95% CI 34.83 to 37.79) and refresh rate a main effect of 1.81 percentage points (95% CI 0.90 to 2.82), with no evidence of interaction. Under a shared six-action interface and identical perception constraints, the proposed scheduler exceeded a greedy heuristic by 3.44 percentage points (95% CI 2.03 to 4.91, Holm-adjusted p = 0.0078). Replacing confusion-matrix sampling with replayed YOLOv8 predictions on held-out images reduced completion by 1.28 percentage points, and temporally persistent detection errors extended the longest uninterrupted error run to seventy-one steps. Structural exposure of the state matrix to the scheduling policy, rather than refresh frequency alone, accounts for the observed performance of the framework.

abstract: Insulin resistance is a complex metabolic state involving impaired insulin sensitivity, compensatory insulin secretion, abnormal lipid metabolism, and altered fat distribution. However, the shared genetic architecture underlying these correlated phenotypes remains incompletely defined. In this study, we applied Genomic Structural Equation Modeling to genome-wide association summary statistics of fasting insulin, insulin sensitivity index, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio to construct an insulin resistance-related latent genetic factor. SNP-level association analysis was then performed for the latent factor, followed by risk locus annotation, fine-mapping, transcriptome-wide association analysis, gene-level prioritization, enrichment analysis, and exploratory structural biology assessment of selected missense substitutions. The single-factor model showed acceptable but not optimal approximate fit and captured a biologically consistent genetic pattern, with positive loadings for fasting insulin, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio and a negative loading for insulin sensitivity index. The latent factor showed detectable SNP heritability and revealed 3,067 genome-wide significant candidate SNPs, with Q_SNP retained as a complementary SNP-level heterogeneity diagnostic.. Functional annotation identified 100 genomic risk loci and 1,530 FDR-significant genes in MAGMA. Fine-mapping prioritized multiple candidate regions, including loci near PPARG, RSPO3, SLC38A11, SLC39A8, BCL2, GDF5, and SPATA5. TWAS and FOCUS further highlighted candidate genes involved in adipocyte biology, glucose-lipid metabolism, insulin secretion, and expression regulation, including PPARG, MLXIPL, TCF7L2, FAM13A, CCDC92, and SLC22A3. Enrichment analyses suggested that genetic signals associated with the insulin resistance-related latent factor were mainly linked to fat distribution, cardiometabolic traits, adipose tissue, mesenchymal cell lineages, and active regulatory genomic regions. In a separate exploratory analysis, AlphaFold3 modeling, ThermoMPNN prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations suggested structural perturbations for three ultra-rare missense substitutions in nominated candidate proteins: BCL2-W188G, GDF5-C400Y, and RSPO3-C129Y. These substitutions were selected using functional-impact annotations and modeling feasibility, were not GWAS lead or fine-mapped causal variants, and do not establish the mechanisms underlying the GWAS associations. These findings provide an integrated genetic and structural framework for understanding shared mechanisms underlying insulin resistance-related metabolic abnormalities, while emphasizing the need for further experimental validation.

abstract: Electrooculography (EOG) is a low-cost biosignal modality for gaze-based human-computer interaction, but reliable validation and model interpretability remain important challenges for machine learning-based gaze classification. This study proposes an explainable EOG gaze classification framework using UNIOVI-EOG dataset. Horizontal and vertical EOG recordings from nine participants were converted into 100 ms non-overlapping windows, and only stable windows with at least 90% label purity were retained. Time-domain window features were extracted and evaluated using Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost classifiers under subject-wise five-fold cross-validation, ensuring that participants in the validation folds were not included in training. The final dataset contained 81,481 accepted windows across nine gaze classes. All models achieved very high subject-wise performance, with Random Forest providing the strongest overall results. The high performance was consistent with the controlled fixation protocol and the strong separability of horizontal and vertical EOG amplitude patterns, as supported by simple mean-amplitude baseline and leakage diagnostic analyses. Model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME). The explanations showed that amplitude-related features, especially channel means, medians, quantiles, and absolute mean values, were the main contributors to classification decisions. SHAP-LIME rank correlation and permutation-based faithfulness analysis provided additional quantitative support for the explanations. These findings suggest that leakage-controlled, window-level, explainable machine learning can provide accurate and physiologically interpretable EOG gaze classification in controlled experimental settings.

abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) tools become increasingly integrated into language education, understanding how learners respond to AI-generated feedback during writing revision has become an important research concern. Existing studies have primarily examined the effects of AI on writing performance, with less attention to learners' reported decision-making and reflection during revision. This qualitative study investigated learner-AI interaction, reported revision practices and learner perceptions among 18 first-year non-English-major students enrolled in a university EFL writing course. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews following a Gen AI-assisted revision task and analysed using thematic analysis. The findings identified three interaction patterns with Gen AI: passive AI reliance, adaptive AI engagement, metacognitive AI engagement. Participants differed in how they evaluated and used AI-generated feedback, including passive acceptance, selective uptake, and critical evaluation. Some reported increased confidence, motivation, and awareness of linguistic form, whereas others expressed concerns about overreliance, authorship, and loss of personal voice. These self-reported experiences provide insight into how EFL learners perceive and manage GenAI-assisted revision, highlighting the need for pedagogical approaches that foster critical AI literacy and reflective learner autonomy.

abstract: A slow-growth Escherichia coli isolate, designated E. coli 105X, was recovered from a patient with urinary-tract infection. Initial biochemical profiling misidentified it as Shigella boydii; however, matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry and average nucleotide identity analysis (98.67% relative to uropathogenic E. coli CFT073) unequivocally reclassified the strain as E. coli. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing revealed broad-spectrum resistance to β-lactams, aminoglycosides and fluoroquinolones, which was mediated by 53 acquired resistance determinants, including the extended-spectrum β-lactamase genes blaCTX-M-55 and blaTEM-1, together with an expanded repertoire of efflux pump systems. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) disclosed 45399 single-nucleotide polymorphisms and 1736 insertions/deletions relative to E. coli CFT073. Functional enrichment analyses demonstrated that non-synonymous mutations in 11 flagellar biosynthesis genes (e.g., flgA, fliK), the peptidoglycan synthase-encoding mrcB, and 29 growth-associated loci collectively perturb energy allocation and compromise biofilm formation, resulting in a markedly prolonged doubling time. Concurrently, E. coli 105X lacks canonical virulence factors such as the siderophore enterobactin and P fimbriae, but has acquired temperature-sensitive hemagglutinin and type IV pili. Taken together, E. coli 105X exemplifies a distinctive adaptive strategy in which metabolic bottlenecks synergize with structural mutations to establish a "slow-growth, high-resistance, re-engineered virulence" phenotype. These findings underscore the critical necessity of molecular diagnostic tools for accurate identification of morphologically atypical clinical E. coli isolates, and provide a theoretical rationale for developing targeted combination therapies that interfere with core bacterial energy-metabolism pathways.

abstract: Riptortus pedestris (Fab.) is an important soybean pest in East Asia, where its piercing-sucking feeding behavior leads to soybean syndrome. Triflumezopyrim, a novel mesoionic insecticide, has been widely applied to control sap-sucking insects. However, its lethal and sublethal impacts on R. pedestris remain poorly understood. This study investigated the lethal and sublethal effects of triflumezopyrim on R. pedestris using bioassays, age-stage two-sex life table analyses, and enzyme activity measurements. Results demonstrated that triflumezopyrim exhibited strong toxicity (LC50 = 7.46 mg/L) and notable repellent activity against R. pedestris. Exposure of nymphs to sublethal concentrations (LC10 and LC30) significantly prolonged nymphal development and the adult preoviposition period, while reducing adult longevity, oviposition duration, and fecundity in the parental (F0) generation. In addition, LC30 exposure produced adverse transgenerational effects in the F1 generation, including extended adult preoviposition period, decreased male longevity, reduced oviposition duration, fecundity, net reproductive rate (R0), intrinsic rate of increase (r), and finite rate of increase (λ) of the population. Moreover, both LC10 and LC30 treatments led to substantial elevation in the activities of antioxidant (superoxide dismutase and peroxidase) and detoxification (multifunctional oxidase and glutathione S-transferase) enzymes. These findings indicate that triflumezopyrim exerts strong acute toxicity and pronounced sublethal inhibitory effects on R. pedestris, ultimately suppressing population growth potential. This study offers a scientific basis for the rational use of triflumezopyrim as well as the development of strategies for the management of this species.

abstract: Woody shrubs are important components of temperate forest understories, contributing to forest structure, diversity, and succession. However, the extent to which variation in canopy openness and soil texture influence shrub occurrence, diversity, and composition remains unclear. Because woody tissues require comparatively high light availability and sandy soils may favor shrubs over trees, we hypothesized that shrub richness and cover would increase in canopy gaps and sandier microsites. To address this, we quantified soil texture, canopy gap structure, and recorded shrub abundance in twenty randomly stratified plots within sixteen different mesic forests in Wisconsin, USA. Using a mixed-effects modeling approach, we determined that shrub richness, Shannon diversity, and coverage increased significantly in more open canopy gaps, while soil sand content had no significant impact on these metrics. Canopy gaps also had a significant effect on the composition of shrub communities at the plot level. At the stand level, neither sandier nor more open-canopied forests had more diverse, dense shrub layers, though more heterogenous canopies had a weak negative correlation with shrub richness. Broadly, shrub abundance and cover increased in more open gaps, though individual species demonstrated significantly different preferences in terms of light availability and soil sand content. Our results demonstrate the importance of local light availability for shrub growth. However, species-specific responses to soil texture and light availability and the modeled importance of unmeasured site-level factors suggest that additional environmental and biotic factors are likely to impact this diverse temperate guild.

abstract: The cohesin complex is critical for both proper gene expression and for pairing sister chromatids during mitosis to ensure proper chromosome segregation. Acetylation and deacetylation of SMC3, a component of cohesin, is a critical regulatory mechanism controlling stability and reformation of the complex. Patients with Cornelia de Lange Syndrome have been observed to have mutations in cohesin-related genes, including in the lysine deacetylase KDAC8 (HDAC8), leading to disruption of complex formation and recycling. To further understand the cellular consequences of disrupting the SMC3 acetylation cycle, we utilized cell lines in which KDAC8 is replaced by a catalytically-inactive variant (8CDm) or knocked-out (8KO). Although the 8CDm cell line completes mitosis at the same rate as wild-type cells, 8CDm cells display severe chromosomal instability, characterized by increased presence of micronuclei and a significant subpopulation of cycling tetraploid cells. These defects were not observed in 8KO cells. Although total SMC3 protein levels are similar in all cell lines, SMC3 and other cohesin-associated genes are differentially expressed in the mutant cell lines. We hypothesize a model in which 8KO cells compensate for the inability to deacetylate SMC3 by increasing both SMC3 turnover and gene expression, and 8CDm mediated suppression of SMC3 turnover and expression results in fewer functional cohesin complexes and the severe chromosomal instability phenotype. Overall, these observations provide a greater understanding of the importance of SMC3 deacetylation by KDAC8 and insight into the phenotypic range observed in Cornelia de Lange Syndrome patients.

abstract: Purpose A proportion of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) present with subclinical low-level proteinuria at initial diagnosis that does not meet the formal classification criteria for lupus nephritis (LN). This study aimed to investigate the association between low-level proteinuria at SLE onset and the risk of developing proteinuria-predominant LN. Patients and methods This was a retrospective cohort study using medical records of patients newly diagnosed with SLE from Fujian Medical University Union Hospital between December and March. Inclusion required urine dipstick proteinuria ≤2+; if quantified, protein excretion <500 mg/24h (by the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio [UPCR] or 24-hour proteinuria). Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected at the time of initial diagnosis, as well as urinalysis, urine sediment, UPCR, and 24-hour proteinuria during follow-up, where available. The association between various baseline variables and the subsequent development of proteinuria-predominant LN was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model. Results Of 330 patients screened, 297 were eligible for inclusion in the final analysis, of whom 85 patients had low-level proteinuria at the initial diagnosis. According to multivariable-adjusted models, low-level proteinuria significantly increased the risk of proteinuria-predominant LN (P < 0.001, hazard ratio[HR] = 3.355, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.6646.765), as did male sex (P = 0.001, HR = 3.178, 95% CI: 1.563-6.460). Conclusion This study highlights that SLE patients with low-level proteinuria at initial diagnosis may require enhanced monitoring for LN, enabling early detection. Future studies are needed to determine the necessity of early intervention.

abstract: Dysphagia, or difficulty swallowing, is a matter of serious concern among older adults. While thickening agents are essential for dysphagia management, they are not pharmacologically inert; their physicochemical interactions with oral medications remain poorly understood and can pose an iatrogenic hazard of mechanical esophageal obstruction. Following a case of acute esophageal obstruction of unknown origin, this study aimed to identify the foreign body, to assess the reproducibility of any disintegration failures across formulations and thickeners, and to examine the systemic barriers that would allow such a hazard to remain unaddressed. This foreign body, a magnesium oxide (MgO) tablet, caused obstruction in a malignant esophageal stricture. It was analyzed using ex vivo computed tomography and chemical analysis. A static immersion model was used to mimic esophageal stasis. The disintegration behaviors of four MgO formulations (n = 6 each) were compared using thickeners (1.0-3.0%) and a pharmaceutical swallowing aid jelly (SA-J). Furthermore, a cross-sectional market survey was conducted in nine regions in Japan to assess the economic barriers to the clinical adoption of SA-J as an alternative swallowing aid. The foreign body was identified as a non-disintegrated, swollen MgO mass. In vitro experiments confirmed a consistent phenomenon observed across all tested formulations: thickeners completely inhibited disintegration in every combination tested, increasing tablet weight by approximately 2.2-fold at concentrations of 2.0-3.0% and forming rigid masses. Conversely, the tablets disintegrated in SA-J in approximately 25 s. The market survey revealed that SA-J costs were approximately 14.5-fold higher per administration than thickeners (p < 0.001). Although based on a single case, these findings highlight that xanthan gum-based thickened water represents a physicochemical hazard that may remain unrecognized in current clinical practice. Choice of swallowing vehicle should be made with full awareness that xanthan gum-based thickeners can prevent the disintegration of MgO tablets.

abstract: As technology advances, the research on mathematical dynamic integration models has yielded a potent instrument for the analysis and optimization of complex systems, thereby fostering progress across multiple domains. To solve the issues of traditional dynamic integration models, such as the lack of solid mathematical theoretical support, imbalanced weight allocation among multiple participants, and insufficient dynamic adaptability, this study integrates the Shapley value method from cooperative game theory with Monte Carlo sampling techniques to construct an information evaluation model. The calculation of the marginal contributions of participants in different alliances enables the quantification of the value of multi-source information, thus resolving the issue of imbalanced weight allocation. Furthermore, a dynamic optimization model is built by integrating Nash equilibrium and Markov decision processes, utilizing state transition probabilities to capture temporal changes in strategies and achieve stable strategy optimization. Finally, a mathematical model that includes integration is designed. Experiments that compare the two models show that the average time it takes to make a decision goes up by only 0.2 seconds when the number of samples is between 25 and 150, and the amount of memory used goes up by only 1.2GB. In the InfiMM-WebMath-40B dataset, the model's standard deviation increases from 0.020 in 25 samples to 0.030 in 150 samples, an increase of only 0.010. In the MV-MATH dataset, the standard deviation increases by only 0.011. Furthermore, the proposed model outperforms the comparative models in all metrics, reducing convergence time by 14.7%, training time by 15.3%, energy consumption by 16.3%, and iteration count by 21.5%, while maintaining a low central processing unit utilization rate. Therefore, the proposed mathematical dynamic integration model can more accurately handle uncertain information in complex systems, optimize system decisions, reveal the inherent laws governing dynamic changes in systems, and provide stronger theoretical support and methodological guidance for solving practical problems.

abstract: Prostate cancer is common in older men, and the treatment decision depends strongly on the patient's general condition and comorbidities. However, the medication background of men who reach prostate biopsy has rarely been described. We used a large Japanese administrative claims database (Medical Data Vision) to profile the medications of men who underwent prostate needle biopsy between April 2008 and June 2019. We examined the number of medications and the drug classes in relation to body mass index (BMI) and age. We identified 67,812 men, all aged 60 years or older. The mean number of medications was lowest at BMI 20-25 and increased toward both low and high BMI, showing a U-shaped pattern (minimum 1.44 drugs at BMI 22.0-22.5); the increase was driven mainly by high BMI. This pattern was consistent across age strata, and in a negative binomial regression adjusted for age the quadratic term of BMI remained significant (p < 0.001), with an adjusted minimum at BMI 20.5. The composition of drug classes differed by body size: metabolic drugs (antihypertensive/cardiovascular, dyslipidemia, diabetes, and hyperuricemia drugs) were more common at high BMI, whereas gastrointestinal and analgesic drugs were relatively more common at low BMI, and all classes increased with age. In conclusion, among men undergoing prostate biopsy, the number of medications was lowest at BMI 20-25 and the qualitative medication profile differed by BMI. These findings describe the medication background of this population and may inform the design of future risk-stratified or prospective studies.

title: Personalized and differentially private federated learning for mobility data mining via the TrajectoryGuard framework.

author_details.name: Ali Alqazzaz
author_details.affiliation: Department of Information Systems and Cybersecurity, College of Computing and Information Technology, University of Bisha, Bisha, Saudi Arabia.

abstract: This paper presents TrajectoryGuard, a personalized and privacy-preserving federated learning framework for secure and efficient mobility data mining. The framework integrates differential privacy, secure multiparty aggregation, and adaptive gradient compression to ensure that raw location traces, such as GPS logs or geo-tagged user activities, remain confined to user devices, thereby minimizing privacy leakage risks. Unlike conventional approaches, TrajectoryGuard introduces a dynamic noise-aware optimization mechanism and personalized aggregation scheme to enhance both model accuracy and robustness under non-IID and heterogeneous client scenarios. Experimental evaluation on the GeoLife dataset and the T-Drive Beijing taxi trajectory dataset demonstrates competitive performance, achieving 92.5% accuracy and 30% reduction in total per-round communication overhead (comprising gradient payload, model broadcast, and encryption metadata) while maintaining strong privacy guarantees (ε = 0.9 at σ2 = 1.0). Comparative results against FedAvg, FedProx, AdaptFL, and Fed-Ensemble confirm TrajectoryGuard's superiority in convergence stability, privacy resilience, and predictive utility. The framework's practical viability is illustrated through a real-world case study in urban trajectory forecasting, highlighting its relevance for applications in smart transportation and behavior modeling. The accuracy metric specifically corresponds to next-destination classification, a multi-class problem where the model predicts a destination category (e.g., home, workplace, or shopping location) from partial GPS trajectories. Evaluation follows an 80/20 time-based train/test split per user to prevent data leakage across temporal boundaries.

abstract: Background Central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) is a common vision-threatening retinal disease that affects predominantly working-age adults. Although often self-limiting, a substantial proportion of cases are either chronic or recurrent, resulting in significant visual, psychological, social and economic burdens on sufferers. Current treatment options are limited and lack robust long-term evidence, reflecting an incomplete understanding of underlying disease mechanisms. Traditionally, CSCR has been researched as a solely ocular condition, however numerous non-ophthalmic physical risk factors have been implicated in the disease, suggesting a broader systemic aetiology. A comprehensive synthesis of physical risk factors for CSCR is needed to inform future mechanistic research and therapeutic development. Objective The main objective of this systematic review and meta-analysis is to summarise physical risk factors associated with CSCR, including genetic, hormonal, metabolic and drug- or toxin-related factors. The secondary objective is to describe any associations between individual risk factors and disease severity. Methods and analysis This protocol has been written in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic review and Meta-Analysis Protocols (PRSIMA-P). The PRISMA-P Checklist for this protocol can be found in Supplemental Information S2: PRISMA-P Checklist. Observational and interventional studies that report on any physical risk factors for CSCR will be included. Eligible participants are adults (≥ 18 years) with CSCR. Searches will be conducted on MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Scopus and CENTRAL, and supplemented by grey literature and clinical trial registry searches. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data and assess the risk of bias, with any disagreements adjudicated by a third reviewer. Where feasible, meta-analyses will be performed using random-effects models to pool odds ratios for associations between risk factors and CSCR. Heterogeneity of the included studies will be assessed using the I2 statistic. A narrative synthesis will be undertaken when meta-analysis is not possible, in accordance with Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis (SWiM) guidelines. Risk of bias will be assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The certainty of evidence will be evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) system. Ethics and dissemination Ethical approval is not required as this study uses previously published aggregate data. Findings will be disseminated through publication in peer-reviewed journal and presentation at relevant scientific conferences. Trial registration This review protocol is registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO), under registration number CRD420251088489.

abstract: Fungal endophytes considered one of the major sources of promising bioactive compounds. This study aimed to isolate endophytic fungi from leaves of Reseda pruinosa for the first time, and to evaluate their biological activities. Results illustrated that, two fungal endophytes isolates were isolated, identified as Alternaria sp. and Alternaria alternata morphologically and genetically. Phytochemical analyses of these two fungal isolates metabolites showed significant amounts of phenolics, flavonoids, tannins, and alkaloids. GC-MS analyses of the crude extracts of these two fungal isolates showed that, major compounds in these extracts belong to the classes of fatty acid esters, fatty acids, and terpenoids. Results revealed that the MCF-7 cancer cells was susceptible to the anticancer effects of both fungal isolates crude extracts, with IC50 values of 96.3 and 117.4 µg/ml, respectively. Additionally, it showed promising antibacterial efficacy against pathogenic bacteria and fungi. Moreover, both crude extracts of fungal isolates exhibited antioxidant activity, with EC50 values of 234.8 µg/ml and 133.4 µg/ml respectively. Endophytic Alternaria species from leaves of R. pruinosa are a novel source for bioactive compounds that used in different medical fields.

abstract: Background This study aimed to identify factors associated with improvement in distance presenting visual acuity (dpVA) after refraction and with successful reading rehabilitation among patients aged 50 years or older with low vision. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study using medical records from a low-vision rehabilitation center in Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo, Brazil, between 2009 and 2019. Improvement after refraction was defined as a gain of at least two 0.2 logMAR after manifest refraction for distance correction. Successful reading rehabilitation using spectacles and/or magnifiers was defined as the ability to read texts of 1.5 M or smaller. Candidate predictors included age, sex, dpVA, distance best-corrected visual acuity, anatomical region responsible for low vision, educational level, spherical equivalent, and cylinder power. Logistic regression was performed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results Overall, 558 patients were included, with a mean age of 67 years. Retinal involvement was the most frequent anatomical finding. Improvement in dpVA after refraction occurred in 20.3% of patients, and dpVA and spherical equivalent were significant predictors of this outcome. Among 346 literate patients, 252 (72.8%) were able to read 1.5 M texts after rehabilitation. Successful reading rehabilitation was associated with better distance best-corrected visual acuity, retinal involvement, higher educational level, and female sex, whereas older age and worse distance best-corrected visual acuity were associated with lower odds of success. Conclusions Clinical, refractive, and demographic factors were associated with dpVA improvement after refraction and successful reading rehabilitation in older adults with low vision.

abstract: Refractive surgery corrects vision using different corneal techniques; however, dry eye disease (DED) is one of its commonest side effects. This descriptive survey questionnaire-based study aimed to evaluate prevalence and factors associated with dry eye symptoms after refractive surgery among survey respondents using ocular surface disease index (OSDI) questionnaire in Saudi Arabia. Four hundred and thirty nine participants were included. Dry eye OSDI scores compared across different epidemiological risk factors, focusing on refractive surgery type and postoperative duration. Photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) or Femtosecond (FS)-LASIK, and small incision lenticule extraction procedures were performed on 201 (45.79%), 222 (50.56%), and 16 (3.65%) participants, respectively. According to OSDI scores, 391 participants (89.1%) had dry eye symptoms after surgery, with 69.5% classified as severe, 11.4% as moderate, 8.2% as mild, and only 10.9% as normal. Insignificant gender differences were observed; however, OSDI-defined dry eye symptoms prevalence was lower in Eastern Province and in participants with longer post-surgery durations. Participants who underwent PRK reported higher prevalence of OSDI-defined dry eye symptoms versus those underwent LASIK/FS-LASIK. In conclusion, Self-reported OSDI-defined DED were common after refractive surgery, especially after PRK. Females and early post-surgery patients have more severe OSDI-defined dry eye symptoms. Living in a humid area (Eastern Province) may reduce risk of OSDI-defined DED post-surgery.

abstract: Background Malignant distal biliary obstruction (MDBO) is commonly managed with endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP)-guided transpapillary stenting. Fully covered self-expandable metal stents (FCSEMSs) provide durable biliary drainage but may increase the risk of acute cholecystitis due to cystic duct obstruction. Prophylactic endoscopic transpapillary gallbladder stenting (ETGBS) at the time of FCSEMS placement has been proposed to reduce the risk of cholecystitis after FCSEMS placement. However, the available evidence is limited. This study aims to explore the potential clinical benefit of attempting prophylactic ETGBS by estimating the incidence of acute cholecystitis after FCSEMS placement and characterizing the technical feasibility and safety of the strategy in patients with MDBO. Methods This multicenter, prospective, single-arm exploratory study (PROTECT study) will be conducted at four institutions in Japan. In all eligible patients undergoing FCSEMS placement for MDBO, prophylactic ETGBS will be attempted. The primary endpoint is the incidence of acute cholecystitis within 30 days after FCSEMS placement. Secondary endpoints include the technical success rate of ETGBS, procedure-related adverse events, the incidence of acute cholecystitis within 30 days among patients with technically successful ETGBS, and the cumulative incidence of acute cholecystitis from day 31 until the end of follow-up. The target enrollment is 50 patients. The primary endpoint will be summarized as a proportion with a two-sided 90% Wilson score confidence interval. A two-sided 95% Wilson score confidence interval will also be reported as a supplementary analysis, and a supplementary exploratory two-sided one-sample score test will compare the observed proportion with the historical benchmark of 12.1%. Discussion This study will provide prospective data on the potential clinical utility, technical feasibility, and safety of attempting prophylactic ETGBS and may inform the design of future comparative studies. Trial registration Japan Registry of Clinical Trials number: jRCT1030250361. Registered on 12 September 2025.

abstract: Background Routine clinical breast examination (CBE) services contribute to breast cancer early-detection activities in Bangladesh, but national program performance and reporting completeness are poorly characterized. We assessed reported CBE activity, geographic variation, positivity, reporting completeness, and temporal trends from 2019 through 2025. Methods We retrospectively analyzed routine CBE program data from 1,209 location-specific eligible facilities across Bangladesh from January 2019 through December 2025. Because individual-level identifiers were unavailable, records were analyzed as CBE events rather than unique women screened. Reported CBE examination rates used estimated populations of women aged 30-69 years, with district denominators proportionally allocated using census-based population distributions. Reporting completeness was defined as submitted facility-month reports divided by expected reports. Interrupted time-series regression assessed changes associated with March 2020 using calendar-month fixed effects and heteroskedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent standard errors. Results A total of 3,193,080 reported CBE events were recorded. The reported examination rate increased from 0.3% in 2019 to 2.4% in 2023, then declined to 1.8% in 2024 and 1.1% in 2025. In 2025, division-level rates ranged from 0.7% to 1.7% and district-level rates from 0.2% to 2.8%. Overall positivity was 1.0% (31,624 positive events), reaching 1.6% in 2025. Mean annual reporting completeness rose from 12.1% in 2019 to 42.2% in 2024 and was 39.7% in 2025; no month reached 60% national completeness. Interrupted time-series analysis found no significant immediate level change (14,416 events; 95% CI -7,438-36,269; P = 0.196) or post-intervention slope change (-375 events/month; 95% CI -1,673-923; P = 0.571). Conclusions Reported CBE activity expanded through 2023 but subsequently declined, with marked geographic variation and persistently incomplete reporting. These findings describe reported program activity rather than true population screening coverage. Strengthening routine reporting, individual-level tracking, quality assurance, and referral follow-up is needed for more reliable program evaluation.

abstract: Handwritten digit recognition has considerable potential for automating document analysis. However, in real-world scenarios, character adhesion is a critical constraint on the performance of traditional automated educational scoring systems. To address the challenge of segmenting touching handwritten digits, this research presents a systematic investigation from both data and methodological perspectives. First, a standardized, category-balanced Two-digit Touching image dataset is constructed. By covering all 100 combinations from "00" to "99," it simulates realistic adhesion patterns by defining a maximum overlap ratio and introducing random misalignment, thereby providing a fair benchmark for algorithm evaluation. On the methodological front, this paper proposes a "cutting domain" graph-theoretic segmentation framework. This framework decouples the adhesion segmentation problem into two stages: constructing a structured, low-cost search space (the cutting domain) with a threshold-free growth algorithm, and then transforming the segmentation task into an optimal path search on a graph. Within this cutting domain, the globally optimal Dijkstra's algorithm and a family of direction-biased A* heuristic algorithms are implemented and compared with traditional methods (the Vertical Projection Method and the Watershed algorithm) as well as a deep supervised segmentation baseline (U-Net). Experimental results show that the proposed graph-theoretic segmentation method significantly outperforms traditional methods. Among the methods tested, the Left-Biased A* algorithm achieves the highest recognition accuracy of 93.13% on the test set, an improvement of over 5 percentage points over traditional methods. Ablation experiments confirm the critical role of connectivity constraints. Further evaluation on real-world handwritten digit strings (the CVL dataset) confirms the framework's generalization, maintaining 91.4% accuracy, whereas a cross-paradigm comparison shows a supervised U-Net baseline collapsing from 95.90% to 53.05% under the same domain shift. This study provides a standardized evaluation benchmark and novel methodological insights for segmenting touching characters, thereby advancing document image analysis technology.
