abstract: Ground-Based Synthetic Aperture Radar (GB-SAR) systems frequently suffer from insufficient transceiver isolation due to their compact architecture. This insufficiency leads to transmitted signal leakage into the receiving channel, generating third-order intermodulation distortion (IM3). Consequently, the imaging signal to noise ratio (SNR) is degraded and artifacts in the range direction are introduced. Utilizing an independently developed Ku-band GB-SAR system termed S-SAR M, this study explores the influence mechanism of transceiver isolation on imaging quality through dynamic adjustment of antenna spatial parameters. It identifies a system-specific critical isolation threshold and an optimal design range, thereby offering a theoretical basis and practical guidelines for hardware optimization of GB-SAR systems. The isolation model is quantitatively calibrated against the measured horn radiation pattern and antenna geometry with a root-mean-square error of 1.8 dB, and the critical threshold is derived analytically from receiver nonlinearity parameters through the third-order input intercept point (IIP3). The results indicate that antenna angle is the dominant factor for isolation improvement, with an average enhancement of 56.3 percent achieved as the angle increases from 0 to 60 degrees. Antenna separation exhibits a synergistic effect on isolation at larger angles. A critical isolation threshold of 74 dB is established to suppress range artifacts induced by IM3 in the S-SAR M system; below this threshold, artifacts consistently occur. Moreover, a tri-segmented nonlinear relationship between isolation and SNR is observed, with an optimal balance region located between 74 dB and 80 dB where the peak SNR is maintained. One-way analysis of variance delivers a result with p less than 0.001 and confirms the significance of these trends. A quantitative artifact-to-background energy ratio further corroborates the visual artifact classification. These findings offer important insights for enhancing the performance of GB-SAR systems. It should be noted that the reported numerical thresholds are specific to the S-SAR M hardware configuration; a normalized isolation-margin framework is therefore provided to transfer the methodology, with platform-specific calibration, to GB-SAR systems using other frequency bands or receiver architectures.

abstract: Rip currents cause most surf-beach lifeguard rescues and most beach drowning incidents, yet automated detection relies on costly instrumentation that scales poorly across the many beaches that lack lifeguards. We propose an end-to-end pipeline producing pixel-level rip-current likelihood maps directly from raw unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) video without manual ground-control points - to our knowledge the first to do so from uncalibrated drone video, prior automated approaches operating at video-clip granularity or requiring surveyed camera installations. The pipeline composes (i) dense optical-flow estimation with five classical algorithm variants; (ii) a sphere-aware projection mapping pixel coordinates to local-isometric ground coordinates, with a tilt-aware Jacobian correction of per-pixel velocity; (iii) a CNN six-class scene parser (sky/sea/land/foam/structure/void), trained on frames verified by dense pixel-matching to contain no extraction from either evaluation video; (iv) a per-pixel temporal accumulator flagging pixels whose flow direction agrees with the locally-estimated offshore direction within ±90∘ - the physical boundary of seaward-directed flow, shown robust in an 18-scene sensitivity sweep; and (v) post-processing by Gaussian smoothing (σ=25 px) and a normalized cross-algorithm ensemble. We evaluate on two UAV-captured rip-current videos at Palm Beach and Haulover Park, Florida, annotated by consensus among three coastal-science domain experts. At the physically-neutral T=90∘ default the framework attains precision-recall AUC 0.636 at Palm Beach and 0.660 at Haulover; per-scene selection - of the angular tolerance, ensemble membership, mixing weight, sphere tilt, and which modules are engaged - against the same expert annotation used for evaluation raises these to 0.7066 and 0.7040, reported as an optimistic upper bound rather than an expected-performance estimate. We release the source code, the trained sea-mask refiner, a YOLOv8m-seg deep-learning baseline, and the evaluation scripts. Evaluation is limited to these two expert-annotated scenes, and the method requires visible surface tracers (foam, dye, or sediment fronts) advected by the current.

abstract: Schistosomiasis and salmonellosis are major public health problems in Africa, contribute substantially to morbidity. Schistosoma-Salmonella co-infection is a neglected and overlooked health condition with important clinical and public health implications. Therefore, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize evidence on the epidemiology, biological mechanisms, and antimicrobial resistance of Schistosoma-Salmonella co-infection in Africa. A systematic review and Meta-analysis were conducted following the PRISMA framework. The pooled prevalence of co-infection was estimated using a random effects model, with at 95% confidence intervals. Between studies heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q test and the I2 statistic. Subgroup analyses were performed according to Schistosoma species and country to explore potential source of heterogeneity. This systematic review found that the pooled prevalence of Schistosoma-Salmonella co-infection in Africa was 9%. Species specific pooled prevalence was 4% for Schistosoma mansoni-Salmonella co-infection and 12% for Schistosoma hematobium-Salmonella co-infection. Country based subgroup analysis showed prevalence of Schistosoma mansoni-Salmonella co-infection of 2% in Ethiopia, 9% in Sudan, 2% in Democratic republic of Congo and 4% in Nigeria, while Schistosoma hematobium-Salmonella co-infection prevalence were 0%, 25%, and 8% in Ethiopia, Sudan, and Nigeria respectively. Schistosoma-Salmonella co-infection is driven by immune modulation, tissue pathology, and parasite bacterium interactions that support persistent infection and compromise therapeutic efficacy, thereby contributing to treatment failure and the emergence of antimicrobial resistance. Schistosoma-Salmonella co-infection represents an important and under-recognized public health concern in Africa, with a pooled prevalence of 9%. The findings demonstrate notable variation in co-infection prevalence across Schistosoma species and geographical settings, with higher rates observed among Schistosoma haematobium compared with Schistosoma mansoni. Strengthened surveillance systems, improving early diagnosis, and implementing integrated control strategies are essential to reduce the burden and enhance clinical management of this neglected co-infection in Africa.

abstract: Background Serial ultrasound measurements may help characterize muscle wasting in critically ill patients. The flexor carpi ulnaris (FCU) is a superficial forearm muscle that may provide an additional assessment site. We described longitudinal FCU and biceps brachii (BB) cross-sectional area (CSA) changes and explored between-muscle differences and clinical associations. Methods This prospective two-center observational study enrolled 23 intensive care unit (ICU) patients; 20 were included in the analysis (median age, 57 years; range, 33-82). CSA was measured on days 0, 5, 7, and 14 after ICU admission. Analyses used Friedman tests, exact conditional Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction, and exploratory Spearman correlations. Post hoc between-muscle comparisons assessed participant-level percentage changes. Results Mean FCU CSA decreased from 1.36 to 1.08 cm² and mean BB CSA from 6.08 to 5.09 cm² over 14 days, corresponding to reductions of 20.9% and 16.4% in the unrounded group means. The median paired difference in percentage change (FCU minus BB) was -11.9 percentage points on day 7 (unadjusted p = 0.0023), meeting the Bonferroni threshold of 0.05/3. Differences on days 5 and 14 did not meet this threshold (p = 0.1429 and p = 0.2024). Baseline CSA values were correlated (ρ = 0.845, p < 0.001), as were 14-day percentage changes (ρ = 0.549, p = 0.0122); correlation p-values were unadjusted. Conclusions Serial ultrasound documented decreases in FCU and BB CSA in this small cohort, with an exploratory direct comparison identifying a greater proportional FCU decrease on day 7. These findings support further evaluation of FCU ultrasound as an additional muscle-monitoring measure. Its value for earlier detection of muscle wasting or diagnosis of ICU-acquired weakness requires direct validation.

abstract: Neurotropic single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) viruses can disrupt brain function, yet little is known about how host virus receptor expression develops across the human lifespan or whether these trajectories differ between females and males. We focused on postnatal development using postmortem transcriptomic data from 33 human donors (4 months-82 years; both sexes), comprising 52 cerebral hemispheres and 15 brain areas, to characterize developmental patterns of 67 host receptor genes that mediate entry of major ssRNA viral families. Using sex-specific LOESS trajectory modelling, hierarchical clustering, and sliding-window differential expression analyses, we identified multiple non-linear developmental programs governing virus receptor expression. About half of female-male gene-area trajectory pairs exhibited divergent developmental patterns. Sex differences were most pronounced in the cortex, where high-dimensional receptor expression profiles were sufficient to predict the sex of individual cases. Sex differential expression was most frequent during early childhood, coinciding with sensitive periods of cortical circuit refinement. A targeted prenatal analysis revealed that virus receptor expression was predominantly male-biased before birth, contrasting with the predominantly female-biased expression observed during the early postnatal period. Although receptors from most viral families were broadly distributed across developmental programs, a subset of sex-by-age expression clusters showed some enrichment for specific viral lineages and glial-associated cell-type signatures. Together, these findings reveal that virus receptor expression in the human brain is organized into structured, sex-biased trajectories that dynamically reorganize over development, providing the first developmental atlas of viral entry receptors in the human brain.

abstract: The stoichiometric ratios of soil available nutrients serve as a pivotal indicator for assessing the sustainability of farmland and nutrient cycling efficiency within fragile ecosystems. Soil texture and depth are significant factors influencing nutrient availability, however, their regulatory mechanisms within highland lakeshore agricultural systems remain poorly understood. This study, conducted in the Yilong Lake watershed of the low-latitude plateau in southwest China, collected 216 soil samples. It innovatively determined both total organic carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus (SOC, TN, TP) and available carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus (DOC, AN, AP) simultaneously. Path analysis was employed to examine the direct and indirect associations between soil texture (Clay, Loam, Clay Loam, Sand) and depth (0-20 cm, 20-40 cm, 40-60 cm) on nutrient ratio measurements. Findings indicate: (1) Distinct nutrient limitation and leaching risk patterns emerged across soil textures: Loam exhibited strongest carbon and nitrogen sequestration capacity; Although Clay Loam exhibits reduced phosphorus availability due to iron and aluminium oxide immobilisation, it demonstrates pronounced nitrogen limitation rather than phosphorus limitation; Sand though rich in available phosphorus, had the lowest C:N, suggesting heightened carbon and nitrogen leaching risks. (2) Soil depth significantly altered nutrient ratios: topsoil (0-20 cm) showed marked nutrient enrichment, while subsoil (40-60 cm) exhibited elevated TN:TP, suggesting that nitrification may have intensified with increasing depth. (3) Path analysis revealed that texture directly regulates nutrient measurement ratios (DOC:AN) and indirectly governs C:N:P balance by influencing SOC, AP, and AN content; depth directly or indirectly affects measurement relationships through pathways such as TP. This study elucidates the key regulatory roles of soil texture and depth in nutrient ratios, particularly available nutrient balance, providing direct scientific evidence for implementing differentiated, precision nutrient management based on soil physical properties in Yilong Lake basin agroecosystems and other ecologically fragile areas.

abstract: Background Helping professionals face elevated risks of compassion fatigue and burnout, yet the daily processes through which emotional transformation occurs during therapeutic interventions remain poorly understood. This study examined how participants' daily reflections shifted across the Emotion-Focused Training for Helping Professions (EFT-HP), analyzed through three complementary theoretical frameworks: Emotion-Focused Therapy's inner dialogue model (self-criticism, self-compassion, self-protection), Compassion-Focused Therapy's three-systems framework (threat, drive, soothing), and Ekman's basic emotion theory (primary emotions). Method Two hundred twenty-five helping professionals (88.0% female; M age = 38.7 years) from healthcare, social work, psychology, and education began the 14-day online EFT-HP intervention. Primary analyses focused on the 146 participants who completed at least 9 of the 14 days (completers), whose daily written reflections yielded 7,307 coded reflection units. Reflections were analyzed with directed content analysis and frequency quantification, applying non-exclusive, AI-assisted coding within three theoretical frameworks-EFT inner-dialogue categories, CFT emotion-regulation systems, and Ekman's discrete emotions-with a verbatim textual evidence excerpt retained for every assigned code. Results Across the intervention, participants' reflections shifted from threat- and self-criticism-related content toward soothing and self-compassion. Within the EFT inner-dialogue framework, Self-Compassion was the most frequent category (17.9% of units) and was sustained throughout (Day-13 peak 30.8%), while Self-Criticism fell from 14.3% on Day 1 to 3.9% on Day 14 (73% relative decrease) and Self-Protection peaked on Day 6 (11.3%). Within the CFT emotion-regulation framework, the soothing system was the most frequently coded system overall (31.8% of units), followed by drive (20.4%); over the 14 days the threat system declined from 35.4% on Day 1 to 7.0% on Day 14 (80% relative decrease). Within Ekman's discrete-emotion framework, specific emotions were named less frequently: Fear declined from 2.7% to 0.8%, Anger peaked on Day 6 (15.0%), Joy rose to a Day-13 peak (14.8%), and Love was comparatively prominent (11.9% overall, Day-5 peak). Conclusions Across the 14-day intervention, participants' daily reflections showed substantial shifts in emotional content, characterized by marked self-criticism and threat reduction alongside sustained self-compassion and soothing activation. Triangulated findings across three analytical frameworks: EFT inner dialogue, CFT emotion systems, and Ekman's primary emotions, are consistent with the emotional-transformation processes proposed by EFT-HP and with findings from previous controlled trials. Because the three frameworks were applied to the same reflection data, their convergence reflects analytic (theoretical) triangulation rather than independent confirmation.

abstract: Forecasting stock price volatility at the individual stock level is a major challenge in managing financial risks; it has widespread implications for portfolio strategies, pricing derivatives, and assessing regulatory capital adequacy. Although there have been a number of studies using market indices (e.g., VIX and associated methods) to study forecasting stock market volatility, relatively few studies have applied and evaluated a number of different types of machine learning methods to individual stock data in terms of actual (realised) volatility forecasting. This study fills that gap by presenting a comprehensive analysis of the relationship between stock price volatility and various machine learning techniques on a sample of ten well-known US stocks (across three sectors: technology, finance, and energy) based on data from January 2018 to December 2024 (1,759 trading days). We apply five modelling approaches: a classical GARCH(1,1) econometric model, a classical GJR-GARCH(1,1,1) econometric model, a Random Forest regressor, a two-layer Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, and a two-layer Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) network. For each of the four modelling techniques, we use a rolling 5-day annualised actual (realised) volatility forecast as our final outcomes. Evaluation of the prediction results of each of these models was measured using RMSE, MAE, QLIKE loss, parametric Value-at-Risk (VaR) measures, Expected Shortfall (ES), and the Kupiec backtest. We also performed an analysis of the prevailing market regime through K-Means clustering, created an ablation study using variables as features in the models to assess the importance of those variables, and developed a computational efficiency benchmark for each model. In terms of predicted errors, Random Forest was proven to yield very low predicted error (mean RMSE = 0.0892) in comparison to deep learning methods, plus Random Forest was able to be trained approximately 7 times faster than deep learning methods. GRU was ranked second and outperformed LSTM on most of the metrics used in this evaluation. GARCH models remain a viable option for estimating risk measures and calibrating VaR, especially during period of stability in the financial markets.

abstract: Breast cancer (BC) represents the most prevalent malignant tumor among women globally, with its pronounced heterogeneity presenting significant challenges for precision diagnosis and treatment. Aberrant lipid metabolism, particularly the ratio of low-density lipoprotein to high-density lipoprotein (LHR), has garnered considerable interest in relation to BC development and progression. Nevertheless, the association between LHR and clinicopathological characteristics remains inadequately explored. To address this gap, the present retrospective study analyzed 583 BC patients who underwent surgical treatment at Qilu Hospital of Shandong University. Preoperative blood lipid profiles and clinicopathological data were systematically collected to investigate the association between LHR and critical features, including molecular subtypes. The findings indicated that LHR levels were significantly elevated in patients aged 46 years or older, postmenopausal women, and individuals with a body mass index of 25 kg/m2 or higher. Subgroup analyses incorporating age, menopausal status, and BMI suggested potential interactions between these clinical factors and LHR. Although univariate analysis demonstrated an association between LHR and certain clinicopathological features, multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that menopausal status, rather than LHR, was the sole independent predictor of ER-positive and PR-positive status. Therefore, LHR should not be considered an independent predictive biomarker for receptor status. In conclusion, although the LHR demonstrates statistically significant associations with certain clinicopathological characteristics, its modest effect sizes and discriminative ability close to chance indicate limited clinical utility as an independent biomarker. These preliminary findings highlight the need for future research focused on identifying reliable metabolic signatures. Such studies should consider utilizing multi-marker panels instead of relying exclusively on individual lipid metrics for risk stratification in breast cancer.

abstract: Background Glioma is a highly malignant intracranial tumor with dismal prognosis. Tumor angiogenesis critically drives glioma growth and invasion, making vascular endothelial cells a promising therapeutic target. Buthus martensii Karsch chlorotoxin (BmK CT) presents favorable antitumor properties, whereas its regulatory role in glioma angiogenesis and the specific mechanism remain poorly defined. Aim To investigate the regulatory role of BmK CT in glioma angiogenesis and the underlying mechanism. Methods HUVECs were cultured alone or exposed to glioma conditioned medium prepared from primary glioma cells. Functional assays were performed to assess the impacts of BmK CT on endothelial proliferation, migration and tube formation. Quantitative proteomics and bioinformatics analysis were applied to screen differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) and explore underlying mechanisms. Results BmK CT significantly inhibited the proliferation of HUVEC cells and reduced their migration and tube formation abilities. BmK CT reversed the promoting effect of primary glioma cells on the migration of HUVEC cells. Proteomics identified multiple DEPs. Enrichment analysis suggested that BmK CT exerts an anti-glioma angiogenesis effect through a multi-target mechanism by inhibiting pro-angiogenic pathways, blocking energy metabolism, and regulating the inflammatory microenvironment. Furthermore, expression pattern clustering analysis revealed six DEPs expression patterns. Parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) analysis supported nine candidate proteins (THBS1, THBS4, COMP, F2, A2M, C3, RIGI, EZR, and ITGA6) associated with glioma angiogenesis. Conclusion: This study demonstrated in vitro that BmK CT inhibits endothelial angiogenic behaviors relevant to glioma progression and modulates the tumor microenvironment, and identified nine candidate DEPs, providing a theoretical basis for future molecular targeted therapy strategies for glioma.

abstract: Accurate species-level taxonomic classification of microbial amplicon sequences remains challenging due to the difficulty of resolving subtle variations within conserved ribosomal regions. Traditional similarity-based methods struggle with short amplicons and sequences with poor database representation. No existing method performs robustly across the full spectrum of amplicon lengths, limiting applicability across diverse sequencing platforms and variable-region targets. We present Taxonova, a deep learning framework for both short- and long-read ribosomal amplicons. Evaluated across physical and biome-simulated mock communities representing seven biomes (via the accompanying benchmark tool Taxobench), Taxonova attains species-level F-measures of 0.76-1.00 (median 0.94) for short-read and 0.82-0.99 (median 0.97) for long-read amplicons spanning 250 bp to 4,900 bp, reduces the species-level abundance-estimation error (L1 norm) by a median of 0.52 to 1.50 depending on amplicon region, and has a species-level false-positive rate that is a median of 16.2 × 10-4 lower than that of the other classifiers. Species-level assignment is expected to be most reliable for well-characterised communities, such as human-associated microbiomes. To demonstrate real-world applicability, we also compared amplicon-derived taxonomic profiles to paired shotgun whole-genome sequencing from gut, soil and vaginal microbiomes; Taxonova achieves the strongest species-level concordance (Jaccard) in all three studies, with a species-level Jaccard index 0.009 to 0.022 higher than that of the next-best classifier across both high- and low-complexity communities. Taxonova runs at a throughput of roughly 100 sequences per second on a single CPU core, making it suitable for routine deployment in research settings.

abstract: Background Growing awareness of alcohol harms and health consciousness has increased public interest in reducing alcohol consumption. However, little is known about how public interest in nonalcoholic beverages and lifestyles has changed over time. This study analyzed long-term and seasonal patterns in Google searches related to nonalcoholic beverages and lifestyles in the US from 2004 to 2026. Method Google Trends data assessed monthly relative search volume (RSV) for five alcohol reduction-related search terms representing two categories: non-alcohol lifestyles ("quit drinking", "Dry January", and "sober curious") and nonalcoholic beverages ("non alcoholic" and "mocktail"). Descriptive analyses were conducted to assess temporal patterns in RSV. Long-term trends, seasonal patterns, and changes in interest associated with COVID-19 were analyzed using quadratic regression and segmented regression models with Newey-West standard errors to address autocorrelation and heteroskedasticity. Results Public interest in both alcohol reduction-related lifestyles and nonalcoholic beverages increased substantially over the study period. Beverage-related searches demonstrated more rapid growth following the COVID-19 pandemic, with significant positive post-pandemic trend changes observed for both "nonalcoholic" (β = 0.564, p < 0.001) and "mocktail" (β = 1.103, p < 0.001) terms, whereas lifestyle-related searches remained stable or grew slowly after the pandemic. Seasonal analyses showed lifestyle search "quit drinking" peaked in January, while beverage search "non alcoholic" peaked in December. Conclusions Public interest in alcohol reduction via nonalcoholic beverages and lifestyles has risen, reflecting changing cultural and behavioral attitudes towards alcohol. These findings highlight the potential of Google search behavior to provide real-time insights into changing alcohol-related attitudes, harm reduction behaviors, and interest in no- and low-alcohol (NoLo) alternatives.

abstract: This study evaluates the agricultural co-benefits of large-scale environmental regulation. Existing studies often focus on crop yields and condition on production inputs that may themselves respond to policy interventions, potentially understating the overall production effect. Using Chinese county-level panel data from 2000 to 2024, we employ a reduced-form difference-in-differences (DiD) design to estimate the net total effect of the Air Pollution Prevention and Control Action Plan (hereafter, the Action Plan) on per-capita agricultural output, with double machine learning used as a robustness check for flexible meteorological adjustment. The baseline DiD estimates indicate that the policy increased per-capita output of grain, vegetables and edible fungi, and oilseeds by approximately 42.6%, 10.4%, and 18.1%, respectively, in key regulated regions. Mechanism analysis shows that the policy significantly reduced fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations, consistent with the proposed biophysical pathway linking improved air quality to agricultural production. The reduced-form design may also retain production adjustments induced by environmental improvement, although these behavioral responses are not directly identified. Heterogeneity analysis indicates stronger grain responses in northern regions, whereas vegetables, edible fungi, and oilseeds show stronger responses in the South; grain and oilseed responses are also stronger in high-population areas. These findings provide evidence of agricultural co-benefits from air-pollution regulation and support closer coordination between environmental and agricultural policies.

abstract: Children draw on multiple sources of information during word learning, including speaker testimony and lexical expectations. Yet, little is known about how these cues jointly influence children's ability to learn new words. The present study examined the combined effect of speaker accuracy and mutual exclusivity (ME) on short-term retention of label-object associations in 4- to 7-year-old monolingual English speaking children. Children were presented novel and familiar object pairs, and were taught novel labels by either an accurate speaker (one who previously labeled familiar objects correctly) or an inaccurate speaker (one who previously labeled familiar objects incorrectly). Novel labels were introduced under two conditions: Align-with-ME (speakers labeled the novel object with novel names) and Conflict-with-ME (speakers labeled the familiar object with novel names, conflicting with ME). Results showed that children retained novel labels for novel objects from both accurate and inaccurate speakers when speaker testimony aligned with ME expectations. This suggests that children are open to learning novel words from speakers regardless of their prior accuracy and may also draw on other available cues, such as label-object co-occurrences, during learning. However, when speaker testimony violated ME expectations, children performed poorly, possibly due to difficulty disambiguating between speaker testimony and their existing lexical knowledge. Together, these findings suggest that children's short-term retention of label-object associations is supported when available cues align, irrespective of speaker accuracy status. These associations, however, become less robust when ME and speaker cues provide conflicting information.

abstract: Training enhances classification accuracy in citizen science by directing visual attention toward predefined features, but may constrain attention to unexpected objects or features. We examined this tradeoff through an analysis of 206 citizen science discoveries and through controlled experiments using eye-tracking and verbal protocols. The analysis of existing discoveries showed that untrained contributors produced a broader range of discovery types, including the majority of opportunistic and serendipitous discoveries. In the primary experimental study, explicitly trained observers showed 34% fewer fixations on non-diagnostic features compared to untrained observers. Training also reduced attention to secondary entities and constrained how observers described novel stimuli, a phenomenon we term classification transference. Trained observers described unfamiliar entities by referencing missing trained-category features rather than reporting new attributes. Implicitly trained observers preserved broader attentional sampling while maintaining sensitivity to variation. The second experimental study provided a robustness check with 84 additional participants using written responses and confirmed the patterns observed in the first experiment. These findings demonstrate that training shapes both where observers look and what they report, establishing a perceptual boundary on discovery potential that conventional accuracy measures cannot detect.

title: Transient feedforward communication between somatosensory and premotor cortex supports goal-directed behavior.

author_details.name: Yadollah Ranjbar-Slamloo

abstract: Goal-directed behavior requires sensory information to be transformed into motor commands, yet the precise temporal structure of communication between sensory and motor cortices during this process remains poorly understood. By simultaneously recording spiking activity from primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and secondary motor cortex (M2) in mice performing a tactile delayed go/no-go task, we identified a brief, stimulus-triggered communication window that predicted behavioral success. Time-shifted canonical correlation analysis revealed a sharp, feedforward surge in S1 → M2 coupling peaking at a short latency, as expected for a potentially direct transmission pathway. This transient interaction conveyed stimulus-selective information such that the S1 → M2 communication subspace aligned with stimulus-coding axes in both regions. In contrast, M2 → S1 feedback interactions were weaker and delayed. Brief optogenetic suppression of S1 reduced both M2 stimulus selectivity and behavioral discriminability, consistent with a functional role of the transient S1 → M2 coupling. These findings demonstrate that sensorimotor transformation is supported not by sustained linear coupling along the stimulus- or choice- axis, but by a short-lived and highly selective feedforward communication channel that rapidly transmits reliable sensory representations into motor-planning circuits.

abstract: In cut slopes composed of strongly weathered mudstone, coupled wetting-drying cycles and traffic-induced vibration readily trigger progressive structural damage and slumping. Conventional single tests-such as isolated dynamic triaxial tests or independent wetting-drying simulations-cannot accurately capture the underlying microstructural evolution. As demonstrated by recent research, such as the experimental investigation of acidic dry-wet cycles on coal-rock combinations, relying on uncoupled testing fails to reproduce synergistic damage mechanisms, highlighting a critical need for multi-field experimental frameworks. Therefore, here we report a new experimental framework in which ultrasonic responses measured during wetting-drying cycling alone and during coupled wetting-drying-vibration loading were compared, including wave velocity, first-arrival amplitude, time-domain features, frequency-domain features and spectral centroid, to identify the deterioration state of remoulded strongly weathered mudstone. Uniaxial compressive strength and elastic modulus were evaluated concurrently to clarify the evolution of hydraulic damage caused by repeated swelling and shrinkage of hydrophilic clay minerals and the associated transition of macroscopic mechanical behaviour towards plastic deformation. The arrival time of the received wave lagged markedly, and under coupled loading the waveform changed from a steep, prominent peak to a right-shifted attenuated response. During wetting-drying cycling alone, the decrease in first-arrival amplitude could be divided into an initial sharp-drop stage and a later slow-accumulation stage. When high-frequency vibration was superimposed, microcracks coalesced more rapidly, and both wave velocity and strength decayed faster. The migration of the frequency spectrum and its centroid towards lower frequencies can serve as a rapid and convenient indicator of different damage states in strongly weathered mudstone. Accelerated microcrack coalescence driven by high-frequency resonance and frequent displacement cycling is the main reason why acoustic attenuation under superimposed vibration is stronger than that under wetting-drying cycling alone, with frequency exerting a greater influence than amplitude. Using wave velocity, first-arrival amplitude and spectral centroid as ultrasonic parameters, we further constructed a dimensionless vibration-disturbance coefficient (IfA) based on the entropy-weight method to quantify vibration disturbance under different working conditions, and we suggest that it can be incorporated into a three-dimensional strength-surface model. By bridging non-destructive acoustic monitoring and macroscopic mechanical degradation under coupled environmental-dynamic loading, this research establishes a rapid, non-destructive, and cost-effective quantitative tool for real-time tracking of internal micro-fatigue damage and estimating residual peak strength in weathered rock masses. Ultimately, these findings provide essential theoretical insight and data-driven decision support for long-term stability assessment, risk mitigation, and early warning of transportation corridor slopes subjected to seasonal weathering and vehicle traffic.

abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) are proteinopathies characterized by pathological accumulation of amyloid beta, phosphorylated-tau, and alpha-synuclein. Impaired clearance of these proteins is thought to contribute to disease pathogenesis, whereas preserved or enhanced clearance may be compensatory. Beyond intracellular degradation within neurons and glial cells, an extracellular clearance pathway, the glymphatic system, facilitates cerebrospinal fluid flow into perivascular spaces, exchange with interstitial fluid, and subsequent clearance from the brain. Glymphatic transport may therefore be critical for removal of excess proteins and metabolic waste, and its dysfunction could promote protein aggregation and neurodegeneration. The Glymphatic's Role In Proteinopathies (GRIP) study is an observational case-control imaging and biomarker study comparing glymphatic clearance in patients with AD, PD, and DLB versus healthy controls. We aim to recruit 70 participants: PD (n = 20), DLB (n = 10), AD (n = 20), and age- and sex-matched healthy controls (n = 20). The AD group will be stratified by pathology, with half amyloid-positive/tau-negative (A + T-) and half amyloid- and tau-positive (A + T+). The PD group will be stratified by disease duration. Participants will undergo baseline MRI followed by intrathecal injection of gadobutrol (0.25 mmol) and serial MRI at 5, 24, 48, and 72 hours. Influx and efflux of tracer will be modeled from T1 signal changes. Blood will be sampled repeatedly from 1 to 72 hours; cerebrospinal fluid will be collected at baseline. Individual glymphatic clearance will be estimated using population pharmacokinetic methods, where gadobutrol serves as a tracer. Sleep will be monitored with triaxial accelerometry and sleep diaries. The primary outcome is group differences in glymphatic clearance metrics between each disease group and controls; secondary analyses will explore associations with cognition, disease severity and duration, sleep quality, and cerebrospinal fluid protein levels.

abstract: Digital Surface Models (DSMs) are widely used as important sources of topographic information for earth science and environmental applications. The accuracy of DSMs has direct impacts on several environmental calculations and processes. Therefore, it is imperative to select the most suitable DSM based on the aim and accuracy requirements of each application. However, the use of an appropriate DSM has always been a challenge. This study evaluated the vertical accuracy and performance of the freely available Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM), NASA DEM (NASADEM), and Advanced Spaceborne Thermal Emission and Reflection Radiometer (ASTER). The DSM elevations were measured against high-precision national geodetic control points. Among other accuracy metrics, we computed Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and examined the influence of elevation, slope, aspect, curvature, and land cover. At the national scale, SRTM (RMSE of 19.55 m) and NASADEM (RMSE of 19.99 m) showed comparable performance, while ASTER produced a higher RMSE of 22.13 m. However, the principal finding was that DSM accuracy varied substantially across Malawi's diverse terrain. All the DSMs performed particularly well in the low-lying Lower Shire Valley, with RMSEs of 3.25 m (NASADEM), 4.30 m (SRTM), and 6.91 m (ASTER). Errors increased markedly in the Highlands, where RMSE reached 35.03 m for NASADEM, 33.62 m for SRTM, and 36.94 m for ASTER. In addition, accuracy decreased with increasing elevation and slope, particularly in highland regions and on slopes steeper than 30°. Aspect showed the highest relative importance in the Random Forest analysis. However, the differences in accuracy among aspect classes were comparatively modest, and greater underestimation was observed on north- and west-facing slopes. These findings demonstrate that national-scale accuracy statistics alone do not adequately describe DSM suitability across Malawi's diverse landscapes. DSM selection should therefore consider the terrain and land-cover characteristics of the intended application area.

abstract: A common explanation for bats being a conspicuous source of zoonotic viruses is their purported ability to coexist with viruses without suffering overt disease. Widespread acceptance of the idea that bats have unusual antiviral traits has catalyzed the discovery of unique features of bat immune systems which may have translational value as broad-spectrum antivirals, particularly if they evolved as a byproduct of bats' unique life history rather than through conventional co-evolutionary processes. Surprisingly, whether bats compared to other host groups suffer less disease from co-evolved viruses or from viruses generally has not been formally assessed. Here, synthesizing 86 years of experimental infections, involving 54 viruses, 85 host species, and over 5,600 animals, we document disease in bats following inoculation by taxonomically diverse viruses, including ones that are relatively benign in humans. The occurrence of overt disease, the likelihood of mortality, and the severity of disease in bats were indistinguishable from those experienced by rodents, another group associated with many zoonotic viruses. These patterns were consistent when considering only bat-associated viruses inoculated into bats and rodent-associated viruses inoculated into rodents and among inoculations which lacked shared co-evolutionary history. Instead, disease outcomes following infection were shaped by experimental design, viral host range, and evolutionary context. Unexceptional disease in bats from novel or co-evolved infections suggests that order-level host life history traits such as flight have inconsistent consequences for antiviral immunity and highlights the need to evaluate the functional properties of putatively unique features of bat immunity in vivo. While these results do not exclude the possibility of developing broader-acting or more potent antivirals from bat immune systems or diminish the potential value of mechanistic insights into bat immunity, they suggest that bat immune systems were shaped by conventional co-evolutionary processes rather than through unique circumstances that endow exceptional antiviral defenses.

title: Wealth-anchored category validation: A diagnostic for categorical orderings in fragile-state household surveys.

author_details.name: Gudi V Chandra Sekhar
author_details.affiliation: Department of Economics, College of Business and Economics, Gambella University, Gambella, Ethiopia.

affiliation_resolution.input: Department of Economics, College of Business and Economics, Gambella University, Gambella, Ethiopia.

abstract: Asset-based wealth indices and binary "improved" or "clean" service indicators both assume that the response options of a categorical survey variable are coded in the wealth order they imply. The assumption is rarely tested. I set out a procedure, Wealth-Anchored Category Validation (WACV), that tests it, and I am careful about what a failed test means. WACV ranks a variable's categories by their average position on a wealth index built from the other indicators, so no variable is judged against itself, and attaches stratified cluster-bootstrap intervals in which the whole estimation chain, including the index itself, is re-estimated in every replication. It reports two things: whether the categories sit on the local wealth gradient in the order the coding assumes, and whether a binary someone has already built from the variable falls where that gradient actually steps. Divergence on either is a diagnostic signal with several possible explanations: a coding fault, an analytical recoding fault, a context-dependent classification, or noise. The procedure does not adjudicate between them from wealth data alone. Applied to five ordinal variables in three waves of the South Sudan High Frequency Survey, the ordering diagnostic finds no robust inversion in the main specification; equivalence tests and a simulation locate what that null can and cannot rule out. The cut-point diagnostic finds one severe anomaly: an improved-housing binary used in earlier analysis of these data places the two poorest dwelling types on the improved side, and sits 0.26 standard deviations below the households it excludes. That anomaly replicates in a survey wave not used to develop the method. A codebook audit shows the binary originates in analysis rather than in the survey instrument, which makes it an instructive case of analytical recoding rather than a defect in the data.

abstract: The X-linked RNA helicase DDX3X is a high-risk gene for autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability primarily in females. Individuals with pathogenic variants in DDX3X have pervasive and often severe motor manifestations. Using mouse models, we studied the circuits underlying the motor phenotypes associated with Ddx3x deficiency and examined the feasibility of an early intervention to ameliorate motor trajectories. We show that Ddx3x controls both the development and later plasticity of motor circuits connecting the motor cortex with the pontine nuclei. Ddx3x haploinsufficiency during development affects the dendritic arborization of corticopontine neurons. Juvenile-onset Ddx3x loss in corticopontine neurons is sufficient to induce adult motor impairments overlapping with those caused by chemogenetic disruption of corticopontine circuits. Further, Ddx3x mutant mice engage corticopontine circuits in skilled motor tasks in a sex-dependent manner. Last, Ddx3x haploinsufficient female mice undergoing a juvenile motor intervention show long-lasting specific benefits in their adult motor function. Together, these findings establish Ddx3x as an essential regulator of corticopontine neuron development and function and provide an early motor intervention to ameliorate motor outcomes in a mouse model of DDX3X haploinsufficiency.

abstract: Axonal growth machinery is largely shared across neurons, but axons exhibit strikingly different fates depending on developmental and environmental context: sustained elongation in peripheral neurons under permissive conditions, length homeostasis in cortical neurons after target innervation, and pathological collapse into dystrophic endbulbs in injured adult central nervous system (CNS) axons. These divergent outcomes have resisted explanation by length-sensing and biomechanical models that treat long-range transport and local force generation as separate problems. We unify these phenomena through a mechanochemical model that couples bidirectional motor transport and intracellular signaling to growth-cone balance of axonal tension, actomyosin contraction, and adhesion within a single feedback loop: The lengthening axon uses its own growing transport delay to establish self-limiting mechanical feedback, as the accumulating delay reshapes signaling waveforms to progressively elevate myosin contractility against actin-driven protrusion. Two physical parameters, the transport delay and the signaling feedback strength, organize axon fate into a unified state-space landscape spanning sustained growth, length homeostasis, and pathological collapse. Reduced feedback strength weakens this self-limiting mechanical feedback by simultaneously enhancing protrusion and suppressing contractility, providing a mechanistic interpretation of axon lengthening under partial reduction of retrograde transport. Bistability in the inhibitory regime explains why mature CNS tracts persist where nascent sprouts collapse, recasting regenerative failure as a state-dependent gate rather than a capacity limit. The framework predicts that partial rather than complete inhibition of retrograde transport could shift collapsed axons across the bifurcation into a growth-permissive regime, identifying a class of interventions complementary to existing capacity-restoration strategies for nerve injury.

abstract: The brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) signaling axis is a key effector of synaptic plasticity and neuroprotection. While TrkB activation is a major target to prevent neural dysfunction, stimulation with exogenous BDNF administration has not proven tractable given the unfavorable physiochemical properties of BDNF. In addition, BDNF also activates a cell death pathway by binding to the neurotrophin receptor p75. The TrkB agonist antibody ZEB85 provides an alternative route to the selective activation of TrkB. To understand the ZEB85 mechanism of action, we mapped the binding site for ZEB85 to the TrkB extracellular juxtamembrane domain and found a sulfotyrosine modification at residue 400 crucial for ZEB85 interaction and activation of TrkB signaling. We determined the structures of ZEB85 and BDNF bound to their respective binding sites on human TrkB suggesting independent sites for each ligand, despite prior evidence of direct competition. Using structure-guided BDNF- and ZEB85-binding deficient TrkB mutants, we assessed their ability to sequester ligands from full-length TrkB in cultured human neurons. We found that the BDNF binding site extends into the juxtamembrane domain of TrkB but does not require the sulfotyrosine 400 to activate TrkB. Together with biophysical analysis and AlphaFold modeling, these results explain how BDNF can displace ZEB85 from TrkB through an overlapping epitope. Our findings reveal unique features of TrkB, not present in the related neurotrophin receptors TrkA and TrkC and suggest future directions to explore the role of sulfotyrosine in TrkB signaling.

title: A symbiogenic merger enabled by oxygen initiated the evolution of eukaryotes.

author_details.name: Dave Speijer
author_details.affiliation: Medical Biochemistry, Amsterdam University Medical Center location University of Amsterdam, Meibergdreef 15, 1105 AZ, Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

affiliation_resolution.input: Medical Biochemistry, Amsterdam University Medical Center location University of Amsterdam, Meibergdreef 15, 1105 AZ, Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

abstract: Recently, extensive genetic information about archaeal hosts at the basis of eukaryogenesis has come to light. Characterization of these first eukaryotic common ancestor (FECA) related organisms allows improved understanding of the enigmatic FECA to last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA) transition. However, these gene-centered discoveries have the unfortunate side effect of entrenching erroneous ideas about early eukaryotic evolution. This is apparent in the two-Domain vision of life, with eukaryotes seen as specialized Asgard archaea, while underestimating the contribution of the endosymbiont to eukaryogenesis. Establishment of the alpha-proteobacterium as the future mitochondrion is treated as one of many such endosymbiotic occurrences, ignoring its unique evolutionary position. I will marshal evidence for symbiogenic mechanisms involved in the FECA to LECA transition, with a key role for the endosymbiont's electron transport chain and its acceptor molecular oxygen, especially in the incarnation of reactive oxygen species occurring in the host cytoplasm. We should overcome overestimating gene determinism, while not sufficiently allowing for effects of biological hierarchies, emergent properties, and chance. Many eukaryotic properties are best understood by envisaging the crucial uptake of the future mitochondrion as a merger instead of an acquisition. This merger is characterized by a new kind of elaborate cellular entity emerging as a result of rapid coevolution, replacing a scenario in which already complex pre-eukaryotes acquired endosymbionts, accompanied by important, but limited, changes. Successful mergers are rare because they are intrinsically more difficult, but synergistically open up completely new areas of possibilities, as illustrated by incredible eukaryotic success.

abstract: We address the inverse problem for complexity functions of infinite words, which asks which functions can occur as complexity functions of infinite words. We survey our recent advances on this problem and several of its ramifications. We describe an asymptotic solution to the inverse problem, realizing every function satisfying two necessary conditions as the complexity function of an infinite word up to asymptotic equivalence. We then turn to phenomena beyond asymptotic equivalence, presenting constructions of infinite words with seemingly contradictory behavior of the discrete derivatives of their complexity functions. These lead to a solution of a 1995 problem of Cassaigne and to applications in symbolic dynamics, including the question of convergence of Rauzy graphs, as well as to the growth and asymptotic invariants of algebraic structures.

abstract: We study a problem at the interface of enumerative algebraic geometry, algebraic combinatorics, and the statistical mechanics of vertex models with long-range interactions. We develop methods to explore the values [Formula: see text] of Schubert polynomials (called principal specializations), which count reduced bumpless pipe dreams (RBPDs) with boundary permutation [Formula: see text]. We exhibit counterexamples to the conjecture of Merzon and Smirnov that [Formula: see text] is maximized on layered permutations; the smallest such example we find is at n = 17. Despite the counterexamples, we present bounds that support a refined conjecture that the maximum of [Formula: see text] over all [Formula: see text] grows at the same asymptotic rate as the maximum over layered permutations (found by Morales, Pak, and Panova). We implement and benchmark four recurrences for Schubert specializations: the descent formula of Macdonald, the transition formula of Lascoux-Schützenberger, the cotransition formula of Knutson, and the formula of Billey, Jockusch, and Stanley. We also explore typical random permutations drawn with probability proportional to [Formula: see text], equivalently from uniformly random RBPDs. Our simulations reveal a permuton-like limit analogous to the Grothendieck setting studied by Morales, Panova, Petrov, and Yeliussizov. For sampling, we show that the standard monotone Coupling From The Past framework does not apply to RBPDs, leaving exact uniform sampling open. To bypass this, we develop an efficient Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler augmented with macroscopic "droop" updates that preserve connectivity and accelerate mixing. Our publicly available fast implementations reach n = 20 for exact computation of [Formula: see text] and n = 100 for Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling using a chain whose stationary distribution is uniform on RBPDs (run on a cluster).

abstract: The accumulation of microswimmers near walls has been studied for decades. While hydrodynamics and single-cell kinematics are well-explored, the role of cell-cell interactions remains understudied. However, in realistic, crowded environments such as the human gut, these interactions can be just as crucial. Here, we demonstrate that they actively weaken bacterial surface accumulation. Analysis of entrapped cell tracks reveals that crowding enhances orientational fluctuations, which increase the effective rotational diffusion and facilitate wall escape. A minimal model shows that this collective effect is equivalent to raising the system's effective temperature with density.

abstract: Clay minerals, ubiquitous across diverse geological systems, exert fundamental controls on critical geochemical processes, particularly through their adsorptive interactions with economically vital elements such as heavy rare earth elements (HREEs). The adsorption of HREEs onto clay surfaces is not only the key process that enriches these critical resources but also a potential archive for dating significant weathering events. However, the atomic-scale mechanisms governing the preferential adsorption and fractionation of rare earth elements (REEs) at mineral-water interfaces have remained poorly constrained. Here, employing in situ atomic-scale imaging via high-resolution atomic force microscopy, we systematically investigate the adsorption behaviors of light and heavy REEs (La, Y, Yb) onto key crystallographic planes-Si-basal, Al-basal, and edge terminations-of representative clay minerals (kaolinite, illite, mica) under environmentally relevant conditions (pH 4.8 to 6.4). We directly visualize and quantitatively reveal that Si-basal planes selectively enrich HREEs with pH-enhanced adsorption capacity, whereas Al-basal planes exhibit negligible REE adsorption below pH 5.8 but preferential HREE adsorption at pH 6.4. Integrating synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we identify the adsorption mechanism of REE on Si-basal and Al-basal/edge planes as outer-sphere complexation and inner-sphere binding, respectively. Furthermore, we quantify the contributions of distinct planes via surface complexation modeling, revealing Si-dominated to Al- and edge-controlled adsorption with elevating pH. These atomic-scale findings not only resolve long-standing debates about clay mineral-mediated REE fractionation but also redefine fundamental paradigms of surface reactivity at silicate mineral-water interfaces, offering insights into the cycling and metallogeny of other critical metals in aqueous and sedimentary environments.

abstract: The biological identity of nanoparticles is often redefined upon exposure to physiological fluids through the formation of a protein corona (PC), However, the molecular rules linking synthetic design to biological fate remain elusive owing to the fragmented and inconsistent proteomics data. Here, leveraging a standardized deep proteomic database of 42 diverse nanomaterials, we reveal the general molecular selection rules that govern the PC formation. We demonstrate that the PC is not a product of random adsorption but is shaped by strict property-dependent recruitment. First, surface charge regulates cellular uptake, with anionic nanoparticles specifically recruiting adhesion proteins to promote Itgav-mediated endocytosis, thus forming a causal charge-corona-receptor chain. Second, PEGylation engineers immune evasion by selectively depleting specific complement and coagulation factors, rather than merely preventing protein adsorption. Third, nanoparticle geometry imposes structural constraints and selects proteins based on specific physicochemical features such as lysine content. Beyond mechanistic insights, we show that material-specific PCs can rebalance the serum proteome and enable the detection of low-abundance disease biomarkers. This work shifts the paradigm from empirical description toward rule-based prediction and provides a foundational framework for rationally engineering nanomedicines with predictable and programmable biological identities.

abstract: Bioregionalization, the partitioning of the globe into areas of biotic similarity, is one of nature's most striking patterns, and highly congruent boundaries have been identified across plants, tetrapods, ants, and butterflies. However, these taxa also share a unimodal latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG), raising the question of whether bioregionalization and the LDG are mechanistically coupled or instead arise from largely independent processes acting on different timescales. Bees (Hymenoptera: Anthophila) provide a natural test, their diversity peaking at mid-latitudes rather than in the tropics. Using range estimates for 3,370 species and a phylogenetic beta-diversity framework, we recover 21 bee bioregions nested within at least six major realms (Australasia, Indomalaya-Oceania, Nearctic, Neotropics, Palearctic, and Sub-Sahara) that closely align with those of other taxa despite bees' atypical diversity gradient. We propose that bioregionalization and species richness are decoupled because they arise from distinct processes: the former reflects historical dispersal and evolutionary history, the latter local diversification, extinction, and environmental filtering. Our analysis provides a global biogeographic framework for future bee research and highlights the processes shaping the world's major biogeographic boundaries.

abstract: Whether and how the subduction processes result in water enrichment at the base of the mantle transition zone (MTZ) remain elusive. The major orogenic belts of the Asian continent, including the Central Asian, Tethyan, and Alpine-Himalayan belts, which record extensive subduction processes, offer an ideal target to address the hydration of the MTZ and its relationship with subduction. Here, we map water content at the MTZ base by combining mineral physics constraints on hydrous pyrolite and global seismic observations of velocity structure and 660-km discontinuity topography. Our results indicate an average global water content of approximately 0.14 wt%, with pronounced hydration anomalies in parts of Asia. Linking these anomalies with reconstructions of past subduction events since 410 Ma reveals extensive water delivery to the MTZ, particularly beneath parts of the Mongol-Okhotsk suture zone, the Central Asian Orogenic Belt, and the Tethyan orogenic domain, where water content exceeds 0.5 wt%. These results connect ancient subduction history to present-day mantle hydration, offering insights into Earth's deep water cycle.

abstract: Programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD-L1) is an immune checkpoint protein expressed in vascular endothelial cells (ECs). In contrast to cancer, our understanding of endothelial PD-L1 in relation to metabolic syndromes and its vascular complications is less studied. For example, its regulation and intrinsic function remain unclear. Here, we showed that endothelial PD-L1 is regulated by leptin receptor signaling in male mice. In particular, endothelial PD-L1 expression is affected by leptin resistance. A lack of leptin receptors leads to PD-L1 downregulation in vascular ECs via posttranslational degradation. To understand the fundamental roles of endothelial PD-L1, RNA interference and selective knockout are employed in human endothelium and animals, respectively. Silencing or deleting endothelial PD-L1 expression delays cell cycle progression and proliferation due to rat sarcoma (RAS)/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) inactivation. In obesity, endothelial PD-L1 deficiency impairs the EC turnover and worsens the vascular function. Overall, we provide an insight into how endothelial PD-L1 contributes to vascular homeostasis, suggesting its pathophysiological importance in maintaining cellular turnover.

abstract: Advances in nanoscale patterning of superconducting films [Y. L. Wang et al ., Nat. Nanotechnol. 13 , 560-565 (2018)] and the availability of submicron-sized superconducting single crystals with controlled geometry allow for the investigation of superconducting vortex matter under extreme confinement [A. K. Geim et al ., Nature 390 , 259-262 (1997)]. It has been observed in these systems that the interplay between sample geometry and vortex number results in the emergence of so-called "magic number" configurations which show unusually high stability against thermal fluctuations. However, a detailed, comprehensive theoretical study of the ground state and metastable states of confined vortex matter has not yet been developed. Here we show that the intricate properties of a system of vortices under extreme confinement can be characterized in detail by mapping the potential energy landscape of the system onto a network [J. P. K. Doye, Phys. Rev. Lett. 88 , 238701 (2002)] with nodes corresponding to local potential energy minima and edges to transition states between local minima. We apply these techniques to systems featuring repelling particles/vortices confined in small containers of various geometric shapes. We demonstrate that the ground state almost always belongs to a subset of system states within the deepest network core. We find that the emergence of magic number configurations in the ground state results in a drastic decrease in the complexity of the entire network. We use large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to study the size dependence of melting in different configurations. We find that as confinement effects increase, magic number configurations transition to states with lower symmetry.

abstract: Natural selection enriches populations for genotypes that are well adapted to their environments, accumulating information about the selective conditions in the process. Therefore, selection can be viewed as a learning process through which populations acquire information about the environment. Motoo Kimura derived a relationship between the amount of information gained by selection and a measure of the inefficiency of the selective process, known as substitution load [M. Kimura, Genet. Res. 2, 127-140 (1961)]. Due to the gradual nature of selection and the ongoing mismatch of types to the environment, a lineage that is still acquiring information has lower mean fitness than a lineage that already has it. While this has been an influential insight, we find that Kimura's model is inconsistent with selection experiments involving Escherichia coli . To address limitations in this model and develop a more robust measure for the efficiency of selection, we turn to computational learning theory. We show that the learning-theoretic concept of regret quantifies the inefficiency of selection as a learning process in terms of relative lineage fitness. We establish bounds on the efficiency of information gain in general settings, including frequency-dependent selection and arbitrary environmental change. We experimentally validate these bounds and demonstrate that our extended theory recovers Kimura's fundamental insight. Finally, we show that selection is an asymptotically optimal algorithm for the basic problem faced by evolving populations and that it acquires information more efficiently than comparable processes in complex environments.

abstract: Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at the S locus with multiple alleles. In Papaver rhoeas , the S determinants were previously identified as PrpS and PrsS . However, we found that PrpS-PrsS was absent in many S haplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphic S genes, S locus oligopeptide transporter ( SOPT ) and S locus glycine-rich protein ( SGRP ), segregating at the S locus when PrpS-PrsS is absent. SOPT and SGRP display hallmark S determinant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed in Arabidopsis thaliana . Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, the Papaver SI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

abstract: Martian meteorites provide a record of the planet's geological history. However, most are geologically young samples that are not representative of Mars' surface, which is dominated by ancient rocks. We describe the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 (Teg 001), a slowly cooled igneous rock that formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. Its composition, mineralogy, and texture are distinct from other Martian meteorites. We determine that Teg 001 is a sample of ancient crust, which formed from a geochemically distinct mantle source with primordial composition. The presence of aqueously altered minerals, combined with bulk and mineral-specific oxygen isotope measurements, indicate that Teg 001 experienced reactions with fluids enriched in 18 O, before ejection into space by an impact.

abstract: At the skin's surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E 2 , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

abstract: Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF 2 showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF 2 . This finding highlights the potential for polarized INS to characterize altermagnets through its sensitivity to fine structure in magnon spectra.

abstract: Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic g -wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning-assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth-based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

abstract: A Chern metal is a two-dimensional metallic state of matter carrying chiral edge states. We report the observation of a Chern metal at the onset of the magnetic Kondo breakdown in a frustrated moiré Kondo lattice--angle-aligned MoTe 2 /WSe 2 bilayers. The state is compressible and is manifested by a nearly quantized Hall resistance and a finite longitudinal resistance arising from a bad metallic bulk. We demonstrate the presence of a chiral edge state by nonlocal transport measurements and current-induced quantum anomalous Hall breakdown. Magnetic circular dichroism measurements further reveal a magnetization plateau for the Chern metal before a metamagnetic transition at the Kondo breakdown. Our results open an opportunity for moiré engineering of exotic quantum phases through the interplay between band topology and Kondo interactions.

abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension-the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as "Least Concern" on the International Union for Conservation of Nature's Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development-its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

abstract: Many animals use the Sun compass to guide their movement, sometimes over thousands of kilometers. Consistent use of the Sun compass relies on the endogenous clock to track the Sun's arc, yet animals traveling east-west experience time shifts, potentially causing mismatches between their internal clock and local time. Using GPS, we reveal that Manx shearwaters ( Puffinus puffinus ) experience such shifts during homing flights, generating predictable errors in Sun compass orientation. Use of the Sun compass persists even when shearwaters have access to compass-independent cues during coast following. Our findings provide a new avenue for chronobiology research in the wild, suggesting that rapid longitudinal movements may affect other processes governed by the endogenous clock and that conserved chronobiological mechanisms impose substantial constraints on navigation.

abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium-derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2 FEM1B boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2 FEM1B agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich's ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

abstract: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed regions are strongly affected by multiple overlapping threats. Although threats vary across taxa and regions, increasing threat probabilities elevate extinction risk and population declines, with freshwater species experiencing greater threat intensity and distinct spatial patterns than terrestrial species. Our findings establish a spatially explicit baseline for targeting the most urgently needed freshwater conservation and management interventions.
