abstract: Erythropoietin (EPO) products stimulate production of erythrocytes in patients with anemia. The drugs are delivered intravenously or subcutaneously up to several times per week due to short plasma half-life. Improving the pharmacokinetic properties of EPO will allow less frequent administration, and thus impact therapeutic utility and patient compliance. In this study, we took advantage of an albumin variant (QMP) engineered for improved engagement of FcRn, a key regulator of the plasma half-life of albumin. After genetic coupling of EPO to QMP, the fusion protein shows favorable neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) binding, and 5.2-fold prolonged plasma half-life in human FcRn expressing mice upon intravenous administration, when comparing with EPO fused to WT albumin, with a similar half-life obtained following subcutaneous administration. Importantly, both fusions bind the EPO receptor with binding kinetics equal to that of the product darbepoetin alfa. After intravenous administration, mice receiving darbepoetin alfa experiences a faster drop in EPO levels compared to those given EPO-QMP, and moreover, we measure a prolonged increase in erythrocytes with EPO-QMP. Furthermore, intranasal administration results in 5-fold higher circulating amounts of EPO-QMP and a prolonged increase in erythrocytes compared to darbepoetin alfa. Thus, long-acting EPO-QMP could be an attractive design to explore for both invasive and non-invasive delivery to patients with anemia.

abstract: Volumetric computed tomography (CT) segmentation supports quantitative image analysis, but most AI-based methods remain organ-specific, with fragmented models, inconsistent label definitions, and heterogeneous training and evaluation protocols. Here we present CADS, a unified data–model framework for scalable and generalizable whole-body CT segmentation. We construct a SNOMED-CT-referenced anatomical label space harmonizing heterogeneous cohorts from over 100 imaging centers, yielding complete annotations of 167 structures across 22,022 CT volumes and markedly expanding anatomical coverage and scale beyond existing resources. To complete labels on sparsely annotated CTs, we combine self-training with shape-informed quality control based on neural implicit functions, curating high-quality pseudo-labels. Trained on this resource, CADS shows robust whole-body segmentation across distribution shifts and improved performance relative to state-of-the-art approaches across 18 public datasets. We further validate it in an independent, expert-reviewed real-world oncology cohort of 2864 CTs. The curated dataset, pretrained models, and user-friendly software together provide an accessible, reproducible foundation for large-scale anatomical segmentation and computational anatomy research.

abstract: Circular RNAs regulate gene expression through interactions with ribonucleic acid binding proteins, but their binding sites remain difficult to predict across proteins and cellular contexts. Existing methods often focus on transcript features while making limited use of protein-specific information and structural context. Here, we show that an integrated deep learning framework combining circular transcript sequence composition, physicochemical properties, secondary structure, pretrained representations and protein features improves interaction-site prediction across 37 benchmark datasets and generalizes across cell lines; model interpretation recovers conserved single-stranded sequence patterns, while analyses of proteins linked to Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis identify recurrent pathways involving nucleocytoplasmic transport, lysosomal signaling and guanosine triphosphatase activity and prioritize compounds for experimental follow-up, supporting accurate and interpretable mapping of circular ribonucleic acid protein interactions without implying therapeutic efficacy.

abstract: The flavivirus nonstructural protein 5 performs multiple functions during infection, including RNA replication and type I interferon signaling antagonism. Although flavivirus NS5 proteins inhibit IFN signaling through distinct mechanisms, which suggests evolutionary flexibility, the evolutionary constraints for these activities to coexist within a single protein remain to be determined. Here, we map the Zika virus NS5 STAT2 antagonism determinants and compare them with replication constraints defined by deep mutational scanning. Antagonism and replication determinants extensively overlap, and no single amino acid substitution eliminates antagonism without impairing replication. Resolving these fitness landscapes in parallel identifies specific combinations of partially functional substitutions that retain replication capacity while markedly reducing antagonism. These viruses are profoundly attenuated in human STAT2 knock-in mice. Our results uncover a fundamental evolutionary constraint linking replication and immune evasion activities in NS5, highlight that STAT2 antagonism is essential for ZIKV pathogenesis and provide new avenues for attenuated ZIKV vaccines.

abstract: Genetic modifiers of Huntington’s disease (HD) disease onset and progression implicate somatic instability (SI) of the expanded CAG repeat as a key pathogenic driver, with MSH3 emerging as a therapeutic target. Here, we generated a computational model that uses HD patient data to infer therapeutic effects of reducing SI and in parallel designed an artificial miRNA to lower MSH3 mRNA (miMSH3) after delivery with AAV-DB-3, a previously described medium spiny neuron (MSN)-targeting AAV capsid variant. AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 achieved 48–94% MSH3 mRNA reduction in MSNs of nonhuman primates (NHPs), which when applied to predictive modeling predicts 50–120 % slowing of HD progression as measured by change from baseline in the composite Unified Huntington Disease Rating Scale. Additionally, AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 reduced SI reduction by up to 46% in HdhQ111 mice. Cumulatively, the preclinical experimental data and the computational model support the translational potential of AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 as a disease-modifying therapy for HD.

abstract: Despite extensive structural analysis of the complement cascade, a detailed understanding of complement C5 activation is lacking. Here we show using cryo-EM that C5 in complex with the CVFBb surrogate convertase undergoes a proteolysis independent two-step rearrangement to a C5 * conformation that enables the C5 scissile bond to reach the catalytic site of the Bb protease. C5 * can form a complex with C6 and initiate membrane attack complex formation without C5 cleavage. Moreover, we observe an unusual convertase conformation where Bb rotates 155° relative to CVFBb in the putative Michaelis complex. This work demonstrates that the C5 * conformation is functionally relevant and can help rationalize the mode of action for known C5 inhibitors, and we propose that large Bb rotations may allow the endogenous surface bound C5 convertases to cleave in trans C5 bound to a neighboring C3b molecule, presenting a refined model of C5 cleavage in vivo.

abstract: Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited increased richness and turnover, reflecting ecological structuring during early life. Temperate phages dominate the URT phage community and share virulence- and mobility-associated genes with bacterial hosts, likely contributing to host adaptation and colonization persistence. Vertebrate-associated viruses emerge after the first week of life. Targeted reassembly from bovine URT viromes recovers near-complete betacoronavirus-like (CoV-D180) and adenovirus-like (AdV-D56) genomes positioned phylogenetically between bovine and human viral lineages. Competitive mapping of bovine-derived CoV-D180 and AdV-D56 to human respiratory metatranscriptomic datasets reveals genome-specific, regionally structured coverage patterns distinct from reference viruses, supporting shared sequence features in conserved genomic regions across host-associated viral lineages. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework.

abstract: Evidence for Earth’s oxygenation during the Great Oxidation Event (GOE) and Neoproterozoic Oxidation Event (NOE) comes primarily from the geological record. We report rising oxidation state of carbon (Zc) in proteins over billion-year timescales, a consistent trend recovered from diverse genomic datasets. Combining statistical and thermodynamic modeling, we link this trend to environmental drivers including Earth’s progressive oxygenation and secular cooling. The oxidation trend appears in the amino acid composition of modern genomes from methanogens and sulfur-cycling organisms, phylostratigraphic gene age groups in eukaryotes, and reconstructed ancestral sequences for Rubisco, nitrogenase, thioredoxin, and 3-isopropylmalate dehydrogenase (IPMDH). Major Zc steps broadly overlap the GOE but do not exactly coincide with it; uncertainties in phylogenetic age and limited spatial associations complicate direct comparison with geochemical proxies. Gene age groups in unicellular, but not multicellular, eukaryotes show a second rise of protein Zc around the NOE. These widespread genomic signatures of protein oxidation are consistent with a thermodynamic hypothesis in which energy minimization directs protein sequence evolution across metabolic functions.

abstract: Cell type-specific chromatin accessibility QTL (caQTL) mapping is a promising approach to understand genetic control of chromatin landscapes and identify regulatory mechanisms underlying GWAS associations. However, current caQTL studies lack resolution and do not distinguish nucleosome-free regions (NFR) from positioned nucleosomes. Here, we leverage statistical modeling of fragment position and length to decompose ATAC-seq profiles into NFRs and phased nucleosomes. With single nucleus (sn)ATAC-seq from 281 human muscle biopsies, we map cell type-specific genetic effects on NFRs (76,027 nfrQTLs) and nucleosome occupancy (24,623 nucQTLs) across skeletal muscle cell types. Colocalization and causal inference analyses identify 1,528 instances where nfrQTLs have likely causal effects on adjacent nucleosome positioning, supporting a causal relationship in shaping chromatin profiles. Hundreds of nfrQTLs colocalize with GWAS signals for muscle-related traits, including grip strength, atrial fibrillation, and fasting insulin, and the majority of colocalizing signals mapped to credible sets overlapping the corresponding nfrPeak. This approach adds mechanistic insights for how variants underlying skeletal muscle caQTLs and GWAS signals exert their cis regulatory effects by initially modifying NFR accessibility and subsequently shaping broader chromatin landscapes, nucleosome positioning, gene expression, and ultimately higher-level traits and disease.

abstract: Brain-wide association studies have linked brain structure to complex mental health phenotypes, yet the genetic underpinnings of these effects remain largely unclear. Here, we leverage multimodal neuroimaging, behavioral and genetic data from the UK Biobank to develop an integrative framework combining brain-wide association studies and GWAS to elucidate how genetic variants affect the relationship between brain structure and mental health. Our multivariate brain-wide association study identifies two reproducible brain structural modes: a cerebellar-dominant mode and a cortical-dominant mode that explain individual differences in mental health measures. Using GWAS, we subsequently identify 30 and 15 independent significant variants respectively for each mode, indicating distinct genetic architectures with no signal overlap. Post-GWAS analyses indicate distinct biological pathways: the cerebellar-dominant mode is enriched for genes involved in chromatin organization and epigenetic regulation, while the cortical-dominant mode is linked to neurotransmitter metabolism. Moreover, we identify shared genetic influences between the brain modes and both mental health and cognitive traits, as well as causal effects of the brain modes on these outcomes. We validate the framework in the independent HCP cohort, supporting the cross-cohort generalizability of the identified brain–behavior and genetic associations.

abstract: Evidence on the health impacts of ambient temperature relies largely on population-level analyses, providing limited insight into risks among clinically and socially vulnerable individuals, including those with pre-existing disease or socioeconomic disadvantage. Here we show, in 275,763 Finnish adults and an independent UK cohort of 9,681 adults, that health risks during extreme temperatures differed substantially across vulnerability groups. We compared mortality and emergency hospital visits during the hottest and coldest 2.5% of seven-day periods with those during non-extreme temperature periods. Excess heat- and cold-related mortality was more than tenfold higher among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability than among those with neither or only one vulnerability in both the Finnish and UK cohorts ( P = 0.03 and P = 0.003, respectively). By contrast, excess temperature-related mortality differed little between individuals with neither vulnerability and those with only one vulnerability. Our modelling suggests that future warming could increase temperature-attributable mortality across the population, particularly among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability. These findings identify individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability as a priority group for climate adaptation strategies.

abstract: Radiological impressions are critical for clinical decision-making, yet expertise is unevenly distributed, and current large language models lack domain-specific reliability. We develop and evaluate Impression-R1, a domain-specialized large reasoning model for radiological impression generation, trained through an Imitation–Reasoning–Reinforcement pipeline integrating large-scale supervised learning, clinically conditioned reasoning, and radiology-aware reward optimization. Across 11,884 cases from six institutions and three public datasets spanning imaging modalities, anatomical regions, and diseases, including cross-lingual testing on English-language benchmarks, Impression-R1 outperforms or matches state-of-the-art general-purpose models. In a 200-case head-to-head evaluation, Impression-R1 shows stronger objective agreement with institution-derived reference impressions than all participating radiologists and subjective performance within the range of less-experienced radiologists under the study evaluation framework. Prospectively, radiologists rate its reasoning and clinical relevance highly. In a randomized within-reader study of 360 interpretations, AI assistance improves report quality (adjusted difference 0.28, 95% CI, 0.10–0.46) and reduces completion time by 27% (95% CI, 19.0%–33.9%); harmlessness scores are not significantly different (adjusted difference 0.08, 95% CI, −0.11–0.28). Here we show that Impression-R1 exemplifies a clinically informed framework for developing and evaluating domain-specialized reasoning models and can improve radiological reporting quality and efficiency, while requiring continued validation before broader clinical deployment.

abstract: Viral infections remain a persistent global threat, necessitating development of broad-spectrum antiviral agents targeting conserved sites to combat emerging variants. Here, we develop S-880008, a lipid-modified macrocyclic peptide identified through mRNA display screening and structural optimization, as a novel class of fusion inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2. S-880008 exhibits potent broad-spectrum antiviral activity against diverse variants including Omicrons. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals that S-880008 employs an unprecedented dual-binding mechanism targeting conserved, cryptic sites: the macrocyclic peptide portion anchors the receptor-binding domain (RBD)–subdomain 1 interface, while the lipid chain penetrates the N-terminal domain of the adjacent protomer. These interactions enforce an RBD 3-up conformation, suppressing protomer dissociation and blocking viral fusion. Crucially, intranasal administration of S-880008 significantly reduces viral titers and improves survival in a murine infection model. These findings highlight a novel mechanism whereby S-880008 deeply engages conserved interprotomer regions, providing a rationale for designing broad-spectrum antiviral fusion inhibitors.

abstract: Telomeres are essential for maintaining genomic integrity and are associated with cellular aging and disease, yet the factors influencing their inheritance across generations remain poorly understood. Using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and 75 parent-offspring trios ( n = 225) from the Genomic Answers for Kids program, we analyze individual telomeres across chromosomes and their inheritance. Telomere length varies between chromosome arms in a way that is consistent in parents and offspring, with average values ranging from 5000 to 8000 base pairs. Maternal and paternal telomere length together are a strong predictor of child telomere length ( R ² = 0.623). Notably, using telomeric variant repeats, we develop a tool that enables allelic tracing for 53.3% of maternally and 49.9% of paternally inherited telomeres. In children, paternally transmitted alleles are significantly longer than age-matched maternal ones (Δmean = 448 bp, p = 0.048), particularly when from older parents (Δmean = 732 bp, p = 0.041) and at chromosome arms with shorter average telomere length (Δmean = 754 bp, p = 0.0012). These findings reveal parent-of-origin effects and heritable influences on telomere length, providing insights into telomere dynamics and their potential implications in age-related disease susceptibility.

abstract: Lipid metabolism rewiring is an essential determinant of cancer progression, yet the key metabolic checkpoints which govern this process remain poorly defined. Using functional genomics in a mouse model of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we identify the sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter SPNS2 as a critical sphingolipid checkpoint protein which modulates leukemia progression. SPNS2 expression is regulated by MYC and progressively declines during AML differentiation, highlighting its tumor-suppressive role in a subset of Core Binding Factor AMLs. By integrating steady-state and serine isotope-tracing lipidomics, RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and high-resolution microscopy, with gain- and loss-of-function approaches, we show that SPNS2 modulation rewires sphingolipid metabolism by modifying sphingomyelin abundance. This remodeling alters membrane nanodomain organization, active RAS localization, and MAPK signaling. Exogenous reintroduction of SPNS2 decreases sphingomyelin levels, disrupts nanodomain organization, and limits leukemic progression in various AML mouse models. We further reveal in a cohort of patients with AML that low SPNS2 expression is associated with increased sensitivity to MAPK pathway inhibition, and demonstrate functionally in vivo that SPNS2 silencing sensitizes AML cells to MEK1/2 inhibition. Collectively, our data reveal a mechanism by which sphingolipid transport dynamics intersect with oncogenic signaling to control cancer progression.

abstract: While serine restriction is known to suppress tumor cell proliferation, its therapeutic application remains challenging. Unexpectedly, we show that serine supplementation therapeutically suppressed tumor growth and metastasis in multiple preclinical models while simultaneously boosting CD8⁺ T-cell proliferation and effector functions. Mechanistically, IFNγ released by activated T cells triggers STAT1-dependent induction of the serine transporter SLC1A4 in tumor cells, enabling them to deplete extracellular serine and thereby starve infiltrating CD8⁺ T cells. Genetic deletion of SLC1A4 reverses this metabolic hijack, restores serine availability within the tumor microenvironment, and markedly enhances anti-tumor immunity. Dietary serine supplementation not only replicates the immune-activating effects of SLC1A4 loss but also overcomes resistance to PD-1 blockade, producing durable control in checkpoint-refractory tumors. Collectively, these data position serine supplementation rather than restriction as a readily translatable strategy to reinvigorate exhausted T cells and improve immunotherapy outcomes.

abstract: Root-associated fungi and bacteria play pivotal roles in terrestrial ecosystem processes. However, identifying keystone taxa driving below-ground microbial assembly remains a major challenge. Here, we present a statistical framework for identifying microbes that reorganize microbiome assembly. Using 1,270 root samples collected from a cool-temperate forest in Japan, we reconstruct assembly landscapes describing the probabilistic structure of community states. We then find that several endophytic fungi (e.g., Phialocephala and Oidiodendron ) are strongly associated with the reorganization of assembly landscape topography along abundance gradients, coinciding with shifts in mycorrhizal symbiosis. Independent datasets from Europe confirm that the highlighted genera are significantly associated with changes in mycorrhizal colonization patterns. Prokaryotic communities exhibit transitions among states characterized by core taxa, Pseudomonadota, or Actinomycetota, strongly associated with abundance gradients of Candidatus Udaeobacter and several endophytic fungi. These findings provide a scalable framework for prioritizing candidate keystone taxa and linking microbiome assembly to ecosystem-scale processes.

abstract: Efficient DNA replication requires coordinated use of replicative and error-prone polymerases, which provide flexibility at the cost of mutagenesis. DNA polymerase η (Pol η) tolerates UV-induced lesions via translesion synthesis (TLS), but may contribute more broadly to DNA synthesis. Using polymerase usage sequencing (Pu-seq), we map Pol η activity genome-wide during unperturbed replication in human cells. Pol η preferentially participates in lagging strand replication, as in budding yeast. This bias requires direct PCNA interaction, suggesting stochastic engagement of PCNA-bound intermediates at replication forks. Pol η usage also varies across S phase, with PCNA ubiquitylation-dependent enrichment in late-replicating domains. In cancer genomes, characteristic Pol η mutations are enriched in late-replicating regions and correlate with RAD18 expression, linking PCNA ubiquitylation to Pol η-mediated mutagenesis. Thus, Pol η usage is biased by strand and replication timing during unperturbed replication and may contribute to mutational burden in human genomes.

abstract: Proteolytic processing of α-Synuclein (Syn) contributes to the molecular diversity and toxicity of its aggregates in Parkinson’s disease, yet the proteases responsible for disease-relevant truncations remain incompletely defined. Here, we show that thrombin, a serine protease associated with inflammatory conditions, selectively cleaves Syn at Lys6–Gly7, generating a 7–140 fragment despite the presence of multiple potential cleavage sites. Cleavage is modulated by ionic strength and the conformational ensemble of Syn, with more extended states being preferentially cleaved. The resulting 7–140 fragment adopts a more compact conformational ensemble, delays the formation of aggregation-prone species, produces fibrils with altered morphology and shows reduced membrane-induced α-helix formation. Although 7–140 aggregates are modestly less toxic, the truncation also impairs physiological functions of the protein. These findings describe a mechanism by which an inflammation-associated protease, thrombin, may contribute to Parkinson’s disease by selectively modifying Syn structure, aggregation and function.

abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing mediated by endogenous ADAR enzymes represents a promising therapeutic strategy because it can correct mutations at the transcript level without inducing permanent changes to the genome. However, existing systems face challenges, particularly the limited editing efficiency, which limits their practical applications. Here we introduce MARRS (multivalent ADAR1-recruiting RNA editing system)—an efficient and specific RNA editing platform that leverages engineered multivalent RNA aptamers to robustly recruit endogenous ADAR1 enzymes. By optimizing aptamers targeting the Zα domain of ADAR1 p150 and embedding them in a circular RNA scaffold, MARRS enables near-complete adenosine-to-inosine editing of RNA targets in cultured cells and mouse models, achieving efficiencies up to 100% in vitro and 84% in vivo. MARRS also exhibits remarkable versatility across a range of transcript targets while maintaining high specificity with minimal off-target effects. Operating without the need for exogenous enzymes, the MARRS system offers a safe, efficient and programmable platform.

abstract: Extending the depth reach of multiphoton microscopy for imaging neuronal population activity in the scattering mammalian brain is an ‘exponentially hard’ problem. Three-photon (3p) microscopy has enabled imaging of neuroactivity at depths up to ~1.2 mm in the mouse brain; however, the fundamental depth limit of 3p imaging, as set by the depth at which out-of-focus background fluorescence exceeds the in-focus fluorescence signal, is well beyond 2 mm. Reaching this fundamental depth limit in 3p imaging has been hampered by insufficient in-focus fluorescence signal. Here we demonstrate a three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) system that approaches this fundamental depth limit via systematic and principled optimization of the in-focus fluorescence signal. TrUDI matches the parameters of the excitation laser, the optical system, and the acquisition to linear and nonlinear limits for safe laser exposure while satisfying the spatiotemporal requirements of single-cell resolution calcium (Ca 2+ ) imaging. TrUDI achieves a ~250-fold increase in detected fluorescence photon yield at the same laser power as in previous approaches thereby enabling in vivo cellular-resolution recordings of neuronal population activity within fields of view of ~230 × 230 µm 2 at 8.6 Hz at tissue depths of up to ~2 mm in mouse cortex and hippocampus.

abstract: Brain myeloid cells, including infiltrating monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) and microglia, play critical roles in ischemic brain injury, clearing debris and shaping neuroinflammation and neurological outcomes. Yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, using single-cell RNA sequencing and fate mapping with an MDM-specific Ms4a3 creERT2 -Ai14 mouse line, we identified serotonin receptor Htr2b + MDMs as a crucial cell population involved in resolving neuroinflammation within the ischemic penumbra. Htr2b + MDMs significantly accumulate in the peri-infarct region and exhibit enhanced phagocytosis and inflammation-resolving gene signatures. Mechanistically, Htr2b activation promotes nuclear translocation of Tfe3, a key lysosomal regulator, enhancing lysosomal biogenesis and supporting phagocytic activity. MDM-specific Htr2b ablation impairs debris clearance, exacerbates neuroinflammation and ischemic injury, whereas pharmacological agonism or Tfe3 activation restores lysosomal biogenesis in brain MDMs and improves post-stroke outcomes. Thus we demonstrate a previously unrecognized Htr2b + MDM subset that integrates serotonin signaling to license intrinsic phagocytic function, alleviating ischemic brain injury.

title: A foot-level motion remapping framework for inclined stair walking in virtual reality.

author_details.name: Jong-Hyun Kim
author_details.affiliation: College of AI Convergence (Dept. of Artificial Intelligence, Design Technology), Graduate School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Inha University, Incheon, South Korea.

affiliation_resolution.input: College of AI Convergence (Dept. of Artificial Intelligence, Design Technology), Graduate School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Inha University, Incheon, South Korea.

abstract: This paper proposes a foot-level motion remapping framework that enables users to experience inclined stair walking in virtual reality (VR) while physically walking on flat ground. Existing stair-walking and motion remapping approaches often focus on discrete step-height changes, root-level avatar correction, or hardware-assisted interaction, and therefore have limited ability to represent the continuous geometric variation and asymmetric foot-contact behavior that occur on inclined stair-like surfaces. To address this limitation, the proposed method models the foot using separate toe and heel components and decomposes the gait cycle into Lift, Contact, and Release states. For each gait state, toe and heel contributions are adaptively weighted according to the virtual inclination angle using an anchor-based continuous weighting scheme. The resulting foot motion is temporally stabilized and hierarchically propagated to the waist and head to reduce excessive visual oscillation. The framework was implemented in a real-time Unity-based VR system and evaluated under flat, intermediate, and steep inclination conditions. The evaluation additionally includes a non-anchor inclination condition, sequence-level trajectory-fidelity measures, and comparison with a prior stair-remapping method. The results show that the proposed method reduces frame-wise height jitter, improves motion stability, and maintains real-time performance compared with baseline remapping variants. These findings support foot-level state-based remapping as a practical approach for generating trajectory-stable inclined locomotion in VR without requiring a physical stair apparatus.

abstract: Emotionally intelligent dialogue systems should not only express sentence-level sentiment but also sense shifts in emotion from sentence to sentence, from speaker to speaker, and over time, and be interpretable down to the decision level. Existing approaches consider only sentiment as a single and static feature, and they either do not consider multi-turn context, temporal variation, speaker-specific trends, or the correlations between emotion and action. To fill these gaps, we introduce a unified 5-stage framework for systematically encoding, transforming, and operationalising emotion in multi-turn conversations. First, Context-Aware Multi-Level Sentiment Encoding (CMLSE) uses RoBERTa embeddings, self-attention, and Dynamic Time Warping (DTW), while preserving the speaker identity, turn order and sentiment continuity. Second, Emotion Clustering Topological Signal Mapping (ECTSM) uses an emotion vector sentiment and persistent homology to obtain robust emotion clusters based on topology and shape. Third, Emotion-Memory Reinforced Graph Aggregation Network (EMR-GAN) constructs a dynamic emotion graph and a long-term memory network, learning the best manner for optimizing emotional coherence through Reinforcement Learning (RL). The Adaptive Causal Decision-Graph Transformer (ACDGT) incorporates causal inference into graph attention to discover hidden emotion-behaviour causality and imitate counterfactual decisions. Finally, the Emotion-Driven Reinforcement Policy Synthesizer (EDRPS) combines emotional memory and causal representations with dual-reward Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to generate policies in real-time, emotion-aware mode. Our model shows an average accuracy of 78.8% (+6.4% above the best baseline) on MELD, 0.61 Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) for emotion clustering, and 92.5% accuracy in aligning the policy on DailyDialog. These assessments show scores of empathy, relevance, and naturalness to be higher, marking a new state-of-the-art for affective dialogue systems.

abstract: An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model was created to predict how injection-molded parts made from flexible mechanisms would hold up under twisting fatigue. These parts were made from three common plastics-ABS (Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene), PP (polypropylene), and PA6 (Polyamide 6)-strengthened with up to 30 wt.% short glass fibers. The team also looked at how many times the parts were cycled during manufacturing.To test them, the samples were twisted back and forth ±40° for 100 cycles. The study examined how the type of plastic, the amount of glass fiber, and key injection molding settings affected the results. It turned out that PA6's ability to withstand fatigue really improved when it had more glass fiber, especially 20 wt.% or more. PA6 turned out to be the strongest material in this test, followed by ABS. PP was the most consistent but also the weakest in terms of twisting strength. The ANN model was quite successful at predicting the twisting force, with a match range (R ≈ 0.94 to 0.98) and cross validation 0.93 and 0.97. The research also pointed out specific injection molding conditions-like melt temperature, filling pressure, and packing pressure-as being particularly important for the final performance. Overall, this proposed approach offers a tool to help engineers design and make plastic flexible mechanisms more effectively.

abstract: In most societies, using more than one language or language variety is the norm, yet the reference data against which children's speech is judged derive largely from monolingual speakers. Systematic cross-linguistic variation is therefore liable to be read as atypical development, placing multilingual children at risk of misdiagnosis of speech sound disorder (SSD). This risk is most acute for closely related, understudied varieties, where difference and disorder overlap and community-specific data are scarce. Acoustic measures (e.g., voice onset time, vowel formants, segment durations) quantify fine-grained, continuous properties of speech production that categorical, transcription-based description obscures. No existing review, however, has mapped which acoustic measures have been applied to multilingual children, across which language varieties, or against which reference baselines their productions are interpreted. The objective of this review is to provide that map, showing where acoustic evidence is concentrated and where it is absent, to support clinical assessment and to identify where community-specific reference data are most needed. The review will follow updated Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review methodology and will be reported per the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews. Searches will be conducted in MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase (Ovid), CINAHL (EBSCO), Web of Science Core Collection, and Linguistics and Language Behavior Abstracts, with grey literature sought through ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global and conference proceedings; no date limits will be applied. Children from birth to 18 years are eligible regardless of clinical status, and a preschool subset (≤ 5;11) will be reported separately. After pilot calibration, two reviewers will independently screen and chart sources, resolving disagreements by discussion or a third reviewer. Charted data will be mapped through an acoustic-measure taxonomy crossed with language variety and reference baseline. This protocol has been registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/R2EX5).

abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive dilatative disease of the abdominal aorta with high rupture-related mortality, emphasizing the need for early risk assessment. Conventional anatomical indicators, such as maximum diameter, are insufficient to characterize rupture risk, motivating the incorporation of hemodynamic parameters. Image-based CFD enables the estimation of these parameters but remains clinically limited by high computational cost and long processing times. To overcome these limitations, deep learning-based surrogate models such as MultiViewUNet have recently been proposed, though previous studies were constrained by relatively low spatial resolution and limited coverage of hemodynamic parameters. In this study, we propose MH-UNet, a multi-view, high-resolution surrogate modeling framework that extends the original MultiViewUNet to a higher input resolution and additional hemodynamic parameters. MH-UNet converts three-dimensional AAA geometries into two-dimensional images from multiple viewing angles and predicts TAWSS, OSI, RRT, and ECAP using data from 101 patients. Both single-inference and dual-inference strategies were implemented and compared. Single-inference consistently outperformed dual-inference across all parameters; the cascaded dual-inference scheme amplified errors through the nonlinear OSI and RRT formulations, resulting in negative R² values for OSI, RRT, and ECAP. Among the single-inference predictions, TAWSS was predicted most reliably (R² = 0.803), whereas OSI was the most challenging to predict. Agreement between single-inference predictions and CFD-derived results demonstrates the potential of MH-UNet as a rapid surrogate tool for estimating WSS-derived hemodynamic indices in AAA under fixed boundary conditions.

abstract: Objective This study aimed to investigate sputum CCL28 expression in patients with acute asthma exacerbations and its association with type 2 airway inflammation and secretory IgA. We further evaluated whether sputum CCL28, alone or in combination with routine clinical indicators, could assist in identifying eosinophilic asthma. Methods This study included 75 patients with non-severe acute asthma and 27 healthy controls. Induced sputum samples were collected, and the levels of CCL28, IL-4, IL-5, IL-10, IL-13, and secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) were measured in both sputum and serum samples. Sputum cytology was performed to classify airway inflammatory phenotypes as eosinophilic asthma (EA), neutrophilic asthma (NA), mixed granulocytic asthma (MA), and paucigranulocytic asthma (PA). Intergroup differences were analyzed using nonparametric tests, and correlations between variables were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation analysis. A predictive model for asthma phenotype identification was subsequently developed, and its predictive performance and potential clinical utility were further evaluated. Results CCL28 levels in induced sputum were significantly higher in patients with asthma than in healthy controls (P < 0.01), while the correlation between sputum and serum CCL28 levels was weak (ρ = 0.29). Sputum levels of IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, and secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) were significantly increased, whereas IL-10 levels were decreased (P < 0.01). CCL28 levels were significantly higher in the EA group than in the NA and PA groups (P < 0.05) and were positively correlated with IL-5, IL-13, sIgA, and sputum eosinophils (r = 0.83, 0.75, 0.66, and 0.55). In the EA prediction model, the combination of CCL28, fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), and lung function parameters showed the best predictive performance (AUC = 0.79). Incorporation of CCL28 improved model discrimination and reclassification performance (IDI = 0.246, continuous NRI = 0.880, P < 0.001) suggesting additional predictive value beyond routine clinical indicators, and decision curve analysis demonstrated a greater net clinical benefit. Conclusion Sputum CCL28 was associated with type 2 inflammation and airway mucosal immunity in patients with asthma. An exploratory prediction model incorporating sputum CCL28 showed potential value in assisting the identification of eosinophilic asthma.

abstract: Managing large carnivores benefits from understanding their vital rates, including survival. For cougars (Puma concolor), the hazards relevant to survival across the landscape are poorly understood. The risks that landscape features present can change temporally, increasing survival in one season while creating mortality risk in another. Between 2016 and 2021, 80 cougars were radio-collared and tracked in west central Alberta, Canada, for a total of 1082 cougar months with a mean monitoring time of 13.5 months/individual. We documented 37 deaths, determined causes of mortality, generated survival estimates using Kaplan-Meier models by sex and age class annually and for two seasons (i.e., warm and cold), and investigated factors affecting survival using Cox proportional hazard models. Humans were responsible for 29 of the 37 documented mortalities, including harvest, removal of problem individuals, landowner removals, incidental trapping, and vehicle collisions, with harvest representing the largest single source of mortality (16/37 deaths) for both sexes. However, we were unable to detect a difference in survival estimates between sexes or age classes and found no evidence of a male-biased harvest. Mean annual survival was 0.60 (95% CI: 0.50-0.72) and varied seasonally with lower survival in the cold season (0.62, 95% CI: 0.52-0.74) than the warm season (0.96, 95% CI: 0.92-1.00). Using Cox proportional hazards models (Andersen-Gill), model selection identified a best-supported mixed model combining biological, environmental, and anthropogenic features: season, proximity to residences, proximity to secondary roads, linear-feature crossing rate, and step length.

abstract: Background Frail older adults are particularly susceptible to pressure ulcer development due to complex health conditions and functional decline. Pressure ulcers category II and III involve partial- and full-thickness skin loss, and current treatment options often yield suboptimal outcomes. The study evaluated the effects of adjunctive photobiomodulation compared with standard-of-care in frail older adults, with category II and III pressure ulcers. The objectives were to assess: 1) ulcer healing 2) healing time; 3) factors associated with healing, and 4) ulcer recurrence following photobiomodulation. Methods Quasi-experimental study with two prospective intervention groups and matched registry-based control groups, conducted in accordance with TREND guidelines. Baseline differences analysed using Independent Samples T-test, Independent Samples Mann-Whitney U test or Pearson chi-square test. Times to healing evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and log-rank tests. Age-stratified multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were applied to identify healing-associated factors. Ulcer recurrences were analysed descriptively. Participants and setting Intervention groups comprised frail older adults (≥70 years) receiving municipal home healthcare: category II (n = 39) and category III (n = 37). Photobiomodulation was administered twice weekly, using GaAs laser (904 nm) and AlGaInP laser (635 nm). Control groups treated with standard-of-care were identified from the Swedish national registry RiksSår for ulcer treatment: category II (n = 117), and category III (n = 111). Results The photobiomodulation groups demonstrated higher proportions of healed ulcers and significantly shorter healing times (p < 0.001). Median healing times were 33 and 70 days for the category II and III ulcers, respectively, compared with 153 and 195 days in the control groups. Ulcer recurrence within 24 months following photobiomodulation was 0% for category II and 6,7% for category III. Conclusions Photobiomodulation may be an effective treatment for pressure ulcers in frail older adults, substantially accelerating healing, and reducing recurrence, with potential to lessen patient burden and improve outcomes. abstract: Prior research on NIH R01 grants peer review found that selection of proposals for panel discussion constituted the decision point with the largest contribution to Black-white NIH funding disparities. We use a causal decomposition framework to understand what factors causally contribute to reducing Black-white disparities in selection into discussion, and to assess how recent procedural changes may affect Black-white disparities in selection into discussion. We first use causal decomposition methodology to explore whether hypothetical interventions eliminating Black-white disparities and/or differences in attributes would reduce Black-white disparities in selection of proposals for panel discussion. The attributes we consider include those associated with applicants (degree, career stage, their institution's funding bin) and their submitted proposals (application type, amended status, Preliminary Overall Impact Score, and NIH assigned Administering Organization and Integrated Review Group). Under reasonable assumptions, we find that among the attributes considered, Preliminary Overall Impact Score was the only one that, after equalizing, could dissolve Black-white disparities in selection into discussion. In addition, we conduct a thought experiment to explore potential impacts of the NIH's move to binary scoring for the Investigator and Environment criteria in the new Simplified Peer Review Framework on Black-white disparities in selection into discussion. Analyses from our thought experiment suggest that changing to binary scoring of the Investigator-and-Environment factor may not have any effect on disparities in selection into discussion. Overall, under the assumptions of the causal decomposition framework, these results suggest that efforts aimed at reducing disparities in selection into discussion should focus on identifying upstream, policy-relevant, and practically feasible interventions for eliminating racial disparities in Preliminary Overall Impact Scores. In contrast, the transition to the Simplified Peer Review Framework is unlikely to substantially reduce disparities in selection into discussion.

abstract: This study aimed to investigate climate-sensitive temporal patterns associated with premature mortality due to cardiovascular diseases (CVD), ischemic heart disease (IHD), and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in a large subtropical city in southern Brazil. Daily premature mortality records (ages 30-69) from 2010 to 2019 were analyzed together with meteorological data, including temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, precipitation, wind, and solar radiation, as well as temporally aggregated climatic indicators. An exploratory analytical framework combining multivariate analysis, clustering, and classification rule mining was applied to identify temporal patterns and combinations of climatic conditions associated with mortality outcomes. The approach was designed to support pattern discovery and hypothesis generation rather than causal inference.Linear associations between individual climatic variables and mortality were weak. However, exploratory analyses revealed distinct climate-sensitive temporal patterns. Premature IHD mortality was more frequently associated with colder temperatures, elevated long-term humidity, and specific combinations of atmospheric pressure and temperature. In contrast, AMI mortality showed associations with intermediate maximum temperatures, lower atmospheric pressure, and moderate levels of solar radiation. The classification models demonstrated moderate performance across outcomes, with the highest accuracy observed for AMI, indicating that complex temporal patterns may not be captured by linear analyses alone. The findings demonstrate that climate-sensitive temporal patterns in premature cardiovascular mortality can be identified using exploratory, data-driven approaches. Although causal relationships were not assessed, the results highlight the value of integrating climatic indicators and temporal aggregation into exploratory environmental health research and hypothesis generation. This framework is transparent, reproducible, and applicable to other urban settings, particularly in low- and middle-income countries facing increasing climate variability.

abstract: Drug-induced QT/QTc prolongation is a central component of cardiac safety assessment. Concentration-QT/QTc modelling uses measured or model-predicted systemic drug exposure to estimate the magnitude and uncertainty of effects on ventricular repolarisation and can support regulatory decision-making in early clinical development. However, the evidence is dispersed across dedicated thorough QT studies, early-phase studies, population pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic analyses, and secondary pooled analyses, with substantial variation in exposure metrics, electrocardiographic acquisition, heart-rate correction, model structure, assessment of active metabolites and delayed effects, and reporting of uncertainty. This protocol describes a systematic review of quantitative human concentration-QT/QTc evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar will be searched from inception without date or language restrictions. Original human studies will be eligible when drug or metabolite concentrations are measured or estimated from a pharmacokinetic model informed by study data and are quantitatively related to QT or QTc outcomes. Two reviewers will independently screen records, extract data, and assess methodological limitations. The primary estimands will be the concentration-QT/QTc drug-effect parameter and the predicted placebo-adjusted change from baseline in QTc at a clinically relevant exposure. Random-effects meta-analysis will be undertaken only within the same active moiety when analyte, endpoint, correction method, model estimand, and exposure scenario are sufficiently comparable; otherwise, structured synthesis without meta-analysis will be performed. Risk of bias will be assessed using design-appropriate tools where applicable, supplemented by a prespecified concentration-QT/QTc methodological framework. Certainty will be evaluated for coherent drug-specific bodies of evidence. This review will provide a transparent map of clinical concentration-QT/QTc methods and estimates and identify priorities for future cardiac safety studies. PROSPERO registration: CRD420261469142.

abstract: The neurodiversity movement advocates for a societal framework that recognises neurodivergence as a difference, rather than a disorder. Despite the advocacy efforts, neurodivergent people still face issues with their physical and mental health at higher rates than the general population. Some scholars argue that these disproportionate rates originate from stress resulting from discrimination and societal stigma faced by neurodivergent people. This study aims to challenge these societal views through exploring one of the reported strengths of being neurodivergent: creativity. This study aims to explore why neurodivergent populations may be creative. To research this complex relationship between being neurodivergence and creativity a qualitative study was conducted. Ten neurodivergent adults who had studied or were currently studying a creative degree were interviewed on Zoom, exploring their beliefs about this relationship. An inductive thematic analysis was then carried out. The analysis gave rise to three themes: (1) The Construct of Creativity, (2) Resilience, & (3) Empowerment. These themes provided hypotheses for understanding the connection between neurodivergence and creativity. The results provided two hypotheses. The 'innate trait hypothesis' posits that traits thought to be intrinsic to neurodivergence may be beneficial in fostering creativity. The innate traits that arose were divergent thinking, monotropism and communication differences. The 'social isolation hypothesis' posits that the discrimination that neurodivergent people face leads to profound isolation and in some cases mental health challenges. Neurodivergent people may then use creativity as a method for regulating their emotions, providing solace from distress. Moreover, the isolation they experience provides an opportunity for introspection, which fuels creativity. Our results highlight that some neurodivergent traits, when placed within a creative context, can become strengths. This highlights the possibility that the pathologisation of neurodivergent traits is not just damaging but also invalid, with the reality being much more nuanced.

abstract: Background Immune-mediated hemolytic anemia (IMHA) is a common autoimmune disease of dogs that is difficult to treat effectively. Little is known about how clinicopathological and immune variables change with time in dogs with IMHA, and whether these changes could guide therapeutic interventions. Aims To investigate dynamic changes in clinicopathological variables as well as immune and glucocorticoid-regulated gene expression in dogs with IMHA, and to determine whether these changes are associated with recovery from anemia and severity of treatment-related adverse effects. Animals 29 client-owned dogs with non-associative IMHA. Methods Dogs with IMHA underwent clinical monitoring, with collection of residual blood samples at serial time points. Expression of immune and glucocorticoid-regulated genes was quantified using real time quantitative polymerase chain reactions, with serum cytokine concentrations measured using multiplex arrays. Results Several clinical and gene expression variables changed with time in dogs with IMHA undergoing treatment, and we identified 6 major clusters representing different patterns of temporal change. No candidate dynamic variables were associated with more rapid recovery from anemia, but early increases in serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity were associated with severity of later polydipsia. Conclusions Immune and clinicopathological variables are highly changeable after onset of treatment in dogs with IMHA, with early increases in serum ALP activity being associated with later severity of polydipsia. This parameter is therefore a key candidate for further investigations of individualization of immunosuppressive therapy for dogs with IMHA.

abstract: Backgroud This study explored the molecular mechanisms by which dibutyl phthalate (DBP) contributes to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) pathogenesis using integrated network toxicology and bioinformatics. Methods DBP's carcinogenic potential was evaluated with ADMETLAB 3.0 and ProTox3. DBP-related targets were obtained from ChEMBL, SwissTargetPrediction, and PharmMapper; HCC-related targets from GeneCards and OMIM. Overlapping genes were identified by Venn analysis. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed using STRING and analyzed with Cytoscape to identify hub genes. Functional enrichment analysis (GO/KEGG) was performed with DAVID. Expression validation and survival analysis used TCGA-LIHC and GEO (GSE39791) data. A prognostic nomogram integrating gene expression and clinical variables was developed. Single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE299340) was analyzed with Seurat to examine hub gene expression. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations investigated DBP interactions with core targets. Results A total of 242 overlapping genes between DBP-associated and HCC-associated targets were identified. PPI network analysis revealed seven hub genes: KRAS, GRB2, ESR1, HSP90AA1, SRC, EGFR, and TP53. Enrichment analysis indicated significant involvement in cancer-related pathways. Expression analysis in TCGA and GEO datasets confirmed significant dysregulation of GRB2, ESR1, HSP90AA1, and SRC in HCC tissues, which correlated with patient survival outcomes. The prognostic model incorporating these genes showed good predictive accuracy. Single-cell analysis indicated distinct expression patterns of ESR1 (hepatocytes) and HSP90AA1 (immune cells) in HCC. Molecular docking demonstrated stable binding of DBP to ESR1 and HSP90AA1 with favorable binding energies (-6.8 and -6.1 kcal/mol, respectively). Molecular dynamics simulations supported the stability of these complexes, with van der Waals interactions being the primary binding force. Conclusions This integrative analysis suggests that DBP exposure may contribute to HCC pathogenesis by modulating core genes and pathways, although these findings are associative and require experimental confirmation. Hub genes, especially ESR1 and HSP90AA1, are potential biomarkers and targets. Direct DBP-protein interactions provide mechanistic insights into HCC etiology.

abstract: Wild edible plants grow in natural environments with little direct human management; consequently, their productivity and quality frequently exhibit pronounced spatiotemporal variability, making stable supply difficult. This variability represents a major constraint on the exploitation of wild edible plants as local food resources, and overcoming it requires an ecological understanding of the factors affecting variation in both productivity and quality. Here, we examined the effects of human harvesting and environmental factors on the taste characteristics of young culms of Sasa kurilensis. No statistically significant differences were detected between harvested and control plots in any major taste index, including umami, bitter aftertaste, astringency, umami richness, and sweetness (measured as Brix values). In contrast, taste characteristics showed substantial variation among study plots, suggesting a strong association with local environmental conditions. Elevation and slope angle were significantly correlated with bitter aftertaste, umami, and sweetness; plots at higher elevations and on steeper slopes tended to produce plants with a less bitter aftertaste, and higher sweetness and umami. Principal component analysis integrating multiple taste indices revealed that the major axis of taste variation was significantly associated with elevation, and that harvesting treatment had no detectable effect. These results suggest that the taste characteristics of young culms in the study area are governed primarily by topographic gradients rather than by human harvesting. Although wild edible plants are important food resources in boreal and temperate forests worldwide, many are poorly managed. By quantitatively establishing relationships between taste characteristics and environmental factors in young culms, this study provides a scientific basis for determining the optimal timing, location, and selection criteria for wild edible plant harvesting, thereby contributing to the development of sustainable use strategies.

abstract: The development of aluminium matrix composites with improved structural and tribological performance has attracted considerable interest for lightweight engineering applications. This work investigates the microstructural, mechanical, tribological, and hot-deformation response of an AA8011 aluminium composite containing 5 wt.% TiB2, fabricated by ultrasonic-assisted stir casting and subsequently processed by equal-channel angular pressing (ECAP). The effect of accumulated severe plastic deformation was evaluated in the as-cast condition and after 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 ECAP passes. Phase constitution and elemental characteristics were examined using X-ray diffraction and energy-dispersive spectroscopy, while microstructural evolution was characterized using optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, electron backscatter diffraction, and transmission electron microscopy. Repeated ECAP progressively refined the aluminium matrix, improved the spatial distribution of TiB2 particles, and reduced pronounced casting-related structural discontinuities. The EBSD-measured grain size decreased from 12.45 μm in the as-cast condition to 0.54 μm after 10 passes. The resulting microstructural refinement and densification were accompanied by increases in hardness, tensile strength, compressive strength, flexural strength, impact energy, and elongation. The ultimate tensile strength increased from 182 to 266 MPa after 10 passes. Dry-sliding tests performed at loads of 10-50 N and a sliding distance of 5000 m showed reductions in wear rate of approximately 55-58% and in coefficient of friction of approximately 62-75% relative to the as-cast condition. Processing-map analysis further indicated an expansion of the stable deformation region with increasing ECAP passes. The combined results demonstrate that ultrasonic-assisted stir casting followed by multi-pass ECAP provides an effective route for tailoring the microstructure and mechanical, tribological, and hot-deformation response of AA8011-5 wt.% TiB2 composites within the investigated processing conditions.

abstract: Smallholder farmers in southwestern Ethiopia face overlapping challenges that trap them in cycles of poverty and land degradation, yet the feedback mechanisms sustaining these traps remain poorly understood. This study addresses the research question what distinct feedback mechanisms perpetuate low productivity across four coexisting farming systems and system-specific leverage points. We used system dynamics modeling, collecting data from 375 households across three purposively selected districts (Dedo, Gera, and Sekoru), complemented by 21 key informant interviews and 8 focus group discussions. Causal loop diagrams (CLDs) were constructed to map feedback cycles within each system. Our results identified four major farming systems with observable disparities across each system. Farm income ranges from 15,691 Ethiopian Birr (ETB) (subsistence, 33% of households) to 46,114 ETB (coffee-honey, 33%). Meanwhile, frequent extension contact varies from 5.7% (subsistence) to 36.1% (wheat-livestock, 19%). Maize-livestock farmers (15%) overgraze at 2.3 TLU/ha (vs. recommended 0.8), mining soil fertility. Coffee-honey farmers face deforestation declined (canopy cover 60% → 25%) and 81% climate impact perception; wheat-livestock farmers have only 8.3% formal credit access. CLDs identified distinct reinforcing traps: the food-labor nexus in subsistence, the soil mining trap in maize-livestock, the input-labor-pest complex in wheat-livestock, and the deforestation-pollination-price triad in coffee-honey. The findings indicate that each farming system is locked into a distinct self-reinforcing cycle, and that system-specific, testable intervention ranging from nutrition-sensitive safety nets for subsistence to climate-smart agroforestry for coffee-honey are required to break these cycles. These findings provide a dynamic, multi-system framework to guide policy design and future empirical evidence for sustainable smallholder agriculture in Ethiopia and similar contexts.

abstract: To address insufficient lateral restraint and the susceptibility of the flat walls of traditional concrete-filled steel tubular (CFST) rectangular flat columns, a built-up rectangular CFST flat column with integrated longitudinal cold-formed stiffening ribs is proposed. The FE model was validated against the global response of a welded-plate CFST flat-column specimen. The model was then used to study the axial-compression and quasi-static cyclic behavior of the proposed columns. The coupled effects of aspect ratio, tube thickness, and rib dimensions were evaluated. The individual effects of tube thickness and rib dimensions under axial compression were further examined through the supplementary decoupled analysis. The results indicate that, compared with the non-stiffened control specimen, the stiffened configuration provides higher axial and cyclic load-bearing capacity, and more effective suppression of local outward bulging. Within the investigated parameter range, the coupled increase in tube thickness and rib dimensions improves axial and cyclic performance, while the decoupled analysis indicates that tube thickness is the dominant parameter governing axial load-bearing capacity and rib dimensions mainly contribute to local outward deformation control and post-peak load retention. These findings provide a reference for the parametric design and engineering application of stiffened cold-formed built-up rectangular flat CFST columns.

abstract: Background While effective national clinic networks exist for a select few conditions, the availability and use of multidisciplinary specialty care for most genetic or congenital conditions, including Down syndrome (DS), remain uneven. This uneven distribution creates significant geographic and social gradients in healthcare access. To understand these differences within a geographically expansive and socio-demographically diverse setting, this study quantified travel burden to pediatric DS specialty clinics in Texas, identifying differences based on key maternal socio-demographic and geographic factors. Methods A cross-sectional analysis of 8,201 individuals with DS presumed living and 477 deceased individuals with DS born between 1999-2020 from the Texas Birth Defects Registry was performed. One-way driving time and distance along the road networks from the maternal residence to the nearest seven pediatric DS specialty clinics were calculated using ArcGIS Pro. Travel burden was analyzed by maternal race/ethnicity, education, age and residence at delivery. Travel burden measures were categorized as low, moderate to high, and very high. Results Among 8,678 live‑born individuals with DS, 45% resided over 90 miles from the closest in-state DS specialty clinic, and 41% faced one‑way driving times exceeding two hours. Those born to mothers in border counties experienced the greatest travel burden, with median one-way driving times exceeding 7 hours. Rural residents had a four times greater travel burden than urban residents. Individuals born to Hispanic mothers traveled twice as far as those born to non-Hispanic mothers. Residents of high‑poverty tracts had a median one-way distance of approximately 150 miles, triple the 35 miles seen in low‑poverty tracts. Conclusion Our findings suggest that substantial travel burden to DS specialty clinics exists in Texas, affecting individuals with DS born to Hispanic and younger mothers, as well as those in rural, border, and concentrated-poverty regions. Further research is needed to explore life course residential history and clinic utilization to address these differences.

abstract: Changing sowing dates has been a farming low-cost strategy to mitigate climate induced water stress during the juvenile stage of crops. This study evaluates the potential of drought-tolerant maize varieties and fertilizer microdosing to enhance maize productivity under different sowing dates in rainfed conditions. We conducted a two-year strip split-plot trial with three sowing dates (early, normal, and late), five maize varieties (DMR, TZEE, TZE, 2008Syn, and 2000Syn) and five fertilizer treatments (control: no fertilizer, three microdosed rates MD1: 25 kg N + 4 kg P ha-1, MD2: 25 kg N + 8 kg P ha-1, MD3: 35 kg N + 8 kg P ha-1, and the recommended rate RR: 76 kg N + 13 kg P ha-1). DMR is a drought-susceptible variety; and TZEE, TZE, 2008Syn, and 2000Syn are drought-tolerant. Results show that grain yield was 9.9% higher and 10.2% lower under early and late sowing, respectively, compared to normal sowing. Grain yield was 29.9, 37.8, 26.5 and 12.5% higher under TZEE, TZE, 2008Syn, and 2000Syn, respectively compared to DMR; and 153.3, 200.9, 247.2 and 220.8% under MD1, MD2, MD3 and RR, respectively compared to control. DMR achieved its highest mean grain yield under the recommended fertilizer rate, whereas the drought-tolerant varieties achieved their highest mean yields under MD3. The findings confirm that late sowing reduced maize performance, while drought-tolerant varieties and fertilizer microdosing independently improved average productivity.

abstract: Background Patients with cancer experience substantial psychosocial challenges throughout the cancer journey. Psychosocial cancer care is crucial for addressing patients' psychological, emotional, social, spiritual needs, and for promoting well-being and quality of life. Despite its importance, psychosocial cancer care services remain insufficiently provided within routine cancer care services in many settings. Aim of the study To explore healthcare providers' perceptions of barriers to providing psychosocial cancer care services within routine care at a tertiary cancer hospital in Tanzania. Materials and methods This study adopted an explorative qualitative design. This study was conducted at Ocean Road Cancer Institute in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Purposeful sampling was used to recruit 18 healthcare providers until information saturation was reached. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a semi-structured interview guide. All interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using a thematic analysis approach to identify key patterns and themes. Results Three themes emerged that describe health care providers' perceptions of barriers to the provision of psychosocial cancer care. These barriers include inadequately trained healthcare providers, an unsupportive organizational structure and environment for psychosocial care services, and challenges in establishing a trusting therapeutic relationship between patients and providers. Conclusion Despite its recognized importance in promoting quality of life, the provision of psychosocial cancer care remains insufficiently provided in cancer settings. Findings from this study indicate that psychosocial care provision is limited by inadequate and incompetent staff, a lack of coordination, and an unsupportive organizational structure, and that building effective patient-provider therapeutic relationships was reported to hinder the provision of psychosocial care. To address these barriers, training, the establishment of coordinating units, and the development of protocols to guide the multidisciplinary team are essential. Integrating psychosocial care competencies into healthcare professionals' training curriculum is also essential to bridge the gap.

abstract: Taxi traffic safety arises from the complex interplay among road infrastructure, driver behavior, vehicle characteristics, and environmental conditions. However, driver, vehicle, and environmental factors are typically challenging to regulate directly through policy or design, whereas road characteristics can be systematically adjusted through infrastructure planning and traffic management strategies. Therefore, understanding how specific road features contribute to crash risk offers a more practical and sustainable pathway for enhancing taxi travel safety. This study aims at investigating how road characteristics heterogeneously influence the severity of taxi-involved crashes. To accomplish this, a latent class clustering method is first leveraged to classify crashes with similar contextual features. Subsequently, a partial proportional odds model is applied to quantify the class-specific impacts of road characteristics on taxi-involved crash severity. The taxi crash data reported by the London police from January 2019 to June 2024 are utilized to achieve this study. The results demonstrate substantial heterogeneity in how road characteristics affect taxi-involved crash outcomes across different crash classes. Among the examined factors on taxi-involved crashes, speed limits and junction controls exert the most pronounced influences. Higher speed limits (≥40 mph) substantially elevate the probabilities of serious injuries (+14.76%) and fatalities (+0.93%). In contrast, moderate speed limits (31-40 mph) are associated with notably lower marginal effects on serious injuries (+8.27%) and fatalities (+0.46%). The installation of traffic signals at junctions decreases the likelihood of serious injuries (-11.68%) and fatalities (-0.50%). These findings indicate that uniform safety policies may be insufficient for mitigating class-specific taxi risks. This study contributes empirical evidence and practical insights for road safety management. By identifying the heterogeneous influence patterns of road characteristics, the findings support targeted infrastructure design, speed management, and signal control strategies to effectively reduce both the frequency and severity of taxi-related crashes.

abstract: Nighttime unmanned aerial vehicle object detection is challenged by degraded visible-light textures, cluttered infrared thermal responses, and local spatial discrepancies between infrared and visible images. To address these issues, we propose IV-PAFNet, an infrared-visible purification, alignment, and fusion network designed for object detection in nighttime and low-visibility conditions. IV-PAFNet consists of two primary components. The infrared signal purification and spatial alignment module applies learnable high-pass filtering and gated residual fusion to refine infrared responses, followed by visible-guided offset prediction and differentiable resampling to alleviate local cross-modal spatial discrepancies. The multi-scale fusion attention enhancement module performs channel-wise modality recalibration and spatial reliability weighting at multiple feature-pyramid levels, allowing the network to adapt the contribution of each modality to local imaging conditions. In the training-based DroneVehicle and generalization-based Camera-vehicle1 datasets, IV-PAFNet achieves 62.81% mAP@0.5:0.95 and 51.4% mAP@0.5:0.95, respectively. Additional controlled experiments investigate the distinct roles of infrared purification, visible-guided alignment, channel recalibration, and spatial reliability modeling, while statistical and computational analyses characterize run-to-run variation and inference cost. The code is available at https://github.com/iv-pafnet/IV-PAFNet.

abstract: Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying disorders of consciousness (DoC) remains a major challenge, particularly in distinguishing limited awareness in minimally conscious state (MCS) and complete unawareness in unresponsive wakefulness syndrome, also coined vegetative state (UWS/VS). In this multicentre study, we fitted a biophysically informed corticothalamic neural field model to high-density EEG data from two large independent datasets, comprising 203 UWS patients, 270 MCS patients and 74 healthy controls. We then used the fitted parameters to simulate EEG time series on a per-subject basis and compared empirical and simulated complexity metrics. The model reliably captured the spectral features across different states of consciousness and revealed reduced corticothalamic integrity in DoC patients that was more pronounced in UWS than in MCS, supporting the mesocircuit hypothesis. Furthermore, the simulated EEG reproduced the complexity patterns of the empirical recordings, with permutation entropy emerging as a sensitive marker capable of distinguishing between MCS and UWS for both real and simulated time series.

abstract: Objectives Although molecular detection of Cyclospora cayetanensis is increasingly incorporated into multiplex gastrointestinal diagnostic workflows, dedicated external quality assessment (EQA) programmes for Cyclospora remain limited. We performed a nationwide interlaboratory comparison to evaluate routine molecular detection of C. cayetanensis across decentralized ISO15189-accredited laboratories in the Netherlands. Methods An anonymized 11-sample panel containing unpreserved stool specimens and eNAT-preserved stool suspensions was distributed to laboratories in the Netherlands (n = 8) and Curaçao (n = 1). Laboratories analysed samples using their routine diagnostic workflows. Workflow characteristics, DNA extraction procedures, molecular platforms, and interpretation criteria were collected by a structured questionnaire. Because detection of Cryptosporidium spp. is usually performed within the same workflow and present similar extraction challenges, Cryptosporidium-positive samples were included as internal workflow controls. Aggregated retrospective laboratory data were collected to explore surveillance feasibility and to gain insight in seasonality of C. cayetanensis and Cryptosporidium spp. Results Seven laboratories performed molecular detection of C. cayetanensis, while all nine performed detection of Cryptosporidium spp. Complete qualitative agreement was observed for Cryptosporidium spp. detection. For C. cayetanensis, overall qualitative agreement was high, although one false-positive and three false-negative results occurred among core samples. Detection of a low-positive educational sample varied substantially between laboratories, indicating reduced reproducibility near assay-specific limits of detection. This study shows that eNAT-preserved stool suspensions remained stable under ambient transport conditions. Retrospective laboratory data showed low-level year-round C. cayetanensis detection and a seasonal increase in Cryptosporidium spp. positivity during late summer and autumn. Conclusions Routine molecular detection of C. cayetanensis demonstrated good overall interlaboratory agreement across decentralized diagnostic laboratories. However, reproducibility decreased for low-positive samples, highlighting the importance of assay validation, external quality assessment, and cautious interpretation of weak positive C. cayetanensis PCR results.

abstract: Shark microbiome studies offer acute insights into host health, immunity, and ecological interactions, yet remain poorly studied compared to other marine vertebrates. Shark-associated microbial communities, despite being species-specific, are influenced by environmental conditions and feeding ecology. In this study, we aimed to characterize shifts in the microbiome of the Critically Endangered angelshark (Squatina squatina) during the early stages of development and to assess how environmental factors contribute to the shaping of a specific microbiota. Samples from thirty-nine juvenile angelsharks were collected from Las Teresitas nursery area in the Canary Islands over one year. Skin, oral and cloacal microbiomes were analysed using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. The sizes of individuals ranged between 24 and 42 cm in length. The shark microbiome was clearly distinct from the surrounding environment, indicating a unique composition from early life stages. Dominant bacteria present in the shark microbiomes included Vibrionaceae (up to 96%), Pseudoalteromonas (up to 63%), Rhodobacteraceae (up to 57%) and Alteromonadaceae (up to 20%). Seawater had a greater influence than sediment on the external skin microbiome, especially in younger individuals. This was not expected due to the burial behaviour of the species. Notably, the abundance of Pseudoalteromonadaceae (assessed by qPCR) was positively correlated with shark growth but was independent of the skin mucus. This suggests a protective role of this phylotype in younger individuals and may help in the adaptation to habitat conditions. This is the first comprehensive microbiome study in angelsharks, highlighting the importance of environmental preservation for microbial integrity and juvenile fitness.
