abstract: Computational modeling of spatial biochemical processes in neuroscience is increasingly important as advances in experimental and imaging techniques provide detailed insights into cellular organization. Reaction-diffusion models are commonly used to study the diffusion and interactions of ions and molecules within neuronal cells, and multiple open-access simulation platforms have been developed to support such analysis. However, a comprehensive analysis of commonly used simulation tools, including MCell, STEPS, NeuroRD, and NEURON, remains lacking, particularly for realistic glial cell geometries, as these tools were originally developed for neurons. Here, we present a systematic analysis of these four simulation environments by implementing equivalent calcium diffusion and calcium-calmodulin reaction-diffusion models across a range of spatial domains. These include simplified geometries (cylinders and rectangular cuboids) as well as biologically realistic astroglial morphologies derived from electron microscopy data, including mouse Bergmann glia and mouse and human cortical astrocytes. Using matched kinetic parameters and diffusion constants, we examine simulation outputs and morphological variations across platforms under comparable conditions. We find that all tools produce overall consistent results for the systems considered, indicating that each can reliably capture diffusion and reaction-diffusion dynamics in simplified and complex geometries. At the same time, we show that the structural heterogeneity of branchlets from human astrocytes and mouse Bergmann glia gives rise to distinct calcium signaling, demonstrating that fine-scale morphology critically shapes astroglial dynamics and must be accurately captured by simulation frameworks. In addition, notable differences emerge in geometry representation, implementation strategies, computational aspects, and usability of the tools. By highlighting key trade-offs between geometric fidelity, flexibility, and computational cost in modeling intracellular biochemical processes, these findings provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate simulation tools. More broadly, our results support the use of reaction-diffusion modeling in morphologically realistic astrocytic environments and contribute to enabling mechanistic studies of localized signaling events at synaptic and perisynaptic sites.

abstract: Pollen and nutrient analyses of the faeces of the Himalayan marmot (Marmota himalayana) were made to understand its preferred dietary plants and ecology. Pollen preserved in the faeces accurately reflected its diet as a mixed feeder including Artemisia, Caryophyllaceae, Asteroideae, and Ephedra, characteristic plants of the Alpine steppe vegetation under a cold and arid climate in the higher Himalaya. Pollen ratio values between Artemisia/Chenopodiaceae, Artemisia/Cyperaceae, and Artemisia/Ephedra are identified from the Pensilla Pass and Rimkhim regions, as useful tools that characterize the Alpine steppe vegetation and climate in the higher Himalaya. Principal Component Analysis of the pollen taxa indicated only a slight difference in the relative abundance between the two localities sampled, Pensila Pass and Rimkhim areas. Coprophilous fungal spores, Sporormiella and Saccobolus, were abundant and considered useful for understanding the interrelationship between vegetation and the marmot's preferred habitat. Fifteen nutritional elements were recorded, and the high concentration of carbon, nitrogen, calcium, silicon, and, phosphorous is considered significant with a direct dietary relationship with the preferred plants consumed. This study provides a modern analogue and a baseline for coprolite and palaeoecological analyses in marmot inhabited regions and to observe the species future response to vegetation and climate change resulting shifts in altitude in the higher Himalaya.

abstract: Background Nutrition plays a crucial role in oral health, influencing the risk of caries, periodontal disease, erosion, and oral cancers. Dentists are key providers of dietary guidance, but require adequate knowledge to do this effectively. This study compared the impact of multimedia versus audio-based educational interventions on the knowledge and self-reported behavior of general dentists in Tehran regarding nutrition and oral health. Methods In this randomized controlled trial, 166 general dentists in Tehran were recruited in 2023 through professional online platforms and randomly allocated to either a multimedia-based or an audio-based educational intervention. Knowledge (11 items) and behavior (9 items) regarding the impact of nutrition on periodontal health, dental caries, oral cancer, and erosion were assessed using a validated questionnaire. The educational intervention was delivered over a one-month period. Within-group changes were assessed using paired t-tests, between-group differences using repeated-measures ANOVA, and the effect of demographic variables on post-intervention scores using ANCOVA, with baseline values as covariates (α = 0.05). Results Of the participants, 53.6% were women, and 37.9% worked in private practice. Both groups demonstrated significant improvements in knowledge and behavior scores following the intervention (p < 0.001), with greater gains observed in the multimedia group. Analysis of covariance indicated that baseline knowledge and behavior were not significantly associated with age, gender, dental school, years of professional experience, or practice setting. Conclusion Both multimedia- and audio-based educational interventions effectively improved dentists' knowledge and self-reported behaviors related to nutrition and oral health. Therefore, given dentists' busy work schedules, the use of these educational approaches may enhance their capacity to provide evidence-based counseling in the field of nutrition and oral health.

abstract: Contemporary food environments are dominated by dynamic food cues such as moving videos of food, which may engage neural pathways differently than static images. Yet most neuroimaging studies of food cue reactivity have relied on static images. This preliminary study aimed to explore neural responses in reward- and appetite-regulating brain regions to dynamic versus static presentations of high- and low-calorie food stimuli. Seventeen healthy adults (8 with healthy weight and 9 with overweight; mean age = 32.7 ± 10.1y; 53% female) completed a novel functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) paradigm involving dynamic (video) and static (image) presentations of food and non-food object stimuli. Two fMRI runs were conducted: high-calorie food and object cues were presented in Run 1 and low-calorie food and object cues were presented in Run 2. Stimulus format (dynamic vs. static) was manipulated within each run, and analyses of format effects were conducted separately for the high- and low-calorie conditions. Primary analyses examined whether stimulus format (dynamic vs. static) elicited differential activation of visual food cues relative to non-food objects, with high-calorie and low-calorie conditions tested separately. Regions of interest included a priori reward- and appetite-related regions, including the amygdala, dorsal striatum, ventral striatum, insula, and substantia nigra/ventral tegmental area. Secondary whole-brain analyses and exploratory comparisons by weight status were conducted. Stimulus format did not significantly modulate activation to food cues relative to objects in a priori reward- and appetite-related regions for either high- or low-calorie foods. Whole-brain analyses showed that the dynamic-versus-static high-calorie food contrast (relative to objects) elicited greater activation in the right occipital fusiform gyrus. Frontal, insular, occipital, and postcentral activation was observed to the dynamic high-calorie food-versus-object contrast. Exploratory analyses showed that, for high-calorie foods, individuals with overweight showed greater dynamic-versus-static food-related activation (relative to objects) in the dorsal striatum than individuals with healthy weight; for low-calorie foods, individuals with healthy weight showed greater dynamic-versus-static food-related activation (relative to objects) in the substantia nigra/ventral tegmental area than individuals with overweight. In this pilot study, effect sizes for dynamic-versus-static differences in reward-related regions did not reach statistical significance, and thus findings should be interpreted with caution given the limited sample size. Dynamic cues were well tolerated and showed similar appeal compared with static images, while engaging broader networks related to perception, attention, and salience. Larger studies and designs that randomize the food cue type are needed to confirm and extend these observations.

abstract: Infectious disease models are used to predict the spread and impact of outbreaks of a disease. Like other complex models, they have parameters that need to be calibrated, and structural discrepancies from the reality that they simulate that should be accounted for in calibration and prediction. Whilst Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) techniques have been applied to infectious disease models before, they were not routinely used to inform policymakers in the UK during the COVID-19 pandemic. In this paper, we will argue that during a fast moving pandemic, models and policy are changing on timescales that make traditional UQ methods impractical, if not impossible to implement. We present an alternative formulation to the calibration problem that embeds model discrepancy within the structure of the model, and appropriately assimilates data within the simulation. We then show how UQ can be used to calibrate the model in real-time to produce disease trajectories accounting for parameter uncertainty and model discrepancy. We apply these ideas to an age-structured COVID-19 model for England and demonstrate the types of information it could have produced to feed into policy support prior to the lockdown of March 2020.

abstract: Insects and fungi are among the most destructive pests and pathogens affecting agriculture and public health. Although chemical pesticides have long been the primary means of control, their broad‑spectrum activity and widespread use have accelerated resistance in many systems. RNA interference (RNAi) has therefore emerged as a promising species‑specific alternative. RNAi is initiated by double‑stranded RNA (dsRNA), which triggers sequence‑directed degradation of target transcripts. However, RNAi efficiency varies markedly across species, influenced by nuclease activity, dsRNA length, and the cellular uptake route. We previously showed that long dsRNA uptake in Aedes aegypti depends on clathrin‑mediated endocytosis (CME), whereas paperclip RNA (pcRNA), a compact dsRNA structure developed in our laboratory, bypasses CME and enters cells through a distinct pathway. Here, we compared the uptake and RNAi performance of two dsRNA formats, long dsRNA (210-230 bp) and pcRNA (21-23 bp), in three representative species: Aedes aegypti (mosquito), Spodoptera frugiperda (moth), and Sclerotinia sclerotiorum (fungus). To assess cellular uptake of these dsRNAs, we used two CME inhibitors, chlorpromazine (CPZ) and bafilomycin A1 (BafA1), along with fluorescein‑labeled dsRNAs. CME inhibition prevented long dsRNA from entering the cytoplasm and abolished its ability to induce RNAi. In contrast, pcRNAs were readily internalized and produced significant gene knockdowns under both inhibitor treatments. Microscopy further revealed that all three cell types, pretreated with either CPZ or BafA1, prevented long dsRNA from entering the cytoplasm. pcRNA, consistently reached the cytoplasm and showed superior uptake across all species. Together, these findings demonstrate that pcRNA uses an uptake mechanism distinct from long dsRNA, enabling it to circumvent CME-dependent barriers. This unique internalization route likely reflects its compact size and structural configuration and highlights pcRNA as a promising platform for improving RNAi-based pest and pathogen control.

abstract: Healthcare safety is a major global concern since unsafe and low-quality services can lead to poor health outcomes and even harm to patients. Promoting a strong patient safety culture is a prerequisite for improving patient safety. The present study aimed to assess patient safety culture in dental clinics in Herat, Afghanistan in 2024. This cross-sectional study included 210 dental team members selected by random cluster sampling from 7 regions. The assessment tool was the Medical Office Survey on Patient Safety Culture (MOSOPS) modified for use in dentistry. A pilot study confirmed content validity and reliability (Cronbach's alpha > 0.70). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, bivariate tests (t-tests and ANOVA), and multiple linear regression to examine associations with patient safety culture. The total patient safety culture score was (0.70 ± 0.10) (on a 0-1 scale), indicating a moderate level. The strongest mean scores were for organizational learning (0.78 ± 0.14) and teamwork (0.77 ± 0.17). The lowest score was observed for office processes and standardization (0.62 ± 0.13). Multiple linear regression revealed that being female (B = 0.031, p = 0.049) and holding a managerial position (B = 0.073, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with higher patient safety culture scores. Overall, patient safety culture was generally favorable, although important organizational gaps remain. Future improvement efforts should focus on standardizing office processes and strengthening information exchange with external healthcare providers. In resource-limited settings such as Afghanistan, feasible interventions including locally adapted protocols, and ongoing managerial support and supervision may further strengthen patient safety culture.

abstract: The increasing frequency of arboviral diseases' outbreaks in Cameroon necessitates evidence-based vector control. However, the efficacy of chemical control interventions is seriously threatened by the rapid evolution of insecticide resistance in Aedes vector populations. This study investigated the insecticide resistance profiles of Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus across ecologically diverse cities in Cameroon. Aedes larvae were collected from April to November 2024 in eight major cities representing diverse ecological landscapes across Cameroon: Yaoundé (Congo-Guinean equatorial forest); Douala and Kribi (coastal areas); Nkongsamba, Bafoussam, Mbouda, and Maroua (highland areas); and Bertoua (sub-tropical/savanna transition zone). World Health Organization (WHO) insecticide susceptibility bioassays were conducted on F1 adults against pyrethroids (0.75% permethrin, 0.05% deltamethrin), carbamates (0.1% propoxur, 0.1% bendiocarb), and organophosphates (0.05% pirimiphos-methyl). Molecular mechanisms potentially driving insecticide resistance were characterized using multiplex TaqMan qPCR to genotype kdr mutations and RT-qPCR to quantify the expression of detoxification genes such as cytochrome P450s, Glutathione S-transferases, and Carboxylesterases. Ae. aegypti displayed widespread resistance to pyrethroids, with mortality as low as 17.4% (permethrin, Kribi). This resistance could possibly be attributed to distinct geographic distribution of target-site mutations, with F1534C ranging from absent in Bafoussam to 95% in Kribi and Bertoua (alongside high frequencies in Yaoundé and Douala), and V1016I peaking at 46.3% in Bertoua while remaining absent in Bafoussam and Maroua. Furthermore, double-mutant homozygous haplotypes (CC-II) reached up to 15%, alongside massive metabolic upregulation, notably a 184.8-fold increase in GSTD4 expression in Bafoussam. In contrast, Ae albopictus populations appeared generally more susceptible across most sites, though localized resistance to permethrin and deltamethrin emerged in Douala and Nkongsamba. Susceptibility to bendiocarb and pirimiphos-methyl was observed across all sites for both species. In contrast, most of these populations were found to be resistant to propoxur. The continued susceptibility of Ae. albopictus in most regions, contrasted with its emerging resistance in urban centers, underscores the need for species-specific and geographically tailored management interventions. Overall, these findings emphasize the urgent need to deploy targeted larviciding approaches in breeding sites and integrate routine resistance monitoring to mitigate the spread of arboviral vectors across Cameroon.

abstract: Academic institutions privilege norms of continuous productivity and uninterrupted availability, creating conformity pressures that systematically disadvantage those who deviate from an implicit template of the 'ideal academic'. This study explores how doctoral students and faculty in the health sciences perceive the reproduction of social homogeneity. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with nine participants at a German university hospital. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis with extended idiographic engagement. Participants perceived homogeneity as reproduced through external exclusion, enacted by others through networks, normative expectations, or institutional arrangements, and self-exclusion, whereby individuals withdrew, reduced visibility, or reshaped identity in anticipation of exclusion ('anticipatory compliance'). Across both processes, the tacit norm of the ideal academic organised access and belonging. Supportive supervision and visible role models were perceived as partial buffers but did not structurally alter underlying norms. Interpreted through the social identity threat framework, these accounts support an exploratory interpretation of a possible self-reinforcing cycle: structural homogeneity may generate identity-threatening environments that activate concealment and withdrawal, potentially concentrating homogeneity further. These findings suggest that achieving substantive inclusion requires challenging the structural conditions that naturalise presence, mobility, and availability as measures of academic success.

abstract: Objective To evaluate the associations of peripheral perfusion index (PI) and end-tidal carbon dioxide (PETCO2), individually and in combination, with sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) in adults with in-hospital cardiac arrest, and to assess their predictive performance. Methods This prospective observational study included 125 adults with in-hospital cardiac arrest, of whom 62 achieved sustained ROSC and 63 did not. Measurements obtained after ROSC or termination of resuscitation were excluded. Changes in PI and PETCO2 during resuscitation were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Event-average PI and PETCO2 were evaluated for their ability to predict sustained ROSC using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. The combined model was internally validated using 2,000 bootstrap resamples. Results The median time to ROSC was 11 min (IQR, 5-20). Significant group-by-time interactions were observed for both PI and PETCO2 (both P < 0.001). Event-average PI was higher in the ROSC group than in the non-ROSC group [0.62% (IQR, 0.42-0.90) vs. 0.37% (0.31-0.52)], as was event-average PETCO2 [15.5 mmHg (12.2-17.8) vs. 12.0 mmHg (10.4-13.7)] (both P < 0.001). The areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) were 0.756 (95% CI, 0.670-0.842) for PI, 0.753 (95% CI, 0.666-0.839) for PETCO2, and 0.808 (95% CI, 0.731-0.886) for their combination. The optimism-corrected AUC for the combined model was 0.800. Pairwise comparisons showed no significant differences among the AUCs. In the exploratory fully adjusted model, PETCO2 remained independently associated with sustained ROSC (adjusted OR, 1.626; 95% CI, 1.148-2.302; P = 0.006), whereas PI was not statistically significant (adjusted OR, 1.359 per 0.1% increase; 95% CI, 0.962-1.920; P = 0.082). Conclusion Higher PI and PETCO2 during resuscitation were associated with sustained ROSC. Combining PI with PETCO2 yielded numerically better discrimination than either measure alone, although the differences in AUC were not statistically significant. External validation is needed before the combined model can be applied in clinical practice.

abstract: Operating modern power grids requires coordinated solutions for optimal dispatch, state estimation, price prediction, and contingency analysis, yet these tasks are usually modeled separately. We present PhysBridge, a response-oriented pretraining framework in which historical windows provide context while solver-generated perturbation responses, active constraints, and local sensitivities define the pretraining targets. PhysBridge combines a temporal-graph encoder with a Primal-Dual Response Bridge (PDR-Bridge) that performs safeguarded local refinement and outputs transferable primal, projection-dual, sensitivity, and health tokens. Across IEEE 14-, 30-, 57-, 118-, and 300-bus systems, the benchmark contains 26.3 million solver-generated perturbation-response pairs; in the 300-bus transfer setting, pretraining uses only the 21.04 million nominal pairs from the 14-, 30-, 57-, and 118-bus source topologies. Across three runs on unseen IEEE 300-bus transfer with 10% labels, PhysBridge obtains a 2.21±0.05% OPF cost gap, 96.3±0.2% feasibility, 1.84±0.05 $/MWh LMP MAE, and 91.6±0.3% contingency/fault event macro F1. Relative to a matched rollout-only model trained on the same source corpus without response targets or bridge refinement, these values correspond to a 50.8% lower OPF gap and a 7.4 percentage-point higher event F1. The bridge requires 12.4 ms per 300-bus forward pass and activates fallback on 4.6% of stressed windows. Comparisons with supervised-only OPF specialists that do not receive matched solver-generated pretraining are interpreted as task-relevant performance under the proposed pretraining regime, not as architecture-only superiority.

abstract: Existing studies on resource and environmental carrying capacity (RECC) have primarily focused on comprehensive evaluation and linear identification. But the quantification of driving effect on RECC have not been fully explored, especially the interaction and nonlinear effects. Therefore, this paper constructs an explainable machine learning framework, to comprehensively assess the RECC index of 31 provincial regions in China and to reveal nonlinear and interaction mechanisms of influence factors. Firstly, the XGBoost model is utilized to surrogate the evaluation results, which demonstrates outstanding predictive performance (R2 = 0.95, RMSE = 0.08) and stability. The results shows that the average RECC index in China dropping from 1.18 to 0.39, marking a transition from a high-risk state to a safe and sustainable state. Then, the SHAP model quantifies the nonlinear and threshold effects of key influence factors. The results indicate that the total emissions of pollutants in wastewater (X2) and industrial sulfur dioxide emissions (X3) are the two most critical factors, with a cumulative contribution rate of 49%. 50000 tons is a threshold for X2, beyond which the RECC index significantly increases with the increase of X2. 10 billion cubic meters is the marginal contribution of X3, with the greatest impact on RECC index. The interaction effect indicates a significant positive synergistic effect between X2 and X3, with the maximum increase in SHAP value reaching 0.1. There is a significant antagonistic effect between resource availability and environmental pressure. This study offering new directions for understanding the underlying mechanisms of complex environmental systems.

title: Robustness asymmetry under edge failures: A unified framework based on structural controllability and power domination.

author_details.name: Bader Alwasel
author_details.affiliation: Unit of Scientific Research, Applied College, Qassim University, Buraydah, Saudi Arabia.

affiliation_resolution.input: Unit of Scientific Research, Applied College, Qassim University, Buraydah, Saudi Arabia.

abstract: Modern complex networks require effective mechanisms for network control and monitoring to ensure reliable operation under failures. Structural controllability and power domination provide fundamental frameworks for assessing these capabilities, yet a systematic comparison of their robustness under random failures remains limited. Unlike prior studies that typically examine structural controllability and power-domination-based monitoring separately, this work presents a unified framework for analyzing their robustness under identical edge-failure conditions in Erdős-Rényi random graphs. Using a simulation-based evaluation across a broad parameter space of network sizes, edge densities, and edge-survival probabilities, together with Monte Carlo estimation of the expected monitoring coverage and driver-node requirements under random edge failures, the analysis evaluates degradation through sensitivity, balance, and gap metrics. The results reveal a configuration-dependent robustness asymmetry, with structural controllability exhibiting its most pronounced relative vulnerability under sparse and severely degraded network conditions. Notably, following edge failures, the two frameworks are reevaluated through different structural mechanisms: the power dominating set is recomputed on the degraded network to determine the updated monitoring-node requirement, whereas the maximum matching is recomputed to determine the updated driver-node requirement for structural controllability. Network density also plays a critical role, with sparse networks exhibiting higher vulnerability and dense networks showing greater resilience. These findings indicate that, for the considered Erdős-Rényi random-network model under independent random edge failures, the stronger relative vulnerability of structural controllability is concentrated primarily in sparse and severely degraded network configurations.

abstract: We present ScaffoldForge, a 3D conditional diffusion framework for the generative design of bone scaffolds. ScaffoldForge maps a set of standardized trabecular descriptors (bone volume fraction BV/TV, trabecular thickness Tb.Th, trabecular spacing Tb.Sp, trabecular number Tb.N, connectivity density Conn.D, structure model index SMI, degree of anisotropy DA, and permeability k) to a 3D scaffold architecture in a single forward pass. A multi-objective conditioning mechanism couples these descriptors through adaptive instance normalization, and a physics-constrained loss adds empirical penalties for stiffness, manufacturing feasibility, and perfusion, evaluated on the denoiser's reconstruction of the clean scaffold so that the penalties carry gradient. To address the scarcity of paired geometry-property data, we describe a procedural pipeline whose generated scaffolds reproduce the morphometric distributions of real micro-CT references. In an in silico evaluation on three benchmark datasets, ScaffoldForge attains an estimated 56.6 MPa compressive strength (8.2% over topology optimization; paired t-test, p = 0.043, n = 5 seeds) and reduces design-time cost from 8,400-12 seconds per design, a 700× speedup. Generated structures are diverse rather than memorized, and morphometric accuracy holds across all seven shape descriptors. Three analyses probe the reliability of these results given the small training corpus. Equivalence testing replaces the earlier argument from non-significant difference tests: the procedural and real descriptor distributions are equivalent at a medium margin of 0.5 standard deviations for all seven descriptors, but the 50 available real reference volumes cannot establish equivalence at a strict 0.3-standard-deviation margin for five of them. A classifier two-sample test shows that generated scaffolds retain a measurable but shrinking signature of the procedural generator. Enlarging the corpus from 250 to 2,050 scaffolds leaves in-distribution accuracy nearly unchanged while reducing the cross-dataset descriptor error on unseen anatomy from 0.079 to 0.058, which localizes the cost of the small corpus in generalization rather than in fit. We further illustrate a CT-to-scaffold pipeline for personalized generation. All results are computational; physical, biological, manufacturing, and regulatory validation remain future work.

abstract: Background Identifying spontaneous abortion (SAB) and induced abortion (IAB) in administrative data compared to other pregnancy outcomes is challenging due to shared billing codes and lack of reimbursement by many insurers. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study using the Merative MarketScan Commercial Database from 2018-2024. We adapted a previously published hierarchical algorithm to reduce the number of unknown or ambiguous pregnancy outcomes. We then tested the assumptions of the hierarchy by alternating the order of the diagnosis, procedural, and diagnosis-related group (DRG) codes within the algorithm for SAB and IAB. Results Our dataset included 2,418,986 pregnancy episodes. Our modified algorithm improved the sensitivity for SAB, identifying a 17.5% incidence compared to 14.9% for previously published algorithms and reduced unclassified outcomes from 17.4% to 13.4%. Prioritizing IAB in the algorithm hierarchy over SAB identified an additional 8,623 IAB cases. However, IAB identification remained low at less than 5% of pregnancy episodes. Conclusions Following the Dobbs decision, it is critical that researchers accurately identify early pregnancy claims and remain transparent in their methodology. Our algorithm improved sensitivity for SAB and reduced unknown outcomes. However, claims-based analyses may systematically undercount IAB, with implications for research-informed reproductive health policy.

abstract: Background Sign Language (SL) is essential for Deaf communities, yet limited SL proficiency sustains communication barriers in education and services. We propose an interactive tutoring system for Ecuadorian Sign Language (EcSL) that combines real-time, vision-based gesture assessment with an embodied "reward" delivered by a robotic arm, using fruit vocabulary as an initial learning domain. Methods We will conduct a two-arm randomized controlled experimental design, pretest-posttest control-group study with individual random assignment. About 70 university students without formal EcSL training will learn EcSL fruit signs through video and sign recognition feedback module. The system uses a webcam, MediaPipe landmark extraction, and a landmark-based fusion classifier that combines a local bidirectional LSTM with a transferred ST-GCN motion encoder; modules communicate via Robot Operating System (ROS). Outcomes. A total of six dependent variables will be assessed in both the experimental and control groups: (a) handshape, (b) palm orientation, (c) location, (d) movement, (e) non-manual signals and expressions, and (f) global coordination. Analyses will use descriptive statistics, reliability checks when applicable, and a mixed repeated-measures MANOVA. Discussion By coupling immediate feedback with embodied reinforcement, delivered through a robotic arm, the platform aims to support early sign accuracy and provide a motivating practice environment for learners. The robotic arm responds to participants' performance with physical rewards, thereby reinforcing correct execution through tangible, real-time stimuli. Results will guide improvements in robustness and inform extensions to broader vocabularies and deployment in educational contexts.

abstract: Female breast cancer presents high incidence and mortality rates and is considered a significant public health problem. The timeliness of oncological treatment is a fundamental factor in the prognosis and survival of patients. The objective of this study was to analyze the spatial distribution pattern of the percentage of women who initiated breast cancer treatment within 60 days and its association with socioeconomic indicators and the availability of health services in Brazil. An ecological study was conducted using 133 Intermediate Regions of Urban Articulation (IRUA), based on records from the period 2013-2019. Data on the percentage of treatment initiation within 60 days were obtained from the Hospital Cancer Registry Integrator (IHCR). Socioeconomic variables were collected from the Atlas of Human Development in Brazil and the Institute for Applied Economic Research (IPEA). Data on the availability and density of health professionals and services were obtained from the National Registry of Health Establishments (NRHE) and the Hospital Information System (HIS). The Global Moran's Index and the Local Indicator of Spatial Association (LISA) were used to verify the existence of territorial clusters. Multivariate analysis employed models with global spatial effects. The percentage of breast cancer cases that initiated treatment within 60 days was 48.9% (95% CI: 48.6% - 49.1%), with the highest adherence observed in the IRUA of Cascavel (85%) and the lowest in the IRUA of Rio de Janeiro (16.6%). In the final Spatial Lag Model, positive associations were observed with the density of Family and Community Physicians (β = 0.35; p = 0.007) and the proportion of surgical procedures (β = 0.30; p = 0.001). The analysis indicates that compliance with the 60-day law is related to the structure and organization of health services, highlighting the importance of primary health care as the coordinator of care and the role of surgical capacity in the spatial distribution pattern.

abstract: Bacteria rapidly initiate growth when entering warm-blooded hosts to ensure reproductive success. We investigated the temperature-dependent stimulation of the specific growth rate at the onset of the logarithmic phase (defined as μ at ODratio = 0.2) in Escherichia coli. High-frequency automated monitoring revealed that this stimulation peaks near 37°C and is strain-specific. Comparative analysis between MG1655 and W3110 type A identified the Rac prophage as a primary genomic determinant for this acceleration. However, growth stimulation is uniquely dependent on H-NS, which we redefine as a nucleoid structural organizer. Genetic complementation and comparative analysis of nucleoid-associated proteins (NAPs), and single-cell nucleoid imaging confirmed that H-NS provides a mandatory physical scaffold specifically at host temperatures. We propose that H-NS undergoes a conformational switch to a parallel dimer form around 37°C, enabling the nucleoid to adopt the highly condensed state required for managing replication-transcription conflicts during rapid growth bursts. Notably, while MG1655 relies primarily on H-NS for this stimulation, W3110 type A requires a distributed network of NAPs, including HU and StpA, to maintain its growth velocity. This effect is environment-specific, becoming particularly significant under minimal media conditions where metabolic and structural coordination requirements are more stringent, but less pronounced in nutrient-rich conditions. These findings resolve the silencing paradox: hns-deficient mutants grow slowly at 37°C because they lack the structural infrastructure required to physically coordinate the rapid onset of growth, regardless of the de-repression of growth-promoting genes. We conclude that H-NS-mediated physical organization of the genome is a fundamental prerequisite for temperature-dependent growth adaptation and successful host colonization.

abstract: The multivariate time series collected from numerous sensors exhibit complex interwoven relationships, arising from both the coupling among different components and the temporal dependencies of fluctuations within each component. Disentangling these relationships remains a persistent challenge for the time series community. Existing reconstruction-based methods attempt to unravel the intertwined relationships through sequence decomposition and multi-scale modeling. However, the decomposed components remain mixtures of complex latent factors. Moreover, most methods overlook anomalies present in the training set, which inadvertently causes the model to develop a certain affinity toward anomalous patterns. To address these limitations, we propose TFCdetector. Motivated by the intrinsic properties of anomalies, TFCdetector leverages time-frequency domain analysis to explicitly suppress the model's representation learning of anomalies across diverse granularities and components. To further constrain the model's learning of anomalies, we propose an energy-correlation constraint loss that operates on both segment-level energy and sequence-level correlation. Notably, the adaptively updated memory storage block enhances the expression of normal patterns by leveraging the affinity between normal patterns in the input sequence and the memory storage block. Furthermore, the meticulously designed twin frequency attention enables the model to dynamically select local or global frequency information beneficial for the task. Extensive experiments on 1 synthetic dataset and 7 real-world datasets show that TFCdetector achieves competitive results in multivariate time series detection tasks.The implementation code is available at https://github.com/FanJY3/TFCdetector.

abstract: Background Endothelial dysfunction is a central contributor to the development of diabetic foot complications. However, the regulatory mechanisms underlying impaired vascular endothelial cell (VEC) function in diabetic foot remain incompletely understood. Transient Receptor Potential Melastatin 7 (TRPM7) is implicated in cardiovascular pathology, yet its role in diabetic foot-related endothelial impairment is unclear. Methods Primary VECs were isolated from foot vascular tissues obtained from control participants and patients with DFUs and identified by CD31 and factor VIII immunofluorescence. Proliferation, apoptosis, migration, and in vitro tube formation were quantitatively assessed. TRPM7 was overexpressed in control-derived VECs and knocked down using shRNA in DFU-derived VECs. TRPM7 expression and VEGFA-AKT-ERK-related proteins were evaluated using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) concentrations in conditioned culture supernatants were measured by ELISA. Results Compared with control-derived VECs, DFU-derived VECs exhibited reduced proliferation, migration, and tube formation, together with increased apoptosis and elevated conditioned-supernatant AGE and iNOS protein concentrations. TRPM7 expression was higher in DFU-derived VECs. TRPM7 overexpression in control-derived VECs induced a dysfunctional cellular phenotype, whereas TRPM7 knockdown in DFU-derived VECs partially restored proliferation, migration, and tube formation and reduced apoptosis. TRPM7 manipulation was also accompanied by changes in VEGFA expression and AKT and ERK phosphorylation, indicating an association between TRPM7 status and dysregulated VEGFA-AKT-ERK-related signaling. Conclusion In primary human VEC cultures, increased TRPM7 expression was associated with impaired endothelial proliferation, migration, and tube formation and with altered VEGFA-related AKT/ERK signaling. This supporting TRPM7 as a candidate regulator of endothelial dysfunction under diabetic-foot-related conditions.

abstract: The proliferation of targeted media platforms enables firms to deliver tailored advertising to specific consumer segments, yet the heterogeneous influences of pre-purchase information search and post-purchase sharing on targeted advertising performance remain underexplored in extant research. This paper constructs a two-period symmetric duopoly game model with fully rational firms and consumers to analyze theoretical associations between two distinct consumer information behaviors and firms' equilibrium advertising and profit outcomes. We set homogeneous products, symmetric competitors, and two types of consumers (loyal buyers and comparison shoppers) to explore the strategic interplay of corporate advertising, pricing and consumer information activities. This model adopts a differentiated search cost framework: digital information access incurs zero monetary expenses, yet endogenous cognitive information overload creates non-negligible mental frictions. Search intensity s is the consumer's generic choice variable; s* denotes the endogenous equilibrium search intensity solved from consumer utility maximization (not an exogenous primitive parameter), which lies within interior range (0,1) rather than corner solution s=1. Experience‑sharing intensity e is treated as an exogenous symmetric parameter for analytical tractability. Model-derived predictions are summarized as follows: (1) Consumer information search acts as a complementary force for targeted ads by lowering information frictions, lifting conversion rates and raising equilibrium profitability within valid parameter ranges; (2)Experience sharing generates dual competitive effects: moderate peer reviews expand market awareness, while excessive price-related sharing intensifies cross-brand price rivalry and suppress firm returns; (3) The joint interaction of search and sharing shapes equilibrium advertising intensity: optimal ad spending falls as primitive cognitive‑friction parameters shift to raise endogenous equilibrium search intensity s*, and firms need context-dependent strategies to cope with consumer sharing. Theoretically, this work unifies pre-purchase search and post-purchase sharing into a single dynamic duopoly framework to fill research gaps that separate the two consumer behaviors. Practically, the model provides neutral theoretical insights; tentative suggestions for advertising‑message content represent directions for future empirical testing rather than formal model outputs. All theoretical conclusions derived in this paper hold only within the feasible interior-equilibrium parameter domain defined in Text S2.9. Numerical simulation figures serve purely as numerically illustrated examples; formal mathematical proofs are provided in the appendices. All conclusions are mathematical predictions derived under preset model assumptions, rather than empirically validated causal relationships.

abstract: Foraging under threat of predation is a paradigmatic scenario involving the interplay between approach and avoidance motivation across species. Previous foraging paradigms in humans have revealed aspects of approach-avoidance behavior and its neural underpinnings, but have generally involved simple choices such as a binary decision to stay or flee. Here, we present results from 40 adult participants who completed the Weighing Opportunity and Loss in Foraging (WOLF) task, a novel two-dimensional foraging context with threat of predation in which participants choose from five possible actions at each turn. We fit computational models in which choices depend on the subjective utility of each option, which itself depends on approach motivation (resource richness) and avoidance motivation (predator distance). Model comparison revealed that an inverse power law model, in which the marginal subjective utility of additional distance from the wolf diminished with wolf distance, outperformed a linear model. Model parameters explained more than 75% of the variance in task performance, mediated by the average resource richness of choices (for the approach-related parameter) and the number of deaths on the task (for the avoidance-related parameters). An exploratory analysis found that self-reported anxious arousal was associated with a more linear relationship between wolf distance and avoidance motivation. The results demonstrate that a behaviorally rich foraging paradigm in which participants select from multiple options at each turn can enable explicit modeling of subjective utilities in the interplay between approach and avoidance motivation. Future work can examine neural underpinnings of complex approach-avoidance behavior and their alteration in mental health disorders.

abstract: The morphology of the rectus abdominis muscle is closely related to its biomechanical functions in trunk stabilization and breathing across different activities. However, the three-dimensional morphological characteristics of this muscle remain poorly documented in vivo. Therefore, the present observational cross-sectional study aims to evaluate how size, sex and running discipline influence the 3D shape of this muscle, hypothesising that there are allometric effects, sexual dimorphism effects and that the explosive demands of sprinting require a more specialised morphology than endurance running. This work models the in vivo shape of this muscle at rest in a sample of athletes specialised in endurance running or sprinting. The rectus abdominis muscles were measured directly from CT scan slices, and 3D geometrical models of the muscle were created from the triangulation of 3D coordinates. The shape of the muscle was studied through 3D geometric morphometric analyses. The study revealed the significant effect of sex and running discipline in the 3D shape of the rectus abdominis. The results highlight distinct morphological features in males and females and in sprinters and endurance runners. Males show a more triangularly shaped rectus abdominis (wider in its superior part) compared to females, who show a more rectangular muscle. Similarly, sprinters show thicker and more rectangular muscles, compared to endurance runners. These findings suggest that the functional anatomy of the rectus abdominis muscle could differ depending on sex and running discipline, pointing to potential differences in biomechanics and respiratory performance. This novel approach opens the door to further exploration of in vivo muscle morphology and its implications in physiology applied not only to sports science, but also in clinical settings.

abstract: Evolution occurs in populations of reproducing individuals. In stochastic descriptions of evolutionary dynamics, such as the Moran process, individuals are chosen randomly for birth and for death. If the same type is chosen for both steps, then the reproductive event is wasted, because the composition of the population remains unchanged. Here we introduce a new phenotype, which we call a replacer. Replacers are efficient competitors. When a replacer is chosen for reproduction, the offspring will always replace an individual of another type (if available). We determine the selective advantage of replacers in well-mixed populations and on one-dimensional lattices. We find that being a replacer substantially boosts the fixation probability of neutral and deleterious mutants. In particular, fixation probability of a single neutral replacer who invades a well-mixed population of size N is of the order of 1/N rather than the standard 1/N. Even more importantly, replacers are much better protected against invasions once they have reached fixation. Therefore, replacers dominate the mutation selection equilibrium even if the phenotype of being a replacer comes at a substantial cost: curiously, for large population sizes and small mutation rates, the relative reproductive rate of a successful replacer can be as low as 1/e.

abstract: In the post-pandemic period, telemedicine services are a new addition to health sectors that facilitate bridging the gap for patients in rural and marginalized areas. The study aims to comprehend the different influential factors associated with adopting telemedicine services in Bangladesh. The study developed several hypotheses from two technology acceptance models, including the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). An explanatory research design was followed using a quantitative approach. The study developed a semi-structured questionnaire to collect primary data. It used Partial Least Squares-Structure Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to identify influential factors in adopting telemedicine services in Bangladesh. Key findings indicate that trust (β = 0.469, p < 0.001) and perceived usefulness (β = 0.418, p < 0.001) are the strongest predictors of behavioral intention to use telemedicine. Perceived ease of use (β = 0.325, p < 0.05) also significantly was associated with resistance to use, emphasizing the importance of user-friendly interfaces. However, resistance to use didn't find any significant relationship with behavioral intention (β = 0.046, p > 0.05), suggesting that the urgency created by the COVID-19 pandemic may have overridden previous resistance to telemedicine. The study also highlights the negative influence of perceived risk (β = 0.286, p < 0.05) and technology anxiety (β = 0.242, p < 0.05) on resistance to use, pointing to concerns about data security and digital literacy. Surprisingly, social influence (p > 0.05) and facilitating conditions (p > 0.05) were not found to have a significant impact on resistance to use. This research underscores the importance of addressing security concerns, improving digital literacy, and enhancing the user-friendliness of telemedicine platforms to promote widespread adoption from the implication perspective. These insights are critical for policymakers and healthcare providers aiming to take immediate policy-level initiatives expanding telemedicine services in Bangladesh.

abstract: Purpose Firearm access in dementia caregiving households poses safety risks. This study examines household firearm ownership and storage practices among dementia caregivers, identifying factors associated with unsafe firearm storage. Methods We analyzed pooled data from 2017, 2021, 2022, and 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS). Weighted logistic regression assessed associations between caregiver characteristics and firearm storage behaviors (unloaded vs. loaded, locked vs. unlocked). Results Dementia caregivers were more likely to live in firearm-owning households than non-caregivers (40.57% vs. 35.12%). Among caregivers in firearm-owning households, 35.8% reported loaded storage, and 50.8% of those also reported unlocked storage. Older caregivers are more likely to report unlocked firearm storage (50-64 years: OR=3.74, 95%CI: 1.75-8.01; 65 + years: OR=5.39, 95%CI: 2.02-14.40; reference: < 50 years). Male caregivers had higher odds of reporting a loaded firearm in the household (OR=1.98, 95% CI: 1.32-2.96). In contrast, longer caregiving duration (>5 years: OR=0.36, 95%CI: 0.16-0.78) and assisting with household tasks (OR=0.27, 95%CI: 0.11-0.63) were associated with safer storage, though this protective effect was only observed among younger caregivers. Conclusion Household firearm storage patterns among dementia caregivers varied by caregiver age, sex, and caregiving context, highlighting the need for tailored firearm-safety counseling and caregiver-focused public health strategies.

abstract: This study examines the association between book-tax differences (BTDs), sales decline, and earnings persistence among non-financial listed firms in Vietnam. Adopting a conditional perspective, the study treats BTDs as observable signals of accounting-tax divergence, reporting environments, and transitory earnings components, while sales decline is conceptualized as an adverse operating state that may weaken the association between current and future earnings. Using a balanced panel of 325 firms from 2013 to 2023, comprising 3,575 firm-year observations, earnings persistence is measured through the association between current and one-year-ahead pre-tax book income. Earnings are further decomposed into operating cash flows and accruals to examine component-level persistence. The empirical analysis uses OLS regressions with industry and year fixed effects and firm-clustered standard errors. Additional analyses control for earnings management and tax avoidance and test the robustness of the findings using a continuous measure of sales decline, a sample excluding the COVID-19 period, and an alternative annual-decile classification of large BTDs. The results show that pre-tax book income is persistent, but its persistence is significantly lower during periods of sales decline. The evidence for BTDs is asymmetric: large positive BTDs are more consistently associated with lower earnings persistence, whereas the evidence for large negative BTDs varies across model specifications and earnings components. The three-way interactions among sales decline, BTD classifications, and current earnings are not statistically significant in the main analyses, indicating that the evidence does not support a broad BTD-specific amplification mechanism. Overall, the findings suggest that earnings persistence is shaped by earnings components, accounting-tax reporting signals, and operating conditions. The study highlights the importance of interpreting BTDs jointly with sales trends and earnings components in the Vietnamese institutional setting.

abstract: Hugging is a ubiquitous form of social touch, yet little is known about how individual differences shape the remembrance of such experiences. In a large-scale survey (N = 15,049), we investigated whether various traits predict the likelihood of recalling a hug for its positive emotional impact and the reasons why it was remembered. Participants were recruited through promotion on public broadcasting programs (BBC) and other media. Overall, 69.5% of participants reported recalling a hug for its positive emotional impact. In regression analyses, empathy, body perception, and attachment-related anxiety were associated with a higher likelihood of such recall, whereas attachment-related avoidance was associated with a lower likelihood. Men were more likely than women to report physically arousing hugs as the most memorable. These findings suggest that hugs are predominantly remembered because they convey comfort, support, and understanding, and that individual differences shape autobiographical memories of hugging.

abstract: Dlx genes have fundamental roles in the generation, differentiation, and functions of virtually all forebrain GABAergic neurons. Here we used scRNA-Seq to identify genes that are dysregulated in Dlx1/2 conditional mutants in mouse immature CGE- and MGE-derived cortical and olfactory bulb GABAergic interneurons. Dlx1/2 -regulated genes included Cxcl14 and Nr2f2 that are important for cortical interneuron (CIN) survival. We also identified DLX2-bound putative regulatory elements (pREs) of these Dlx -regulated genes. Within the Dlx -expressing lineage, some DLX-bound pREs were specific to CINs, others appeared to be constitutively bound; the latter class having activity in mature CINs. One such pRE and its associated gene, Cxcl14 , is strongly activated by Dlx1/2 and is essential for synaptogenesis onto CINs.

abstract: Pancreatic cancer remains one of the most lethal malignancies, largely due to the lack of reliable biomarkers for early detection. Aberrant glycosylation presents a promising source of diagnostic signatures, yet polysialic acid (polySia), a distinctive glycan, has remained underexplored, primarily owing to limitations in detection methods and recognition tools. Here, we report the development of a polySia "superbinder," a nanoscale molecularly imprinted polymer (nanoMIP) that exhibits superior specificity and affinity for polySia over monoclonal antibodies, enabling precise recognition and quantification of this glycan. Leveraging this superbinder, we uncover a previously unrecognized association between polySia and pancreatic cancer and establish polysialylated CD56 (polySia-CD56) as a specific and robust biomarker. PolySia-CD56 outperforms multiple previously reported pancreatic cancer biomarkers, including the clinical standard carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9). Notably, its expression pattern is complementary to that of CA19-9, and the combined use of both biomarkers significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy to 94.1%, effectively addressing the limitation of CA19-9 in detecting CA19-9-negative patients. Together, this study not only identifies polySia-CD56 as a precise biomarker for pancreatic cancer but also highlights the potential of antiglycan nanoMIPs as transformative reagents for decoding glycosylated targets and advancing clinical translation.

abstract: Wearable microneedle sensors analyze biomarkers in situ from interstitial fluids (ISF), enabling minimally invasive, precise, and continuous monitoring of metabolic diseases. However, conventional designs either lack adequate conformability to skin or suffer from electrode fractures during skin penetration and body motion, leading to signal instability that undermines reliable multiparameter acquisition. Here, we present a fully integrated system with a soft microneedle sensor array featuring nano-hill topographies on strain-resilient electrodes to delocalize strain via geometric confinement. This design reduces signal variability by 14-fold compared to conventional designs, enabling stable, simultaneous in situ monitoring of multiple ISF biomarkers. It achieves clinical-grade accuracy for continuous glucose monitoring (mean absolute relative difference of 10.8%) and captures dynamic synchronized variations in glucose, local tissue pH, and temperature in a living subject in real time. The system integrates a reusable electronic module with a disposable microneedle array with a sensor footprint of just 1.8 cm 2 . By combining high signal stability with multiparameter synchrony in a compact form factor, this system offers a practical solution for reliable, real-time ISF analysis under dynamic in vivo conditions.

abstract: The ongoing emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants in an increasingly immune-experienced population is largely enabled by the plasticity of the Spike protein, which lies at the frontline of host immune pressure. Here, we investigated how extensive remodeling of the N-terminal domain (NTD) in Spike influences its antigenic properties. Using BA.2.87.1, a variant heavily mutated in this domain, we found that even large deletions do not substantially disrupt overall Spike structure or pseudovirus infectivity. However, our structural and binding analyses revealed that the NTD exhibits increased flexibility and that interaction with a heme-metabolite, known to facilitate the exposure of an immunodominant epitope, is lost. These conformational effects, coupled with 33 NTD mutations, compromised the ability of human convalescent antibodies to engage this domain, contributing to their reduced neutralizing capacity. Consequently, BA.2.87.1-like variants may escape recognition by the preexisting NTD-targeting antibodies, potentially reducing protection. Together, our results highlight the intrinsic adaptability of the Spike beyond the receptor-binding domain, with implications for immune escape during viral evolution.

abstract: Intracellular Ca 2+ signals are essential for many cellular processes but must be tightly regulated to ensure precise spatial and temporal control. The large conductance calcium- and voltage-activated K + channel (BK) integrates intracellular Ca 2+ signaling and membrane depolarization to generate hyperpolarizing K + currents that regulate membrane excitability. In many cell types, BK channels achieve rapid activation through functional coupling with voltage-gated calcium (Ca V ) channels that provide localized Ca 2+ signals. However, the mechanisms that regulate the nanoscale organization of BK+Ca V channel complexes remain poorly understood. Here we investigated whether the BK auxiliary subunit β 4 (BKβ 4 ), which is widely expressed throughout the brain and modulates BK gating properties, influences the spatial organization and functional coupling of BK and Ca V channels. Using proximity ligation assays, electrophysiology, and superresolution stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we show that BKβ 4 promotes BK+Ca V nanodomain organization by increasing channel clustering and altering their spatial proximity at the plasma membrane. These structural changes enhance functional coupling between Ca 2+ influx and BK channel activation. Notably, the effects of BKβ 4 on nanodomain organization and coupling depend on the Ca V subtype involved. Together, our findings reveal that the BKβ 4 auxiliary subunit regulates the nanoscale architecture of BK+Ca V channel complexes and thereby modulates their functional interaction.

abstract: Primary cilia play an essential role in molecular signaling transduction during development, coordinating cell fate decisions and morphogenesis. Defects in components of the primary cilium result in an array of developmental syndromes called ciliopathies. Here we report 24 patients with nine rare and seven novel variants in the primary cilia gene C2CD3, which has previously been implicated in the ciliopathy Orofaciodigital syndrome XIV. Patients displayed an array of dental defects impacting the number, shape, and timing of tooth development. To understand the etiology underlying these defects, murine and avian models were analyzed during embryonic development. Ap2Cre;C2cd3 ex4-5 fl/fl mouse mutants showed a range of dental defects prenatally, mimicking several of the phenotypes observed in patients. Shh was upregulated in the developing upper jaw, leading to a widening of the midline, while Shh expression in the lower jaw was reduced, highlighting the context-dependent impact of cilia on hedgehog signaling. In avian mutants carrying a C2CD3 variant, talpid 2 , tooth buds were evident with SHH expression upregulated during early development in both upper and lower jaws. Cartilage defects were additionally observed in both conditional mouse knockouts and talpid 2 embryos. These changes in Shh signaling provide a mechanism to explain the phenotypes in patients and highlight the conserved role of C2CD3 in coordinating the morphogenetic potential of the jaw and patterning of the forming dentition. Given the conserved phenotypes, alterations in C2CD3-dependent ciliogenesis may have played a role in modulating Shh signaling to alter the timing and position of tooth germs across vertebrate evolution.

abstract: Cooperativity of residue interactions is prevalent in proteins and plays an essential role in protein folding. However, whether cooperativity exists in intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and their assembled biomolecular condensates remains elusive. Here, we reveal the presence of residue interaction cooperativity in various IDP condensates using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations. In all these condensates, cooperative residue interactions manifest as packing between finite residue motifs (3 to 5 residues) with lifetimes three orders of magnitude longer than residue contacts. Notably, these higher-order interactions (HOIs) exhibit a significant nonadditive free energy, which originates from a local low-dielectric environment. The underlying sequence patterns like "Y-X-Q", "D-X-R", and "S-Y-X" are identified. Furthermore, HOIs dominate the cohesive energy of IDPs and condensates can be treated as HOI-crosslinked networks. This model can successfully reproduce experimental results of condensate physical properties, including saturation concentration, viscoelasticity, and interfacial tension.

abstract: TGF-β signaling plays a pivotal role in regulating numerous cellular processes, primarily through the Smad-dependent pathway. Disruptions of the pathway are associated with developmental disorders and life-threatening diseases, such as cancer. It has been reported that TRIM33 inactivates Smad4 signaling and also drives its own signaling responses. However, the mechanism controlling TRIM33 activity has remained unclear. In this study, we identify DCAF6 as a previously unrecognized ubiquitin ligase for TRIM33. DCAF6 targets TRIM33 at Lys850 for ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation, thus abolishing TRIM33-mediated mono-ubiquitination of Smad4. As such, DCAF6 induces dual consequences: it enhances Smad4-dependent transcriptional and growth inhibitory responses, while simultaneously eliminating TRIM33-dependent developmental responses. Conversely, DCAF6 knockout suppresses Smad4-dependent responses while amplifying TRIM33-dependent responses. Therefore, DCAF6 operates as a critical regulator in the balance of TGF-β signaling between the Smad4 and TRIM33 pathways. These insights deepen our understanding of the dynamics and fate control of TGF-β signaling and may open avenues for therapeutic approaches targeting TGF-β in diseases.

abstract: Diverse social, engineered, and biological systems are made up of multiple interacting dynamical components; to work properly, certain components must be carefully regulated so that their dynamics avoid instability. However, many desirable properties, like optimized computation and control, emerge close to the tipping point between stability and instability, i.e., near criticality. Claims that such dynamical systems operate near criticality have been controversial because it is difficult to assess proximity to criticality when control parameters are unknown, hard to manipulate experimentally, and fluctuating in response to changing environmental or internal conditions. Moreover, observations of system dynamics are often limited to time series measurements of one or a few components. Here we develop a temporal renormalization group theory for defining criticality for univariate time series models and an information theoretic definition of proximity to criticality that is independent of model parameterization. We apply this theory to order-n autoregressive models resulting in a data-analytic strategy for time-resolved estimates of proximity to criticality based on measured univariate time series. After benchmarking our approach on diverse ground-truth cases, we apply it to recordings of spiking activity in the mammalian brain. Our estimate of proximity to criticality predicts behavior and suggests that brain dynamics shift closer to criticality during wakefulness and shift away during deep sleep.

abstract: Benthic suspension feeders have long been thought to depend solely on particulate organic matter (POM) for their nutritional needs. Our research, conducted in the Gulf of Aqaba (Red Sea), shows that the available concentration of planktonic carbon in the reef water is too low to meet the metabolic demands (measured through in situ oxygen uptake) of common bivalves ( Spondylus sp. and Chama pacifica ) and ascidians ( Polycarpa mytiligera and Halocynthia spinosa ). In situ measurements confirmed a concentration-dependent uptake of bulk dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and protein-like dissolved organic compounds (fDOM, analyzed via spectrofluorometry) by Spondylus sp. and P. mytiligera , suggesting that DOC uptake may balance their carbon budgets. Stable isotope (δ 13 C) mixing models indicate that reef-derived DOC (mean δ 13 C = -18.4 ± 0.7‰) emerges as the primary carbon source for bivalves (57% of their body composition), far surpassing contributions from particulate sources (26% from POC > 100 µm and 14% from POC < 100 µm). While ascidians still rely primarily on POM (60 to 71%), DOC plays an essential role as a supplementary food source (23 to 29%). These results challenge the prevailing assumption that POM is the exclusive food source for these organisms. Given the widespread presence of bivalves and ascidians in benthic habitats, our findings highlight their ability to bypass the microbial loop and directly utilize dissolved organic compounds, prompting a reevaluation of current benthic carbon budgets.

abstract: The transition of RNA polymerase II from initiation to elongation requires the timely exchange of many factors. Some initiation factors and elongation factors contact the same RNA polymerase II surfaces in an apparently mutually exclusive manner. For example, space occupied by the initiation factor TFIIH and elongation factor Spt4/5 (also known as DSIF) are predicted to overlap. To determine whether Spt4/5 actively displaces TFIIH, or binds only after TFIIH dissociates, labeled yeast nuclear extracts were combined with single-molecule fluorescence microscopy to observe their dynamics in real time. TFIIH categorically dissociates before Spt4/5 arrives, with a clear interval in between when neither factor is present. Therefore, Spt4/5 binding is not required to dissociate TFIIH from RNA polymerase II.

abstract: Environmental diagnosis of schistosomiasis, a disease affecting over 250 million people globally, remains challenging, thereby limiting efficient eradication efforts. Current methods, including environmental DNA (eDNA), cannot distinguish between infectious parasite life stages present in the environment. Here, we develop and validate an environmental RNA (eRNA) approach that enables detection and quantification of Schistosoma mansoni miracidia (infective to snails) and cercariae (infective to humans) directly from water samples. We identified life stage-specific transcripts and designed ddPCR assays highly specific to S. mansoni and each life stage. Laboratory experiments demonstrate that stage-specific eRNA assays accurately detect and quantify the relative abundance of each life stage. While eRNA and eDNA assays showed similar analytical limits of detection (LOD), eRNA provided enhanced organism-level detectability due to higher target molecule availability per life stage, also resulting in longer signal persistence in water that may facilitate the detection of the highly transient free-living stages of S. mansoni in the environment, especially cercariae. Field validation at six endemic sites in Brazil confirms that eRNA outperforms eDNA and conventional snail surveys in detecting S. mansoni cercariae indicating local transmission risk to humans. By enabling living stage discrimination and improving detectability compared to eDNA, our study advances both fundamental understanding and environmental surveillance of schistosomiasis transmission, supporting elimination initiatives in affected regions.

abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is associated with an increase in hippocampal neurogenesis and memory benefits, but the causal mechanism is unclear. Here, we use a mouse model of Rett syndrome, a severe learning disability syndrome caused by MECP2 loss of function, to find that DBS promotes the maturation and integration of newborn dentate granule cells (DGCs) into the neural circuit. Suppressing hippocampal neurogenesis prevented DBS from improving learning and memory. Newborn methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MeCP2)-deficient DGCs in Rett syndrome mice showed attenuated development and synaptic dysfunction, but DBS rescued DGC dendritic arborization, synaptogenesis, and long-term synaptic plasticity. DBS achieves this, at least in part, by increasing the protein level and shifting the phosphorylation of potassium chloride cotransporter 2, thereby restoring the conversion of GABAergic signaling from depolarization to hyperpolarization, a process that is otherwise delayed by MeCP2 deficiency. This study pinpoints one mechanism by which chronic DBS promotes neuronal maturation and enhances memory.

abstract: The atypical cyclin-dependent kinase subfamily (CDK14-18) encompasses five related proteins with unclear function, and for which individual depletion has not demonstrated sustained therapeutic relevance. We report here that CDK16 and CDK18 compensate each other and liver cancer cells are sensitive to the concomitant inactivation of both kinases, resulting in persistent defects in DNA repair and subsequent cell death. These effects are linked to a role of CDK16/18 in regulating nucleocytoplasmatic transport through phosphorylation of nuclear pore complex components, including NUP35. Genetic ablation of Cdk16 and Cdk18 in established liver tumors driven by MYC and beta-catenin oncogenes triggers DNA damage in cancer cells without affecting adjacent normal tissue, ultimately leading to tumor regression. Collectively, these findings provide a rationale for the development of CDK16-18 inhibitors-likely targeting multiple subfamily members due to their structural similarity-as a strategy against aggressive cancers, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, where effective treatment options remain limited.

abstract: Conventional whole tumor cell cancer vaccines have demonstrated limited clinical success due to insufficient immunogenicity and challenges in adjuvant codelivery, despite their rich antigen repertoire and high patient-specific activity. Here, we introduce a simple, single-step approach to load immunostimulatory CpG oligodeoxynucleotides into tumor cells undergoing immunogenic cell death using an ionic liquid-containing cocktail. Results indicate that these adjuvant-loaded tumor cells (referred to as IL-Vax) enhance the uptake of cell-based vaccines by dendritic cells and their subsequent activation, leading to potent antitumor immunity. IL-Vax offered strong protection against tumor growth in a prophylactic B16F10 melanoma mouse model. Furthermore, IL-Vax synergized with PD-1 blockade to slow tumor growth and extend survival in a therapeutic model. The modularity of IL-Vax enables the loading of different cargos or cargo combinations, which may be conducive for additional tailoring of such vaccines and potentially other cell loading applications.

abstract: Unlike dissolved inorganic nitrogen, which is scarce in much of the tropical, subtropical, and temperate surface ocean, dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) has significant concentrations and gradients. Accordingly, the lateral transport of DON may fuel biological productivity in nutrient-depleted low-latitude surface waters. Here, we report measurements of the concentration and 15 N/ 14 N ratio (δ 15 N) of DON in surface waters over the Pacific and Atlantic basins. DON concentration is generally highest in subpolar and equatorial waters, with minima in the subtropical gyres. A δ 15 N correlation is observed between surface DON and the nitrate consumed in the surface waters, indicating in situ DON production and consumption. Samples with lower DON concentrations tend to have anomalously high DON δ 15 N, confirming net DON transport to, and consumption in, the subtropical gyres. Net local DON production or consumption appears to dominate the observed spatial variation in the DON-to-subsurface nitrate δ 15 N difference. For example, N 2 fixation tends to lower the δ 15 N of surface DON relative to subsurface nitrate mostly through encouraging DON accumulation rather than by the specific δ 15 N of the nitrogen introduced by N 2 fixation. Unique conditions appear to apply in the equatorial Atlantic, where despite high productivity, a local minimum in DON concentration and a slight elevation in DON δ 15 N suggest net DON degradation. In this phosphorus-rich, nitrogen-poor upwelling environment where low iron may restrict N 2 fixation, net decomposition of DON may supply needed recycled nitrogen to the ecosystem.

abstract: Histone posttranslational modifications, particularly lysine acetylation (Kac), are critical epigenetic regulators of transcriptional programs underlying long-term memory consolidation. Beyond Kac, several other non-acetyl acylations have been identified with the ability to regulate transcription; however, their role in memory consolidation remains unknown. Here, we identify histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a molecular switch for long-term memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. We find that spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions. Through genetic manipulations, we show that reducing hippocampal Kcr levels impairs memory, while increasing Kcr levels by means of crotonate administration enhances long-term memory. Single-nuclei transcriptome and chromatin accessibility analyses reveal that crotonate facilitates activation of genes regulating glutamate signaling. Cell-cell communication analysis further suggests a strengthening of glutamatergic signaling within hippocampal excitatory neurons following crotonate administration. Real-time fluorescence imaging with genetically encoded sensors functionally validates our multiomics and computational findings-demonstrating the role of Kcr in regulating presynaptic glutamate release and neuronal activity. In summary, our findings elucidate a key mechanism underlying long-term memory consolidation and excitatory neurotransmission, linking epigenetic events to synaptic function and behavior.

abstract: Human social networks involve multiple kinds of relationships-such as friendship, health support, and economic exchange-that serve different functions and compete for limited time and resources. Here, we deploy a compositional framework to infer functional roles in directed multiplex networks. We distinguish outgoing ties that reflect social behavior of individuals' allocation of social effort from incoming ties that capture structural dependence, or social appeal. The method accounts for heterogeneity in individual activity levels and layer density across relational domains. Applying this approach to multiplex sociocentric network data from 23,378 individuals across 176 rural Honduran villages, we uncover well-defined role structures spanning friendship, health-related support, and economic interactions. We find a pronounced asymmetry: behavioral (outgoing) roles exhibit weaker demographic association but stronger geographic organization than incoming roles. This is consistent with shared local environments at the village-wide level shaping social action. In contrast, structural (incoming) roles show more pronounced life-course transitions and socioeconomic differentiation, with little geographic association. Taken together, these patterns reveal a systematic difference in how social behavior and social appeal are organized in multiplex social systems. This approach illustrates a general framework for studying social roles, inequality, and life-course dynamics in complex social systems.

abstract: Fasting-based interventions improve metabolic health and are also explored as adjuncts in other clinical settings, but hunger remains a barrier to adherence. Fasting activates AgRP/NPY neurons (ANs), a hunger-promoting population whose inhibition reduces eating in hungry animals. Here we identify hypocretin/orexin neurons (HONs), classically associated with arousal, as rapid suppressors of AN activity. HON ablation increased AN population activity, whereas HON optostimulation rapidly suppressed it. Combined recordings of AN activity and pupil size-a direct arousal metric not previously linked to AN dynamics-revealed that HONs contributed to pupil dilation-associated AN suppression. In fasted mice, sensory stimulation rapidly recruited this pupil-HON pathway, and suppressed AN activity and eating. These findings reveal an arousal-hunger pathway through which self-initiated pupil dilations, or dilations driven by salient environmental events, interrupt fasting-induced hunger signals. They also suggest a framework for noninvasive, sensory-, and pupillometry-guided approaches to hunger control during fasting.
