abstract: Understanding how the heterogeneous activity patterns of individual neurons give rise to coherent population dynamics and cognition is a central challenge in neuroscience. In the hippocampus, neurons are tuned to spatial location, yet their activity is also modulated by multiple external and internal variables and appears to drift randomly over time, making it difficult to link hippocampal computations to behavior. By analyzing hippocampal population dynamics in behaving mice, we reveal a structured organization underlying the diversity of single-neuron responses—the hippocampus encodes different aspects of experience as disentangled variables represented in the co-activity dynamics of cell assemblies. The temporal and contextual components of these representations are governed by local inhibitory interactions and input-driven cell–assembly dynamics, respectively. Our findings reveal the circuit basis of disentangled hippocampal representations, offering a unifying geometric principle of population coding that supports flexible memory representations and enables rapid generalization of prior knowledge to new situations.

abstract: Controlling whether an experience is encoded into long-term memory and thus later remembered is a crucial aspect of memory. Here we examined single-neuron activity in the human brain while participants formed memories for novel visual stimuli and later retrieved them with confidence ratings. Category-selective amygdala neurons exhibited elevated firing during encoding of later remembered items relative to later forgotten items. This effect was predictive of the episodic aspect of the memory, was restricted to the preferred category of each cell, emerged earlier and was stronger in the amygdala compared to the hippocampus, and did not depend on stimulus valence and arousal. Successful memory formation was accompanied by enhanced spike-field coherence between the activity of amygdala category cells and hippocampal field potentials. These findings demonstrate that stimulus-specific recruitment of the amygdala predicts memory formation and suggest category cells in the right amygdala as a target for interventions to treat disorders affecting episodic memory in humans.

abstract: Recent studies have identified bi-directional communication between neurons and glioma tumors as a key driver of hyperexcitability and malignant progression. Although much of this work has focused on the activity of excitatory neurons, the roles of inhibitory neurons remain poorly defined. Using in vivo screening approaches in autochthonous glioma models, we found that the loss of a γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transporter (Slc6a1) enhanced glioma progression, promoted network hyperactivity, and influenced tonic GABA release by tumors. Mechanistically, we show that glioma tumors influence the activity of inhibitory neurons and that their subsequent stimulation suppresses tumor growth. Further screening of these phenomena identified diazepam binding inhibitor (DBI), a secreted negative allosteric modulator of GABA-A, as a link between glioma-related hyperexcitability and proliferation that functions through modulating inhibitory neuronal signaling. Collectively, our findings indicate that glioma tumors utilize multiple mechanisms to manipulate the activity of inhibitory neurons as a means to drive network hyperactivity, which ultimately facilitates malignant progression.

abstract: Although tau pathology correlates with cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD), some individuals exhibit resilience by maintaining cognitive function. The mechanisms enabling this protection, particularly before widespread cortical degeneration occurs, remain elusive. Here, we identify a dynamic interplay between cellular vulnerability and circuit-level resilience that shapes cognitive outcomes in AD. Tau accumulation in the Edinger-Westphal nucleus (EW) impairs attention by inducing hypoexcitability in CART + neurons via Kcnma1 upregulation, a vulnerability predictive of future decline in both 3×Tg-AD mice and AD patients. Conversely, a subset of AD mice with heightened exploratory behavior activates a compensatory medial parabrachial (mPB)-EW circuit, mediated by substance P-Tacr1 signaling, which sustains CART + neuron function and delays cognitive deterioration. These findings reveal resilience as an active state enabled by trait-linked circuit plasticity that balances cellular vulnerability, defining multilevel targets for early intervention.

abstract: Objectives Sleep loss is a common experience amongst first-time parents and can result in postpartum fatigue. There is a lack of research on first-time parents' lived experiences of sleep and sleep loss, and its associated effects on mental health, parental relationships, and overall wellbeing as new parents. We examined first-time parents' perceptions, experiences and attitudes to sleep loss, tiredness and wellbeing during the first six months postpartum in Ireland. Methods One-to-one semi-structured interviews were conducted with fourteen first-time parents (female n = 10, male n = 4) from October to December 2025. The interviews took place online. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings Four themes were identified: 1) the gendered experience of sleep as a new parent, 2) (in)ability to sleep, 3) postpartum wellbeing struggles and 4) resilience and adapting. These themes highlighted how first-time parents navigate their sleep in their new role as a mother or father, their difficulty getting adequate sleep, complex wellbeing struggles as a result of sleep loss, and the discovery of new ways to function when dealing with sleep loss in the postpartum period. Conclusions These findings highlight the need for healthcare professionals to recognise postpartum sleep loss as both a physiological and psychological experience, and to incorporate holistic, routine discussions of sleep into postnatal care.

abstract: To address the challenges of small object detection in remote sensing images, such as susceptibility to background noise and difficulties in feature extraction, this paper proposes a method for detecting small objects in remote sensing images based on feature enhancement and scale-adaptive optimization under complex scenarios. First, we constructed a bidirectional complementary feature fusion network, employing a bidirectional feature fusion mechanism to enhance the interaction between shallow-level details and deep-level semantic features, thereby enabling more effective multi-scale feature fusion. Second, we developed a Multi-scale Local-Global Attention (MLGA) module that uses multi-scale pooling to capture both local details and global context, and employs dynamic weights for adaptive feature fusion, effectively suppressing background noise and highlighting the features of small objects. In addition, we designed a scale-adaptive bounding box regression loss function (SAWIoU) that addresses the scale bias issue for small objects by introducing a scale scaling factor, thereby ensuring balanced optimization across objects of different scales and further improving localization accuracy. Finally, experimental results on two public remote sensing datasets DIOR and RSOD show that the proposed method achieved mAP50 scores of 0.885 and 0.971, respectively, significantly outperforming current mainstream detection models, with particularly notable improvements in small-object detection accuracy. Additionally, ablation studies further validate the effectiveness and robustness of this method in detecting small objects in remote sensing under complex backgrounds.

abstract: Lithology identification is vital for improving geological exploration accuracy, optimizing petroleum exploration schemes, and ensuring construction engineering safety. Traditional identification methods suffer from low efficiency, high cost, and heavy dependence on domain expertise. This study proposes a lithology identification approach based on the ResNet18 backbone, in which five lightweight attention mechanisms, namely CBAM, channel-only attention, ECA, SE, and spatial-only attention, are systematically compared, and the best-performing CBAM module is embedded to strengthen feature extraction and discrimination capacity. The Open-Source Computer Vision (OpenCV) library is adopted for dataset preprocessing, where raw images are converted to grayscale to suppress interference from irrelevant information. Comparative experiments demonstrate that CBAM outperforms the other evaluated attention modules and is therefore incorporated into the final network architecture. A hyperparameter sensitivity analysis of the CBAM-based model demonstrates that the model performance varies with different combinations of learning rate and batch size. When trained with a learning rate of 0.0001 and a batch size of 16, the model achieves a lithology identification accuracy of 86.36%, substantially improving overall recognition performance. By integrating CBAM into ResNet18, the proposed method enables accurate recognition to support multi-field engineering applications, reduce risks, and promote intelligent precision.

abstract: Reproductive longevity decline characterizes both natural aging and premature ovarian insufficiency (POI). While our previous work established C. elegans LMD-3 as a critical regulator of reproductive capacity, the in vivo consequences of specific clinical mutations remain unclear. Here, we modeled the POI-associated human NCOA7 W804C mutation by engineering the orthologous W690C substitution into the C. elegans lmd-3 locus. We demonstrate that this single-nucleotide substitution severely compromises LMD-3 protein stability and reduces transcript levels. This mutational destabilization is associated with profound systemic autophagic-lysosomal dysfunction, which impairs macromolecular degradation and leads to widespread proteotoxic accumulation of misfolded proteins. Coincident with these organismal defects, mutant animals exhibit an early-onset collapse in reproductive capacity driven by elevated germline apoptosis. Crucially, this pathology is consistent with reduced vitamin B12 availability; mecobalamin supplementation can mitigate the lysosomal block, restoring autophagic flux, proteostasis, and fecundity. These findings elucidate how a clinical mutation drives systemic lysosomal failure and reproductive decline, suggesting vitamin B12 supplementation as a promising metabolic intervention worth further translational exploration.

abstract: The number of people living with dementia and related costs continue to grow worldwide. Although generally associated with memory difficulties, non-cognitive symptoms of dementia are common and usually stem from unmet needs. Evidence emerging suggests that social prescribing improves the wellbeing of people living with dementia. This study explored adaptations to key elements of social prescribing for people living with dementia, as well as barriers to and enablers of positive experiences among people living with dementia and service providers. The qualitative study engaged people living with dementia (n = 8), carers (n = 9) and service providers (n = 17) involved in social prescribing through primary care. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, and the essential ingredients of social prescribing schemes comprised the initial organising categories for template analysis. The final template included four integrative themes: unique challenges of dementia; interpretations of the social prescribing role; integration of social prescribing into dementia care; and evaluation, improvement and sustainability. Positive workplace cultures and skills in dementia care and support enabled multidisciplinary collaborations and the successful adaptations of the generic social prescribing model to improve the experiences among people living with dementia and service providers. Resistance to and confusion about the social prescribing link workers' role, and inappropriate referrals were barriers to positive experiences and bottom-up feedback. Primary care networks' agreements on core outcomes within proactive systems of dementia care and support may promote meaningful bottom-up feedback on the effectiveness of social prescribing for people living with dementia, guiding service improvements.

abstract: An increasing body of evidence indicates that systemic changes to the food system are necessary to mitigate ongoing environmental degradation. The adoption of sustainable dietary practices is an actionable individual-level strategy that may benefit both human health and environmental sustainability. This paper aimed to explore the barriers and facilitators to adopting a sustainable diet among adolescents in Ireland. The data from this research seeks to clarify the steps needed to support this dietary transition. Data were collected from four sites, involving 48 participants aged 15-17 years in seven semi-structured focus groups. Non-probability convenience sampling was employed. Transcripts were audio-recorded, transcribed, and inductively coded to identify barriers and facilitators, which were then deductively mapped onto the Theoretical Domains Framework and presented on the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation - Behaviour model. Barriers (n = 33) were more frequent than facilitators (n = 8) in the adoption of a sustainable diet. Prominent barriers to adopting a sustainable diet included a lack of knowledge about the characteristics of a sustainable diet, a current diet that does not align with a sustainable diet, a lack of practical skills for preparing a sustainable diet, unaccommodating school canteens, and cultural influences such as a strong attachment to meat. Facilitators to the adoption of a sustainable diet were the view that this diet promotes human health, and the acknowledgement of the changes required to make their diet more sustainable. However, although participants could identify changes to make their diets more sustainable, most were unwilling to transition at present. This research is important because it provides insights into the design of future interventions using the Behaviour Change Wheel intervention framework to facilitate behaviour change to support adolescents' transition to a sustainable diet.

abstract: As a core component of intelligent transportation systems, the security authentication and privacy protection mechanisms in Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) are of paramount importance. To address key security issues in VANETs, such as the vulnerability of identity privacy to leakage, the complexity of certificate management, the high risk of key escrow, and the challenge of balancing authentication efficiency with security, the paper proposes a privacy-preserving identity authentication and key agreement method based on certificateless public key cryptography (CL-PKC) and non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs (NIZK). This method utilizes a composite identity identifier and combines it with Pedersen commitments to propose a dynamic anonymous identity generation mechanism. It stores static commitments containing identity information on the blockchain, and generates one-time dynamic identities through re-randomization in each authentication process, thereby solving the certificate management issue and achieving anonymity. Furthermore, the method designs an authentication protocol based on CL-PKC and Schnorr NIZK, integrating private key validity verification with dynamic identity verification. A vehicle only needs to construct a single zero-knowledge proof to complete both verifications simultaneously, eliminating the risk of key escrow and improving authentication efficiency and security. For experimental evaluation, the paper constructs a simulation environment based on standard elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) and the Ganache blockchain testnet, utilizing benchmark testing data to conduct a comprehensive performance comparison between the proposed method and existing typical authentication methods. Security analysis and experimental evaluation demonstrate that the proposed method satisfies security requirements such as conditional anonymity, unlinkability, and forward security, effectively reduces the system's computational and communication overhead, and is applicable to highly dynamic and resource-constrained VANET environments.

abstract: Objective This study investigated the altered landscape of messenger RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C) methylation and the functional involvement of m5C-related regulators in a rat model of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). Methods A PCOS rat model was established by dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) induction, with the phenotype confirmed through estrous cycle monitoring, serum sex hormone analysis, and ovarian morphological assessment. Differentially m5C-methylated mRNAs were identified using an m5C epitranscriptomic microarray, and their associated biological pathways were predicted by KEGG analysis. Global m5C methylation levels and the expression and m5C enrichment of selected pathway-related genes were validated in ovarian tissues and isolated primary ovarian granulosa cells using dot blot, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and methylated RNA immunoprecipitation quantitative PCR (MeRIP-qPCR). The functional roles of TET2 and NSUN6 were further evaluated using shRNA-mediated knockdown, followed by analysis of PI3K/AKT-related signaling proteins, serum sex hormones, and ovarian histopathology. Results m5C modifications were predominantly localized within coding sequences and 3' untranslated regions. Among 1,090 RNAs showing both differential m5C methylation and expression, 36 genes exhibited significant correlations between methylation and expression changes. Global mRNA m5C methylation was significantly elevated in the PCOS group. The m5C-related regulators Nsun6 and Tet2 showed increased m5C enrichment and significantly elevated protein expression. KEGG analysis linked the differentially modified transcripts to endocrine resistance and insulin-related signaling pathways. Tet2, Nsun6, Src, Pi3k, and Akt transcripts exhibited increased m5C enrichment in PCOS ovarian tissues and primary granulosa cells. Concurrently, SRC and PI3K protein expression was increased, whereas AKT protein expression was decreased in the PCOS group. Knockdown of TET2 and NSUN6 was confirmed at the mRNA and protein levels and differentially modulated PI3K/AKT-related protein expression and phosphorylation status, as assessed by PI3K, p-PI3K, AKT, and p-AKT levels. TET2 and NSUN6 knockdown also partially improved PCOS-associated abnormalities in serum FSH, LH, the LH/FSH ratio, testosterone, estradiol, and ovarian morphology. Conclusion This study reveals a significantly altered mRNA m5C methylation landscape in a DHEA-induced PCOS rat model and primary ovarian granulosa cells. The functional knockdown data suggest that TET2 and NSUN6 may contribute to PCOS-associated ovarian dysfunction through differential regulation or remodeling of PI3K/AKT signaling. However, the opposite changes in the p-PI3K/PI3K and p-AKT/AKT ratios indicate that the pathway is differentially regulated rather than uniformly activated or inhibited. Because the DHEA model primarily mimics hyperandrogenism and MeRIP-qPCR does not provide single-nucleotide resolution, further validation in human samples and high-resolution m5C mapping is required to establish the precise molecular mechanism and clinical relevance of these findings.

abstract: Background Unsafe abortion remains a critical public health challenge globally and in India, despite the legal provision under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act for over 50 years. Multiple barriers -including limited access to trained providers, inequities in health facility readiness, stigma, poor awareness of legal entitlements, and widespread reliance on self-managed medical abortion- contribute to unsafe practices, which result in preventable maternal morbidity and mortality. Evidence on hazardous abortion in India is fragmented across facility-based studies, community surveys, and qualitative research. This protocol outlines methods for a mixed-methods systematic review integrating quantitative and qualitative data to comprehensively assess the prevalence of unsafe abortion, its determinants, associated morbidities, decision-making pathways, and the role of providers, methods, and settings. Methods The review will include quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies conducted in India and published from 1972 onwards. Eligible quantitative designs include surveys, cross-sectional, cohort, case-control, quasi-experimental studies, randomised controlled trials, and hospital series with at least ten instances. Qualitative designs will include studies using interviews, focus groups, ethnography, or participatory approaches. Mixed-methods studies will be eligible if India-specific results can be extracted. The electronic databases to be searched include PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL supplemented by grey literature from WHO, UNFPA, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and other national sources. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data, and appraise quality. The Newcastle - Ottawa Scale will be used for observational studies, the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for trials, the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) or Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklists for qualitative studies, and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) for mixed-methods studies. Quantitative data will be synthesised using random-effects meta-analysis, while qualitative findings will be analysed through thematic synthesis guided by abortion decision-making trajectories. Integration will follow a convergent segregated design. Discussion This review will generate an integrated synthesis of unsafe abortion in India, including prevalence, morbidities, determinants, women's decision-making, and the contextual role of providers and settings. Findings may inform national policy, programmatic interventions, and strategies to strengthen Comprehensive Abortion Care under the National Health Mission. Anticipated challenges include heterogeneity in definitions of "unsafe abortion," variation in outcome measures, and gaps in subnational data. Despite these limitations, the review will provide essential evidence to guide policy and improve women's health outcomes. Registration This protocol is reported in accordance with PRISMA-2020 guidelines and has been registered with the Open Science Framework (OSF). [https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/R4JPT].

abstract: Background The varicella-zoster virus, which causes herpes zoster upon reactivation, remains a public health concern, particularly among older adults. Although Zostavax and Shingrix are effective vaccines, monitoring adverse events remains important. Limited vaccine uptake and low public awareness in Saudi Arabia further highlight this need. This study seeks to assess the adverse events linked to herpes zoster immunization throughout the Saudi Arabian population. Methods This cross-sectional study used a Google Form questionnaire administered from 16 September 2024-15 August 2025. Results A total of 382 participants completed the survey. The largest age subgroup was 18-25 years (22.3%). For the first dose, 185 participants (48.4%) did not know the vaccine type, whereas 144 (37.7%) received Zostavax and 53 (13.9%) received Shingrix. Among second-dose recipients (n = 152), 85 participants (55.9%) received Zostavax, 41 (27.0%) received Shingrix, and 26 (17.1%) were uncertain of the vaccine type. The most frequently reported adverse effects after the first dose were fatigue/headache, injection-site pain, and dizziness, whereas chills, injection-site pain, and dizziness were most frequent after the second dose. No adverse effects were reported by 112 participants (29.3%) after the first dose and 28 (18.4%) after the second dose. Participants who received Zostavax reported significantly higher self-reported severity scores than those who received Shingrix after both the first dose (p = 0.003) and the second dose (p < 0.001). Conclusion Self-reported symptom severity was higher among participants with chronic disease and varied significantly by age after the first dose. The most commonly reported symptom duration was 1-2 days. No significant gender differences were observed. In unadjusted analyses, participants who reported receiving Zostavax had higher self-reported severity scores than those reporting Shingrix.

abstract: Background Children with cleft lip and/or palate may present unique challenges during perioperative airway management because of altered upper-airway and craniofacial anatomy. These children frequently undergo surgical procedures requiring general anaesthesia and airway instrumentation. Several airway-management and anaesthetic techniques have been evaluated to facilitate tracheal intubation and reduce perioperative airway complications, but the comparative evidence from randomised controlled trials has not been systematically evaluated. Methods This systematic review and meta-analysis will include randomised controlled trials involving children < 18 years with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia. Eligible studies will compare alternative techniques or devices for airway management or other anaesthetic strategies between two groups of cleft lip/palate patients. The primary outcome will be difficulty in tracheal intubation. Where definitions vary substantially, outcomes will be analysed separately or synthesised narratively. Secondary outcomes will include difficult mask ventilation, oxygen desaturation, airway obstruction, difficult laryngoscopy, first-attempt intubation success, number of intubation attempts, time to successful intubation or airway establishment, failed intubation and other perioperative airway or respiratory adverse events. Two reviewers will independently select RCTs, extract data and assess risk of bias. Risk of bias will be evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analysis will be performed where clinically appropriate. Risk ratios will be used for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences or standardized mean differences for continuous outcomes. Certainty of evidence for important outcomes will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Registration and review status The review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO on 10 March 2026 (CRD420261326076). Full-text screening and data extraction are ongoing and not yet complete. Protocol amendments are documented transparently in PROSPERO.

abstract: Background Globally, 272 million children and youth were out of school in 2023, nearly half of whom are of secondary school age. Disparities disproportionately affect girls, displaced populations, and rural communities in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Digital technologies are increasingly promoted as alternative pathways to re-engage out-of-school youth in secondary education. However, evidence on intervention models, outcomes, and implementation challenges remains fragmented, with no comprehensive synthesis to inform policy and practice. Objective This scoping review protocol aims to systematically map the available evidence on intervention models, outcomes, and implementation challenges of alternative digital secondary education for marginalized, out-of-school youth in LMICs. Materials and methods This review will follow Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. The protocol is registered on the Open Science Framework https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/5SRUD. A comprehensive search will be conducted across education, multidisciplinary, health, and regional databases, supplemented by grey literature from international organizations and preprint repositories. Eligible sources include empirical studies, program evaluations, policy documents, and reviews published from 2010 onwards - with no language restrictions, focusing on alternative digital secondary education for marginalized youth aged 13-24 years in LMICs. Two reviewers will independently screen studies and extract data using a standardized form, with a sample verified by a second reviewer. Findings will be synthesized using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis to identify patterns in intervention models, outcomes, implementation factors, and equity considerations. Conclusion This review will provide the first comprehensive mapping of alternative digital secondary education for marginalized youth in LMICs, synthesizing fragmented evidence across sectors. Findings will inform evidence-based investments - guiding decisions on low-tech versus high-tech approaches, targeting of underserved populations, and priority areas for future evaluation. All data will be made publicly available on OSF. Protocol OSF Registration DOI https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/E8RZ3.

abstract: Demand-responsive transport (DRT) is a dynamic service whose performance depends not only on dispatching and routing algorithms but also on how externally submitted demand is captured, interpreted, and incorporated into operations. Although prior studies have largely emphasized algorithm-level optimization using pre-defined demand scenarios, integrated validation of externally submitted demand, user- and operator-facing interfaces, and operational analytics remains limited. This study proposes an LLM-assisted real-time DRT operation framework comprising Service User, System Manager, and Real-time DRT Simulator layers. The Service User layer uses function calling to transform unstructured trip requests into structured dispatch parameters. The System Manager combines function-calling-based quantitative analysis with retrieval-augmented generation to support natural-language access to operational data and domain knowledge. Based on Discrete Event System Specification, the simulator processes externally submitted and simulation-generated demands within a unified event structure under common dispatching and routing logic. Three experiments were conducted. Experiments 1 and 2 functionally evaluated the rider request-processing interface and the function-calling-based quantitative-query path of the System Manager, yielding average response latencies of 1.22 and 2.21 s, respectively. Experiment 3 independently evaluated the simulator through a system-level stress test using context-based synchronized demand. Across all scenarios, synchronized demand increased waiting times for the target passenger group. Although this group represented approximately 20% of successfully served passengers, it accounted for 26.5-28.5% of total waiting time. The effect appeared largely localized and was partially obscured in aggregate metrics because background-passenger performance was stable. These results demonstrate the functional feasibility of the LLM-assisted interfaces under the prototype conditions and show that synchronized-demand stress testing can reveal localized delay burdens that aggregate evaluations may overlook.

abstract: Three-dimensional chromatin interactions play essential roles in gene regulation, yet computational prediction of diverse interaction types remains largely dependent on specialized, single-task models. Here, we present UniLoopNet, a multi-task deep learning framework that predicts multiple types of chromatin interactions including enhancer-promoter interactions, enhancer-enhancer interactions, CTCF-mediated loops, and stripe-associated interactions from DNA sequences. UniLoopNet employs a shared encoder-decoder architecture with hierarchical adaptation strategies, integrating multi-task, transfer, and continual learning based on task semantic similarity. Comprehensive benchmarking across multiple cell lines demonstrates that UniLoopNet outperforms existing specialized and multi-task approaches, with AUROCs exceeding 0.90 in most tasks. Under stringent evaluation settings, including chromosome-matched, distance-matched, realistic imbalanced, and locus-disjoint tests, AUROCs range from 0.8934 to 0.9366. In the realistic 1:5 class-imbalance setting, the AUPRCs for enhancer-promoter and enhancer-enhancer interaction prediction are 0.7956 and 0.6935, respectively. Cross-cell-line transfer experiments further show that applying UniLoopNet to another cell line requires adaptation by supervised fine-tuning on target-cell-line data, after which performance is comparable to that of within-cell-line training. Notably, the framework exhibits data efficiency in experiments with substantially reduced training data. Interpretability analyses reveal that the learned sequence features are associated with known transcription factor binding sites and uncover differential regulatory effects of disease-associated variants. UniLoopNet provides a versatile and data-efficient framework for sequence-based prediction and interpretation of diverse 3D genome interactions, complementing existing sequence-to-map approaches while improving the understanding of sequence-encoded regulatory potential.

abstract: En-route sector congestion poses a critical challenge to air traffic safety, operational efficiency, and resource-efficient airspace operation in high-density airspace. Because sector operations are spatially networked, locally emerging congestion may propagate through adjacent or upstream grid areas, leading to large-scale delays, increased fuel consumption, and elevated controller workload. This study proposes an operational spatiotemporal prediction framework for 15-minute-ahead sector congestion warning. First, processed grid-level operational states are converted into three congestion levels using K-means++ clustering based on six direct observable operational-state indicators. Second, a hybrid GNN-BiLSTM-Cross-Attention model predicts future congestion levels and local T2 hotspots from historical 5-minute grid-window sequences, without using future observed features. Third, SHAP/SHEP-style post-hoc grouped attribution is applied after inference to distinguish external triggering risk from congestion-propagation risk and to decompose external contributions from weather, restricted areas, controller workload, and wake intensity. A case study using 2023 processed grid-level operational data from the ZGGGAR15 high-altitude en-route sector achieves TEST@VAL Weighted F1 = 0.9773, L2-F1 = 0.9602, Precision = 0.9545, Recall = 0.9660, and AP = 0.9767 for rare high-congestion warning.The results indicate that the proposed framework provides accurate and spatially interpretable predictions with potential decision-support value for proactive air traffic flow management.

abstract: With the expansion of urban development, air pollution has become increasingly severe. In recent years, ozone (O3) pollution has emerged as a major threat to air quality in China. Existing studies have rarely explored the impact of vegetation types on O3 from a micro-scale perspective. Taking Hangzhou, a city with severe O3 pollution, as an example, street-view images from eight districts were first collected. A DeepLabV3+ semantic segmentation model trained on the ADE20K dataset was employed to accurately classify trees, shrubs, and grasses in the images. Meteorological and urban structural factors were incorporated, and Bayesian-optimized Optimization-based Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), and Geographically Weighted Random Forest (GWRF) models were applied to analyze the independent effects of the three vegetation-type factors on O3 concentration and their synergistic interactions from both global and local scales. The results indicate: (1) Xiaoshan District and the core urban areas such as Xihu District and are severely polluted, with an overall decreasing trend in O3 concentration (the area with O3 concentration in the range of 120.01-160.00 μg/m3 decreased from 2,100 km2 to 0 km2). (2) Meteorological factors dominate O3 variation, while the contributions of vegetation-type factors are relatively low. Nevertheless, vegetation-type factors still exhibit stable and differentiated contributions to O3 concentration. At the global scale, tree area proportion (TAP) shows either positive or negative effects on O3 concentration at high levels (average contribution = 0.002), shrub area proportion (SAP) has a positive influence, and grass area proportion (GAP) demonstrates a negative influence (average contribution = 0.006 for both). (3) At the local scale, the extremely high-importance areas of TAP shifted from northern Xihu District and Gongshu District in 2014 to southern Xihu District and Binjiang District in 2017. SAP exhibited relatively high and extremely high importance in southern Xihu District and western Xiaoshan District. The relatively high and extremely high importance areas of GAP were distributed in core urban zones such as eastern Xihu District, southern Gongshu District, Binjiang District, and Shangcheng District. The extent of extremely high-importance areas for all vegetation-type factors showed a decreasing trend. (4) High-importance areas of building density (BD) and industrial impervious surface percentage (ISP) spatially overlapped with those of vegetation-type factors, concentrating in core urban areas and the industrial zone of Xiaoshan, whereas meteorological factors played an independent role mainly in the peripheral areas of the city. This study aims to provide a scientific basis for precise O3 pollution control and optimal configuration of urban green spaces.

abstract: Plants rely heavily on root-associated microflora to mitigate various environmental stresses such as drought and the use of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) as a biological instrument to enhance plant drought tolerance, through the formation of mutualistic associations, seems like a novel strategy for sustainable agriculture. Thus, a glasshouse study was undertaken with two citrus rootstocks (Troyer citrange and Cleopatra mandarin) under 20 days of differential moisture regimes (well-watered and water-stress condition), after 270 days of inoculation with two AMF strains (Glomus intraradices and mixed strains of Gigaspora decipiens + Glomus mosseae) alone or in combination with mycorrhizal helper bacteria (MHB), i.e., phosphate solubilising bacteria (PSB), Azospirillum or Providencia, with an objective of testing the hypothesis that AMF and MHB might influence ABA accumulation in citrus leaves, thereby altering physio-biochemical response to declining soil water status. The seedlings dually inoculated with AMF and MHB exhibited significantly higher relative water content of leaf as well as rhizospheric soil. Glomus intraradices in association with PSB or Azospirillum accumulated higher concentrations of osmolytes (phenols, proline and total soluble sugars) and antioxidant metabolites (glutathione and carotenoids) in leaves under WS condition. Significantly altered leaf tissue ABA accumulation was noticed in dual inoculated treatment of Glomus intraradices and Azospirillum for Troyer citrange (3.517 µg g-1 F.W.) and G. intraradices and PSB for Cleopatra mandarin seedlings (3.079 µg g-1 F.W.), under water-stress condition, as compared to other microbial inoculants including control. Thus, water deficit stress induced physiological and biochemical response pathways could be modified by AMF and MHB. Under these experimental conditions, Troyer citrange exhibited higher relative water content, photosynthetic activity, and stomatal conductance under drought conditions than Cleopatra mandarin seedlings, offering a potential microbial intervention strategy for mitigating osmotic stress in semi-arid environments.

abstract: Background Healthcare worker (HCW) HIV-related stigma can reduce participation in HIV prevention services in Malawi, including HIV index testing. However, evidence on interventions to reduce HCW stigma and improve client experiences of care in index testing settings remains limited. We evaluated HCW stigmatizing attitudes and also assessed anticipated stigma and perceptions of respectful care among both people living with HIV (index clients) and their sexual partners (contact clients) in index testing settings. Methods We conducted a cluster randomized controlled trial across 33 clusters providing index case testing in southeastern Malawi. All HCWs received standard, in-person training. Enhanced cluster HCWs additionally received the blended learning training package consisting of tablet-based modules and in-person sessions incorporating stigma-reduction content. HCW stigmatizing attitudes were evaluated one-month (wave 1) and one-year post-training (wave 2). A subset of index and contact clients completed anticipated stigma and respectful care scales at exit interviews. Scales ranged from 0-3 (HCW stigma), 0-1 (anticipated stigma), and 1-5 (respectful care), with higher scores reflecting more stigma or respectful care. Generalized estimating equations with an identity link and gamma distribution estimated adjusted mean differences between arms. Results We enrolled 305 HCWs, 341 index clients, and 194 contact clients. Overall stigma levels were low and respectful care ratings were high across arms. Mean HCW stigma scores were 0.8 (wave 1) and 0.7 (wave 2); adjusted mean differences between arms were -0.1 (p = 0.3) at wave 1 and 0.0 (p = 1.0) at wave 2. Index and contact client anticipated stigma means were both 0.1; adjusted mean differences between arms were 0.0 (p = 0.9) for index and 0.0 (p = 0.7) for contact clients. Respectful care means were 4.0 for index and 4.2 for contact clients; adjusted mean differences between arms were 0.0 (p = 0.9) for index and -0.1 (p = 0.3) for contact clients. Conclusions The enhanced training package did not improve HCW or client stigma-related outcomes. Further research is needed to reduce HCW and client stigma and improve respectful care.

abstract: Background Medical Device-Related Pressure Injuries (MDRPI) are a serious complication in intensive care units (ICUs), yet structured prevention algorithms are lacking. Methods This single-group, pre-test/post-test quasi-experimental study was conducted in the General Intensive Care Unit from February 2025 to April 2025. The sample comprised 38 nurses and 77 patients (39 pre-intervention, 38 post-intervention). Nurses' knowledge was assessed using the MDRPUKQ questionnaire, and patient outcomes were monitored using baseline and post-intervention data on pressure injury prevalence and severity. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26, employing descriptive and inferential statistics including paired t-tests, independent t-tests, chi-square tests, Fisher's exact tests, and multivariable logistic regression. Results The mean knowledge score increased significantly from 57.74 (SD = 11.15) before training to 89.55 (SD = 5.17) afterward (mean difference: 31.81, 95% CI: 28.35-35.27, P < 0.001, Cohen's d = 3.02). Overall, MDRPI prevalence decreased from 38.5% (95% CI: 24.9-54.1%) pre-intervention to 28.9% (95% CI: 17-44%). However, this difference was not statistically significant using Pearson's chi-square test (χ2 = 0.82, P = 0.365). The distribution of pressure injury stages before implementation was: Stage 1 (28.2%), Stage 2 (7.7%), and Stage 3 (2.6%). Following the intervention, prevalence dropped to Stage 1 (21.1%) and Stage 2 (5.3%), with no new Stage 3 injuries reported. After adjusting for potential confounders (age, Braden score, ICU length of stay, and device exposure duration), implementation of the algorithm was associated with reduced MDRPI occurrence (adjusted OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.19-0.91, P = 0.026). Conclusion Implementation of the MDRPI prevention algorithm was associated with significant improvement in nurses' knowledge. A numerically lower prevalence was observed. This suggests that injuries caused by medical equipment are largely absent from current mandatory continuing education or postgraduate nursing curricula, reinforcing the need for a thorough review and the integration of this topic into standard educational programs.

abstract: Understanding how vegetation in ecologically fragile karst regions responds to extreme climate events is critical for global change adaptation. However, the response of net primary productivity (NPP) to extreme climate indices, rather than to mean climatic conditions, has not been systematically investigated across large, contiguous karst areas. To address this gap, this study used MODIS NPP data and 12 ETCCDI extreme climate indices calculated from daily meteorological records (2000-2018) to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution of NPP and its asymmetric response to extreme temperature and precipitation events across Guizhou Province, Southwest China. Pixel-level Pearson correlation and Theil-Sen trend analyses were applied, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons. The results show that: (1) annual mean NPP increased significantly at a rate of approximately 3.8 g C m-2 yr-1, with a west-high, east-low spatial pattern; (2) climate trends showed asymmetric warming (nighttime warming three to four times faster than daytime) and intensified total precipitation but reduced persistence; and (3) NPP exhibited strong, spatially extensive positive correlations with extreme temperature indices (especially warm night frequency and annual minimum temperature), whereas correlations with extreme precipitation indices were weak and highly heterogeneous. Thermal conditions, particularly nighttime warming, appear to be the primary driver of vegetation dynamics in this humid karst region, while the unique dualistic hydrological structure likely decouples precipitation from plant water availability. Future karst ecosystem management should prioritize extreme temperature events and adopt spatially differentiated strategies.

abstract: A characteristic feature of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) is impaired myocardial blood flow (MBF). Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) is also associated with reduced hyperemic MBF. However, it is unknown whether an independent association exists between AF and MBF in symptomatic patients with suspected obstructive CAD. We studied 874 patients at Kuopio University Hospital (Finland) who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and [15O]H2O myocardial perfusion positron emission tomography due to suspected obstructive CAD in 2017-2023. The final cohort comprised 31 AF patients and 120 propensity score-matched sinus rhythm (SR) patients. The matching criteria were age, sex, body mass index, number of traditional risk factors for CAD (0-5), calcium score, and total CCTA status (i.e., the overall severity of CCTA findings). Global hyperemic MBF was lower in AF patients than in SR patients (median 1.9 mL/g/min [IQR 1.4-2.6 mL/g/min] vs. 3.0 mL/g/min [IQR 2.4-3.6 mL/g/min], p < 0.001). Impaired hyperemic MBF (< 2.3 mL/g/min in ≥ 1 segment) was more frequent in AF patients (n = 25/31, 81%) than in SR patients (n = 50/120, 42%, p < 0.001). Furthermore, the presence of AF was independently associated with reduced hyperemic MBF in three multivariate general linear models (p < 0.001 in each model). To summarize, AF was independently associated with impaired hyperemic MBF in patients with suspected obstructive CAD. This association should be considered in clinical practice when interpreting the results of myocardial perfusion imaging in patients with AF.

abstract: Automated loop invariant inference remains a fundamental challenge in formal verification due to the inherently unbounded search space of candidate invariants. Existing approaches either incur substantial computational overhead during invariant synthesis or rely on manually predefined templates, limiting both scalability and automation. Although recent learning-based methods have shown promise, they often fail to fully exploit the rich structural and semantic information embedded within program representations. This paper presents a learning-guided framework for fully automated loop invariant inference based on a systematic analysis of program structure and semantics. The framework performs a joint analysis of syntactic constructs, control-flow structure, and data-dependence relationships to determine invariant structure before instantiation. These complementary representations are embedded and integrated within a learning-based model that identifies structurally and semantically features and infers expressive invariant templates directly from program structure. The inferred templates are instantiated using execution-derived values, yielding constraint systems that are solved and formally validated using a Satisfiability Modulo Theories solver. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves competitive invariant inference performance on challenging benchmarks. By integrating multi-representation program analysis, the framework effectively supports a wide range of loop structures and advances the state of the art in scalable, expressive, and fully automated loop invariant inference.

abstract: Objectives To investigate the relationship between ultrasound-based muscle architecture parameters and isometric knee flexor muscle strength in healthy individuals, and to evaluate whether distal (25%) and proximal (75%) measurement sites differ in their ability to reflect muscle strength compare to the commonly used mid-thigh (50%) region. Methods Isometric muscle strength was measured in 20 healthy (22.15 ± 2.41 y; 8 females, 12 males) participants using a hand-held dynamometer. Ultrasound parameters (cross-sectional area, muscle thickness, pennation angle) of the biceps femoris-long head, semitendinosus, and semimembranosus were measured at 25%, 50%, and 75% of thigh length. Associations between strength and ultrasound-based parameters were examined using multiple linear regression analysis. Results Moderate-to-high correlations (r = 0.615-0.815) were observed between muscle strength and cross-sectional area for all muscles at 50%. The regression model explained 89% of the variance in muscle strength (p < 0.001). Notably, the cross-sectional area of the semimembranosus and the total hamstring cross-sectional area at 25% length demonstrated strong correlations with muscle strength (r = 0.907 and 0.802, respectively). At 75%, the cross-sectional area of the semimembranosus showed a non-significant association with strength, while it could not be measured for the semitendinosus and biceps femoris-long head due to anatomical limitations. Muscle thickness showed significant correlations for the semitendinosus and semimembranosus (r = 0.702 and 0.698, respectively), whereas pennation angle demonstrated weaker and inconsistent relationships. Conclusions The cross-sectional area of the semimembranosus at 50% of muscle length showed the strongest ultrasound-based predictor of isometric muscle strength. However, measurement at the distal site demonstrated robust associations, suggesting this region may serve as a practical alternative. In contrast, proximal measurements were limited and showed non-significant associations with strength. These findings can help expand the clinical and research applications of ultrasound imaging for assessing hamstring strength. Given the exploratory nature of this study, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

abstract: Basketball substitutions are usually interpreted as tactical decisions, but repeated substitution sequences may also reveal stable team-level tendencies in how competitive exposure is organised. We reconstructed 65,657 on-court stints from two complete EuroLeague regular seasons and defined a proposed five-indicator team rotation signature (S5), evaluated over two seasons: structural exposure per minute, fragmentation, rotation irregularity, compressed recovery, and fourth-quarter SEI share. Game-level signatures were identifiable above chance, with leave-one-out nearest-centroid accuracies of 26.7% (95% CI [23.2, 30.0]) and 31.1% (95% CI [27.8, 34.5]) against chance levels of 5.6% and 5.0%, and noisy game-level profiles aggregated into reliable seasonal fingerprints. Across the 17 clubs present in both seasons, matched clubs remained closer to their own previous signature than to randomly paired club-season profiles (mean distance 1.68 vs. 2.62; p < .001). Game state affected rotation depth far more than the signature: a 20-point margin explained 14.33% of within-club variance in effective rotation but 0.80% in signature deviation. Structural consolidation was not detectably associated with winning. However, clubs concentrating structural exposure in the fourth quarter won fewer games (r = -0.38, 95% CI [-0.66, -0.05]); this exploratory association replicated in both seasons but attenuated after controlling for previous-season success and should not be read causally. Rotation architecture therefore behaves as a comparatively persistent club-level property rather than a by-product of in-game substitution decisions.

abstract: Introduction Physical activity interventions for adolescents with depression often show limited effectiveness due to insufficient developmental tailoring, limited autonomy support, and poor contextual feasibility. BRIDGES (Brussels Resilience and Inclusion for Depression - Guidance, Exercise, and Support) is a theory-informed and co-designed physical activity intervention integrating the COM-B model, self-determination theory and motivational interviewing to support autonomous and competence-enhancing engagement. This pilot randomized controlled trial uses a hybrid type 2 implementation-effectiveness design to examine feasibility, acceptability, implementation processes and obtain preliminary estimates of clinical effectiveness to inform a future larger-scale trial. Methods and analysis Sixty physically inactive adolescents aged 12-19 years with depression will be recruited from an outpatient mental health service in Brussels, Belgium. Participants will be randomized in waves using covariate-adaptive minimization with a biased-coin component (p=0.85), balancing baseline depression severity, physical activity level, gender and age. The intervention consists of 18 individualized physiotherapist-led counselling sessions delivered over 12 weeks, including structured support to facilitate transition to community-based physical activity. Primary feasibility, acceptability, implementation outcomes will be assessed using quantitative measures and semi-structured interviews with adolescents, caregivers and community partners, guided by the Practical, Robust Implementation and Sustainability Model (PRISM) and the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation and Maintenance (RE-AIM) framework. Preliminary effectiveness outcomes are changes in physical activity measured using the Physical Activity Vital Sign (PAVS) and depressive symptoms measured using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 modified for Adolescents (PHQ-A). Preliminary effectiveness will be analysed using linear mixed-effects models following an intention-to-treat approach to estimate cluster-level parameters for a future fully powered Hybrid Type 2 trial. Secondary outcomes include social support, exercise self-efficacy, cardiorespiratory fitness and waist-to-height ratio. Qualitative data will be analysed using the Qualitative Analysis Guide of Leuven. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07422909.

abstract: Background Opioid overdose remains a major global public health emergency, with naloxone being an essential response. Benefit from existing naloxone formulations is limited by barriers to acceptability, fixed dosing, and poor real-world carriage. This study describes the protocol for a Phase 1 exploratory investigation of a novel ultra-portable lyophilised naloxone wafer designed to facilitate constant carriage and enable rapid mucosal absorption. Methods This open-label, randomised, random-sequence, five-way crossover pharmacokinetic (PK) exploratory study will recruit 12-15 healthy adults at a UK clinical research facility. Participants will receive five treatments, each separated by ≥36 hours: buccal naloxone wafer 2 mg, buccal wafer 4 mg, sublingual wafer 2 mg, intramuscular naloxone 0.4 mg, and intranasal naloxone 1.8 mg (Nyxoid®). Blood samples will be collected up to 240 minutes post-dose for PK analysis via validated LC-MS/MS methods. The primary endpoint is time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax). Secondary endpoints include Maximum Plasma Concentration (Cmax), Time to 50% of maximum concentration (T50%), Area Under the Curve from time zero to 15 minutes (AUC0-15), Area Under the Curve from time zero to infinity (AUCinf), and safety/tolerability. Dose-proportionality and buccal-sublingual comparisons will be explored. Trial Registration:REC: 25/LO/0701; MHRA CTA (IRAS): 1011060. ISRCTN67173532. Results & significance This study will characterise the absorption profile, early exposure, and relative bioavailability of a novel naloxone wafer formulated for rapid buccal and sublingual administration. Findings will inform whether this technology could provide a practical, effective alternative to current injectable and intranasal products, with potential to substantially improve naloxone carriage and timely overdose response, and will guide the design of a subsequent, larger confirmatory study.

abstract: CD47 delivers a dominant "Don't Eat Me" signal that inhibits macrophage‑mediated clearance of tumour cells. Using immunocompetent, chemoresistant neuroblastoma (NB) models, we tested a Fc‑silent CD47 blocker (ALX301) with anti‑GD2 antibody alone and in combination with a clinically aligned temozolomide/irinotecan chemoimmunotherapy backbone. Tumours expressed GD2 and CD47, and bound ALX301. In macrophage coculture assays, anti-GD2 antibody induced dose-dependent phagocytosis, whereas ALX301 or an anti-CD47 antibody alone did not. CD47 blockade in combination with a suboptimal concentration of anti-GD2 antibody showed an additive effect on phagocytosis in vitro. In vivo, however, ALX301 failed to improve tumour control or survival when added to anti‑GD2 or to chemoimmunotherapy in the dosing regimens and two independent models tested. Toxicity was acceptable, showing only mild, expected red‑cell changes without overt organ injury. This form of CD47 inhibition is therefore mechanistically active in vitro but insufficient to enhance anti‑GD2 antibody-based therapy in immunocompetent mice bearing a chemoresistant NB, highlighting the potential need for myeloid‑reprogramming partners.

abstract: This study develops a causality-enhanced and symmetry-preserving Physics-Informed Neural Network (S-PINN) framework for nonlinear damped elastodynamic partial differential equations. The governing nonlinear elastic wave equation with viscous damping is reduced through Lie symmetry analysis into four invariant ordinary differential equation forms, including scaling, translation, damped, and generalized damped symmetries. The proposed framework combines symmetry-aware solution reconstruction, composite residual and symmetry losses, and causality-based temporal weighting to improve the training stability and physical consistency of PINNs. Numerical experiments are performed using a fully connected neural network with four hidden layers, 128 neurons per layer, the tanh activation function, and the L-BFGS optimizer. The S-PINN solutions are compared with conventional PINNs and exact analytical references for all four symmetry-reduced cases. The results show that the proposed S-PINN framework provides faster convergence, lower loss, and improved solution accuracy. In Case IV, S-PINNs achieve a 35% faster convergence rate during the first 500 epochs and reduce the final loss from 3.8 for PINNs to 2.4. The S-PINN loss stabilizes after approximately 1000 epochs, whereas the PINN loss continues to oscillate with fluctuations up to 15%. The gradient norm remains within 0.5-1.5 for S-PINNs, compared with 0.2-2.5 for PINNs. At α=0.4, the S-PINN solution attains 98% agreement with the exact solution, and its maximum absolute error remains below 0.05, compared with 0.18 for the standard PINN. Contour comparisons further show less than 5% distortion for S-PINNs, while PINNs exhibit distortions up to 18%. These findings demonstrate that embedding Lie symmetries and causal temporal learning into PINNs constrains the solution space to physically admissible manifolds and improves the reliability of neural solvers for nonlinear wave propagation in computational mechanics.

abstract: Background Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder after Alzheimer's disease. Hereditary causes account for 10-15% of cases but present considerably more complex clinical manifestations than idiopathic cases. It is therefore imperative to enhance clinicians' recognition of hereditary forms. Methods This study enrolled 29 patients with early‑onset or familial parkinsonism. 17 cases were identified with reportable genetic findings using PD-targeted or movement disorders gene panels. Clinical data and genetic data were collected. Results Among 17 patients, PARK2/PRKN (n = 9) and PARK8/LRRK2 (n = 5) were predominant subtypes, with two cases of PARK14/PLA2G6, and one case of PARK18/EIF4G1. Clinically, bradykinesia affected 17/17 patients, rigidity 15/17, tremor 13/17, and dystonia 7/17 (including one oculogyric crisis). Hyperreflexia occurred in 6/17, cognitive impairment in 2/17, pyramidal signs in 2/17, ataxic dysarthria 1/17, and pes cavus in 1/17. Diurnal fluctuation and sleep benefit occurred exclusively in PARK2/PRKN and PARK14/PLA2G6 patients. Among patients with PRKN, 7/9 exhibited diurnal fluctuations: five had exon rearrangements, one had a splicing mutation, and one had a homozygous variant. Conversely, the two PARK2/PRKN patients without diurnal fluctuations showed no exon deletions/duplications. PARK18/EIF4G1 mutations may manifest incomplete penetrance. Conclusion Among PARK2/PRKN patients in our cohort, a potential association between diurnal fluctuation and exon rearrangements may exist, although this observation requires cautious interpretation. Furthermore, these variants appear to cluster within the N-terminal region of the protein (the start of the RING1 domain and preceding regions). Beyond the common PARK2/PRKN subtype, PARK14/PLA2G6 may also be linked to diurnal fluctuation and sleep benefit.

abstract: Tenacibaculum maritimum is a major bacterial pathogen of marine fish responsible for ulcerative disease outbreaks and high mortality in numerous fish species and represents an important challenge in aquaculture worldwide. In this study, we characterized seven newly sequenced T. maritimum isolates recovered from farmed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar), Atlantic halibut (Hippoglossus hippoglossus), and lumpfish (Cyclopterus lumpus) in British Columbia (Canada) and Norway, including the first complete genome of T. maritimum isolated from Atlantic salmon in Norway. Comparative genomic analysis revealed the presence of a complete Type IX secretion system (T9SS) and the canonical gliding-associated machinery. We also identified a largely conserved repertoire of candidate T9SS substrates and several major host-interaction proteins. Phylogenetic analysis placed the isolates in several well-supported clades comprising strains from different geographic origins and host species. Characterization of the O-antigen gene clusters identified three different types (1-0, 2-1, and 4-0), whose distribution was not congruent with the phylogenetic relationships among isolates. Colony development of the four Norwegian isolates on agar was strongly influenced by incubation temperature, with rapid growth at 20-24°C, slower growth at 12-16°C, and only limited growth at 8°C. This study expands the available genomic resources for T. maritimum and highlights the importance of integrating genomic and environmental surveillance to improve tenacibaculosis management in aquaculture systems.

abstract: This study compared the refractive prediction accuracy of seven contemporary intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation formulas in eyes with short axial length and assessed the influence of anterior chamber depth (ACD) and lens thickness (LT) on prediction error (PE). A total of 124 eyes with an axial length ≤22.0 mm that underwent uncomplicated phacoemulsification with implantation of a Tecnis ZCB00 IOL were included. Predicted postoperative refractions were obtained using the ESCRS calculator for Barrett Universal II, Cooke K6, EVO 2.0, Hill-RBF 3.0, Hoffer QST, Kane, and Pearl-DGS. Formula performance was evaluated using robust trimmed-mean analyses of trueness, precision, and accuracy implemented in the Eyetemis platform, along with conventional PE metrics and the proportions of eyes within predefined error thresholds. The mean axial length was 21.67 ± 0.31 mm, and the mean implanted IOL power was 25.2 ± 1.6 D. Kane showed a lower trimmed-mean absolute PE than Hoffer QST (0.376 vs. 0.445 D; p = 0.014). No significant inter-formula differences were observed at clinically relevant error thresholds. ACD and LT showed weak, formula-specific associations with PE; however, these findings were exploratory and not clinically actionable. Overall, contemporary formulas provided broadly comparable refractive accuracy in short eyes, although small formula-specific differences were observed.

title: Competence narrowing in AI-assisted oral English instruction: A quasi-experimental study of the spiral synergy framework.

author_details.name: Jinyan Zhang
author_details.affiliation: School of Economics and Management, Jiangsu Maritime Institute, Nanjing, Jiangsu, China.

affiliation_resolution.input: School of Economics and Management, Jiangsu Maritime Institute, Nanjing, Jiangsu, China.

abstract: The rapid integration of generative AI tools into spoken English instruction has produced measurable fluency and accuracy gains, but whether these are evenly distributed across the dimensions of communicative competence remains underexplored. This quasi-experimental study compares the Spiral Synergy Framework (SSF), a three-layer pedagogical sequence (AI Consolidation, Bridging Tasks, Interpersonal Activation), against conventional AI-integrated instruction in two intact Business English classes at a Chinese higher vocational college (experimental n = 36, control n = 34), using oral recordings at three time points scored on five competence dimensions, 15 weeks of classroom observation, and an intra-rater reliability check. The two classes differed significantly at baseline on the oral composite score and three of five dimensions (control higher), though not on CET-4 proficiency or questionnaire items. Because treatment is confounded with class membership and both classes received AI-assisted practice, findings are reported as associations rather than demonstrated causal effects. Linear mixed-effects models testing Group × Time interactions across five outcomes (four dimensions and the composite), corrected for multiple comparisons, identified one outcome - real-time responsiveness - on which the classes diverged: the experimental class maintained responsiveness across the semester while the control class declined despite its baseline advantage (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p = .029), a result that held under a cluster-robust sensitivity check. No corrected between-group difference was found for improvisation, coherence, naturalness, or the composite score; improvisation declined descriptively in both classes over the semester. Classroom observation data (experimental class only) document a recurring, non-monotonic cycle of AI-dependency reduction and rebound across 15 weeks. Intra-rater test-retest reliability of the oral-competence ratings was moderate to good (ICC = .67-.91), though this reflects a single rater familiar with participants rather than independent inter-rater agreement. Implications for multidimensional assessment, task sequencing, and cautious interpretation of AI-integrated curriculum research are discussed.

abstract: Soil nutrient analysis is essential for sustainable agriculture and precision farming. Traditional chemical tests for nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium are reliable but costly, time-consuming, and often unavailable in remote areas. The objective of this study is to develop a novel approach that combines laboratory chemical extraction, controlled image acquisition, image processing, machine learning, and deep learning to classify soil nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium levels. 50 independent soil samples were analyzed, chemically extracted, and classified as Low, Medium, or High for each nutrient. A specially designed black-box prototype was developed to capture high-quality images of soil extract samples under consistent lighting conditions. The images were used to extract color and texture information, which was evaluated using multiple classical machine-learning algorithms, such as K-nearest neighbours, support vector machines, logistic regression, random forest, extra trees, gradient boosting, and Gaussian naive Bayes. A convolutional neural network-based model was also used for comparison. To minimize data leakage, all validation procedures were performed at the physical-sample level, and augmented images were restricted to the training data. The best models obtained using nested cross-validation for nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium were KNN, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression, respectively, with accuracies of 60%, 82%, and 48%. The nitrogen model correctly identified the High category, and the phosphorus model correctly identified the dominant Low category each time. For potassium, Logistic Regression made predictions of all three classes and outperformed the majority class baseline. The Classical machine-learning models slightly outperformed the compact CNN for nitrogen and potassium, while both achieved the same accuracy for phosphorus; however, overall performance remained limited by the small and imbalanced dataset. The findings suggest that the proposed framework could contribute to image-assisted decision-making in smart farming and support improved soil management practices, particularly in regions where laboratory testing facilities are limited.

abstract: The extent to which diabetic foot ulcer transcriptomic findings agree across cohorts remains uncertain. We compared an RNA sequencing cohort of 13 ulcer and eight diabetic foot skin samples with a microarray cohort of six ulcer and three diabetic foot skin samples. Single-cell data from 26 participants were analyzed after aggregating gene counts within each patient and cell type. A further cohort of 10 ulcer and 11 healthy foot-skin samples provided a descriptive directional comparison. Healing-status comparisons were exploratory. The primary analysis selected 4,704 differentially expressed gene identifiers; 2,943 were represented among the 17,502 gene symbols shared with the microarray cohort. Of these, 1,254 had concordant directions and nominal microarray P < 0.05, including 1,028 with microarray false discovery rate < 0.05. Direction agreement was 70.2%, and overall effect-rank correlation was modest (Spearman ρ = 0.29). Five Hallmark gene sets met the cross-cohort enrichment criteria. More specific functional analysis of the stricter supported set highlighted cornified-envelope formation, keratinization and inflammatory-cell migration. In the additional cohort, 611 of 823 represented genes from this set agreed in direction, although its comparator differed. Twelve keratinocyte genes met the cell-type differential-expression threshold; this finding does not establish cell-type exclusivity. Healing-status results were sensitive to covariate adjustment. These data support partial concordance in ulcer-associated epithelial, inflammatory and metabolic expression patterns. Limited cohort coverage, comparator differences and unresolved confounding preclude a universal disease signature, healing predictor or causal interpretation.

abstract: Background Patients with cancer often experience oncological emergencies requiring immediate care, and the quality of acute oncology (AO) care varies between providers. Patient-reported experience measures (PREMs) are a key tool for quality improvement, but none currently exists for AO. This study developed a prototype PREM, the Patient-Reported Experience Measure for Acute OnCology (PREMAC), and conducted preliminary single-site psychometric testing. Materials and methods A quality assessment framework guided development across three stages. Stage 1 generated a conceptual framework of accessing AO services from a scoping review and interviews with patients and health professionals. Stage 2 developed a prototype questionnaire, with content validity assessed by a Service User Reference Panel (SURP) and face validity tested through cognitive interviews. Stage 3 tested acceptability, feasibility, structural validity and internal consistency at one tertiary cancer centre in southern England. Results Data integration identified ten domains, in the chronological order patients accessing AO experience them: reasons for accessing AO; patient preparedness; accessibility of care; the care environment; competence of care; communication and decision-making; compassionate care; the carer's role; patient anxiety; and service issues including discharge. The 46-item prototype was completed by 171 respondents. Exploratory factor analysis of 18 four-category ordinal items, using polychoric correlations with minimum residual extraction and oblimin rotation (n = 121 complete cases), supported three provisional domains: information, communication, involvement and perceived care quality (α = 0.935); care environment, dignity, trust and safety (α = 0.711); and discharge information and preparedness (α = 0.704). Conclusion PREMAC is the first PREM developed specifically for AO. Preliminary testing indicates the prototype is acceptable and feasible, with early evidence of internal coherence across three provisional domains at a single site. The domain structure and item allocations remain provisional; no total score is recommended. Multisite validation is required before PREMAC could support service comparison or benchmarking.

abstract: The alpha-2-adrenergic agonist drug dexmedetomidine induces sleep-like sedation and reduces global metabolic rate. Drug-induced metabolic suppression sustained over days in humans could be a strategy for reducing energy expenditure (EE), oxygen consumption (VO2), and carbon dioxide production (VCO2) during prolonged rescue or austere conditions with limited life-support. We tested the feasibility of reducing EE, VO2 and VCO2 measured with intermittent indirect calorimetry using subcutaneous infusion of dexmedetomidine 1 µg/kg/hour for 18 hours per day over five days in healthy adults. Five participants received multiple days of dexmedetomidine in a laboratory setting, and five separate participants received placebo for one or five days. Relative to resting metabolic rate, dexmedetomidine infusion reduced VO2 (effects, 95%CI, at 6-hour time epoch: -0.084 L/min, -0.145 to -0.023), VCO2 (-0.067 L/min, -0.130 to -0.005) and EE (-577 kcal/day, -1016 to -137). Relative to placebo, dexmedetomidine produced light sedation (Richmond Agitation Sedation Score: -1.25; 95%CI -1.70 to -0.80 relative to placebo), with lower heart rate (-15 beats/minute; 95%CI -23 to -7) and core body temperature (-1.3ºC; 95%CI -1.7 to -0.8). Dexmedetomidine effects on all physiological variables decreased over time and were absent after day 2. Maximum and minimum plasma drug levels did not change over days. Participants reported rebound anxiety and insomnia after the study. Administering a sedating level of dexmedetomidine that reduces VO2, VCO2, and EE for 2 days was feasible in healthy adults. However, tolerance to drug effects develops by 3 days, which is a critical limitation for long-term use of this drug regimen.

abstract: Natural disasters can trigger large-scale population displacement, resulting in labor market shocks in destination areas. Nonetheless, important aspects of migration-driven shocks remain unclear, particularly how relative inflow intensity, the spatially concentrated inflow of low-skilled migrants, and industry structure moderate these impacts. Using Hurricane Katrina as a natural experiment and a Difference in Difference framework, this study reveals that displacement shock reduces wages in the low-skill localized sector, but this negative impact is heavily characterized by non-linear congestion effects, intensifying sharply from $-0.15 to $-0.27 drop in wage rates when the inflow concentration crosses certain threshold. Decomposing the demand-side channels shows that while the influx stimulates local business creation, this countervailing buffer is economically modest and insufficient to offset the supply-driven wage depression. Furthermore, sectoral mobility and joint wage-setting analyses confirm that low-skill localized and traded industries remain highly segmented in the short run. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for both supply and demand channels, non-linear thresholds, and sectoral frictions to improve regional labor market policies after demographic shocks.

abstract: People with pre-existing mental health disorders (PMHD) often have lower cancer screening uptake and later-stage diagnoses. It remains unclear whether these disparities persist within highly accessible universal healthcare systems without strict gatekeeping. We simultaneously investigated the associations between PMHD and both screening participation and stage at diagnosis of breast and bowel cancers within the Taiwan health service. Using nationwide National Health Insurance and Cancer Registry data covering over 99% of the population, we compared outcomes between individuals with and without PMHD. Propensity score matching was applied for the screening cohort. Adjusted odds ratios were estimated using logistic regression, with subgroup analyses for severe PMHD. Overall, PMHD was associated with higher screening participation (adjusted odds ratios [aOR]: breast = 1.04, bowel = 1.12) and reduced odds of metastatic disease at diagnosis (breast = 0.72, bowel = 0.93), although the magnitude of these associations was modest, particularly for bowel cancer. Conversely, individuals with severe PMHD had significantly lower odds of screening (breast = 0.81, bowel = 0.88) despite high outpatient use. Furthermore, while the severe group retained reduced odds of metastatic breast cancer at diagnosis (aOR = 0.79), they showed no staging advantage for bowel cancer. While Taiwan's highly accessible universal healthcare system may contribute to a surveillance effect benefiting the general PMHD population, significant disparities persist for individuals with severe illnesses. Targeted interventions, procedural simplifications for self-administered tests, and multidisciplinary person-centred care models, may be needed to ensure health equity.
