abstract: Microtubule-dependent pronuclear migration and mitotic spindle positioning are fundamental processes during the first embryonic division in many animals. In the one-cell embryo of Caenorhabditis elegans, these events are regulated by well-characterized pulling forces acting on astral microtubules, including cortical forces mediated by the Gα-GPR-LIN-5 dynein complex. Although the overall framework of these dynamics is conserved, recent studies have revealed substantial interspecies variation in their regulation. Here, we investigated nuclei and mitotic spindle behaviors in one-cell embryos of Caenorhabditis inopinata, the closest known relative of C. elegans, using live-cell imaging and functional perturbation. We found that C. inopinata embryos exhibit altered pronuclear migration, reduced anaphase spindle oscillations, and slower centrosome diffusion during telophase compared with C. elegans. These differences suggest weaker cortical pulling forces. Functional analyses using RNA interference showed that GPR retains its essential role in force generation, whereas the contribution of the microtubule depolymerizing kinesin KLP-7 is reduced in C. inopinata. Our results point to evolutionary changes in microtubule-regulated spindle dynamics, and provide insight into how conserved cellular processes can diversify through subtle changes in their underlying mechanisms.

abstract: Background The potential relationship between the consumption of red yeast rice (RYR) and the development of end-stage renal disease (ESRD) remains poorly understood. We aimed to evaluate the risk of ESRD in patients who used RYR. Methods Utilizing insurance claim records from 2010 to 2014, we performed a retrospective cohort analysis comparing 67,876 individuals using RYR against a control group of 90,836 lovastatin users (non-RYR group), with follow-up extending through 2019. The incidence of ESRD was analyzed using adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) within Cox proportional hazard models. Results During follow-up, the ESRD incidence was 0.9 per 1,000 person-years in RYR users, compared to 3.7 per 1,000 person-years in lovastatin users (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.32-0.40). A dose-dependent reduction in ESRD risk was observed with increasing RYR prescriptions. Sensitivity analysis, excluding ESRD cases within the initial six months, confirmed a persistent association between RYR use and reduced ESRD risk (adjusted HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.81). Conclusion RYR intake may be linked to a decreased likelihood of progressing to ESRD. Despite these promising results, factors such as medication adherence necessitate cautious interpretation. Further randomized controlled trials are required to validate these findings and clarify RYR's role in slowing kidney disease progression.

abstract: To reduce labor costs, mitigate plastic pollution, and enhance disease control in cold-region rice seedling nurseries, this study developed a biodegradable film-based seedling system.From 2022 to 2024, large-scale comparative field experiments were conducted over three consecutive years in seven major rice-producing cities and counties in Heilongjiang Province, including Tailai, Tonghe, and Fangzheng, to systematically analyze the effect of this technique on seedling morphology, biomass, vigor, and other key indicators, as well as its ecological and inter-annual adaptability. The results showed that, compared with traditional mechanical transplanting tray seedling raising (CK), the biodegradable film-based treatment (T1) increased seedling height, root length, stem base width,dry weight per hundred seedlings, and the classic strong seedling index (SRI) by an average of 6.82%, 8.97%, 9.52%, 10.26%, and 12.41%, respectively, while maintaining a stable root-shoot ratio and water metabolism.No bacterial wilt or seedling blight was observed throughout the experimental period, and no white plastic residue was detected.The total costof seedling raising was reduced by 15%-20%. Regionally, the technique performed best in high-biomass zones (e.g., Tonghe, Mishan) and balanced robust seedling zones (e.g., Suibin, Qing'an), while also showing positive effects in stress-prone regions. This technique demonstrates potential for improving seedling quality while reducing costs and plastic residue.Across 21 site-year combinations spanning seven major rice-producing regions, the system demonstrated consistent positive effects (T1/CK ratios >1.02) with the highest advantages observed in high-biomass regions (Tonghe and Mishan), confirming broad ecological adaptability.

abstract: Study design Retrospective clinical study. Objective To evaluate the efficacy of endoscopic posterior keyhole decompression for cervical radiculopathy and to investigate the correlation between decompression parameters and clinical outcomes. Summary of background data Cervical radiculopathy traditionally requires anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) or open posterior decompression. Although ACDF is the gold standard, it is associated with adjacent segment degeneration and implant-related complications. Minimally invasive posterior keyhole techniques aim to reduce surgical trauma; however, the optimal extent of decompression required for symptomatic relief remains unclear. Methods Forty patients with single-level cervical radiculopathy treated via unilateral endoscopic posterior keyhole decompression (strictly limited to targeted foraminotomy and partial medial facetectomy) (2021-2024) were reviewed. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Neck Disability Index (NDI) preoperatively, at discharge, and at 6 months postoperatively. Decompression parameters were quantified via postoperative CT. Statistical analysis included paired t-tests and Pearson correlation. Results All 40 procedures were successful. Specifically, 25 patients underwent isolated foraminotomy, and 15 received foraminotomy combined with discectomy, without any progression to interlaminar decompression or laminectomy. The mean operative time was 70.4 ± 24.7 minutes, and the mean blood loss was 11.7 ± 10.9 ml. Significant improvements in clinical scores were observed at all postoperative time points (P < 0.05). Statistical analysis revealed that neither the concurrent execution of a discectomy nor the diameter of the bony decompression window was significantly associated with the degree of postoperative symptom improvement. Conclusions This study demonstrates that endoscopic posterior keyhole decompression is a safe and feasible technique that provides favorable short-term clinical outcomes with minimal surgical trauma. The findings strongly suggest that clinical efficacy depends on targeted neural decompression (determined by intraoperative nerve root mobility) rather than the maximal removal of disc tissue or extensive laminoforaminotomy.

abstract: Daphnia is a widely recognised model organism in ecotoxicological studies, exhibiting environmental sex determination. Environmental cues such as temperature, photoperiod and crowding are known to trigger transitions from parthenogenetic to sexual reproduction. Experimental studies based on exogenous exposure suggest that methyl farnesoate (MF), a juvenile hormone-like compound, is associated with male production and predator-induced defensive traits in Daphnia; however, direct evidence of endogenous MF production and environmental dynamics remains limited. In this study, we investigated the release of endogenous MF into the rearing water of Daphnia pulex. Two D. pulex clonal lineages differing in propensity for male, ephippia and neckteeth production were selected. Experimental conditions simulating crowding and different habitat suitability, including variations in population density, food availability, photoperiod and temperature, were investigated. MF was quantified at ultra-trace levels using solid-phase microextraction coupled to gas chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. In the first generation, MF concentrations decreased from approximately 18.5-20.0 ng/L in controls to 11.0-14.5 ng/L under crowding conditions and 6.7-7.2 ng/L under crowding combined with MK-801. In the second generation, concentrations were approximately 10.5 ng/L in control offspring and 12.0-12.3 ng/L after recovery from crowding. Exposure to crowding over two generations resulted in clone-specific concentrations, whereas MF remained below the limit of quantification of 0.08 ng/L, when parental females had been exposed to MK-801. In the density and seasonal experiments, MF released in the medium was higher release per female under early-spring conditions and in clone S. These variations occurred under conditions promoting male production, ephippia formation and antipredator responses. While not demonstrating a causal endocrine role of MF, our findings provide quantitative and environmentally relevant evidence that D. pulex releases MF into the aquatic environment and this release is modulated by both environmental conditions and genetic background.

abstract: Objective The aim of the study was to investigate whether the addition of an erector spinae plane block (ESPB) to surgical intercostal nerve block (INB) provides additional postoperative analgesic benefits in patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS). Methods This prospective, randomized controlled trial included 60 adult patients undergoing elective three-port VATS. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either combined ESPB plus INB (EI) or INB alone. Patients, surgeons, ward nurses, postoperative outcome assessors, and data analysts were blinded to group assignment, whereas the anesthesiologists performing the intervention were unblinded. The primary outcome was pain intensity at 1 hour postoperatively, assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS). Prespecified secondary outcomes included repeated postoperative NRS pain assessments through 48 hours and cumulative opioid consumption at 24 hours. Results The NRS pain score at 1 hour postoperatively was 5.83 ± 2.86 in the EI group and 5.52 ± 3.10 in the INB group (mean difference 0.31, 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.25 to 1.87, p = 0.691). In a post hoc exploratory longitudinal analysis, a linear mixed-effects model demonstrated no significant group-by-time interaction in postoperative NRS pain scores (F[7, 401.2] = 0.81, p = 0.581). Cumulative opioid consumption at 24 hours, expressed as intravenous morphine equivalents, was 41.0 mg (interquartile range [IQR], 31.0-58.5) in the EI group and 40.0 mg (IQR, 29.1-48.3) in the INB group (between-group difference, 3.0 mg; 95% CI, -6.2 to 12.0; p = 0.501). Conclusions Adding single-injection ESPB to surgical INB did not significantly reduce 1-hour postoperative pain scores or 24-hour opioid consumption following VATS. Larger adequately powered studies are required to determine whether smaller clinically relevant incremental benefits exist. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03949790.

abstract: Background Advanced HIV disease (AHD) remains a significant public health challenge, despite the widespread scale-up of antiretroviral therapy (ART) in South Africa. Understanding long-term treatment outcomes among patients with AHD under routine programmatic conditions is critical. However, there is a paucity of longitudinal data on clinical outcomes in this population, particularly within high-HIV prevalence rural settings. This study evaluated retention in care and virological outcomes among patients initiating ART with AHD in rural KwaZulu-Natal between 2008 and 2020. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using routine data from 10 public health facilities. Adults (≥18 years) with CD4 < 200 cells/μL or WHO stage 3/4 who initiated ART between January 1, 2008, and December 31, 2020, were included. Primary outcomes were retention in care at 6, 12, 24, 36, and 48 months. Secondary outcomes included viral load (VL) completion and suppression (<1000 copies/μL). Competing risk regression and Poisson regression models were used to identify factors associated with loss to follow-up (LTFU) and virological suppression. Results Of 40,432 individuals who initiated ART between 2008 and 2020, 9,608 met the criteria for AHD. Retention in care was 98%, 94%, 89%, and 85% at 12, 24, 36, and 48 months, respectively. Men (adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [aSHR]: 1.35; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.23-1.47) and individuals with CD4 counts <100 cells/µL (aSHR: 1.13; 95% CI: 1.08-1.26) had a higher risk of loss to follow-up. Although viral load (VL) completion declined over time (49.3% at 6 months to 31.5% at 48 months), suppression remained above 83% among those with available VL data. Undetectable VL increased from 25.5% to 33.0% between 12 and 48 months. Patients initiating ART during the Universal Test and Treat (UTT) era (2016-2020) had higher retention (78.8%) than those treated between 2012-2015 (62.8%) and higher viral load (VL) suppression (risk ratio [RR]: 1.13; 95% CI: 1.01-1.28) compared with the 2008-2011 cohort. Women (RR 1.18; 95% CI: 1.11-1.25) and those initiating ART within 7 days (RR 1.30; 95% CI: 1.04-1.38) were more likely to achieve virological suppression at any time point. Conclusion This study demonstrates high retention and virological suppression rates among patients with AHD in rural South Africa, particularly under the UTT strategy. Despite these successes, VL testing uptake remains suboptimal, and a considerable gap persists in achieving undetectable VL levels. Integrating the WHO AHD care package and prioritizing early ART initiation and male-focused interventions may further improve outcomes and support efforts to end the HIV epidemic.

abstract: Background Iliotibial Band Syndrome (ITBS) lacks effective conservative treatment protocols, often relying on expert opinion without addressing individual factors. This study compared the effectiveness of integrating foam rolling and stretching exercises with strengthening routines versus strengthening exercises alone in athletes with ITBS. Twenty athletes with confirmed ITBS (11 males, 9 females; mean age: 33.6 ± 9.5 years) were randomized into two groups: the Integrated Training Group (ITG, n = 10) and the Strengthening-Focused Group (SFG, n = 10). Both underwent 24 sessions over eight weeks intervention, lasting 25-30 minutes per session. Outcomes included a primary measure of pain intensity (Visual Analog Scale) and secondary measures of lower extremity function (LEFS), hip abductor strength, iliotibial band flexibility, and quality of life (SF-36), were measured pre- and post-intervention. The ITG showed significantly greater improvements in pain reduction (79.7% vs. 81.0% reduction, p = 0.02), lower extremity function (25.7% vs. 21% improvement, p = 0.02), iliotibial band flexibility (59.4% vs. 1.7% improvement, p = 0.001), and overall QoL (19.9% vs. 12.6% improvement, p = 0.006) compared to the SFG. However, no significant differences were noted in hip abductor strength or physical and psychological QoL components (p > 0.05). Based on the sample examined, integrating foam rolling and stretching with strengthening exercises versus strengthening exercises alone resulted in greater improvements in pain, lower extremity physical function, iliotibial band flexibility, and overall QoL. However, additional studies with larger sample sizes and in other populations are needed before definitive conclusions can be reached.

abstract: How protein sequences evolve to maintain functional conformational dynamics under thermal stress remains an important question in molecular evolution. Thermophilic enzymes are often considered to achieve stability primarily through enhanced structural rigidity, yet thermal adaptation may also involve the preservation or reorganization of correlated motions across the protein scaffold. Here, we compared three glycoside hydrolase family 1 β-glucosidases-BsBgl1A, 9UPT, and LQBG8-that share a conserved (β/α)8 TIM-barrel fold but display distinct optimal temperatures of approximately 45, 65, and 70 °C, respectively. By integrating comparative structural analysis, three independent 1 μs molecular dynamics simulations at 300, 325, and 350 K, neural relational inference of residue-level dynamic coupling, and family-level coevolutionary analysis, we identified distinct dynamic strategies associated with their thermal phenotypes. All three enzymes retained their global compactness and principal secondary-structure framework across the simulated temperatures, indicating that differences in RMSD and residue flexibility did not reflect large-scale unfolding. BsBgl1A showed the strongest temperature sensitivity, with increased structural deviation and residue mobility at 350 K. Its inferred interaction network exhibited a non-monotonic response, characterized by pronounced overcoupling at 325 K followed by reduced connectivity at 350 K. In contrast, 9UPT maintained relatively restrained residue dynamics and a highly reproducible coupling topology across temperatures. LQBG8 combined substantial local conformational flexibility with persistent long-range coupling and retained the highest directed network density at 350 K. Across the three enzymes, the βα5-βα7 region repeatedly emerged as a shared structural and dynamic center. Coevolutionary couplings were also enriched in TIM-barrel-associated regions that spatially converged on this sector. These findings indicate that thermal adaptation in GH1 β-glucosidases is not adequately explained by uniform structural rigidification. Instead, enzymes with the same conserved fold may adopt distinct organizations of correlated motion, while greater thermal adaptation is associated with the persistence or reorganization of a βα5-βα7-centered dynamic coupling pattern under elevated temperature. The correspondence between dynamic coupling and coevolutionary enrichment is consistent with long-term evolutionary constraint on this structural sector, although it does not establish direct selection on the network as an independent functional unit. Our results therefore provide a testable framework in which thermostability reflects a balance among local stabilization, regional flexibility, and the resilience of higher-order dynamic organization.

abstract: Introduction The COVID-19 pandemic posed significant challenges not only to healthcare systems but also to healthcare professionals. This study explores the experiences, perceptions, and perceived burdens of healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients undergoing oncological surgery during the pandemic, with a particular focus on clinical staff working in hospital-based care in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Methods A qualitative, interpretive-hermeneutic approach was employed using one focus group and one individual semi-structured interview. Participants were healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients undergoing oncological surgery. The focus group included 12 participants, and one additional participant took part in an individual interview. The transcripts were independently coded and analytically annotated by two researchers and systematically analyzed in an iterative process using MAXQDA. The analysis combined deductively informed codes derived from the interview guide with inductively developed codes emerging from the data. The study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) reporting statement. Results In September 2024, one focus group and one individual interview were conducted with a total of 13 participants, predominantly nurses and nursing assistants. Nine categories were identified. Participants described substantial emotional, professional, and organizational burdens during the COVID-19 pandemic, including stress, anxiety, increased demands, uncertainty, and difficulties in maintaining usual standards of patient care. Participants also reported challenges related to postponed or adapted oncological treatments, communication with patients under infection-control measures, postoperative care under capacity constraints, team collaboration, and the availability and use of personal protective equipment. Political measures, changing regulations, and the occupational vaccination mandate were perceived by participants as sources of uncertainty, frustration, and reduced autonomy. Despite these challenges, participants also described experiences of team cohesion and professional commitment. Participants expressed a need for clearer guidance, accessible contact persons, psychosocial support, supervision, and greater involvement in decision-making. Conclusion The findings suggest that healthcare professionals involved in hospital-based oncological surgical care experienced substantial emotional, ethical, and organizational challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants' accounts indicate that pandemic preparedness should extend beyond infection control and include clear communication, consistent guidance, psychosocial support, supervision, and adequate organizational resources. Given the small, convenience-based, and predominantly nursing sample, these findings should be interpreted as context-specific accounts rather than as representative of healthcare professionals in oncological surgery as a whole.

abstract: Background Hypertension requires lifelong treatment and regular follow-up to prevent complications; however, lost to follow-up (LTFU) remains a major challenge in long-term hypertension care, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Objective This study explored patient perspectives on barriers contributing to LTFU in hypertension management. Methods A qualitative study was conducted among 32 hypertensive patients who were LTFU at a tertiary care hospital in Coastal Karnataka, India. Participants were aged 31-69years, with 21 (65.6%) men and 11 (34.4%) women. Participants were identified through hospital records and interviewed using a semi-structured interview guide. Interviews were conducted from February to April 2026 Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically following COREQ guidelines. Results Six major themes emerged.: (1) illness perception and self-management practices, (2) care-seeking and follow-up behaviour, (3) structural and socioeconomic barriers, (4) health system and continuity gaps, (5) patient-perceived strategies to improve continuity of care, and (6) health information continuity and interoperability needs. Participants described symptom-driven healthcare seeking, medication non-adherence, occupational responsibilities, and competing family priorities contributing to irregular follow-up. Financial burden, including treatment costs, transportation expenses, and wage loss, substantially affected continuity of care. Long travel distances, dependence on family members, overcrowding, rushed consultations, and inadequate follow-up mechanisms further influenced disengagement from care. Participants also reported fragmented healthcare utilisation, repeated investigations, dependence on paper-based records, and poor continuity of medical information across healthcare facilities. Several participants perceived that integrated digital health information systems, decentralised services, appointment reminders, and improved counselling could strengthen long-term hypertension follow-up. Conclusions LTFU in hypertension care is influenced by interconnected individual, socioeconomic, and health system-related barriers. A notable finding was the fragmented nature of continuity of care and poor health information continuity across healthcare facilities. Strengthening patient-centred follow-up systems, decentralised chronic disease services, financial protection mechanisms, and interoperable health information systems may improve continuity of hypertension care and reduce long-term disengagement from chronic disease management.

abstract: Background An efficient referral system is an important but often under-recognized determinant of survival in critically ill children. Previous studies have reported high mortality rates among pediatric patients transferred to tertiary care facilities. This study aimed to identify factors associated with Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) mortality among critically ill children transferred and admitted to a tertiary-level referral hospital in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Material and methods This prospective cohort study was conducted over a 12-month period (July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024) and included all critically ill children admitted to the PICU following interhospital referral. Demographic, clinical, referral, and transport data were prospectively collected. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with PICU mortality. Results A total of 334 children were included, with a median age of 6 years. PICU mortality was 25.4%. The most common referral indication based on the Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT) was central nervous system dysfunction. Pre-referral management most commonly included oxygen therapy, antibiotic administration, and fluid resuscitation. Compared with survivors, non-survivors had higher PELOD-2 scores and were more likely to require intubation, mechanical ventilation, and vasoactive support before referral. In the multivariable analysis, pre-referral vasoactive support (adjusted OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.20-4.15; P = 0.011) and higher PELOD-2 scores within the first 24 hours after PICU admission (adjusted OR 1.32 per 1-point increase, 95% CI 1.20-1.45; P < 0.001) were independently associated with PICU mortality. Referral distance, decision time, and transfer time were not independently associated with mortality. Conclusion PICU mortality among critically ill children transferred and admitted to a tertiary-care hospital in Indonesia remains high. Pre-referral vasoactive support and higher PELOD-2 scores at PICU admission were independently associated with PICU mortality. These findings generate the hypothesis that improvements in early stabilization and communication may improve outcomes, warranting prospective evaluation.

abstract: Background Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (IPTp-SP) is a key preventive strategy. However, optimal uptake remains inconsistent despite high antenatal care (ANC) attendance. This study assessed factors associated with optimal IPTp-SP uptake and explored the experiences of postpartum women in rural Ghana. Methods A convergent parallel mixed-method study was conducted among 1,155 postpartum women attending child welfare clinics in Jomoro, Prestea-Huni Valley and Ellembelle districts of the Western Region of Ghana. Quantitative data were collected using structured questionnaires and analysed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests. Qualitative data from in-depth interviews and focus group discussions were analysed thematically to explore women's experiences and perceptions. Results Among the 1,155 women enrolled, 812 (70.3%) took three or more doses of IPTp-SP (IPTp3-SP). Knowledge of malaria in pregnancy was high, with 92.7% correctly identifying its mode of transmission and 91.7% identifying ways of preventing malaria during pregnancy. Factors independently associated with IPTp3-SP included age 10-19 years compared with 20-29 years (aOR 2.17, 95% CI 1.21-3.88), gravidity of three compared with one (aOR 2.67, 95% CI: 1.58-4.50), and gravidity of four compared with one (aOR 1.83, 95% CI: 1.02-3.28). Lower odds were observed among uninsured women (aOR 0.36, 95% CI: 0.20-0.64), single women (aOR 0.64, 95% CI: 0.42-0.97), and cohabiting women (aOR 0.52, 95% CI: 0.34-0.79). ANC attendance showed a strong association with IPTp3-SP: women attending <4 ANC visits had lower odds of receiving IPTp3-SP than those attending 10 or more visits (aOR 0.08, 95% CI: 0.04-0.15). Nausea, dizziness, weakness, abdominal discomfort, vomiting and difficulty chewing the tablets affected their experiences and, for some women, willingness to continue treatment. Conclusions IPTp-SP uptake was relatively high. Predictors of optimal uptake include age, education, marital status, gravidity, health insurance status, and number of ANC visits. Women with fewer ANC visits were less likely to receive three or more doses. Reported side effects posed barriers to adherence. Strengthening ANC attendance and counselling on IPTp-SP expected side effects may improve completion of recommended doses.

abstract: HIV self-testing (HIVST) is a crucial strategy to reach the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets by increasing testing coverage in high-burden areas like Uganda. The ConfiSign HIV Self-Test, a blood-based, direct-sampling, vertical flow, single-use rapid test, demonstrated perfect sensitivity and specificity during laboratory validation. This study assessed its performance and operational characteristics in the field compared to the Wondfo HIV Self-Test, which served as the standard of care. A cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted from 09 April 2025 to 30 May 2025 at 15 health facilities in Uganda. Participants (n = 2,434, aged ≥14 years) performed self-testing with ConfiSign and Wondfo (standard of care) under observation. Diagnostic accuracy was calculated against Wondfo. Usability, acceptability, and feasibility were evaluated via questionnaires (n = 798 for usability/acceptability; n = 90 for feasibility). Discordant results were resolved using ELISA and PCR. Participants were predominantly female (61.7%) and aged 18-29 (51.8%). ConfiSign positivity was 6.2% versus 6.0% for Wondfo. Sensitivity was 100%, specificity 99.8% (95% CI: 99.53-99.93). Three discordant results were resolved as negative via PCR and ELISA. Usability was high, with 94.7% of users finding components easy to handle and 83.3% collecting samples without difficulty. Acceptability was strong, as 98.0% would reuse the test and 99.0% would recommend it. Feasibility assessments across operational, usability, performance, economic, and acceptability domains yielded positive scores, supporting integration into Uganda's HIV testing framework. These findings confirm the kit's diagnostic accuracy and ease of use in field settings, supporting its adoption for HIVST in Uganda. We suggest improvements such as instructions in the local language and the inclusion of additional gauze for better acceptance.

abstract: The injection molding of bridge-type compliant mechanisms is sensitive to non-uniform mold temperature because the thin flexure hinges are prone to premature solidification and incomplete filling. This study evaluates a fluid-layer-assisted mold temperature-control architecture using experimental thermography, transient thermo-fluid simulation, a representative straight-channel thermal baseline, melt-filling analysis, and displacement testing of molded HDPE mechanisms. The fluid-layer thermo-fluid model was validated against infrared measurements, yielding a mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.01 °C and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 6.44 °C across six validation points. Under the numerical benchmark condition of an 80 °C inlet temperature, a mass flow rate of 59.5 g/s, and 40 s heating, the fluid-layer architecture was predicted to increase the average cavity-surface temperature by approximately 4.0 °C and reduce the maximum longitudinal temperature difference by 28.6% relative to the straight-channel model. Independent thermography of a representative steel straight-channel insert under the same inlet-temperature and flow-rate conditions showed a lower and more non-uniform surface-temperature field than the steel fluid-layer configuration, confirming the direction of the predicted thermal advantage. Melt-filling simulations subsequently predicted incomplete filling at the thin flexure region for the straight-channel configuration and complete filling for the fluid-layer configuration; this filling comparison remains simulation-based. For HDPE blends containing 0-25 wt% recycled material, the molded mechanisms retained an approximately linear input-output displacement response over the investigated range. At an input displacement of approximately 175 µm, the mean output displacement decreased from 857 µm for virgin HDPE to 745 µm at 25 wt% recycled HDPE. The results support the fluid-layer architecture as a conventionally machinable approach for improving mold-surface thermal control, while polymer morphology, fatigue durability, and experimental straight-channel filling remain subjects for future work.

abstract: This study examines how organisational and technological antecedents shape management accounting information quality and adoption level among Vietnamese small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and how these characteristics influence decision quality and business performance, with business environment uncertainty as a moderator. Using a cross-sectional survey of 503 Vietnamese SME managers, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and importance-performance map analysis to test a five-antecedent serial mediation model grounded in contingency theory and information processing theory. All ten hypotheses were supported. Information technology capability was the strongest driver of accounting information quality (β = 0.508), and market competition intensity was the strongest driver of adoption level (β = 0.385). Decision quality was the strongest direct driver of business performance (β = 0.558), and business environment uncertainty positively moderated this relationship (β = 0.238). All five serial indirect paths to business performance were statistically significant. The importance-performance analysis identified information technology capability as the highest-priority investment area, combining high importance with low realised performance (52.01 out of 100). To our knowledge, this study offers one of the first comprehensive tests of a serial mediation model linking these antecedents to business performance through accounting characteristics and decision quality in Vietnamese SMEs, one of the first importance-performance prioritisation maps for managers in this context, and extends contingency theory by identifying business environment uncertainty as a pure moderator rather than a direct antecedent. Findings suggest Vietnamese SME managers should prioritise digital accounting infrastructure investment ahead of expanding accounting tool adoption, and that government support for digital accounting tools may be warranted. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, partly addressed through theoretically grounded antecedent ordering, predictive validity testing, and multi-method bias assessment; the single-country scope reflects Vietnam's structural representativeness of wider ASEAN transition economies.

abstract: Digital media can increase the visibility of living heritage without securing understanding or sustained engagement. We examined how public digital discourse about the Twenty-Four Solar Terms can be translated into an interpretive stimulus and how users evaluate it. We collected 3,433 publicly visible online text units and retained 1,101 after cleaning and anonymisation. The retained corpus informed collaborative thematic reading; 1,089 texts met the token threshold for keyword extraction and auxiliary topic-model inspection. Thematic analysis identified six cultural theme categories. They covered seasonal diet and bodily care; temporal order and heritage knowledge; and natural phenology and seasonal perception. They also covered folk customs and ritual life; aesthetic imagery and digital creative expression; and agricultural production and everyday practice. These categories informed a five-page storyboard through theme-design mapping and expert-assisted review. Survey data from 350 valid respondents were analysed with covariance-based structural equation modelling (CB-SEM) and supplementary fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). Information clarity, visual aesthetics, perceived explorability and perceived authenticity were positively associated with perceived cultural value. Perceived explorability had the largest standardised path estimate for cultural value, and perceived authenticity was also associated with cultural identity. Perceived cultural value and cultural identity were associated with sustained cultural engagement intention. Configurational analysis identified four sufficient configurations for high engagement and four for low engagement. The two solution sets were asymmetric rather than mirror images. These findings link perceived interpretive qualities, cultural value and cultural identity with sustained cultural engagement intention.

abstract: Post‑conflict cities exhibit profound socio‑spatial fractures, institutional weakness, and eroded public trust. Conventional planning repeatedly fails to address ethnic segregation, accessibility disparities, and social fragmentation. The aim of this study is to propose and empirically validate an integrated model, the Gamified Spatial-Participatory Model (GSPM), that combines spatial justice theory, participatory co-design, and conflict-sensitive gamification to foster social cohesion. Using Kabul, Afghanistan, as a paradigmatic case, a sequential mixed‑methods design was employed. Quantitative spatial diagnostics mapped severe accessibility deficits, while qualitative inquiry identified deep trust deficits and cultural barriers; these jointly informed gamified co‑design workshops as the intervention. Pilot results provide strong preliminary evidence of GSPM efficacy: 90% of participants reported substantially increased engagement; gamification correlated strongly with intergroup trust (r = 0.76, p < 0.01); perceived accessibility improved by 38% in intervention areas. Critically, 70% of women and 55% of ethnic minorities reported meaningfully stronger belonging. The study demonstrates that this approach shifts planning epistemology from technocratic to deeply human, operationalising spatial justice in fragile settings, and offers transferable principles for fostering inclusion in divided urban contexts.

abstract: Control of mold-cavity surface temperature strongly affects filling, premature frozen-layer formation, and cycle time in thin-wall injection molding. This study evaluates an induction self-heating insert with a thin heating zone directly coupled to a cooling layer using experiments, a sequentially coupled electromagnetic-thermal model, and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN). The design space contains 25 Taguchi L25 geometries defined by T, W, and L; X and Y coordinates are added so that the ANN predicts the surface temperature field. Three cooling states are considered: No Water (NW), Stagnant Water (SW), and Flowing Water (FW). Experimental ANN targets are the mean of five repeated tests. The simulation reproduced the location of the hot zone; among four cases with reported quantitative differences, three differed by no more than about 10 °C and one showed a peak difference of about 20 °C. To prevent data leakage, all 846 points from each geometry were kept together during geometry-wise validation. The resulting R² values were 0.746, 0.653, and 0.493 for NW, SW, and FW, with Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) values of 17.03, 12.97, and 12.62 °C, respectively. The effects of T, W, and L depended on the cooling state and were not consistently monotonic. A proof-of-concept molding test showed complete filling of a Chip 2 part using Low-Density Polyethylene (LDPE); the mean spacing was 28.6 µm for a nominal 30 µm, and the mean height was 106.6 µm for a nominal 100 µm. These results show that combining insert geometry, cooling-water state, and a surrogate model can support local thermal design, delay frozen-layer formation, and improve filling in injection molding.

abstract: The autonomic nervous system regulates cardiovascular homeostasis during stressors such as heat, but the effects of type 2 diabetes (T2D) with hypertension on such responses are unclear. Twenty male participants (10 with type 2 diabetes and hypertension and 10 age-matched healthy controls; mean ages 64 ± 4.14 and 63 ± 5.42 years) underwent a 90-minute whole-body heat exposure at 40 °C and 50% relative humidity. Heart rate variability (HRV), baroreflex sensitivity (BRS), and blood pressure variability (BPV) were assessed before, during and after the heat exposure. Heat exposure increased heart rate in both groups but this response was less in T2D (5.43 bpm; ~ 7% increase) versus controls (13.96 bpm; ~ 22% increase; p = 0.014). Similarly, reductions in HRV indices to heat stress were generally smaller in magnitude among participants with T2D. For example, high-frequency power (HF RR) decreased by 31.21 ms² (~54.5% reduction) in T2D because of heat exposure, compared with a reduction of 179.35 ms² (~74% reduction) in controls (p = 0.038). Further, LF BRS decreased by 1.07 ms/mmHg (~25% reduction) vs. 3.96 ms/mmHg (~51% reduction) (p = 0.021), HF BRS by 1.58 ms/mmHg (~35% reduction) vs. 4.15 ms/mmHg (~62% reduction) (p = 0.034), and mean BRS by 1.18 ms/mmHg (~26% reduction) vs. 4.16 ms/mmHg (~58% reduction) (p = 0.010) in those with T2D versus controls, respectively. Low-frequency power (LF RR), LF/HF ratio and BPV parameters also showed smaller (though nonsignificant) changes in T2D. Overall, combined T2D and hypertension produced blunted autonomic responses to short-term heat exposure, potentially increasing vulnerability to temperature extremes.

abstract: This work investigates a plasmonic metal-insulator-metal (MIM) ring structure periodically coupled to dual resonators and a defect cell, engineered for infrared filtering and gas sensing. The optical response is modeled numerically using the finite element method in COMSOL Multiphysics, enabling accurate analysis of strong field confinement and loss in the subwavelength MIM geometry. By tuning the geometrical parameters of the rectangular and lateral resonators and of the defect cavity, we show that the transmission spectrum, band-gap position, and defect resonance wavelength can be precisely controlled, and that introducing a defect resonator into a periodic dual-resonator array generates a sharp, highly localized mode inside the plasmonic band gap. Small variations of the refractive index in the gas-filled device lead to clear, nearly linear shifts of this defect resonance, yielding a high sensitivity of about 1920 nm/RIU together with a Q-factor above 100 and a low detection limit, so that sensitivity, spectral selectivity, and detection capability are simultaneously enhanced. These results highlight the novelty of combining periodic band-gap engineering, dual-resonator coupling, and defect optimization in a single MIM platform, and demonstrate that the proposed structure can function as both a narrowband photonic filter and a high-performance infrared gas sensor in a compact, integrated configuration.

abstract: Open-access biodiversity databases are valuable resources in the structuring and accessibility of species occurrence data. By compiling different data sources, they reveal the uneven spatial distribution of knowledge, with certain areas and taxonomic groups being better represented. Understanding the determinants of spatial and taxonomic knowledge gaps helps in informing the use of open-access data. Here, we identified determinants of knowledge gaps within a French regional biodiversity database, in the largest administrative region in France. Knowledge gaps were assessed using two metrics, completeness and ignorance scores, for 8 taxonomic groups covering five vertebrate and three insect groups. The data were analyzed for the entire region, but also at the level of the three former sub-regions, to identify the potential drivers that may account for knowledge gaps' determinants locally. Our findings show that insects were characterized by higher knowledge gaps than vertebrates. Overall, knowledge gaps are influenced by variables related to sites' accessibility rather than ecological appeal across both metrics. All groups shared similar determinants of gaps, except for the impact of agricultural pressure which is found to be more significant for insects than vertebrates. Ultimately, our study emphasizes the impact of biodiversity governance, through local funding and regional political decisions, on knowledge distribution in open-access databases. We recommend limiting these biases by redirecting biodiversity funding towards under-sampled taxonomic groups and under-prospected areas. When not possible, users of data extracted from these databases should correct for spatial-sampling biases (SSP) using maps of knowledge gaps in order to get a more accurate understanding of species occurrence.

abstract: Nicotinic acetylcholinergic receptors (nAChRs), comprising of α and β subunits are present in the brain and whole body. The less abundant α2-subunit is a fast-acting receptor subtype and plays an important role in cognition and learning. To understand cellular functional consequences, this study evaluated glucose metabolism using [18F]FDG PET/CT in α2 knockout (α2KO) and α2 hypersensitive (α2HS) mice. Control (CN; 4M, 3F), α2 knockout (α2KO; 4M, 4F) and α2 hypersensitive (α2HS; 4M,4F), 12-16 month old mice were used. Mice were fasted and injected with [18F]FDG (3-5 MBq) while awake. After 40 minutes they underwent whole body PET/CT. On a separate day, nicotine challenge [18F]FDG studies were done. Reconstructed images were analyzed to obtain standard uptake values (SUV) of [18F]FDG in brain and interscapular brown adipose tissue (IBAT). Statistical analysis was performed comparing the three groups of mice. The α2HS male mice exhibited the largest brain increase in [18F]FDG compared to α2KO male mice. The rank order of brain [18F]FDG uptake in the three groups: α2HS♂ > CN♂ > α2KO♂ > CN♀= = α2KO♀ ≥ α2HS♀. Nicotine treatment reduced brain [18F]FDG uptake in all mice. Females had lower [18F]FDG uptake compared to males and were less sensitive to α2 nAChR. In the case of IBAT, α2KO mice had significantly higher baseline [18F]FDG uptake compared to the other two groups: α2KO♂ > α2KO♀ > α2HS♀ > α2HS♂ > CN♀ > CN♂. Nicotine decreased IBAT in α2KO mice rather than increase as observed in CN and α2HS mice.This preliminary study shows that α2 nAChRs play a significant role in brain activation as exhibited by the increase in [18F]FDG in α2HS mice. In the absence of regulatory control by the α2 nAChR, the α2KO mice IBAT exhibited higher [18F]FDG uptake compared to controls and α2HS mice. Female mice were less affected by nicotine compared to the male mice.

abstract: Microbial strains undergo notable biomass expansion in industrial applications subjecting populations to Darwinian selection. The consequent adaptive evolution may threaten the often tediously developed desired metabolic traits of the strains, such as flavor or platform chemical production. Yet, it remains unresolved how to predict the evolutionary trait robustness. Here, we propose TRAEV (Trait Robustness Against EVolution), a computational framework for in silico prediction of evolutionary robustness of metabolic traits and trajectories of desired traits in application environments. TRAEV uses constraint-based metabolic models for predicting environment-dependent trait-fitness dependencies and accounts for the stochasticity of adaptive evolution by using Monte Carlo-based perturbation analysis. First, TRAEV predicts the immediate metabolic phenotype in the new environment, and then, the subsequent evolutionary trajectories of fitness and desired trait. Metabolic trait robustness is quantified from the evolutionary trajectories as two scores: Robustness Score (RS) and Trade-off Score (TS). RS represents trait robustness and the overall trait level during evolutionary adaptation, whereas TS captures trait-fitness trade-offs. We validated TRAEV by predicting relative evolutionary robustness of heterologous pigmentation of two engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains and two desired aroma generation traits by multiple wine strains of S. cerevisiae if they were developed via a laboratory selection process. Thus, we showed how TRAEV predictions could guide strain development. TRAEV can be integrated into computational strain design workflows across microbial strains, desired metabolic traits, and application environments. Ultimately, model-predicted evolutionary robustness of desired metabolic traits can guide both strain and process development and help enhancing the economic attractiveness of industrial applications using microbial cells.

abstract: Introduction In the United Kingdom (UK) thousands of wild animals enter veterinary clinics and wildlife centres requiring medical support and rehabilitation care due to natural and anthropogenic diseases and injuries. The objectives of this empirical research were to survey veterinary professionals, wildlife centre personnel and academic educators to explore the influences of culture, working relationships, education and professional obligations on wildlife treatment experienced by the veterinary community. Methods A mixed-method of a semi-quantitative survey and qualitative interviews was conducted. Purposive, convenience sampling was used for an online survey which was completed by 409 veterinary participants and 20 veterinary professionals, seven wildlife centre personnel and six academic educators were interviewed. The survey data was analysed descriptively and the interview data was analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Themes associated with promoting wildlife treatment composed of Competency, Motivation and Collaborations. Themes associated with inhibiting wildlife treatment consisted of Uncertainty, Lack of Resources and Conflicts. The Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (RCVS) had an influential role on both promoter and inhibitor themes. Conclusion A proactive wildlife medicine culture in the UK would benefit from the recognition and promotion of the values and benefits of working with wildlife. Starting with the inclusion of wildlife medicine to veterinary curricular. Support and communication within and between veterinary practices and wildlife centres to utilitise resources and information, develop networks and mitigate challenges to promote competency, motivation and collaboration. With support from the RCVS to refine educational and professional standards and enforce the regulation of the veterinary community in their provision of wildlife medicine.

abstract: To enhance the operational stability of the power system and address the issues of weak inertia support and sluggish dynamic response of traditional inverter control strategies when dealing with complex scenarios involving a high proportion of new energy sources, a new intelligent control strategy has been proposed. This study adopts the VSG control strategy as the core technology for the regulation of wind-solar-storage power generation inverters, and divides the dynamic response process into acceleration period, deceleration period, reverse acceleration period and reverse deceleration period. Different control strategies are adopted for different system states at different stages. Additionally, the DDPG algorithm is introduced, and the single DDPG agent is extended to a multi-agent interactive deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm. Finally, the multi-agent collaborative optimization is achieved in a "centralized training and decentralized execution" form. The research results show that in the case of sudden load increase, the voltage deviation at the grid connection point is stabilized at 371.7 V, and the voltage recovery time is significantly shorter than the comparison strategy. At the same time, the time-weighted absolute error integral reaches optimal values of 1.82 V/s2 and 1.85 V/s2 in scenarios of sudden load increase and sudden drops in photovoltaic power, and the strategy efficiency reaches 97.83%, and the steady-state accuracy reaches 99.63%, demonstrating superior control capabilities. In the three typical fault conditions of practical application, the average frequency deviation of the control strategy was 0.197 Hz, the number of protection lockouts was 0.3 times, the average depth of voltage sag was 24.63%, the average recovery time was 1.21 hours, and the number of abnormal warnings did not exceed 5 times. The proposed framework for coordinated wind, solar, and storage regulation, based on distributed power generation and virtual synchronous machine, can effectively support the safe, flexible, and efficient operation of the new power system under high penetration of renewable energy.

abstract: A major threat to the stability of pipes crossing rivers at width is scouring around such structures. Pipe failure and the consequent serious damage to and life-threatening cutoff of vital streams are possible outcomes of this phenomenon. Although numerous studies have investigated scour around pipes in straight channels and bends, changes in bed topography along the straight reach downstream of a sharp bend, which is affected by the complex flow pattern issuing from the bend, have received less attention. Therefore, this study examines the effect of pipe installation at the end of a sharp bend and its influence on the downstream bed topography along the straight reach. In addition, from both an operational and hydraulic perspective, placing the pipe outside the bend would be a preferable option for designers and engineers. The study investigated, among others, the pipe position relative to the bed level as well as the hydrographic parameters in terms of flow unsteadiness and the effect these could have on the pattern of scouring downstream of the 180-degree sharp bend. The experiments were conducted under three pipe-installation conditions relative to the initial bed level, namely level with the bed, above the bed, and buried, with the pipe positioned perpendicular to the flow direction and under four different ratios of hydrograph peak timing to flood duration in unsteady flow. To evaluate the effects of different pipe installation conditions as well as the flow hydrograph, parameters such as the extent of scour-hole development, the maximum scour depth, the maximum deposition height, and the bed topography changes in the straight reach downstream of the bend were measured and analyzed. The main focus of the research was toward identification of the scour hole development and the maximum scour depth variations and how this phenomenon interacted with the stated parameters. The study findings indicated that the most critical case of bed topography variations under the influence of pipe occurred when the pipe was in a level position with the bed, where altering the pipe level from bed level to buried levels decreased the maximum scour and sedimentation by respectively 37.1% and 38.0%. Furthermore, alteration of unsteady-flow related parameters had less effect toward scour reduction than that of pipe level position with respect to the initial bed level. The findings of this study can be used to identify the most suitable pipe installation condition in the straight reach downstream of sharp bends, reduce scour risk, predict bed changes, and improve the design and protection of pipelines in river engineering projects.

abstract: Background Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is a key mediator of neuroplasticity and has been associated with disease progression in multiple sclerosis (MS). While aerobic exercise is consistently linked to BDNF modulation, the specific contribution of isolated resistance training (RT) remains unclear, as previous reviews have largely combined multimodal exercise interventions. Objective To systematically review and meta-analyze the effects of isolated RT on peripheral BDNF levels in individuals with MS (PROSPERO: CRD420251141069). Methods Searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Scielo, Scopus, PEDro and Cochrane up to January 10, 2026, using PICOT criteria. Controlled experimental studies investigating isolated RT and BDNF outcomes were included. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2.0 and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Due to methodological heterogeneity, a random-effects model was applied to estimate pooled effects. Results Four studies (three RCTs and one controlled non-randomized trial), totaling 126 participants with MS, were included. Interventions lasted 8-24 weeks, with training frequencies of 2-3 sessions per week. Meta-analytic synthesis revealed positive pooled effects (SMD = 0.49; 95%CI: 0.15 to 0.83; Z = 2.80; p < 0.005; I2  = 0%; Q = 1.681) with wide confidence intervals without crossing zero. With the Hartung-Knapp adjustment, due to the reduced number of studies, the analysis continued to show a positive intervention effect: (SMD = 0.49; 95%CI: 0.42 to 0.56; t = 3.716; p = 0.0339). Two studies using low-to-moderate intensity protocols (Pilates-based RT and low-load RT with bands/weights) showed significant increases in serum BDNF after 8 weeks. In contrast, studies employing higher loads (≈80% of one-repetition maximum: 1RM) demonstrated no significant BDNF changes despite functional gains. Overall certainty of evidence was rated as low due to risk of bias, inconsistency, and imprecision. Conclusion Isolated RT may increase peripheral BDNF levels in individuals with MS, but this effect is supported by limited and low-certainty evidence. Furthermore, given that only four studies were included in the meta-analysis, we suggest interpreting the results with some caution.

abstract: Distinguishing closely related viral strains requires identifying genomic regions where subtle sequence differences carry biological significance. While k-mer-based approaches offer computational efficiency for genome analysis, existing methods lack standardized frameworks for evaluating which k-mers are most informative. Current selection strategies focus primarily on statistical discriminative power without integrating biological context. We introduce KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a k-mer prioritization framework combining three components: an information-theoretic method measuring strain-distinguishing capacity, an optimized amino acid substitution matrix (MIYATA_EVO) for mutation impact assessment, and a protein characterization score derived from annotations and database cross-references retrieved through UniProt. All three component scores and the integrated KSS are bounded in [0,1] by construction, providing a common numerical scale for ranking positions within a dataset. The discriminative component achieved a mean F1 of 0.881, not significantly different from chi-squared (0.876), the strongest of eight baselines. Top-ranked selections from the discriminative component nonetheless differed from those produced by chi-squared, especially for SARS-CoV-2 and HIV-1. The MIYATA_EVO matrix, optimized using a genetic algorithm, increased the composite agreement score across eight amino acid characteristics by 28.4% over the original MIYATA matrix. Across 17,471 viral proteins, the protein characterization score tracked UniProt's five-level annotation score closely (Kendall's τ=0.775), as expected for measures drawing on overlapping annotation content. Within each level, the continuous score provided finer numerical resolution among proteins. Literature cross-referencing on SARS-CoV-2 (278,738 sequences, 19 Pango-derived lineage labels), HIV-1 (12,223 sequences, 15 subtype labels), and human cytomegalovirus (HCMV; 399-646 sequences, 4-8 locus-specific genotypes) found that the top-ranked k-mers reported here map to established variant-defining mutations, subtype-specific polymorphisms, and genotype markers. KSS provides a standardized framework for viral k-mer prioritization with potential applications in variant surveillance, molecular epidemiology, and functional annotation. The tool is available at https://github.com/bioinfoUQAM/KmerSignificanceScore.

abstract: Emotional barriers can shape participation in second-language (L2) learning, yet evidence about affective support attributed to artificial intelligence (AI) remains conceptually and methodologically uneven. This cross-sectional online survey examined university-affiliated L2 English learners' reported emotional challenges, perceptions of AI-mediated affective support, and views of the boundary between AI and teacher support. The Chinese-language, researcher-developed questionnaire used categorical and multiple-response items rather than psychometric scales. Of 425 submissions, one non-university respondent and four respondents younger than 18 years were excluded, yielding an adult analytical sample of 420. The non-probability convenience sample was institutionally concentrated and should not be interpreted as representative of all Chinese university L2 learners. Frequencies, percentages, and three Pearson chi-square tests were calculated. Helplessness (59.05%), fatigue (55.95%), and anxiety (53.33%) were the most frequently reported emotional challenges. Overall, 67.38% perceived that AI could provide affective support, and 84.76% reported using AI for learning challenges. Immediate feedback was the most frequently selected support mechanism (79.52%), while relief of learning pressure or anxiety was the most frequently selected function (70.71%). Perceived AI affective support was associated with reported motivation change, χ²(2) = 53.27, p < .001, Cramér's V = .356, and interest change, χ²(2) = 59.57, p < .001, V = .377. The combined belief that AI might fill or replace teacher affective support was associated with continuing need for teacher support, χ²(1) = 72.97, p < .001, φ = .417. These results indicate patterned learner perceptions, not causal effects or evidence that AI possesses genuine emotion. AI may offer scalable, low-pressure support for routine learning, whereas teachers remain important for relational, contextual, and pedagogical judgment. Longitudinal studies using validated measures are needed.

abstract: Manual sorting of date fruits is time-consuming and labor-intensive, while automated optical sorting lines remain costly for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This study presents a deployment-oriented benchmark of five lightweight object detectors for single-fruit date-variety recognition, namely the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based YOLOv8, YOLOv10, YOLOv11, and YOLOv12 Nano variants and the Transformer-based D-Fine-Nano, with RT-DETR-Large included as a high-capacity accuracy reference. Models were evaluated on 1,658 controlled-environment images of nine commercial varieties using grouped 5-fold cross-validation, which kept identified repeat photographs of the same fruit within the same cross-validation fold. Latency was measured on an NVIDIA T4-class edge GPU/industrial-PC accelerator, and the CNN detectors were also exported to Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) and TensorRT half-precision (FP16) engines. All Nano models met the 30 frames-per-second threshold for model-side detection latency under the tested conditions and achieved high accuracy, while a Friedman-Nemenyi analysis detected no statistically significant accuracy difference among the lightweight models. Under TensorRT FP16, YOLOv10-Nano achieved the lowest model-side end-to-end latency of 6.27 ms with no observed accuracy degradation. YOLOv8-Nano attained the lowest inference-stage latency of 3.31 ms, but its mean average precision (mAP@50-95) decreased by 1.2 percentage points after TensorRT FP16 conversion. YOLOv12-Nano had the numerically highest mean cross-validation mAP@50-95 and the lowest fold-to-fold variability, albeit at higher latency. These findings characterize model-level detector behavior rather than a complete sorting line. Within that scope, YOLOv10-Nano represents one practical configuration for a T4/TensorRT FP16 pipeline, while the other models offer different speed, stability, and deployment trade-offs, providing SMEs with a well-characterized starting point for the vision component of affordable date-sorting systems.

abstract: Objective Problematic micro-drama use (PMDU) has received increasing attention as micro-dramas have become widely consumed among young adults in China. This study examined the associations between academic stress and PMDU among Chinese university students, explored which dimensions of academic stress were uniquely associated with PMDU, and examined the associations between PMDU and loneliness, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 510 Chinese university students. Participants completed measures of academic stress, PMDU, loneliness, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms. Multiple linear regression analyses were conducted while controlling for gender and age. The Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure was applied to relevant families of multiple tests. Results Higher academic stress was associated with greater PMDU (β = .447, p < .001). Among the five dimensions of academic stress, learning effectiveness pressure remained significantly associated with PMDU after correction for multiple comparisons (β = .292, FDR-adjusted p < .001), whereas the other dimensions did not show statistically significant unique associations after correction. PMDU was positively associated with loneliness (β = .331), depressive symptoms (β = .323), and anxiety symptoms (β = .305), and all three associations remained significant after FDR correction (all FDR-adjusted p < .001). Conclusions Academic stress, particularly stress related to perceived learning effectiveness, was associated with greater problematic micro-drama use among Chinese university students. Higher PMDU was also associated with greater loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. These findings identify PMDU as a media-use behavior relevant to both academic stress and psychological well-being, although the cross-sectional design does not establish the direction of these associations.

abstract: Purpose This study investigated apoptosis-related responses to a standardized 24-hour lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge in primary limbal stromal cells (LSCs) derived from patients with congenital aniridia (AN-LSCs) and control donors. Methods LSCs were isolated from limbal tissue obtained from patients with congenital aniridia and control donors. Cells were treated with 0, 2.5, 10, and 17.5 µg/mL LPS for 24 hours. Apoptosis was assessed using Annexin V-APC/PI staining and flow cytometry. Apoptosis-related mRNA levels were quantified by qPCR, cell-associated protein fluorescence was assessed by flow cytometry, and secreted TNF-α was measured by ELISA. Results The mean basal apoptosis rate was numerically higher in AN-LSCs than in control LSCs (2.10% vs. 0.52%), although the donor-level difference was not statistically significant. The exploratory linear mixed-effects model showed a significant main effect of LPS condition and a significant Group × LPS interaction. Apoptosis increased significantly at 10 and 17.5 µg/mL LPS compared with the corresponding untreated condition in both groups, and the increase from the untreated condition to 17.5 µg/mL LPS was significantly greater in AN-LSCs than in control LSCs (adjusted P = 0.003). qPCR and flow-cytometry analyses identified marker-specific LPS-associated changes, but no molecular Group × LPS interaction reached statistical significance. Cell-associated TNF-α fluorescence was distinguished from secreted TNF-α measured by ELISA. Conclusions Acute LPS exposure increased apoptosis in both groups, with a greater increase in AN-LSCs at the highest concentration. Molecular changes were marker- and concentration-specific without evidence of differential molecular response patterns between groups. Given the small number of independent donors, the marked donor-age imbalance, and the acute nature of the model, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in a larger independent cohort of appropriately age-matched donors.

abstract: Introduction The COVID-19 pandemic significantly affected physical activity and lifestyle, potentially increasing Body Mass Index (BMI) and obesity risk. We examined changes in BMI and obesity across Pre-Pandemic, Pandemic Peak, and Peri-Pandemic periods and identified sociodemographic correlates. Methods We analyzed longitudinal electronic health record data from the All of Us Research Program for adults ≥18 years with at least one BMI record in each period (N = 38,632). Periods were defined as Pre-Pandemic (Jan 1, 2018-Mar 12, 2020), Pandemic Peak (Mar 13, 2020-Dec 31, 2021), and Peri-Pandemic (Jan 1, 2022-Oct 31, 2023). BMI was modeled using linear mixed-effects models and obesity (BMI ≥ 30) using GEE logit models, adjusting for age, sex, race, ethnicity, income, and employment. A sensitivity analysis was conducted by expanding eligibility to participants with BMI data in at least two periods (N = 83,698). Results Mean BMI increased from 30.05 (SD = 6.67) Pre-Pandemic to 30.14 (SD = 6.76) during the Pandemic Peak, then declined to 29.96 (SD = 6.66) Peri-Pandemic; obesity prevalence followed a similar pattern (43.1% → 43.4% → 42.8%). In adjusted models, the linear time effects were positive and the quadratic terms negative for both outcomes (BMI: β = 0.218 and -0.018; obesity: aORs = 1.053 and 0.996; all p < 0.001). Female, Black/African American, and Hispanic/Latino participants had higher adjusted BMI and greater odds of obesity than their respective reference groups, while higher income was associated with lower BMI and obesity odds. Significant time × subgroup interactions were observed, with age and employment status showing the most consistent effects across both outcomes. Conclusion BMI and obesity displayed statistically detectable but modest changes across the pandemic-defined periods. Persistent adjusted differences by sex, race, ethnicity, and income highlight the relevance of equitable access to obesity-prevention resources.

abstract: The literature used for teaching law in universities during the nineteenth century played a decisive role in shaping legal cultures and facilitating the transnational circulation of legal ideas. However, existing research on this topic remains fragmented across disciplines, time, regions, and historiographical traditions. This scoping review aims to systematically map and synthesize the existing academic literature on the books used for teaching law in universities in Anglophonic and Hispanophone countries during the nineteenth century. Following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI, Adapted from JBI. JBI scoping review template. Adelaide: Joanna Briggs Institute; 2020. Available from: https://jbi.global/ebp) guidelines, the review will identify and categorize studies addressing what law manuals, treatises, and other pedagogical texts were employed, as well as the scholarly interpretations of their circulation and use. By gathering the literature that addresses the research question, "What books were employed to teach law in universities in Anglophonic and Hispanophone countries in the nineteenth century?", we hope to assess the scope of existing research and provide a structured foundation for future studies in intellectual history and the history of universities. This article presents the a priori protocol detailing the planned methodology for conducting the Scoping Review.

abstract: Background Hypertension case-finding and management is key to reducing premature morbidity and mortality. In England, 14.8% of people receive treatment for hypertension but the total number of hypertensive individuals remains unclear, as it can only be estimated statistically. This study aimed to estimate how many individuals aged 40 + may unknowingly have hypertension by accounting for differences between clinic and out-of-office blood pressure readings. Methods We analysed individual-level data from the 2017-2019 Health Survey for England (HSE), including individuals aged ≥40 without a hypertension diagnosis. A validated algorithm (Predicting Out-of-Office Blood Pressure- PROOF-BP) was applied to estimate likely out-of-office measurements. Observed BP was defined as the mean of the second and third measurement taken at an HSE visit. Predicted hypertension was calculated using PROOF-BP and observed hypertension using actual clinic measurements. We explored a diagnostic threshold for predicted (out-of-office) hypertension of ≥135/85 mmHg (primary outcome) and of ≥140/90 mmHg (secondary outcome). Weighted hypertension prevalence estimates are presented by age, sex and geographical region. National population statistics were used to extrapolate results to the English population. Results The observed prevalence of undiagnosed hypertension in the study population was 27.7% (95% Confidence Interval [CI]:26.4%-29.1%). The predicted prevalence after adjustment was 21.8% (95%CI:20.6%-23.0%). Predicted prevalence was nearly double in males (29.8%, 95%CI:27.8%-32.0%) compared to females (14.6%, 95%CI:13.3%-15.9%) and varied by region: West Midlands (26.3%, 95%CI:22.2%-31.0%), London (16.9%, 95%CI:13.5%-20.9%). Extrapolating estimates to the total population aged ≥40 in England we estimate approximately 4.2 million people in England are unaware of their hypertension. Of these we estimate that over 2.9 million could be newly diagnosed by the current diagnostic pathway. Conclusions Over 4 million people in England are estimated to have undiagnosed hypertension. This study's refined analytical approach provides a more precise estimate of this population, supporting targeted public health initiatives to identify and address undiagnosed cases.

abstract: Background and aims Neuron-specific enolase 2 (ENO2) has been implicated in tumor metabolism, but its biological role in hepatocellular carcinoma remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to investigate the expression, prognostic relevance, and functional role of ENO2 in HCC. Methods Public transcriptomic datasets, RNA sequencing, WGCNA, survival analyses, and pathway enrichment analyses were integrated to identify HCC-associated genes. ENO2 expression was validated in HCC cell lines and paired clinical tissues.Gain- and loss-of-function, catalytic-rescue, glycolytic-inhibition, and pyruvate-rescue experiments were performed to evaluate glycolytic activity, proliferation, colony formation, migration, invasion, and tumor growth. Results ENO2 was upregulated in HCC and was associated with advanced tumor stage and unfavorable survival outcomes in public datasets. ENO2 overexpression increased glycolytic activity and malignant phenotypes, whereas ENO2 depletion produced opposite effects. In ENO2-depleted cells, re-expression of shRNA-resistant ENO2 wild type restored the impaired glycolytic and malignant phenotypes, whereas the catalytic-deficient ENO2 mutant failed to restore them. Moreover, 2-deoxy-D-glucose attenuated ENO2 overexpression-associated phenotypes, while pyruvate partially rescued phenotypes associated with ENO2 depletion. ENO2 expression was also associated with altered PI3K and AKT phosphorylation. Conclusions ENO2 may contribute to HCC progression by enhancing glycolytic metabolism and malignant phenotypes, partly in association with PI3K/AKT signaling. ENO2 is a candidate metabolic and prognostic biomarker that requires validation in larger independent clinical cohorts and warrants further investigation as a therapeutic candidate.

abstract: Introduction and objectives Artificial intelligence (AI) is a branch of computer science capable of mimicking human cognitive functions. The integration of AI has significantly transformed healthcare and medical education. In medical education, AI has played a crucial role in improving students' educational experiences. However, evidence from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) such as Iraq remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to assess medical students' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) toward AI in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Materials and methods This cross-sectional study was carried out among medical students in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, between 3rd November 2025 and 20th January 2026. A structured, self-administered questionnaire was delivered to students either by paper and pen or digitally using the Google Form platform. A total of 575 medical students were recruited. The final piloted questionnaire consisted of 39 items and was divided into five distinct sections: basic demographics, knowledge, attitudes, practices, and perceived barriers. Results The mean age of the study participants was 21.31 ± 1.7 SD years, and the representation between both genders was approximately equal. Additionally, only one-fifth (19.7%) of the students had attended a workshop about AI in healthcare and medical education. The internet/social media was the most common information source utilized by the students (77.7%). Moreover, AI was most frequently used for homework/assignments (56.5%), and the most significant barrier limiting AI use was fear of over-reliance (53.2%). Female students had significantly lower odds of having better knowledge (adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 0.34; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.22-0.51; p<0.001), and positive attitudes (aOR: 0.46; 95% CI: 0.28-0.77; p=0.003) compared to male counterparts. Additionally, students from Duhok Medical College had significantly lower odds of having positive attitudes (aOR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.30-0.88; p=0.014). Conclusions The present study revealed suboptimal levels of KAP regarding AI among the surveyed medical students. Integrating structured AI education into medical school curricula may strengthen students' understanding and competencies in AI, thereby resulting in better preparedness for AI application in future practice.
