abstract: Purpose This study examined the global landscape of mental health literacy (MHL) education for health professions students, focusing on publication trends, intervention designs, pedagogical approaches, MHL domains addressed, evaluation methods, and contextual influences. Methods Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, an Evidence and Gap Mapping (EGM) scoping review was conducted to identify and visually synthesize MHL education interventions. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCOhost (including CINAHL, PsycINFO, and ERIC), and APA PsycArticles (February 1997-May 2025). The included studies involved pre-licensure health professions students and implemented structured educational interventions explicitly targeting MHL domains. The data were extracted using a standardized framework and analyzed through descriptive synthesis and visual mapping to identify research clusters and gaps. PROSPERO registration: CRD420251050891. Results Fifty-five studies met the inclusion criteria for this review. Notably, the number of publications increased significantly after 2016, with most of the evidence coming from Europe, the Western Pacific, and the Americas, while representation from the African and Eastern Mediterranean regions was limited. Quasi-experimental designs were the most common, characterized by short-term, classroom-based interventions primarily targeting specific professions, particularly nursing and medicine. Although traditional didactic teaching methods remained prevalent, experiential strategies such as simulation, role-play, and reflective practices were increasingly adopted. Within the existing body of evidence, interventions predominantly emphasized knowledge, attitudes, and confidence, whereas skills development, behavioral change, self-awareness, and help-seeking were less consistently addressed. Furthermore, evaluations mostly relied on short-term, self-reported outcomes, with few studies examining behavioral change or long-term impacts. Conclusions MHL education for future health professionals is expanding but remains unevenly distributed, pedagogically conservative, and methodologically limited. Advancing the field will require longitudinal, theory-informed, and experiential approaches, stronger evaluation designs, integration of lived-experience perspectives, and targeted capacity-building in low- and middle-income settings.

abstract: Background This study offers an observational evaluation of how viral and bacterial infections co-occur with alterations in the microbiome and survival of Penaeus vannamei post-larvae, one of the most economically important species in global aquaculture. Methods Eleven commercial larval production tanks were classified into three distinct infection scenarios using histology and PCR: Baculovirus penaei (BP) monoinfection, mixed infections (BP, white spot syndrome virus [WSSV], and acute hepatopancreatic necrosis disease [AHPND]-causing bacteria), and non-infected controls. High-molecular-weight DNA was subjected to shotgun metagenomic sequencing on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform, followed by evaluation of microbial diversity, community structure, and infection-associated microbial signatures. Results Although BP was the most abundant viral genus across infected groups, severe mortality was observed only under mixed-infection conditions, which were closely associated with AHPND-causing bacteria presence and microbiome disruption rather than with BP alone. Deep metagenomic sequencing revealed reduced, distinct microbiome structures in shrimp infected with BP and in those with mixed infections, compared to non-infected individuals. Non-infected post-larvae maintained complex and well-balanced bacterial communities, predominantly composed of Donghicola and Muricauda. Nudiviridae and Oscillospiraceae showed comparable relative abundances in BP-only and mixed-infection groups. In contrast, mixed infections were characterized by a relative increase in Vibrio, together with the PCR-detection of PirAB toxin genes, whereas WSSV remained detectable in the metagenomic dataset despite its comparatively low relative abundance, while the infection remained thermally suppressed and asymptomatic in the larvae. Functionally, infected larval microbiomes were enriched for transposases, retrotransposons, and virulence-factor genes. The near-complete BP-GR25 genome (119,245 bp) was assembled and annotated from larval metagenomes. Conclusion These results highlight the value of high-throughput sequencing in the early detection of pathogens in aquaculture, where subtle microbial shifts during postlarval stages can be valuable indicators of health status for production.

abstract: An inserted SINE-VNTR-Alu(AGAGGG)n repeat into the TAF1 gene is the cause of X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism. Mosaic divergent repeat interruptions affecting both motif length and sequence (mDRILS) of the canonical repeat (AGAGGG)n arise and can diminish repeat instability and delay disease age of onset. The repeat itself may affect gain-of-function disease pathways. Consequently, XDP etiology may involve unusual structures formed by the repeats. To study the effects of mDRILS on the formation of unusual structures of the XDP TAF1-SVA repeat, we designed a series of G-rich DNA and RNA oligonucleotides having the pure canonical repeat 5'-(AGAGGG)4-3', or either of the most common mDRILS 5'-(AGAGGG)2AGGG(AGAGGG)-3'; and 5'-(AGAGGG)2AGG(AGAGGG)-3'. Circular dichroism, thermal melting, binding of the G-quadruplex ligand TMPyP4, shows the first canonical and AGGG-interrupted sequence assume K+-sensitive stable G-quadruplexes, whereas GA duplexes are the prominent structure in the AGG-interrupted form. The complementary C-rich strands, 5'-(CCCTCT)4-3', and 5'-(CCCTCT)2CCCT(CCCTCT)-3', and 5'-(CCCTCT)2CCT(CCCTCT)-3', assumed i-motif-compatible structure. Mixtures of the G- and C-rich complementary sequences, at 1:2 ratios, showed triplex-forming propensity for the canonical and AGGG-interrupted, but not the AGG-interrupted forms. The ability of mDRILS to elicit modifications of the disease-causing XDP TAF1-SVA repeat to enable or disable the formation of specific structures, such as quadruplex and triplex structures, may explain in part how mDRILS mediate their disease-modifying effects.

abstract: Modern library areas require constant environmental adjustment to preserve user comfort and promote learning efficiency. This investigation offers a Multi-Sensor Internet of Things (IoT) Data Source and Artificial Intelligence-Based Adaptation Control Model for Library Indoor Systems, which is intended to transform heterogeneous sensing data into intelligent real-time environmental management decisions. A Multi-Sensor IoT Library Indoor Environment Dataset containing 2,745 time-stamped observations was developed, thereby capturing dynamic indoor environmental variations. Normalization and noise smoothing processes were performed before the analysis of the collected data for improving the quality of the analysis. In order to detect the most useful features of the environment, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was used to perform dimension reduction and simplify calculations. The proposed approach includes edge sensing, intelligent data processing, and actuator cooperation for implementing an efficient closed-loop environmental management system. To classify indoor environmental conditions, a Colony Predation Algorithm enhanced with Random Adaptive Boosting (CPA-RAdaBoost) was developed, where CPA maximizes feature weights and model hyperparameters, Random Forest (RF) enhances ensemble variety, and Adaptive Boosting strengthens the identification of complicated and border environmental conditions. The adaptive control instructions for HVAC, lighting and ventilation are formulated considering the prevailing environmental conditions to facilitate indoor environment control. Experimental implementation using Python demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework, reaching a MAE of 3.9 and control accuracy of 97.1%, indicating its capacity for intelligent, responsive, and energy-efficient smart library environmental management.

abstract: Breast cancer (BC) represents a major global health concern. Lifestyle factors influence both prevention and prognosis, but evidence on their impact on oncological response to BC treatment remains limited. We present the protocol of a randomized clinical trial designed to assess whether a multimodal intervention-combining physical exercise, psychological support, and nutritional counseling during neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC)-could improve pathological response, measured by the Residual Cancer Burden (RCB) index, in women with early BC. A total of 216 women will be randomized (1:1) to control (standard of care, n = 108) or intervention (n = 108). The intervention consists of a supervised, individualized multimodal prehabilitation program that combines physical exercise, psychotherapy, and nutritional support delivered throughout NAC (4-6 months). Tumor pathology, including microenvironment analysis, will be assessed before NAC and after surgery. Data will be collected at baseline, preoperatively, and at 1 and 12 months postoperatively. Long-term oncological outcomes will be reported annually for a minimum of 5 years, with the intention to extend to 10 years. We hypothesize that the intervention group will show higher pathological response rates than controls, with a targeted 20-percentage point improvement in the rate of favorable RCB response (fRCB, defined as RCB class 0 or I), from approximately 40% in the control group to 60% in the intervention group. Additional expected benefits include improved tolerance to NAC, better quality of life, enhanced postoperative recovery, and optimized physical, psychological, and nutritional status. Differences in tumor microenvironment profiles are also anticipated. Ethics approval was granted by the Ethics Committee of the Hospital Clínic de Barcelona (HCB/2023/1036, 26 March 2024). Written informed consent will be obtained from all participants. The DIANA trial will provide evidence on multimodal prehabilitation as a non-invasive, cost-efficient strategy to improve both health and oncological outcomes in BC. Findings will be disseminated via peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, and patient groups. Trial Registration Number: NCT07107594.

abstract: Computational prediction of ABL1 tyrosine-kinase inhibitor (TKI) resistance is difficult because available mutation-drug datasets are small, imbalanced, and heterogeneous. This study evaluates structure-aware resistance prediction under mutation-disjoint internal validation and temporal cross-study outcome validation. The development benchmark comprised 144 ABL1 mutation-TKI records (19 resistant and 125 susceptible) labelled by a ten-fold affinity-loss criterion. A fixed panel of 11 documented structural and energetic predictors was used to minimize data-adaptive feature selection within the validation framework. A calibrated ensemble combining Elastic-Net logistic regression, radial-basis-function support-vector machines, random forests, and XGBoost was evaluated using mutation-disjoint five-fold grouped out-of-fold prediction repeated ten times. Temporal validation used a later prime-editing resistance map, yielding 84 exact mutation-TKI matches across imatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib, and ponatinib; 61 had binary Sensitive/Resistant outcomes and 23 were retained as Intermediate. The 11-feature stack achieved grouped internal AUROC 0.645 (95% CI 0.429-0.830) and PR-AUC 0.230, with mean ± SD AUROC 0.583 ± 0.101 across repeated grouped splits. On the 61 binary later-study outcomes, AUROC was 0.605 (95% CI 0.431-0.874) and PR-AUC 0.835, modestly above the resistance-prevalence baseline of 0.770. External calibration was poor (Brier score 0.583; calibration slope 0.441). Elastic-Net showed somewhat higher temporal discrimination (AUROC 0.643; PR-AUC 0.877). These results indicate limited transportability across mutation identities and experimental platforms and support use of the framework for hypothesis-generating resistance screening rather than clinically calibrated treatment selection.

abstract: Infill fracturing of mature wells involves re-fracturing within previously stimulated clusters, targeting unstimulated regions of the parent well's fracture network. This strategy sustainably enhances hydrocarbon recovery from depleted reservoirs without the environmental footprint of new drilling. Establishing a numerical simulation model for this process is essential for optimization. In this study, a numerical model for mature well infill fracturing was developed based on the extended finite element method and a free-drainage boundary module. The results indicate that prior production from mature wells primarily affects the fracture length and curvature in the infill wells. As infill fracturing-induced fractures propagate toward the far-field region, they are significantly influenced by the heterogeneous pore pressure distribution in the reservoir. This leads to a pronounced increase in fracture curvature. Compared with conventional fracturing, the curvature of fractures under infill fracturing is approximately 30% higher within the same simulation time, while the fracture length is notably shorter. With the increase in production time, fractures in infill wells tend to exhibit greater tortuosity. This enhanced complexity allows for more effective contact between the fractures and the reservoir, thereby improving the production potential of the infill wells to some extent.

abstract: Background Physical activity (PA) is essential for healthy ageing, yet older adults in rural areas face particular constraints. This study applied Amartya Sen's Capability Approach to examine how older adults in a rural German municipality perceive their opportunities for an active lifestyle and to identify factors associated with high PA engagement. Methods A cross-sectional total population survey was conducted in a rural municipality in Bavaria, Germany. All residents aged ≥60 years (N = 593) were invited by post. Perceived capabilities were assessed using an instrument grounded in the Capability Approach. High PA engagement was defined as being physically active for at least 30 minutes on ≥4 days per week. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify associated factors; multiple imputation by chained equations was used as a sensitivity analysis. Results The response rate was 33.0% (N = 196); 166 respondents (84.7%) had complete data for the primary model. Mean age was 69.5 years (SD 7.6); 49.0% were men. Most participants (58.8%) rated their health as good, and 23.5% met the threshold for high PA engagement. Mean daily sedentary time was 6.12 hours (SD 3.37), higher in men than in women (6.64 vs 5.61 hours, p = 0.043). In the multivariable model, fewer perceived environmental opportunities were independently associated with lower odds of high PA engagement (OR 0.59 per SD, 95% CI 0.37-0.95), and poorer self-rated health showed a comparable association that did not reach conventional significance (OR 0.65 per SD, 95% CI 0.41-1.02). Under multiple imputation the association with poorer self-rated health was statistically significant (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.38-0.94), as was male sex (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.20-0.95), whereas the association with perceived environmental opportunities was no longer significant (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.43-1.03). Age and social support were not associated with PA engagement. Living alone was associated with markedly lower perceived capabilities across several domains. Conclusions Perceived environmental opportunities and health status, rather than information or social support, distinguished more from less active older adults in this rural setting. Capability-enhancing interventions should prioritise the built environment and should give particular attention to older adults living alone. Community-Based Participatory Research may help match provision to the capability sets of rural residents.

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly support time-consuming conceptual modeling tasks such as building or combining models from text. In this context, causal maps are labeled, directed graphs that represent causal relationships (edges) between selected factors (nodes) in a problem domain. Modelers control the output through the LLM's prompt and decoding parameters such as temperature, and recent studies either use a default temperature or minimize it by expecting that it supports replicability. However, evidence about this expectation remains limited, as does our understanding of how different LLMs and decoding or prompting strategies shape results. We assess the extent to which findings are an artifact of the LLM or its variability rather than a reflection of the modeler's controls. We focus on the common conceptual modeling task of combining models, exemplified through three algorithms that reflect a variety of prompting techniques. We use five LLMs (DeepSeek, Gemini, GPT, Qwen, Ministral) and different versions to account for the potential impact of the architectures. Using the Design of Experiments approach of factorial analyses (supplemented by paired tests and confidence interval checks), our results show that outcomes differ significantly across LLMs and versions. Depending on the algorithm, randomness from the LLM can be the dominating factor, responsible for up to 96% of the variation in results. This happens even if we directly control the decoding, as evidenced by our comparison of greedy, beam-search, and contrastive decoding. We find that prompt effects are systematic but metric-dependent, while decoding affects performance but there is no universally best strategy. Since our findings suggest that replicability of conceptual modeling studies using LLMs may be limited, future studies may report the distribution of performance measures alongside exact model, decoding, replication, and baseline-normalization settings.

abstract: Osteoporosis is a progressive skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone mineral density and increased susceptibility to fractures, making early diagnosis essential for effective clinical intervention and long-term patient management. Recent advances in artificial intelligence have demonstrated significant potential for automated bone disease assessment using medical imaging modalities. In this study, a unified deep learning framework, termed OsteoNet-X, is proposed for automated osteoporosis detection and multi-class bone health classification using knee X-ray images. Unlike conventional image classification approaches, OsteoNet-X integrates YOLO-based Region of Interest (ROI) localization, DenseNet-based feature extraction, Feature-Aware Learning (FAL) optimization, and Grad-CAM-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enhance both classification performance and model interpretability. The ROI extraction stage automatically identifies anatomically relevant knee joint regions, reducing background interference and enabling more discriminative feature learning. Subsequently, DenseNet facilitates efficient feature propagation and hierarchical representation learning for distinguishing normal, osteopenia, and osteoporosis conditions. The incorporation of XAI further provides visual explanations of model decisions by highlighting clinically relevant regions within the knee joint. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that OsteoNet-X achieves a classification accuracy of 97.08%, a macro F1-score of 96.61%, and a weighted F1-score of 97.11%.

abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a progressive degenerative joint disease characterized by cartilage degeneration, synovial inflammation, and subchondral bone remodeling. Oxidative stress plays a critical role in KOA pathogenesis. This study aimed to identify oxidative stress-related hub genes by integrating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with machine learning to uncover potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for KOA. ScRNA-seq data from KOA cartilage tissues were obtained from the GEO database to characterize cellular heterogeneity and identify disease-associated chondrocyte subsets. CellChat was used to analyze intercellular communication, and Monocle2 was applied to reconstruct cell differentiation trajectories. Oxidative stress activity at the single-cell level was evaluated using AUCell, while high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) was performed to identify oxidative stress-related gene modules. Candidate genes were screened using Venn analysis and further refined by LASSO regression, SVM-RFE, and XGBoost combined with SHAP analysis. Diagnostic performance was assessed, and biological relevance was explored through immune infiltration and pathway analyses. Experimental validation was conducted using qRT-PCR and western blot assays in H2O2-treated chondrocytes. InfC and ProFC were detected specifically in OA cartilage and exhibited high oxidative stress activity. InfC was enriched in inflammatory and immune-related pathways, whereas ProFC was associated with cell cycle regulation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Integrated hdWGCNA and machine-learning analyses consistently identified CYBA and SPP1 as candidate genes. The two-gene model achieved bootstrap-corrected AUCs of 0.937 and 0.825 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. qRT-PCR and western blot analyses further showed increased CYBA and SPP1 expression in H2O2-treated chondrocytes. Conclusion InfC and ProFC may represent OA-associated chondrocyte states characterized by enhanced oxidative stress, while CYBA and SPP1 may serve as candidate diagnostic biomarkers. Given the small cohort sizes and preliminary in vitro validation, these findings require confirmation in larger independent cohorts and functional studies.

abstract: PaECTER is an open-source document-level encoder specific to patents. We fine-tune BERT for Patents with examiner-added citation information to generate numerical representations for patent documents. PaECTER performs better in similarity tasks than current state-of-the-art models used in the patent domain. More specifically, our model outperforms the patent specific pre-trained language model (BERT for Patents) and general-purpose text embedding models (e.g., E5, GTE, and BGE) on our patent citation prediction test dataset on different rank evaluation metrics. PaECTER predicts at least one most similar patent at a rank of 1.32 on average when compared against 25 irrelevant patents. Numerical representations generated by PaECTER from patent text can be used for downstream tasks such as classification, tracing knowledge flows, or semantic similarity search. Semantic similarity search is especially relevant in the context of prior art search for both inventors and patent examiners.

abstract: Background Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic, progressive liver disease characterised by biliary inflammation. Its exact aetiology remains unclear. This study aimed to use a combination of diagnostic methods and blood analysis to better understand the metabolic changes accompanying PSC. Methods PSC patients (n = 60) and healthy controls (n = 60) were evaluated by magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy (hepatic fat and iron content), ultrasonography, standard blood analysis expanded with markers of iron metabolism, and colonoscopy. Results PSC patients exhibited significant liver fibrosis and elevated liver enzymes. Serum hepcidin was increased (p < 0.01), but PSC patients did not show any markers of anaemia. Serum iron concentration and transferrin saturation were increased compared with healthy controls (p < 0.0001 and p < 0.001, respectively) but did not reach levels seen in hemochromatosis. In contrast, the liver iron content was lower in PSC patients (p < 0.0001). Conclusion PSC patients demonstrated an atypical pattern of iron metabolism: elevated circulating iron and depleted liver iron stores despite increased hepcidin levels. This paradox suggests a disruption of hepcidin-mediated iron regulation, potentially sustaining a proinflammatory environment. Further investigation is warranted to clarify underlying mechanisms and therapeutic implications. Trial registration Clinical Trials I.D.: NCT06026449.

abstract: Online group polarization surrounding sports events has emerged as a significant challenge for digital public opinion governance. Drawing on social combustion theory, the study identifies seven explanatory conditions: political triggers, news narrative frames, opinion leaders, capital intervention, first media, event attributes, and stakeholder participation. Using a sample of 24 recent high-profile sporting events, the study employs crisp-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (cs QCA) to investigate the configurational pathways leading to online group polarization and to generate insights for its mitigation. The findings identify five distinct pathways through which online group polarization in sports events emerges, revealing two underlying generative mechanisms. The first is the "sensitive issues-emotional narrative" mechanism, while the second is the "non-sensitive issues-capital involvement" mechanism.

abstract: Background Photobiomodulation (LLLT) is used for myogenous temporomandibular disorders (TMD), but longer-term comparative evidence versus stabilization splints alongside structured self-management remains limited. This study aims to compare pain reduction and maximum painless mouth opening after photobiomodulation+self-management (PBM + SM) versus stabilization splint+self-management (OS + SM), with an additional self-management-only comparator (SM), over 48 weeks. Methods This partially randomized controlled study enrolled 66 patients with DC/TMD-diagnosed acute masticatory muscle pain. Forty-four participants consenting to intervention were randomized 1:1 to PBM + SM (660-nm diode laser, twice weekly, 10 sessions) or OS + SM (maxillary stabilization splint worn at night, 8 h/day for 2 months). Both intervention groups received the same SM programme (education, habit modification, and jaw exercises for 2 months). A non-randomized convenience group received SM alone (n = 22). Assessments were performed at baseline and weeks 2, 4, 12, 24, and 48. Primary outcomes were VAS pain (0-10) and maximum painless mouth opening (MPMO, mm). Secondary outcomes included masticatory muscle tenderness and Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC). Longitudinal analyses used linear mixed-effects models. Results All groups improved over time, with earlier improvement in both intervention arms. In the randomized comparison, PBM + SM and OS + SM showed comparable week-48 outcomes for VAS pain and MPMO. No significant between-group difference in masticatory muscle tender points was observed at week 48 after Holm adjustment. Comparisons involving the SM-only group were exploratory. Conclusions Over 48 weeks, PBM + SM and OS + SM produced comparable improvements in pain and maximum painless mouth opening, with no significant between-group difference in masticatory muscle tender points at week 48. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06419738.

abstract: Phytophthora diversity in urban forested freshwater systems of Fairfax County, Virginia was investigated by sampling 15 streams in the spring and fall from 2021 to 2024. A total of 163 isolates were identified. Based on multilocus sequence and phylogenetic analyses, they were categorized into 14 taxa belonging to 7 Phytophthora subclades including P. pseudocitrophthora in subclade 2a, P. pini in subclade 2c, P. chlamydospora, P. gonapodyides, P. matreminventam sp. nov., P. taxon bitahaiensis, and P. t. sylvatica in subclade 6b, P. lacustris in subclade 6d, P. honggalleglyana, P. irrigata, P. virginiana sensu lato, and P. sp. × Hennops in subclade 9a, P. t. polonicoides in subclade 9b, and P. intercalaris in subclade 10c. Notably, P. matreminventam sp. nov. named in this study was determined to be the maternal parent of P. × stagnum based on their unique genetic traits. Although a few species recovered in this study reportedly possess innate pathogenicity to woody plants, no significant symptoms of Phytophthora diseases were observed in the nearby forests at the sampling sites.

abstract: Brinjal (Solanum melongena L.) requires considerable soil moisture throughout its life cycle, therefore, its cultivation in water constraint area is difficult. Though different soil moisture conservation technologies and lower water use irrigation systems have been developed for crop cultivation, their successful deployment largely depends on the locality, especially on soil characteristics. This study evaluated the effects of irrigation regimes, mulching practices, and their combination on growth, stress physiology and irrigation water use efficiency (IWUE) of brinjal across two field locations with contrasting soil conditions. Location 1 had coarser soil, lower nutrient and organic matter content profiles and lower water-holding capacity than location 2. The experiment comprised three irrigation levels [rainfed (I0), conventional furrow irrigation (IC), and drip irrigation (ID)] and three mulching treatments [no mulch (M0), straw mulch (MS), and plastic mulch (MP)] with three replications at both locations. Irrigation and mulching both significantly influenced growth, stress indicators, fruit yield, and IWUE, though the effects of the treatment on these parameters varied between locations. At Location 1, drip irrigation (ID) produced a fruit yield of 8.90 ± 5.68 t ha-1, with considerable variability among replicates, and did not differ significantly (p = 0.88) from conventional furrow irrigation (IC) or the rainfed treatment (I0). In contrast, at location 2, drip irrigation outperformed (21.88 ± 9.44 t ha-1) other treatments, being 117% and 32% higher than I0 and IC, respectively. Plastic mulching (MP) improved growth, reduced drought stress and increased yield compared to MS and M0 at both locations. The highest yield at location 1 (23.18 ± 6.62 t ha-1) occurred under IC × MP, while the highest yield at location 2 (32.93 ± 1.62 t ha-1) was achieved under ID × MP. IWUE peaked at 38.84 kg ha-1 mm-1 (IC × MP) in location 1 and 65.87 kg ha-1 mm-1 (ID × MP) in location 2. A linear mixed model estimated that plastic mulch increased yield by ~10.63 t ha-1 (95% CI: 6.58-14.68 t ha-1, p < 0.001) over no mulch, and IC × MP produced a synergistic yield gain of 11.03 t ha-1 (95% CI: 5.3-16.76 t ha-1, p = 0.003) over the control. Overall, plastic mulching consistently enhanced brinjal performance, while the benefit of drip irrigation was soil-dependent and was most evident in the higher water-retention field.

abstract: Sexual selection is a central force in evolutionary biology that has been shown to shape phenotypes and population dynamics in animals. While this selective force is increasingly recognized in flowering plants, theory predicts that anisogamy generates sex differences in the fitness benefits of acquiring additional mates-a pattern well supported in animals but with limited tests in plants. Plant studies rely solely on genetic parentage analyses to estimate mate numbers, thereby conflating performance in accessing mates with success in gamete fertilization. Pollinators add an ecological layer, as their behavior and abundance can influence competition for access to mates and their gametes. Here, we disentangle consecutive episodes of sexual selection in the hermaphroditic plant Brassica rapa by combining direct observations of Bombus terrestris movements with genetic paternity analyses in experimental populations, thus providing independent estimates of the observational number of mates acquired and realized fertilization success. Our approach identifies pollen competition for ovules as the primary arena for sexual selection in B. rapa. Competition for access to mates constitutes a secondary force and was found to be stronger in the male compared to the female sex function, as predicted by classic theory. Experimentally reduced pollinator abundance modulated the balance between pre- and post-pollination sexual selection, increasing the opportunity for selection on mate acquisition. Ignoring pollinator movements led to biased estimates of pre-pollination sexual selection. Our findings demonstrate that sexual selection in plants unfolds across multiple, sequential episodes shaped by ecological context.

abstract: Previous research has shown that tool-use can modify neural representations of our body and the space surrounding us. Furthermore, virtual tools can become incorporated into the user's body representation after training. However, the extent to which such changes depend on the amount of sensorimotor experience remains unclear. In the present study, we investigated whether different amounts of virtual tool-use training (30, 60, 90 and 120 trials) influence body and action-oriented spatial representations. Participants completed a tactile distance judgment (TDJ) task, indexing body representation; and a reaching distance estimation (RDE) task, indexing perceived actionable space, before and after virtual tool-use training. Virtual tool-use produced an overall decrease in TDJ responses, indicating plastic changes in the forearm tactile distance perception. Although the magnitude of change varied across training conditions, the strongest and most reliable evidence for TDJ change emerged following 120 trials of practice, suggesting that extended sensorimotor experience may be required for stable modifications of body representations. In contrast, RDE changed modestly from pre-test to post-test but did not vary systematically with training duration, suggesting that perceived reaching distance may adapt more rapidly and with less dependence on additional practice. Arm length was a significant predictor of RDE error, indicating that stable anatomical constraints continue to influence reachability judgments despite tool-use experience. Together, these findings suggest a dissociation between body representation and perceived reaching distance, with each exhibiting distinct temporal dynamics following tool-use training. More broadly, the results demonstrate that virtual tool-use can induce changes that transfer to subsequent physical assessment, highlighting virtual environments as a valuable framework for investigating body representation plasticity and tool embodiment.

abstract: Background Subunit vaccines offer excellent safety profiles but often suffer from limited immunogenicity, requiring potent adjuvants to elicit robust protection. We hypothesized that combining a positively charged biopolymer, trimethyl chitosan (TMC), with a nanoemulsion (NE) would create a synergistic delivery system to enhance immune responses. This study aimed to formulate a TMC-loaded nanoemulsion (TMC-NE) and evaluate its potential as a safe, effective adjuvant for subunit vaccines. Methods TMC was synthesized via the quaternization of chitosan. Its modification and cyto-compatibility were verified by FT-IR, Zeta potential analysis, and cytotoxicity assays. Based on the pseudo-ternary phase diagram, a stable oil-in-water blank nanoemulsion (NE) was prepared. Subsequently, TMC-loaded nanoemulsion (TMC-NE) was prepared with TMC aqueous solution as the aqueous phase. The formulation was characterized for its droplet size, polydispersity index (PDI), and viscosity, and its safety in vivo was evaluated in mice. Using ovalbumin (OVA) as the model antigen, the immune adjuvant activity of TMC-NE was evaluated in mice by intramuscular injection, and compared with the NE and a commercial similar adjuvant M902. Humoral and cellular immune responses were analyzed by measuring serum IgG antibody levels and splenic lymphocyte proliferation, as well as the expression of cytokines IL-4 and IFN-γ. Results Chitosan was successfully quaternized, yielding TMC with low cytotoxicity. The formulated TMC-NE was clear and transparent, with a mean droplet size of 25.41 ± 2.13 nm, a PDI of 0.231, and suitable viscosity. In vivo, TMC-NE showed no significant tissue toxicity. Immunization studies revealed that TMC-NE stimulated IgG antibody levels comparable to the M902 adjuvant and significantly higher than the blank NE. Furthermore, TMC-NE significantly increased the expression of IL-4 and IFN-γ and promoted lymphocyte proliferation and T lymphocyte levels, indicating the induction of both humoral and cellular immune responses. Conclusions The TMC-loaded nanoemulsion (TMC-NE) is characterized as a safe and effective antigen delivery system with potent immune adjuvant properties. These findings strongly support its prospective application as a novel vaccine adjuvant.

abstract: Students with low academic achievement tend to display more maladaptive behaviours in interactions with peers and teachers. Empathy plays a key mediating role in these interactions and is also linked to academic performance. In particular, facial emotion recognition is one component of socioemotional processing that may contribute to empathic responding. To explore the relationship between empathy, emotion recognition, and academic achievement, a comparative study was conducted with 40 students aged 14-17, divided into two groups: one with low academic achievement enrolled in a school support programme, and a control group with adequate academic performance. A multimethod approach was applied, including the Basic Empathy Scale, a facial expression recognition test, and electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings. Results showed significantly lower cognitive empathy in the low-achieving group in the primary between-group analysis. The overall between-group difference in facial emotion recognition accuracy was not statistically significant. EEG analyses identified exploratory between-group differences in source-level oscillatory activity estimates during facial-expression processing. These electrophysiological findings provide complementary information about task-related activity patterns but should not be interpreted as specific neural markers of empathy or as confirmation of a behavioural facial emotion recognition deficit. Overall, the multimethod approach offers complementary perspectives on socioemotional functioning in low-achieving adolescents, although the exploratory EEG findings require cautious interpretation and replication in larger, independent samples.

abstract: To promote the reuse of existing beams, an experimental investigation was conducted on T-shaped reinforced concrete (RC) beams strengthened with U-shaped RC jackets. Three specimens were tested: one unstrengthened T-shaped control beam and two strengthened beams. Each jacket comprised additional reinforcing bars and higher-strength concrete cast along both sides of the web and the beam soffit, transforming the original T-shaped cross-section into a rectangular section. All three specimens were subjected to cyclic loading, and corresponding finite element simulations were performed to investigate their hysteretic response, skeleton response, flexural deformation, and failure modes. The strengthened beams exhibited load-carrying capacities more than twice that of the unstrengthened beam, and the finite element simulations generally reproduced the experimental responses. Based on truss-arch synergy, an analytical model was developed to predict the load-carrying capacity of RC beams. The predictions agreed well with the experimental results, supporting the reliability of the proposed model.

abstract: To address the premature fracture of anchor bolts caused by the mismatched yielding distance between anchor bolts and hydraulic supports in the advanced support section of rock burst-prone roadways, an elongated constant-resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolt was designed-with its yielding distance specifically coordinated to match that of hydraulic supports. ABAQUS numerical simulation was utilized to investigate the mechanical characteristics of this novel anchor bolt under static loading, as well as under varying impact energies and impact velocities. A comparative analysis was further performed against the mechanical performance of conventional anchor bolts. The results reveal the following: Under static loading, the elongated constant-resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolt exhibits a fracture load of 160.6 kN, a fracture displacement of 523.2 mm, an elongation rate of 20.93%, and an energy absorption capacity of 69.7 kJ. Under impact velocities within 9 m/s, the impact velocity has little effect on the fracture load, elongation, and energy absorption of constant-resistance energy-absorbing bolts, while the impact resistance time exhibits a nonlinear decreasing trend with increasing impact velocity. Under both static and dynamic loading conditions, the extended constant-resistance energy-absorbing bolt exhibits superior impact resistance and can effectively address the problem of premature bolt fracture caused by the mismatch between the bolt yielding distance and that of the hydraulic support in the three-level energy-absorbing support system. The findings provide a new perspective for bolt design.

abstract: Psychological resilience has increasingly been recognized as a key factor associated with students' academic performance, especially in demanding disciplines such as mathematics and science. However, limited research has examined the potential cognitive pathways associated with psychological resilience and academic achievement, particularly in subjects such as mathematics and science that require higher-order thinking skills. This cross-sectional and correlational study examined the indirect associations between psychological resilience, computational thinking (CT), and academic achievement in mathematics and science among middle school students. Data were collected from 401 middle school students in Türkiye. Psychological resilience was measured using the Brief Resilience Scale, CT was assessed via a 25-item multiple-choice test, and achievement scores in mathematics and science were obtained from official school records. Descriptive and correlational analyses were conducted using SPSS 28, while mediation analyses were performed in Mplus 8.1. Rasch analysis was applied to evaluate the psychometric properties of the CT instrument. Correlation results revealed significant positive associations among all main variables. Mediation analyses showed statistically significant indirect associations of psychological resilience with mathematics achievement through CT (β = .070, 95% CI [.036,.110]) and with science achievement through CT (β = .064, 95% CI [.026,.102]). After accounting for CT, the direct association between psychological resilience and mathematics achievement became nonsignificant, whereas the direct association with science achievement remained significant. The path model demonstrated an excellent fit. Overall, the findings suggest that CT may be statistically involved in the association between psychological resilience and academic achievement in mathematics and science; however, the cross-sectional design does not permit conclusions regarding temporal or causal mediation.

abstract: Purpose To assess individual retinal layer thickness and volume changes on optical coherence tomography (OCT) in individuals with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) compared to controls. Methods Adults ≥18 years with a PTSD diagnosis were identified. Age- and sex-matched controls (±5 years) without PTSD were recruited. Exclusion criteria included any cognitive disorder, brain injury, glaucoma, diabetes, optic nerve or vitreoretinal disease, uncontrolled hypertension, refractive error >±6 diopters, or best corrected visual acuity <20/40. Non-mydriatic OCT macular cube 512x128 images were obtained using Zeiss Cirrus HD-5000 AngioPlex. The Duke Reading Center DRCVisualizer software was used to segment the ganglion cell/inner plexiform (GC-IPL), inner nuclear (INL), outer plexiform (OPL), outer nuclear (ONL), photoreceptor, and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) layers. Mean retinal thickness and volume were calculated for all layers within the central 1-mm subfield and 3- and 6-mm ETDRS rings, further divided into nasal, superior, temporal, and inferior quadrants. Results 81 eyes of 42 PTSD patients and 81 eyes of 42 controls were analyzed. Average ages were 48 ± 15 years for PTSD and 51 ± 19 years for controls. Groups were 36% male. PTSD eyes showed significantly decreased photoreceptor thickness and volume and increased RPE thickness/volume across all ETDRS rings and quadrants (all p < 0.05). OPL thicknesses were decreased in PTSD eyes versus controls for temporal 3-mm (25.29 ± 1.36 µm vs. 26.64 ± 3.80µm) and temporal 6-mm (23.47 ± 0.88µm vs. 24.00 ± 1.54µm) rings (p < 0.05). OPL inferior 6-mm thickness was decreased in PTSD eyes (23.98 ± 1.58 µm vs. 24.78 ± 2.34 µm) versus controls (p < 0.05). The ONL nasal 6-mm thickness was decreased in PTSD versus controls (55.96 ± 7.90 µm vs. 56.74 ± 7.47µm) (p < 0.05). After adjusting for multiple testing, RPE differences remained significant across all evaluated regions, while photoreceptor differences remained significant within the central 1-mm and 3-mm ETDRS regions. Conclusions PTSD eyes demonstrated decreased photoreceptor layer and increased RPE thickness and volume.

abstract: A few years ago, the Disruption Index (DI) was proposed as a tool for identifying disruptive research. However, it remains unclear whether the index actually measures what it claims to measure. Our proposed survey plans to examine the extent to which the papers identified by the DI as especially disruptive are the same as the papers that scientists working in a field identify as especially disruptive. We, thus, aim to test an assumption about what the DI measures, specifically, that papers with high DI values are papers reporting revolutionary discoveries. We will focus on the field of immunology. Our survey data will be drawn from researchers who have published many papers in immunology.

abstract: Aquapteridospora rhizicola, a dark septate endophyte, was isolated from the roots of Miscanthus sinensis Andersson, which grows naturally as pioneer grass at a sedimentary site in an old mine. In the early successional stage, M. sinensis seedlings begin to grow on bare ground under heavy metal stress (especially Fe) and sharp soil temperature fluctuations. This study aimed to clarify the effects of root-endophytic A. rhizicola on M. sinensis seedling growth and tolerance, in bare-ground soil, while considering the sharp alteration in soil temperature of the bare ground at the study site. We conducted inoculation tests using sterilized bare soil under normal and actual soil temperature conditions, thereby mimicking the bare ground at the study site. Although A. rhizicola did not promote seedling growth under normal temperature conditions, this fungus enhanced plant growth under actual soil temperature conditions. To elucidate the underlying mechanism of these results, we analyzed the production of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and melanin by A. rhizicola under high Fe and high temperature conditions. The root endophyte increased IAA production in response to the combined conditions of high Fe and high temperature, and this might have contributed to the growth of M. sinensis. Moreover, A. rhizicola might alleviate heavy metal toxicity in the host plant by suppressing the translocation of toxic Zn from roots to terrestrial parts under actual soil temperature conditions. This might be explained by the high production of melanin, which possesses heavy metal binding capacity and antioxidant activity, and whose effect was enhanced under conditions of high Fe and high temperature. Our results indicate that A. rhizicola might enhance growth and heavy metal tolerance of M. sinensis in bare ground of the study site, via increased IAA and melanin production by habitat environmental factors, such as high Fe and high temperature.

abstract: Sepsis‑associated acute kidney injury (S‑AKI) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients, yet effective targeted therapies remain lacking due to an incomplete understanding of its pathogenesis. Ferroptosis, an iron‑dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has recently been implicated in AKI, but the upstream regulators of this process in sepsis remain undefined. Here, we identify SIRT5, a mitochondrial NAD ⁺ ‑dependent desuccinylase, as a critical endogenous suppressor of ferroptosis in S‑AKI. Using a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) murine model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)‑stimulated HK‑2 proximal tubular cells, we show that SIRT5 expression is significantly downregulated in septic kidney injury. Renal tubular‑specific ablation of Sirt5 exacerbated CLP‑induced renal dysfunction, structural damage, and tubular cell death, whereas AAV9‑mediated SIRT5 overexpression attenuated these pathological changes. Mechanistically, SIRT5 deficiency tipped the balance of the ACSL4/FTH1 axis toward ferroptosis: it increased ACSL4‑dependent membrane lipid remodeling and reduced FTH1‑mediated iron sequestration, accompanied by suppression of the antioxidant enzyme GPX4. Consequently, lipid peroxidation, iron overload, and mitochondrial damage were markedly amplified. Notably, knockdown of ACSL4 in SIRT5‑deficient HK‑2 cells effectively reversed lipid peroxidation, iron accumulation, and cell death, establishing ACSL4 as a key downstream effector of SIRT5‑mediated ferroptosis suppression. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized SIRT5-ACSL4/FTH1 regulatory axis that governs ferroptotic susceptibility in renal tubular cells during sepsis, and suggest that pharmacological restoration of SIRT5 activity or blockade of ACSL4‑driven ferroptosis may offer novel therapeutic avenues for S‑AKI.

abstract: Background The impact of smoking, nutrition, alcohol, and physical inactivity (SNAP) on the outcome of ventral hernia repair remains underexplored. This trial aimed to evaluate the effect of targeted, intensive lifestyle prehabilitation on postoperative complications. Methods The STRONG-Hernia trial (NCT06611462) was a multicenter, parallel-group, centrally randomized controlled trial at two Danish university hospitals. Adults scheduled for elective ventral hernia repair with ≥1 risky SNAP factor were randomized (1:1) to STRONG prehabilitation or standard care. Prehabilitation comprised six weekly in-hospital sessions of education, motivational, and pharmaceutical support tailored to each patient's SNAP factors. The primary outcome was postoperative complications ≤30 days. Secondary outcomes included lifestyle changes and health-related quality of life (EQ-5D). Final primary outcome assessment and statistical analyses were blinded. Power calculation required inclusion of 2 × 199 patients. Results Between March 2024 to May 2025, 43 patients were randomized with 21 to STRONG prehabilitation and 22 to standard care. Around 75% had one risky lifestyle factor, and 25% had ≥ 2; obesity was most common. Shortly after randomization, two prehabilitation participants were excluded due to no surgery. At end-of-intervention, 13/19 in the prehabilitation group had optimized all risky lifestyles versus 0/22 in the control group (p < 0.01). Three additional participants in each group did not undergo surgery. At 30 days, complications occurred in 3/16 prehabilitation and 4/19 control participants (p = 1.00). EQ-5D VAS remained unchanged in the prehabilitation group from baseline but decreased significantly in the control group (p = 0.03). EQ-5D-5L index changes were similar between groups (p = 0.92). Challenges encountered included outsourcing of patients, insufficient recruitment strategy, and a low inclusion rate. Conclusion The trial was terminated early due to slow recruitment and was therefore not powered to assess the effect of the prehabilitation intervention on postoperative complications. The findings suggest that the STRONG program seems promising for optimizing risky lifestyles, although these lifestyle results should be considered preliminary. Insights from this trial may help address recruitment challenges essential for completing a future adequately powered trial on postoperative complications.

abstract: This study evaluated the oral safety of Sanxan to provide a basis for its application in food. The toxicological characteristics of Sanxan were assessed through an acute oral toxicity test, three genetic toxicity tests, a teratogenicity test in pregnant rats, and a 90-day oral toxicity test. The results showed that no obvious toxic symptoms or mortality were observed in the acute toxicity test, and the maximum tolerated dose was greater than 15 g/kg, indicating that Sanxan had no acute oral toxicity in the test animals. The results of three genetic toxicity tests-the Ames test, the micronucleus test, and the sperm abnormality test-were all negative, and the teratogenicity test in pregnant rats showed no maternal toxicity, embryotoxicity, or teratogenicity, indicating that Sanxan had no mutagenic or teratogenic effects under the tested conditions. The 90-day oral toxicity test showed that Sanxan at doses of 1.3, 2.6, and 5.2 g/kg body weight had no obvious adverse effects on body weight gain, total food intake, total food utilization, hematology, serum biochemistry, organ-to-body weight ratios, or pathological examination in the test animals, and the maximum no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) was 5.2 g/kg body weight. In summary, under the conditions of this study, Sanxan did not exhibit acute toxicity, genetic toxicity, teratogenicity, or subchronic toxicity, indicating that it has good safety under the tested conditions.

abstract: Despite the increasing growth of sentiment analysis (SA) in several languages, Bangla is largely unexplored as a result of the low availability of annotated datasets, class imbalance, and challenging linguistic features such as inflectional morphology and code mixing. Existing work has concentrated mostly on limited or in-domain corpora, which leaves a void for general multi-domain sentiment resources based on real-world usage. The aim of the research work is to present such a balanced three-class sentiment dataset from Bangla social media text messages, with each post annotated by native speakers as positive, negative, or neutral. A robust preprocessing pipeline, including denoising, abbreviation expansion, and tokenization, was applied to improve data quality. Features were extracted using Count Vectorizer and Word2Vec embeddings, followed by the implementation of several machine learning (SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost) and deep learning (GRU, LSTM) models. In addition, fine-tuning was also applied to the BanglaBERT transformer model for comparison. The results show that BanglaBERT outperforms all other pretrained with approximately 80% accuracy, indicating good generalizability over sentiment classes. These observations support the success of transformer-based architectures trained on low-resource languages. The release of this dataset is expected to facilitate further advances in Bangla sentiment analysis and provide a scalable foundation for multilingual and cross-lingual NLP research.

abstract: Purpose Dry Eye Disease (DED) is highly prevalent among university students and may be influenced by modifiable factors such as psychological stress and sleep disturbance. The primary objective of this study was to investigate the associations of sleep disturbance and perceived stress with DED, while the secondary objective was to evaluate their potential interaction. Methods This analytical cross-sectional study included a random sample of university students aged 18-34 years. Perceived stress was assessed using the Perceived Stress Scale, and sleep quality was evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. DED was diagnosed according to TFOS DEWS II criteria using the Ocular Surface Disease Index, tear break-up time, corneal staining, and Schirmer testing. Robust Poisson regression models were used to estimate relative risks (RRs) for DED associated with sleep disturbance and stress. Interaction effects were assessed on both additive and multiplicative scales. Results The prevalence of DED was 77.9%. Sleep disturbance was present in 75.9% of participants, while 21.3% reported high perceived stress. In univariate analyses, both sleep disturbance and stress were significantly associated with DED prevalence (sleep disturbance: χ²(1, 403) = 14.57, p < 0.0001; stress: χ²(1, 403) = 4.20, p = 0.040). After adjustment for sex and the alternate exposure, poor sleep quality (adjusted RR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.05-1.18; p = 0.001) and high perceived stress (adjusted RR = 1.06, 95% CI: 1.01-1.11; p = 0.015) remained independently associated with increased DED risk. Participants with both poor sleep quality and high stress exhibited the highest DED risk (RR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.10-1.27; p < 0.0001), although no significant interaction. Conclusion Sleep disturbance and perceived stress were independently associated with an increased risk of DED in this student population. However, there was no evidence that stress modified the association between sleep disturbance and DED.

abstract: Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) has emerged as a transformative tool for biodiversity assessment in recent years. Despite widespread acceptance and application for conservation-related outcomes, the interactive effects of hardware limitations, signal propagation, and environmental conditions on how far a signal can be reliably detected remain critically understudied. Such studies in regions of high biodiversity such as the Western Ghats of India, can bolster ongoing monitoring of conservation efforts. We quantified changes in signal detectability using Autonomous Recording Units (ARUs) in a tropical agroecosystem in the Western Ghats. We played back standardized pure tone (1-8 kHz) signals in fallow rice paddy fields over 50-300 m distance gradient. We measured detection using a four-ARU array and modeled operative detectability of signals. We found the 'detection space' of an ARU to be highly frequency-dependent and environmentally modulated. Detection probability for low-frequency signals (1 kHz) decreased rapidly (50% threshold at ~100 m), whereas mid-range frequencies (4-6 kHz) occupied an acoustic window that remained reliably detectable up to 250 m. Higher relative humidity significantly enhanced overall detection, while increasing temperatures disproportionately reduced low-frequency detectability. The orientation of the ARU to the signal source was critical, as the detection probability declined from 81% for recorders facing the source (0°) to 14% for rear-facing units (180°). We propose a 'Decision Support Framework' that provides a pathway for researchers to integrate focal taxa traits with technical constraints to determine detection space and optimize study designs when using PAM for monitoring biodiversity and assessing conservation action.

abstract: Video game sound and music have previously been found to influence player engagement and affective responses during gameplay. However, a systematic investigation into the full extent of these effects has not been conducted. This review examined the influence of music and sound on players' affective responses and engagement during video game play, with a meta-analysis of positively valenced experience (enjoyment, fun or positive affect). Fourteen studies met the inclusion criteria, six of which provided data for the meta-analysis. Game audio was associated with more positively valenced experience than silence (g = 0.48, 95% CI [0.22, 0.74]; small-sample adjusted 95% CI [0.14, 0.82]). Heterogeneity (I² = 58%) was accounted for by one self-selected music condition; without it, the effect was smaller and homogeneous (g = 0.34, 95% CI [0.18, 0.50]; I² = 0%). In exploratory subgroup analyses, sound effects showed a consistent benefit (g = 0.46), whereas the added effect of music over game sound was uncertain (g = 0.31, adjusted 95% CI [-0.07, 0.68]). In the narrative synthesis, music and sound were often associated with higher immersion, flow and motivation. Thirteen of the 14 studies were rated at low risk of bias. Evidence that game audio improves players' affective experience is promising but preliminary; its effect on engagement has not yet been tested quantitatively, and further research and standardisation of methods are needed.

abstract: Background Measles remains a major public health concern in Nigeria, contributing disproportionately to the global burden. Persistence of the disease is driven by sub-optimal vaccination coverage and heterogeneous transmission patterns, but the specific spatio-temporal dynamics and the quantitative impact of vaccination gaps at the sub-national level are not fully characterized. Objective This study aimed to provide a comprehensive analysis of measles transmission in Nigeria from 2006 to 2025, with the specific objectives to identify spatial hotspots, quantify their temporal persistence, and evaluate the association between MCV1/MCV2 coverage and measles case ratio. Methods We conducted a national retrospective ecological study, integrating 19 years of surveillance data (2006-2025) and geospatial information, with a focused 4-year analysis of vaccination records (2021-2024). Analytical methods included time-series decomposition, spatial autocorrelation (Local Moran's I and Getis-Ord Gi*), and linear mixed-effects modeling to quantify vaccination effects while accounting for state-level heterogeneity. Results Analysis of 253,595 measles cases revealed a highly clustered geographic distribution, with 86.4% of the national burden concentrated in northern Nigeria. We identified 38 persistent hotspot Local Government Areas that accounted for 23.2% of all cases. Vaccination coverage was low and disparate, with national averages of 73.8% for MCV1 and 38.4% for MCV2. Mixed-effects modeling confirmed a significant negative association between MCV1 coverage and the measles case ratio, while MCV2 coverage did not show a statistically significant independent effect. Conclusion Measles transmission in Nigeria is driven by entrenched hotspots in the north and critical vaccination gaps threatening disease resurgence in the south. Achieving elimination requires a tailored strategy: intensive supplemental immunization activities and RI strengthening aimed at reducing endemic transmission in the northern hotspots, coupled with focused efforts to close routine immunization gaps in specific southern states.

abstract: Background Stroke health literacy refers to the ability of non-medical individuals to recognize stroke symptoms and make timely decisions, which is critical for improving outcomes. However, data on stroke knowledge and intended care-seeking behavior in Bogotá, Colombia, remain limited. Objective To assess stroke symptom knowledge and intended care-seeking behavior among adults with hypertension and type 2 diabetes and to identify sociodemographic predictors of limited knowledge and suboptimal response. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted between October 2023 and April 2024 in Bogotá, Colombia. A structured questionnaire was administered to 5,402 adults with hypertension and/or type 2 diabetes. Participants were recruited using a non-probabilistic sampling strategy, primarily from individuals under routine follow-up within the Bogotá public health network, and were identified through multiple recruitment strategies, including institutional databases. Surveys were conducted either by telephone or in person. Continuous variables were summarized using descriptive statistics, differences in categorical variables were assessed using chi-square tests, and binomial logistic regression models were applied to evaluate adjusted associations. Results Of 6,050 respondents, 5,402 met inclusion criteria (median age 67 years; 46.3% male). Although most participants recognized that ischemic stroke can cause disability (89.6%) and death (91.1%), 32.5% reported no knowledge of stroke symptoms. Limited symptom knowledge was independently associated with male sex (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.12-1.42), low educational attainment (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.38-1.82), and low socioeconomic status (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.85-2.60). Regarding intended response, 26.6% would not activate emergency medical services, and 52% reported they would schedule an outpatient appointment instead. Lower educational attainment was associated with greater likelihood of reporting non-emergency responses (all p < 0.001). Conclusions Despite high awareness that stroke can cause disability and death, substantial gaps in symptom recognition and intended response persist, particularly among socioeconomically disadvantaged individuals. These findings highlight the need for targeted strategies to improve stroke literacy in high-risk populations.

abstract: Some bacteriophages encode lysis proteins that inhibit essential bacterial processes, and elucidating their mechanisms is valuable for developing antibacterial strategies against drug-resistant pathogens. We determined the cryo-EM structure of the complex between the essential Escherichia coli lipid II flippase MurJ and the phage lysis protein SglPP7. Structural, mutational, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation analyses revealed that SglPP7 binds along the intramembrane cleft of MurJ and inserts its C-terminal tail into the internal cavity, stabilizing MurJ in an outward-facing conformation. Structural comparison with LysM (SglM) and SglCJ3 showed that these sequence-divergent Sgl proteins stabilize MurJ in the outward-facing conformation through distinct binding modes, consistent with the possibility of convergent evolution toward MurJ inhibition.

abstract: Background Stroke remains a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide, with a substantial proportion of survivors experiencing persistent limitations in functional mobility. Although many individuals regain the ability to walk in structured clinical environments, only a minority achieve independent community ambulation due to cognitive-motor interference (CMI). The subacute phase is characterized by heightened neuroplastic potential and responsiveness to rehabilitation. Dual Task-Oriented Circuit Training (DTOCT) integrates task-oriented circuit training with concurrent cognitive challenges and may provide a functionally relevant approach to addressing cognitive-motor interference. However, its feasibility, safety, and preliminary effects in subacute stroke remain unclear. Methods This three-arm, participant-blinded, randomized pilot and feasibility trial will recruit 36 individuals with subacute stroke and allocate them equally to DTOCT, Task-Oriented Circuit Training (TOCT), or Dual Task Training (DTT). Participants will receive three supervised sessions per week for 4 weeks (12 sessions). Primary outcomes will assess feasibility and safety, including adherence, retention, adverse events, heart rate, blood pressure, and perceived exertion. Secondary exploratory outcomes will include walking endurance assessed using the 6-Minute Walk Test, gait speed using the 10-Meter Walk Test, walking adaptability using the Standardized Walking Obstacle Course, and serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor as an exploratory peripheral biomarker associated with neuroplasticity. Discussion This pilot study is designed to determine the feasibility and safety of DTOCT and to generate preliminary effect estimates for clinical and neurobiological outcomes. The findings will inform primary outcome selection, intervention refinement, and sample-size estimation for a subsequent adequately powered randomized controlled trial rather than establish definitive efficacy or superiority. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov. Identifier: NCT07494357 (registered prospectively). Protocol ID: IKFR-202603.01).

abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a significant public health concern that disproportionately affects immigrant populations. First-generation Latino immigrants in the United States experience IPV within complex cultural, relational, and structural contexts that remain underexplored. This study aimed to explore and describe how first-generation Latino immigrants in Southern New Mexico experience and make meaning of IPV and to examine the cultural and relational influences shaping these experiences. A qualitative phenomenological design was used, and reporting followed the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) guidelines. Twenty-four first-generation Latino immigrants were interviewed; two who described observing rather than personally experiencing IPV were excluded, yielding an analytic sample of 22 who participated in in-depth, semi-structured interviews conducted in English or Spanish using a trauma-informed and culturally responsive approach. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and translated where necessary. Data was analyzed using thematic analysis informed by phenomenological principles, supported by Intellectus® Qualitative software and manual coding to ensure rigor and depth. Data saturation was reached during data collection. Six major themes emerged: cultural factors, abuse, culture of silence, control, universal factors, and systemic barriers to legal and support resources. Participants described IPV as shaped by cultural norms, normalization of violence, fear, dependency, and limited access to resources. A pervasive culture of silence, reinforced by stigma, immigration-related fears, and social isolation, constrained help-seeking behaviors. Structural barriers further limited access to legal protections and support systems, exacerbating vulnerability. Findings highlight the need for culturally responsive, multilevel interventions that address the social, cultural, and structural determinants of IPV among Latino immigrant populations. Efforts to improve access to support services and reduce systemic barriers are critical to enhancing safety and positive health outcomes.

abstract: Objectives Previous studies have shown that ambient air pollution was associated with an increased risk of cancer mortality. However, the mortality outcome treated every death equally and ignored the significance of premature death. Methods We conducted a time series study to evaluate the short-term impact of ambient air pollution on years of life lost (YLLs) from cancer in Pudong New Area, Shanghai. Data on air pollutants, meteorological factors, cancer deaths, and years of life lost were collected from 2013 to 2021. In this study, the distributed lag nonlinear model (DLNM) combined with linear (for YLLs) and quasi-Poisson (for mortality) regression models was used to investigate the lag-specific association between air pollution exposure and two outcome indicators of cancer. A stratified analysis was performed according to sex, age, and education. Results For YLLs, per 10 μg/m3 increase in PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, and O3 exposure was significantly associated with YLL increases of 2.22 (95% CI: 0.71, 3.74), 1.04 (95% CI: 0.17, 1.91), 5.05 (95% CI: 0.74, 9.36), 1.88 (95% CI: 0.09, 3.66), and 0.96 (95% CI: 0.14, 1.78) years on lag0-1, respectively. Marginal differences in impact estimates were observed among men, younger populations, and those with higher education. In addition, the difference in the impact of O3 exposure on cancer mortality among low- and high-education subgroups was statistically significant. Conclusions Short-term exposure to ambient air pollution was positively associated with increases in YLLs and cancer mortality in Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

abstract: The transportation sector accounts for approximately 20% of global energy consumption and is responsible for nearly 25% of global energy-related CO2 emissions, 75% of which come from road transport. Global energy consumption and CO2 emissions from transportation are projected to increase by more than 50% by 2030, and this energy consumption is causing environmental damage. As autonomous vehicles become more widespread, energy consumption issues in the new context of human-machine mixed driving are gradually attracting attention. To reduce energy consumption in emerging human-machine hybrid traffic flows and promote ecological driving, while accounting for the trend toward mixed traffic comprising autonomous and manually driven vehicles, this study proposes a method to guide manually driven vehicles at signalized intersections by having autonomous vehicles lead them. An ecological driving strategy based on a mixed-traffic-following model is established. The study designed a two-way, four-lane, cross-shaped, connected intersection scenario, employing a two-stage collaborative optimisation strategy for traffic signals and vehicle trajectories to coordinate the driving states of various vehicle types within the mixed fleet, thereby optimising following distances and speeds. By constructing vehicle energy consumption models and trajectory optimization models, effective reductions in vehicle energy consumption were achieved. Simulation results indicate that as the penetration rate of autonomous vehicles increases, the number of stops and energy consumption of vehicles in mixed traffic flow significantly decrease, validating the effectiveness of the proposed strategy and providing strong support for reducing carbon emissions.

abstract: Background Sepsis is a highly heterogeneous condition, yet it is commonly recognised by application of standardised criteria, irrespective of clinical context. Understanding the complexity of sepsis recognition in the heterogeneous populations of patients with sepsis is critical to better target our resources to the needs of patients. Our aim was to examine nurses' clinical experiences to understand the processes involved in sepsis recognition across clinical contexts. Methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 26 nurses with various levels of experience in caring for patients with sepsis from multiple hospital settings. The interviews were phenomenographically analysed using the Arkelind method. The Cynefin framework was used to inform the organisation of findings according to contextual complexity. Findings We identified four categories of description that represent different ways of experiencing sepsis recognition: recognise sepsis by following protocol-based care, recognise sepsis by following disease-specific care, recognise sepsis according to emergent care, and recognise sepsis according to emergency care. The categories emerged from various clinical contexts, ranging from the simple to the highly complex. This variability directed clinical management by helping nurses decide whether guidelines apply to the individual patient and how they should be integrated into clinical decision-making. Conclusions Despite its apparent simplicity, sepsis recognition is complex and context-dependent. Rather than relying on an identical strategy for all patients, effective clinical decisions require personalisation based on the characteristics of the clinical contexts. Our findings show that considering the availability of data, predictability and cause-and-effect relationships can inform the selection of an appropriate approach to sepsis recognition. This approach demands adaptability; however, unless we adopt an approach that is appropriate to the level of clinical complexity, significant improvements in sepsis recognition may not be seen. Prospective research is required to validate our findings.

abstract: Background The shared genetic etiology underlying the comorbidity of skeletal degeneration and metabolic dysregulation remains poorly understood. This study aims to decipher the pleiotropic genetic architecture of multivariate metabolic bone diseases (mvMBDs) through an integrative summary-statistics framework. Methods We applied Genomic Structural Equation Modeling (Genomic SEM) to integrate genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for six complex traits: osteoporosis (OP), chronic kidney disease (CKD), type 2 diabetes (T2D), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and C-reactive protein (CRP). Subsequent analyses incorporated robust fine-mapping (SuSiE/FINEMAP), transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), and partitioned heritability assessments to identify putative functional loci and regulatory mechanisms. Results Genomic SEM revealed significant genetic covariance among the six traits, successfully deriving a latent mvMBD construct. We identified 197 genomic risk loci, including 193 lead SNPs that did not achieve genome-wide significance in the six constituent univariate GWAS, predominantly localized in non-coding cis-regulatory elements (e.g., super-enhancers and intronic regions). Fine-mapping and TWAS prioritized critical pleiotropic genes (e.g., MACF1, CETP, SPP1, and HNF1A). Gene-set enrichment analyses identified enrichment for terms related to bone biology, lipid metabolism, and inflammation. Conclusion Our findings robustly demonstrate that mvMBDs are not isolated clinical entities but rather interconnected systemic syndromes underpinned by glycolipid metabolic dysregulation and shared pleiotropic regulatory networks. This study establishes a novel theoretical paradigm for the genetic basis of metabolic bone diseases, offering promising functional targets for future precision medicine interventions.

abstract: This paper values discretely sampled variance swaps and absolute-return-based volatility swaps under regime-switching stochastic volatility and stochastic liquidity. Extending an existing stochastic-liquidity model, a quadratic liquidity-stress term shifts the variance-factor mean-reversion target. An exponential-quadratic forward transform yields pricing formulas through coupled Riccati equations and a finite-state Markov backward equation. Explicit finite-horizon sufficient conditions establish martingale and transform admissibility. Recomputed numerical experiments assess simulation agreement, integration accuracy and nested liquidity channels. Under the uncalibrated baseline parameterization, delayed variance feedback contributes more than the direct return-liquidity channel, while their cross-channel interaction is small. These conclusions concern the stated illustrative parameter settings and the specified absolute-return contract, whose payoff differs from the square root of realized variance.
