abstract: Probiotic efficacy in inflammatory bowel disease varies widely between individuals, and the sources of that variability remain poorly understood. D-lactate is a microbiota-derived metabolite that accumulates during intestinal inflammation and is associated with epithelial barrier dysfunction, which motivated our use of a consortium selected to contribute none of it. Here we show that its benefit is not an intrinsic property of the administered strains but is determined by the pre-existing ecological state of the recipient microbiome. Across three independent mouse resources, preventive administration reduced disease severity and histopathological damage only where baseline communities carried higher diversity and more complex co-occurrence architecture; in those animals the consortium preserved community structure and metabolic output, restoring disease-disrupted metabolites, and selectively raising butyrate and propionate. Sustained exogenous D-lactate did not abolish protection, placing D-lactate as a tractable readout of ecological restoration rather than its effector. Responsiveness is encoded in the baseline microbiota and predictable before intervention, establishing probiotic efficacy as a stratifiable property of the host microbiome.

abstract: Cardiac involvement in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is increasingly recognized, but its cellular basis remains poorly defined. Using patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) and engineered heart tissues (EHTs), we identify reduced survival motor neuron (SMN) expression, mitochondrial respiratory defects, and impaired contractility in SMA. Transcriptomic analyses reveal cellular communication network factor 1 (CCN1) as a top upregulated gene in SMA iPSC-CMs, consistent with its enrichment in cardiomyocytes across cardiomyopathies. Exogenous CCN1 exacerbates contractile dysfunction in SMA iPSC-CMs. Proteomic profiling reveals sustained p38/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling activation, synergistically amplified by CCN1 and TNFα, thereby linking stress signaling to cardiac dysfunction in SMA. Therapeutic intervention with tanshinone IIA suppresses CCN1 expression, attenuates p38 activation, and improves contractile function. Notably, combining tanshinone IIA with risdiplam produces additive benefits in mitochondrial and contractile performance. Together, these findings identify a CCN1-mediated mechanism underlying SMA cardiac dysfunction and support combination strategies integrating SMN-dependent and independent therapies.

abstract: The papillomavirus life cycle is linked to epithelial differentiation, and the virus manipulates differentiation to facilitate viral production. One such manipulation is the activation of the DNA damage response (DDR), which promotes viral replication via homologous recombination. Here, we show that the papillomavirus transcription/replication/segregation factor E2 activates the DDR. During differentiation, E2 attenuates sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) activity, enhances the acetylation of DDR factors, and displaces cancerous inhibitor of protein phosphatase 2A (CIP2A) from DNA topoisomerase II-binding protein 1 (TOPBP1), resulting in CIP2A-mediated inhibition of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) and ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) activation. E2 associates with TOPBP1 and ATM while reducing TOPBP1-ATR complexes and ataxia-telangiectasia and Rad3-related (ATR) activation. This ATM-high, ATR-low DDR phenotype promotes viral replication and cell proliferation. We observe this DDR activation in E2-expressing keratinocytes, human papillomavirus 16 (HPV16)-positive cells, Mus musculus papillomavirus 1 (MmuPV1)-induced lesions, HPV-positive head and neck cancer cell lines, and HPV16-positive patient-derived xenografts. ATM inhibition preferentially kills E2-expressing cells, supporting ATM signaling as a potential therapeutic target in HPV-associated disease retaining E2 expression and episomal genomes.

abstract: Increasing evidence supports a pathogenic role for impaired energy metabolism in organ damage. Genetic diseases provide opportunities to investigate these mechanisms, as exemplified by Fabry disease (FD), caused by an α-galactosidase A (GLA) deficiency and globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) accumulation, with cardiomyopathy as the leading cause of death. Beyond Gb3 storage, impaired energy metabolism may contribute to cardiomyopathy. Here, we demonstrate mitochondrial dysfunction in FD heart and its therapeutic targeting. Using a humanized FD mouse model (R301Q-Tg/GLA knockout), embryonic fibroblasts, and neonatal and adult cardiomyocytes, we found impaired mitophagy and mitochondrial respiration, increased reactive oxygen species, and a vicious cycle aggravating lysosomal dysfunction. These defects progressed with age, causing accumulation of dysfunctional mitochondria, energetic failure, apoptosis, cardiac hypertrophy, and diastolic dysfunction. L-arginine, promoting NO/PGC-1α-dependent mitochondrial rescue, prevented cardiac abnormalities. Our findings identify mitochondrial dysfunction as a key driver of FD cardiomyopathy and reveal the lysosome-mitochondria axis as a targetable pathway in FD and beyond.

abstract: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) is a highly aggressive malignancy that often arises through anaplastic transformation of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). Although genetic drivers such as BRAF and TP53 mutations are implicated, the mechanisms underlying this transition remain poorly understood. Here, we show that human ATC loses thyroid differentiation and acquires pluripotency-associated features, accompanied by MAPK pathway activation. Guided by parallels with induced pluripotent stem cell reprogramming, we develop an in vivo reprogramming mouse model. Forced expression of Oct3/4, Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc (OSKM) induces anaplastic transformation of Braf-mutant thyroid epithelium even without Trp53 mutation, yielding an ATC-like phenotype that shares molecular and histological features with human ATC. A conventional Braf/Trp53-mutant model shows similar features. Reintroduction of NKX2-1 into human and murine ATC cells partially reverses embryonic reprogramming, suppresses proliferation and induces redifferentiation toward a PTC-like phenotype. Embryonic reprogramming is a central driver of anaplastic transformation and supports redifferentiation strategies.

abstract: APOBEC3 cytosine deaminases are major sources of cancer mutations. In lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), APOBEC3 activity drives tumor evolution and therapy resistance, nominating these enzymes as therapeutic targets. Although APOBEC3A drives most APOBEC3-associated mutational signature burden across cancers, the relative contributions of individual paralogs in LUAD remain unclear. Here, we define the roles of endogenously misregulated APOBEC3 deaminases using CRISPR-Cas9 knockouts and whole-genome sequencing of 197 long-term propagated single-cell clones. APOBEC3 mutagenesis falls into three patterns, driven predominantly by APOBEC3A, by both APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B, or minimal despite detectable enzyme expression. Commonly used surrogate measures, including mRNA and protein levels and in vitro deaminase activity, do not predict these contributions. We also provide the first causal evidence that endogenous APOBEC3A generates the indel signature InD9a, linking it to uracil excision following cytosine deamination. These heterogeneous contributions highlight the need for biomarkers that resolve individual APOBEC3 activities to guide therapeutic targeting.

abstract: Amphetamine-type stimulants (ATSs) disrupt the brain monoaminergic system and strongly stimulate motivation, movement, and addiction. Vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2) plays a vital role in monoaminergic neurotransmission by sequestering monoamines in presynaptic vesicles. How ATS binds to and regulates VMAT2 remains elusive. Here, we report the cryo-EM structures of human VMAT2 in complex with four ATSs (AMPH, METH, MDMA, and MDA) and the inhibitor lobeline, revealing the molecular mechanisms underlying ATS recognition and modulation. ATSs mimic monoamines and occupy the substrate-binding site of VMAT2, indicating that ATSs function as substrates and thus redistribute the vesicular monoamine pools to the cytosolic pools. Lobeline adopts an unexpected dual-binding mode and locks VMAT2 in a lumen-facing conformation, inhibiting monoamine and ATS uptake. Our dopamine release assay revealed that lobeline regulates AMPH-induced dopamine release by modulating both VMAT2 and DAT. This study provides important mechanistic insights into VMAT2 modulation by amphetamines and lobeline.

abstract: The RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK pathway has been extensively studied for its roles in physiology and disease, yet a systems-level view of its interplay with the broader cellular context is lacking, limiting insight into paralog-specific roles, mutation-driven rewiring, and cross-pathway integration. To address this, we simultaneously mapped the interactomes of all pathway components and their activating and inactivating mutations, identifying 2,500 high-confidence interactors, 88% of which previously unreported, and generating a high-confidence, comprehensive reference map of the pathway in resting and activated states. The pathway behaves like a "molecular organism" that connects to other signaling complexes, operates from distinct subcellular sites, and integrates into networks relevant to physiology and disease. Dataset exploration uncovers paralog- and mutation-specific interaction signatures and pathway-level crosstalk, including previously unknown connections to mRNA metabolism and WNT signaling. The interactomes available at RAStoERK.univie.ac.at provide a foundational community resource for unbiased discovery, targeted mechanistic studies, and potential therapeutic exploration.

abstract: How cells integrate nutrient availability to coordinate metabolism and growth remains poorly understood. Here, we identify branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) synthesis as a metabolic sensing system linking mitochondrial activity to translational and transcriptional control. Yeast limits Leu and Val import and instead relies on their synthesis, allowing BCAA production to reflect mitochondrial anabolic capacity. Reduced Val synthesis activates Gcn2, whereas reduced Leu synthesis inhibits TORC1, together decreasing translation efficiency and restricting growth. This response lowers levels of the transcriptional repressor Mig1, suppressing the Warburg/Crabtree effect and promoting alternative carbon source utilization. Remarkably, pharmacological inhibition of Leu/Val synthesis induces this metabolic reprogramming even in nutrient-rich medium, indicating that mitochondrial BCAA synthesis can partially override other nutrient-sensing pathways. Thus, BCAA synthesis couples mitochondrial anabolic capacity to Gcn2 and TORC1 activity and, through translational control of transcription factor abundance, shapes cellular metabolism.

abstract: Like mammalian nucleotide-binding and oligomerization domain receptors (NLRs), bacterial NLR-like proteins mediate antiviral defense. Avs5, a representative of a large family of short bacterial NLR-like proteins, contains an N-terminal SIR2 effector, a central nucleotide-binding domain (NBD), and a C-terminal sensor domain. Whereas canonical inflammasome NLRs use NBD oligomerization to nucleate effector-domain filaments, Avs5 forms SIR2-mediated filaments that couple receptor assembly to NADase activation. In the resting state, ATP-bound Avs5 is monomeric and subsequently forms a SIR2-mediated dimer that likely represents an intermediate in a stepwise activation pathway. Upon activation, ATP-dependent conformational remodeling of the NBD promotes conversion of these dimers into active filaments. Structure-guided mutagenesis, biochemical assays, and functional analyses show that filament assembly is required for efficient NAD + hydrolysis and antiphage defense. These findings reveal an effector-driven activation mechanism and extend the principles by which NLR proteins couple higher-order assembly to immune defense across domains of life.

abstract: T cells differentiate into functionally distinct subsets in response to pathogens, yet essential immune functions such as self-renewal, expansion, cytokine production, and cytotoxicity are common to multiple subsets and therefore must be programmed via shared regulatory mechanisms. To uncover these "archetypal" epigenomic programs, we integrated a single-cell multiomic (scATAC+RNA-seq) dataset of CD4 and CD8 T cells responding to acute and chronic viral infection with a comprehensive bulk ATAC-seq compendium. Our analysis reveals a modular architecture governing T cell identity, implicating distinct transcription factors in reusing regulatory programs across subsets and lineages. Notably, translationally important progenitor CD8 T cells, critical for sustained immunity and present in both acute and chronic infection, exhibit a composite regulatory state, combining a CD8 exhaustion program with a follicular helper CD4 T cell program. In sum, this resource and generalizable computational framework will aid the mechanistic dissection of adaptive immunity and immunotherapy design.

abstract: Human posterior parietal cortex (PPC) is known to play a role in hand-eye (H-E) coordination, yet the underlying encoding mechanisms remain uncertain. We recorded 412 single neurons across 11 sessions from motor cortex (MC; n = 251) and PPC (n = 161) in a single human participant performing an H-E coordinated center-out task. While MC neurons showed negligible modulation by eye movements, 79% of PPC neurons had neural representations that were additively separable into independent hand- and eye-movement tuning curves. Due to this separability, representations could be separated and additively recomposed while maintaining structural similarity. Consequently, compositional decoders trained solely on single-effector movements could match the performance of decoders trained on coordinated H-E movements (hand: 66% vs. 69%; eye: 34% vs. 36%). These results show that, during simple center-out tasks, MC hand-movement codes are unaffected by eye movements and that compositionality can be used to modularly decode H-E coordinated movements in PPC.

abstract: AKT hyperactivation is a hallmark of many human cancers and contributes to poor clinical outcomes, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that AKT undergoes UFMylation, and loss of AKT UFMylation promotes colorectal tumor development and confers resistance to the AKT inhibitor AZD5363 (capivasertib). Furthermore, p53 activates ubiquitin-fold modifier 1 (UFM1) during the cell cycle to inhibit AKT activity. Conversely, AKT phosphorylates UFM1 to reduce its own UFMylation, establishing a feedback loop that sustains AKT activity. Moreover, we provide evidence that UFSP2 functions as a major cellular deUFMylase for AKT, and genetic ablation or inhibition of UFSP2 suppresses AKT activity to retard tumorigenesis in vivo. Together, these findings provide a mechanistic framework for UFMylation-dependent AKT regulation and support further investigation of UFSP2 inhibition as a potential strategy to modulate AKT signaling in colorectal cancer.

abstract: Germline-restricted chromosomes (GRCs) occur only in germ cells and are absent from somatic cells in songbirds, but their contents and evolutionary mechanisms remain poorly understood. We performed comparative genomics on long-read GRC assemblies from male house finch (HF) (Haemorhous mexicanus), common rosefinch (RF) (Carpodacus erythrinus), and blue tit (Cyanistes caeruleus), the first two of which are newly assembled and annotated. The assemblies vary widely in size (6.5-168.4 Mb) and gene content; whereas most GRC-linked genes are species specific, a small conserved set predates the diversification of passerine birds 47 mya. Despite genic variability, GRCs are consistently repeat rich (63.7%-79.5%) and accumulate intact endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) with long terminal repeats (LTRs). This ERV proliferation peaked during the passerine radiation. In contrast, regular chromosomes purge ERVs to generate solo LTRs. Transcriptomic data reveal significantly higher ERV transcription on GRCs than on regular chromosomes in HF testis. We propose that GRCs act as reservoirs of active ERVs, potentially promoting germline transposition and accelerating speciation.

abstract: Effector-triggered immunity (ETI), mediated by nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat immune receptors (NLRs), plays a critical role in protecting plants from pathogens. While the scope of ETI elicited by Pseudomonas syringae type III effectors on Arabidopsis thaliana has been characterized, no equivalent study has been performed on related oilseed crops, limiting our ability to translate fundamental plant immunity research into crop protection strategies. Here, we present a comprehensive screen of the ETI landscapes in Brassicaceous oilseeds Brassica napus (canola) and Camelina sativa (false flax) using 529 P. syringae effectors. We found that 44.6% and 55.4% of the 65 effector families contained alleles that elicited ETI in B. napus and C. sativa, respectively. Mapping ETI-elicitor homologs onto a P. syringae phylogeny revealed that 79% and 88% of strains carry three or more predicted ETI elicitors in B. napus and C. sativa, suggesting a significant ETI load against P. syringae in oilseeds. Oilseed ETI landscapes are expanded relative to A. thaliana, and the number of ETI responses is correlated with the species' NLR repertoire size and ploidy. Interestingly, while the A. thaliana ETI profile is smaller than the two oilseed crops, A. thaliana ETI responses are generally stronger. Further, the A. thaliana ZAR1 NLR has a broader effector recognition spectrum than ZAR1 in B. napus or C. sativa, supporting a role for convergent evolution in expanding immunodiversity. Overall, our findings reveal an expanded functional diversity of crop immune systems compared with a wild relative and highlight both ETI conservation and the divergence of recognition mechanisms.

abstract: Knowing which way you are facing is essential for navigation. In animals, a dedicated set of neurons-head direction cells-acts as an internal compass: each cell fires most strongly when the animal faces a particular direction. The anterior thalamus is a key hub for this system. In humans, however, direct electrophysiological evidence for a comparable head direction signal remains limited. To address this gap, we recorded intracranial electroencephalography (EEG) from the anteroventral thalamus (AVT) in patients with epilepsy while they performed a virtual navigation task. We analyzed neural activity during in-place rotation to isolate virtual head direction (vHD) information. Using inverted encoding models applied to multi-band neural activity, we reconstructed continuous vHD within two distinct virtual environments. Critically, the decoders failed to generalize across environments, indicating that the AVT vHD representation is environment specific rather than a fixed, universal map. This encoding was observed in the AVT and was temporally specific to rotation epochs; no significant encoding was detected in the pulvinar, another thalamic subregion not part of the classic head direction network in rodents. Together, these findings suggest that the human AVT carries environment-specific vHD information, bridging a gap between animal models and human navigation and highlighting a potential link to spatial disorientation disorders.

abstract: Recognizing our body as our own grounds our perceptions, actions, and social interactions. Even newborns detect cross-modal links between self-related perceptions, 1 considered necessary for body ownership. 2 Yet, clear evidence for a sense of ownership only appears once children not simply detect but also correct mismatches between predicted and perceived self-related sensorimotor inputs. So far, this has mostly been measured using mirror self-recognition, which revealed that children typically do not start recognizing themselves before 18 months of age. 3 , 4 , 5 Infants rarely see their own face, however, and mirror self-recognition has been related to sensorimotor 6 and social experiences. 7 We therefore hypothesized that a sense of ownership over the voice might develop earlier, because most infants routinely perceive themselves vocalizing from birth. 8 , 9 , 10 This might allow them to build sensorimotor models supporting the identification of self-generated signals earlier in this modality. Related research with adults has used the altered auditory feedback paradigm to show that they respond to transpositions of the fundamental frequency (f 0 ) of their voice by restoring the alignment between predicted and perceived feedback. 11 , 12 , 13 , 14 Crucially, these compensatory changes depend on the voice being perceived as self-generated. 15 , 16 , 17 , 18 , 19 Using an adaptation of this paradigm with 5-month-old infants, we found that they can already perceive and correct upward transpositions of their f 0 , at an age when they remain unable to recognize themselves in the mirror. This suggests that hearing ourselves routinely allows us to learn what we sound like months before we recognize what we look like, which might be especially crucial for speech acquisition.

abstract: Cellular turnover is a fundamental biological process that counteracts aging by activating stem cells to replace aging cells. This process is especially critical for maintaining the intestinal epithelium, one of the most rapidly renewing tissues in the body. However, the replacement of aging enterocytes cannot be explained solely by the generation of new cells from intestinal stem cells (ISCs); it also requires the complementary process of physically removing aging enterocytes through shedding. Compared with the well-characterized regulation of ISCs, the mechanisms governing enterocyte shedding remain poorly understood. Here, we identify pileup, a novel age-associated antimicrobial peptide (AMP) in Drosophila, as both a genetic marker and a key regulator of enterocyte shedding. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated through age-related mitochondrial dysfunction, a process facilitated by Autophagy-related gene 1 (ATG1) kinase, activate hypoxia-inducible factor 1α, which induces pileup expression specifically in aging enterocytes. Pileup then compromises the membrane of these cells and triggers c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) activation, which we propose promotes their shedding. Notably, pileup has three homologs, and loss of all four genes leads to tumorous cell accumulation, gut barrier dysfunction, microbiome dysbiosis, and premature death. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for AMPs in the turnover of aging host cells, extending their classical function beyond microbial defense. This work provides new mechanistic insights into enterocyte shedding and underscores its essential role in preserving gut homeostasis during aging.

abstract: Engagement in conversation often requires continuous monitoring of relevant speech in a continuously evolving auditory environment. Emotional salience of semantic content may influence this process, but its role in attentional tracking of continuous speech remains unclear. We address this question using an audiovisual "Cocktail-party" paradigm combined with source-localized magnetoencephalography and encoding-decoding analyses. Participants (18 female, 14 male) selectively attended to one dialogue while ignoring a concurrent distractor dialogue, with both emotional salience and semantic coherence of the conversations manipulated independently. Decoding analyses revealed that negatively valenced, high-arousal, and socially relevant semantic content strengthened neural speech tracking, but only for attended dialogues. This effect depended on semantic structure, emerging earlier in semantically coherent than incoherent dialogues. Encoding analyses further showed latency- and region-specific effects across temporal, parietal, and frontal cortical regions. Emotional salience and coherence jointly modulated mid-latency (100 - 250 ms) responses, whereas late-latency (270 - 450 ms) responses were driven primarily by emotional salience. These findings demonstrate that emotional meaning enhances neural prioritization of attended speech and semantic coherence shapes the temporal dynamics of this enhancement. Together, these results indicate context-sensitive emotional modulation of auditory-language processing during selective listening of continuous speech. Significance Statement Understanding how the brain prioritizes and selectively processes information in naturalistic, continuously evolving audiovisual scenes such as conversations is a central challenge in neuroscience. Here, we show that conversations conveying negatively valenced, high-arousal, and socially relevant content enhance neural tracking of attended speech in a noisy cocktail-party setting. This enhanced tracking depends on the semantic structure of the conversation, emerging earlier for coherent dialogues that are easy to follow. Furthermore, we show that emotional content strengthens mechanisms related to speech comprehension and sharpens segregation of relevant from irrelevant talk. These findings demonstrate that emotional meaning and semantic continuity jointly shape cortical processing of continuous speech, providing new insight into how the brain selects and processes meaningful information during a conversation.

abstract: Autistic individuals often show reduced adaptation to changing environmental demands, but the neurocognitive mechanisms underlying this difference remain unclear. We asked whether it may be explained by reduced sensitivity to external feedback and changes in task difficulty. Autistic and non-autistic adults of either sex, matched for cognitive ability, performed a pitch discrimination task in which their response was immediately followed by feedback. Accuracy was similar between the two groups, yet autistic participants exhibited a markedly reduced feedback-related negativity (FRN), an event-related EEG potential differentiating explicit negative versus positive feedback. They also showed weaker modulation of feedback-evoked EEG responses by perceptual difficulty. Lastly, they showed reduced trial-by-trial behavioral updating of perceptual bias following recent correct and easy trials. These effects were replicated in a follow-up experiment conducted 1-2 years later. When combined they classified autistic and non-autistic participants with about 80% accuracy. Together, our findings indicate that multiple processes for evaluating perceptual decisions and adjusting subsequent behavior differ in autism and likely contribute to slow updating in changing contexts. Significance Statement Autism is associated with reduced adaptation to changing environments in both behavior and neural signals, but the underlying neurocognitive mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that autistic individuals exhibit a reduced feedback-related negativity (FRN), an EEG component that is present when receiving negative instead of positive feedback. They also show weaker neural modulation by perceptual difficulty and reduced trial-by-trial behavioral updating of perceptual bias following recent correct and easy trials. These effects were replicated in a follow-up study. When combined, they classified autistic and non-autistic participants with high accuracy. These findings suggest that reduced flexibility in autism is associated with reduced processing of external feedback and task difficulty.

abstract: To detect objects in natural environments, animals must coordinate movement and sensation. This process unfolds dynamically, as perceivers actively shape sensory input through ongoing motor actions in a closed loop. In this study, we use precise tracking of behavioral kinematics to investigate the initial phase of object interaction, asking: what motor-sensory strategies support object detection during natural approach? Using high-speed videography and advanced tracking tools, we tracked whisker and head dynamics as male rats approached and contacted objects. We found that whisker-object interactions converged toward a distinct ratio between changes in whisker angle and curvature, denoted [Formula: see text] In a motor-sensory phase plane this ratio appears as a line, reflecting a regime in which small motor adjustments produce large curvature changes during contact. This motor-sensory ratio cannot stabilize during free-air whisking and thus can serve as a signature for object presence. Rats gradually converged toward this object-dependent mechanical signature across contacts, and proximity to [Formula: see text] predicted subsequent head movements and the termination of object approach. Convergence to [Formula: see text] was invariant to object shape and texture and to whisker's length. Moreover, touch-induced pumps both signaled and reinforced convergence. The results suggest that rats use successful convergence to this object-dependent motor-sensory contingency as a signature of object presence. Object detection thus emerges as a closed-loop dynamical process in which action, mechanics, and sensation jointly shape perceptual inference. Significance Statement How does a rat know it is touching an object with its moving whiskers? We trained freely moving rats to discriminate objects while tracking whisker kinematics at high resolution. We found that the detection phase involved whisker-object interactions that converged toward a distinct ratio between changes in whisker angle and curvature. This ratio can arise mechanically only when whiskers contact an external object, making its attainment a reliable indication of object presence. During object approach, rats steered their exploratory movements to seek this motor-sensory contingency, marking the transition to focused exploration or disengagement. These findings reveal a dynamical, closed-loop mechanism for object detection in freely moving rats.

abstract: After learning a multiple paired-association (MPA) navigation task, rodents can rapidly learn new cue-location associations after a single exposure, a phenomenon proposed to be facilitated by cognitive schemas. However, it remains unclear what schemas support this behavior and how they could be implemented in biological neural circuits. Here, we identify a set of schemas sufficient for gradual then one-shot paired-association navigation, and implement them in a fully neural agent using biologically plausible plasticity rules. The agent gradually acquires a low-dimensional spatial metric representation using a path-integration based temporal-difference error, enabling self-localization across different environments. It also contains a memory network that forms one-shot associations between sensory cues and goal locations, implemented using reward-modulated exploratory Hebbian (EH) plasticity. A third network performs vector subtraction between the agent's current and goal location to compute goal-directed actions. Supplementing these schemas with an actor-critic enables one-shot navigation past obstacles. Lastly, learning a working-memory gating mechanism using the temporal-difference error enables one-shot learning even with brief cue and distractor presentation. The model reproduces key behavioral features of rodent learning in the MPA task and generates testable predictions about the neural mechanisms underlying schema-based one-shot learning. Significance Statement Schema-dependent learning is exemplified by better recall of a lecture when one already has a schema for understanding. A rodent navigation task showing a shift from slow to rapid learning has been proposed to reflect such schema use, yet how schemas are neurally implemented and enable faster learning is poorly understood. We clarify this gap in this computational study by describing several schemas and implement them as neural networks with biologically plausible learning rules. Composing them into an agent reproduces schema-dependent rodent learning behavior. Because schemas also shape self beliefs, clarifying their neural basis has implications for psychopathology. At the same time, understanding how biological schemas support rapid learning may inform advances in machine learning.

abstract: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) complicates coronavirus vaccine development. Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV) is a classic model of coronavirus vaccine-mediated ADE. Here, we develop ferritin-based FIPV nanoparticle vaccines displaying nucleocapsid (N) antigen, antigen-presenting cell (APC)-targeting ligands, and immunostimulatory factors, and evaluate their protective efficacy, serum-mediated ADE risk, and associated immune features. Compared with soluble N protein, the single-module FIPV N nanoparticle vaccine (sfNnps) enhances FIPV N-specific T-cell responses yet confers only 25.0% (2/8) protection. Dual-module vaccines incorporating either the APC-targeting ligand HCV E2 (dfN/Hnps) or the immunostimulatory factor IFNγ (dfN/Inps) further boost N-specific T-cell responses and confer 50.0% (4/8) and 62.5% (5/8) protection, respectively. The tri-modular vaccine co-displaying N, HCV E2, and IFNγ (tfN/HInps) elicits the most robust N-specific T-cell responses and affords 100% (8/8) protection in female cats, while showing no detectable serum-mediated ADE under the tested conditions and reducing peripheral-blood viral RNA levels by 73.0%. Immune profiling associates tfN/HInps with increased cDC1 representation and antigen-presentation gene expression, as well as a shift toward CD8⁺ effector-memory T cells and a FOXO1-centered program linked to transcriptional features of increased proliferation, memory formation, and cytotoxicity. Overall, this engineered FIPV nano‑display vaccine could provide a framework for cellular‑immunity‑oriented vaccine development against ADE‑prone coronaviruses.

abstract: Early eggshell fossils offer invaluable insights into evolutionary innovations in over 300 million years of amniote egg history. However, the incompleteness of the dinosaur eggshell fossil record hinders ancestral state reconstruction and leads to uncertainty about whether the first dinosaur egg was soft-shelled, semi-rigid-shelled, or rigid-shelled. Herein, we present a fossilized soft eggshell ( Mutabilisoolithus dawaensis ) from an Early Jurassic basal sauropodomorph. We find that M. dawaensis has a soft, plastic-like deformation, a thick cuticle, a thin calcareous layer formed by non-interlocking shell units, and a significantly thick shell membrane. Its shell membrane is similar to that of avian eggs in structure, diameter, and arrangement of the fibers, as well as in the distinctions among outer, inner, and limiting membrane layers, but it is much thicker than that of avian eggs. In dinosaurian egg evolutionary history, M. dawaensis provides evidence of early Jurassic soft-shelled eggs, may represent the earliest stage of biomineralization, and bridges the gap between non-biomineralized membranous soft eggshells and biomineralized semi-rigid eggshells.

abstract: The human circadian clock, a key mechanism governing the sleep-wake cycle, starts oscillating before birth. Distinct fetal behavioral states have been described using short-duration ultrasound recordings, but the alignment of fetal activity with day and night cycles (i.e., diurnal rhythms) remains poorly understood due to the lack of long-term monitoring. This study characterizes fetal diurnal activity patterns using continuous third-trimester monitoring over at least five days across 32 mother-child pairs, yielding over 20,000 combined sensor-hours of maternal (acceleration and temperature) and fetal (acceleration) wearable data. We tracked diurnal pattern development from in utero to 6 months of age, assessing infant sleep at three postnatal time points (first weeks, 3 months, and 6 months) with sleep diaries and questionnaires. Multi-level modeling revealed early diurnal rhythms in fetuses that align with maternal activity and circadian rhythms. Random Forest analyses identified fetal day/night sleep duration ratio – a simplified proxy for fetal circadian entrainment – as the strongest predictor of postnatal infant sleep, with fetuses preferring nighttime sleep maintaining this preference postnatally. Maternal sleep regularity (i.e., consistent sleep patterns characterized by low day-to-day variability in sleep timing) during pregnancy also predicted infant sleep, being associated with a stronger preference for nighttime sleep in infants. These findings highlight the potential influence of intrauterine and maternal factors on early circadian entrainment and highlight maternal sleep as an actionable target to improve infant sleep and family well-being. A limitation of this study is the relatively small cohort size and, consequently, the findings should be interpreted with caution until they are replicated in larger, independent cohorts.

abstract: Foundation models (FMs) using self-supervised pre-training are widely advocated as a universal solution for pathology, yet their advantages over task-specific (TS) models remain unclear. Here we show, using over 100,000 prostate biopsies from 6268 patients across 15 sites, that while FMs demonstrate utility in data-scarce scenarios, their performance converges with—and is in some cases surpassed by—TS models with sufficient labeled training data. Concordance with pathologists’ grading reaches quadratic Cohen’s kappas of 0.91 (95% CI 0.90-0.92; all models) on internal and 0.87 (0.86-0.88; TS), 0.86 (0.84-0.87; UNI FM) and 0.85 (0.84-0.86; Virchow2 FM) on external cohorts at full training. Task-specific training markedly reduces misgrading, misdiagnosis of challenging morphologies, and technical variability. Notably, FMs consume up to 35 times more energy. We advocate for considering both FMs and end-to-end learning for robust, resource-efficient, and clinically applicable AI pathology.

abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including ‘reservation’, ‘substitution’ and optional ‘insertion’ or ‘deletion’, before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization.

abstract: Humans are able to track the change of color and orientation (CO) of an object at a stunning rate. However, spatially separating those features slows this rate by an order of magnitude – a temporal limit of feature binding that is little understood. Here, we investigate the underlying mechanisms using high-temporal resolution cortical source localization of the magnetic field response elicited by CO-pairs alternating at different frequencies in color and orientation. We show that (1) binding requires a rapid recurrent modulation (~120 ms) of activity in V1/V2, whose latency is independent of the alternation rate. (2) Performance drops to chance when the alternation rate becomes too high to accommodate the recurrent process within a single alternation. (3) CO binding itself is mediated by color-based attention, which gradually biases re-occurring CO combinations containing the attended color. These observations together demonstrate that CO-binding across space depends on rapid recurrent processing in early visual cortex, with its temporal limit being set by the time this process takes to be completed. Binding ultimately results from a slower and gradual attentional bias of the recurrent process instantiating a form of stroboscopic stationarity in the stream of alternations for unambiguous discrimination of the correct feature-combination.

abstract: Metagenomic sequencing has transformed our view of the global viral diversity, yet a fundamental bias limits our understanding of the diversity of complete viral genomes. Current quality assessment tools rely on identifying circular contigs, systematically underestimating the completeness of linear DNA and RNA viruses, thus leaving a large fraction of the virosphere uncharacterized. Here, we overcome this bias, by leveraging within-species genomic termini conservation across diverse metagenomic datasets. Applying this approach to the metaVR database, we recover and validate 1,585 conserved, complete linear viral genomes, representing a 21-fold increase in recognized linear completeness. Our results reveal previously uncovered complete monopartite RNA genomes and individual segments of multipartite viruses across 13 classes, alongside deeply branching viral dark matter. Furthermore, we expand the known physical boundaries of linear DNA viruses, by recovering intact megaphages up to 220 kb and distinguishing true complete genomes from highly transcribed operons. Ecological profiling reveals a strong enrichment of these reassigned as complete linear viruses in specific ecosystems, highlighting their ecological relevance. By enabling systematic recovery of complete linear genomes, this framework unlocks a previously hidden fraction of the virosphere and reshapes our understanding of viral diversity and evolution.

abstract: The adult heart has limited regenerative capacity after ischemic injury, and abnormal fatty acid metabolism contributes to this failure of repair. Strategies that reduce fatty acid oxidation can promote cardiomyocyte proliferation, but excessive suppression may disrupt lipid handling and worsen injury. Here we show that a platelet-engineered adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery system enables targeted suppression of the fatty acid transporter CD36 and promotes cardiac repair after ischemia-reperfusion injury. By using platelets as injury-responsive carriers, the system preferentially accumulates in damaged myocardium, reduces neutralization by circulating antibodies, and enhances cardiac delivery of the therapeutic vector. In a male mouse model, CD36 knockdown reduces fatty acid utilization, reshapes cardiac lipid metabolism without causing overt lipid overload, increases cardiomyocyte cell-cycle activity, and improves cardiac structure and function. These findings establish a platelet-guided gene delivery strategy that links metabolic reprogramming to myocardial regeneration and suggest a promising approach for ischemic heart repair.

abstract: Restenosis and atherosclerosis remain therapeutic challenges. Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching is a central driver. DNA damage inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4) is implicated in vascular disease, but its role in restenosis and atherosclerosis is unknown. Here we show that DDIT4 is markedly increased in PDGF-BB- or IL-1β-stimulated dedifferentiated VSMCs and reduced in differentiated VSMCs. DDIT4 is upregulated in VSMCs within neointima and atherosclerotic lesions of mice and humans, correlating with disease progression. DDIT4 overexpression promotes VSMC proliferation and phenotypic switching, whereas knockdown suppresses these effects. AAV9-mediated Ddit4 overexpression exacerbates neointimal hyperplasia in atherosclerosis and vascular injury models, while VSMC-specific Ddit4 deletion attenuates it. DDIT4 binds the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, destabilizing subunit interactions and impairing activity. Resulting acetyl-CoA decline reduces histone acetylation, especially at contractile gene promoters, diminishing H3K9/H3K27 acetylation and chromatin accessibility, thereby repressing contractile genes. Targeting DDIT4 is a promising therapeutic strategy for restenosis and atherosclerosis.

abstract: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual’s distress to one’s own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer’s position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer’s spatial representation and consolidated into memory.

abstract: The clearance of apoptotic cells by macrophages, termed efferocytosis, activates multiple pro-resolving pathways, but whether there is a common upstream regulator remains unknown. Here, we report that in efferocytosing macrophages, MerTK activation by apoptotic cells rapidly and transiently activates an IKKβ-NFκB/-p38 pathway, which then promotes interleukin-10 (IL-10) production, continuing efferocytosis, and regulatory T cell expansion. The IKKβ and downstream resolution pathways are linked through the transcription factor Myc, the epigenetic modifier ten-eleven translocation-2 (TET2), and the immune checkpoint protein programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1). Deletion of macrophage IKKβ in male mice blocks the above resolution pathways and compromises efferocytosis-mediated tissue repair in a model of thymic injury and in atherosclerosis regression. Thus, our findings illustrate the existence of a unifying upstream signal for efferocytosis-induced resolution, which could suggest therapeutic strategies to enhance multiple tissue resolution pathways and to optimize anti-inflammatory therapies by avoiding blocking IKKβ-NFκB/p38-mediated resolution.

abstract: Epithelial stem cells are essential for lineage specification, tissue renewal, and regeneration. Here we show that ureterovesical junction (UVJ) of urinary tract harbors a major cluster of label-retaining urothelial cells that exhibit organoid-forming activities. During lineage-tracing, these Foxa2 -expressing UVJ urothelial cells renew ureteral urothelium, but do not migrate into the bladder during homeostasis or mild bladder injury. Upon mechanical and chemical denudation of bladder urothelium, UVJ cells migrate rapidly into the bladder to replace bladder urothelium. This reepithelization also occurs during combination chemotherapies and severe bladder infection. Common to these injury repair processes is the early-phase and selective phosphorylation of TRKA and AKT which drives urothelial proliferation and differentiation. Nascent bladder urothelial cells derived from UVJ express both UVJ and bladder urothelial markers, signifying active remodeling influenced by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Modulating the activities of UVJ cells may enhance bladder urothelial regeneration and combat challenging bladder diseases.

abstract: Prominent employers are increasingly dropping college degree requirements when hiring. Does this provide upward mobility for non-college workers? Matching job postings to 446,500 job starts in US administrative data from 2011 to 2021, we show that employers reduced the share of postings requiring a degree by more than 10%. Non-college workers who move to decredentialed jobs earn 12 log points more than matched workers moving to never-credentialed jobs ( β = 0.124; 95% confidence interval, (0.042, 0.206)), around US$4,600 per year—a premium that endures for at least five years. These hires are more likely to be Black, Hispanic and female than the workers they replace. Employers also benefit, as removing degree requirements reduces labour costs. Yet most employers that drop requirements do not hire non-college workers (non-college hiring rises 1.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, (0.5, 2.0)). Decredentialing is a promising tool for social mobility, but only when employers follow through.

abstract: Upskilling often refers to the process by which workers acquire and expand their skills, enabling them to perform different types of work as market demands change. Here we demonstrate that generative artificial intelligence can act as an ‘exoskeleton’, enhancing workers’ capabilities when attempting new skills, but these gains depend on continued technology use. We run a randomized controlled trial on upskilling by providing management consultants ( N = 487) access and training in using ChatGPT to solve data science tasks outside their skill sets, which cannot be independently solved by ChatGPT. The treated workers scored higher than the control group on three tasks, although we can reject the hypothesis that they performed as well as expert data scientists. We find no evidence that treated workers are better at answering technical questions without ChatGPT post-experiment, suggesting that their demonstrated technical capabilities do not imply knowledge acquisition.

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming computational social science. This Review examines how LLMs now serve four distinct research roles: subjects that simulate human behaviour, assistants that automate analysis, collaborators that generate hypotheses and evaluators that audit and improve research quality. We analyse recent advances across sociology, political science, psychology, anthropology, economics and related fields, revealing how LLMs accelerate discovery while creating new methodological paradigms. This transformation arrives as society itself becomes saturated with artificial intelligence agents—making LLMs both our research tools and authentic research subjects. Yet fundamental challenges persist. LLMs struggle with causal inference and raise urgent ethical concerns about privacy and misinformation, and their ability to reproduce social complexity remains uneven and unproven. We identify critical research directions for harnessing LLMs’ potential while addressing their limitations. As artificial intelligence reshapes human society, understanding this transformation requires the very tools driving it—a recursive challenge that will define the future of social science.

abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in daily life, ascertaining whether an agent is human is critical. Here we systematically benchmark AI’s ability to imitate humans in three language tasks (image captioning, word association and conversation) and three vision tasks (colour estimation, object detection and attention prediction), collecting data from n = 636 humans and 37 AI agents. We also conducted 72,191 Turing-like tests with 1,916 human judges and 10 AI judges. Current AIs are approaching the ability to convincingly impersonate humans and deceive human judges in both language and vision. Even simple AI judges outperformed humans in distinguishing AI from human responses. Imitation ability showed minimal correlation with conventional AI performance metrics, suggesting that passing as human is an important independent evaluation criterion. The large-scale Turing-like datasets and metrics introduced here offer valuable benchmarks for assessing human-likeness in AI and highlight the importance of rigorous, quantitative imitation tests for AI development.

abstract: Quantification of the direct effect of genetic variation on human behavioural traits is important for understanding between-individual variation in socioeconomic and health outcomes but estimates of their heritability can be biased by between-family indirect genetic effects. By contrast, using within-family variation in DNA sharing is robust to most confounding factors including shared environmental effects and population stratification. Yet, accurate estimates for most traits are not available using this design, and none for non-European ancestry populations. Here we analyse approximately 500,000 sibling pairs with diverse genetic ancestries and obtain within-family heritability estimates for 14 phenotypes, including two well-studied model traits: height (0.70 ± 0.03) and BMI (0.49 ± 0.03). For behaviour, we find significant within-family heritability for smoking initiation (0.34 ± 0.05), alcohol consumption (0.18 ± 0.04), number of children (0.27 ± 0.11) and personality (‘talk versus listen’, 0.48 ± 0.13). In addition, we estimated large heritability for type 2 diabetes (0.43 ± 0.06) and asthma (0.34 ± 0.06), whose risk factors include behavioural traits. Overall, we show concordant estimates across ancestry groups and highlight a significant contribution of shared environmental effects for behaviour and type 2 diabetes risk, which may have inflated between-family estimates. Altogether, our results provide within-family evidence that genetic variation is associated with variation in complex traits, common disease and exposures. Our heritability estimates are concordant across genetic ancestries, lower than those from twin-based studies, yet larger than has been accounted for by genome-wide association studies so far.

abstract: The dynamic choreography of biomolecular interactions underpins the processes of life, but its direct observation remains challenging. Here we introduce continuous mass photometry, enabling hour-long, mass-resolved observation of individual biomolecules tethered to supported lipid bilayers, their complexes and interactions, with up to sub-kilodalton mass precision and millisecond temporal resolution. Our approach represents a quantitative time-resolved single-molecule measurement modality for studying complex biomolecular mechanisms in action.

abstract: Dysfunctional immune responses impair remyelination and contribute to neurodegeneration. While immune and metabolic responses to acute myelin injury are well characterized, myeloid cell adaptations to chronic myelin damage remain poorly understood. Here we performed a comparative analysis of genetic and toxic mouse models of acute and chronic demyelination, which identified a distinct microglial state associated with chronic demyelination, characterized by sustained pro-inflammatory activation, lysosomal lipid sequestration and reduced lipid droplet formation. Transcriptomics profiling further revealed a metabolic program marked by upregulated cholesterol synthesis and diminished sterol efflux. Treatment with a desmosterol mimetic possessing 24-dehydrocholesterol reductase inhibitor activity reversed this microglial state, attenuated pro-inflammatory signaling (including C-C Motif Chemokine Ligand 4 expression), reduced myelin damage and improved motor performance in a mouse model of leukodystrophy. Our findings uncover a pro-inflammatory microglial state characterized by lysosomal dysfunction and increased myelin reactivity, highlighting a novel therapeutic target for chronic demyelinating disorders.

abstract: The selective loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta is a defining feature of Parkinson’s disease (PD), yet its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. NUS1 , which encodes neurite outgrowth inhibitor-B receptor (NgBR), was recently identified as a PD risk gene. Here we show that NgBR is highly expressed in microglia, where its deficiency drives progressive PD-like motor deficits and dopaminergic neurodegeneration via the LCN2–SLC22A17 iron-transport axis in mice. NgBR deficiency in mouse and human microglia triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress and PERK–ATF4–NUPR1 signaling, which preferentially induces LCN2-mediated iron efflux over cytokine release. Subsequently, microglia-derived iron-loaded Holo-LCN2, but not iron-free Apo-LCN2, is internalized by SLC22A17, a receptor highly expressed in dopaminergic neurons, leading to iron overload and ferroptosis. Pharmacological inhibition of LCN2–SLC22A17 axis or ferroptosis alleviated dopaminergic neuron loss and PD-like symptoms caused by microglial NgBR deficiency in vitro and in vivo. Our findings identify disrupted intercellular iron homeostasis as a pathological driver of PD and highlight the LCN2–SLC22A17 axis as a potential therapeutic target.

abstract: Remak bundles are groups of small-diameter unmyelinated nociceptive axons ensheathed by Schwann cells (SCs). Whereas the development and maturation of myelinating SCs have been extensively studied, the formation of Remak bundles remains poorly understood. By preventing the secretion of type IV collagen from SCs, we observe normal myelin but abnormal Remak bundles. There is a decrease in Remak bundle density, an increase in bundle size, improperly ensheathed axons, and a decrease in mechanosensitivity. While Remak bundle formation appears to be independent of integrin signaling, the loss of type IV collagen leads to a decrease in postnatal SC proliferation. Inducing the emergence of supernumerary SCs rescues Remak bundle architecture and mechanosensitivity. Taken together, our results demonstrate that SC-secreted basal lamina critically regulates Remak SC number, bundle size, and structure. Our findings provide insight into the functional role of Remak bundles and highlight their potential involvement in peripheral neuropathies and neuropathic pain.

abstract: Dependable data transmission is vital for modern Smart Grid operations, facilitating essential services like demand-side management and Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI). Within these networks, Automatic Modulation Recognition (AMR) acts as a crucial technique for blind signal processing and system security. However, the highly volatile nature of Power Line Communication (PLC) channels severely restricts AMR performance. Traditional statistical algorithms generally fail under severe noise conditions (low SNR), whereas standard single-stage deep learning architectures lack transparency and struggle to distinguish highly similar modulation schemes. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an innovative two-tier recognition architecture that integrates statistical feature engineering with cutting-edge neural networks. The preliminary stage executes coarse classification by feeding Higher-Order Cumulants (HOCs) into a Transformer module, effectively categorizing signals into general modulation families (e.g., PSK or QAM). Here, the Transformer's self-attention mechanism excels at identifying complex correlations among statistical parameters. Subsequently, based on the preliminary result, a specialized Liquid Neural Network (LNN) is deployed for fine-grained analysis. By processing 3D constellation matrices, these specialized LNN models pinpoint the exact modulation order. Their inherent continuous-time properties provide improved adaptability to the temporal fluctuations and heavy noise typical of PLC environments, as evidenced by our low-SNR evaluations. Experimental evaluations confirm that the introduced hierarchical strategy yields markedly higher accuracy rates than traditional algorithms and unified deep learning baseline models, especially in high-noise scenarios. Ultimately, this structured design delivers a highly transparent and robust solution for AMR in challenging communication setups.

abstract: Tubular permanent magnet linear oscillation actuators (TPMLOAs) are widely used in refrigeration, yet traditional radial lamination of silicon steel faces challenges with low stacking coefficients and assembly difficulties. This study proposes a hybrid lamination strategy that embeds silicon steels into fan-shaped soft magnetic composite (SMC) slots to optimize the stator core, aiming to combine the high permeability of silicon steel with the structural flexibility of SMC for a stacking coefficient near unity. A geo-metric model was established to derive material proportions, and 3-D finite element analysis was employed to investigate the effects of silicon steel quantity on electro-magnetic thrust, iron losses, and efficiency. The results indicate that the hybrid lamination method effectively suppresses magnetic saturation during load operation. Compared to traditional radial lamination, the proposed design increases electromagnetic thrust by 26% at the maximum mover displacement (where magnetic saturation is most severe), while thrust performance is comparable at the negative mover position. This thrust enhancement is particularly valuable for compressor applications, where high thrust at maximum displacement is critical. Although the inclusion of SMC increases eddy current losses at high frequencies, the method significantly simplifies manufacturing and reduces assembly errors. It is concluded that the hybrid lamination strategy provides a feasible and high-performance solution for the development of advanced linear oscillation actuators in compressor applications.

abstract: Haemophilia A is a severe coagulation disorder caused by partial or complete loss of function of the X-chromosomal F8 gene. It is a relatively common coagulation disorder that has been reported in at least 17 dog breeds to date. However, only five distinct molecular causes have been identified so far. One molecular genetic cause is a large inversion, which has also been described in humans and was first studied in a research colony of Irish Setters at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. However, the exact location of the inversion breakpoint junctions in dogs has not been determined. Here, we describe the molecular analysis of a case of haemophilia A in a Weimaraner dog family using long-read sequencing. We show that the cause of haemophilia A is an approximately 420kb inversion affecting the F8 gene. The breakpoints of the inversion were identified in intron 22 at position 124,003,000 and between chloride intracellular channel 2 (CLIC2) and epsilon-trimethyllysine hydroxylase (TMLHE) at position 124,432,668 (NC_049260.1:g.124003000_124432668inv). As in humans, the inversion is most likely caused by non-allelic homologous recombination between intron 22 and a region approximately 420kb downstream of the F8 gene. By identifying the inversion breakpoint junctions, it is now possible to test carriers of the disorder at the DNA level and thus prevent the risk of disease in male offspring.

abstract: Background Pressure-sensing insoles offer a portable way to quantify human movement biomechanics beyond the lab, enabling real-world monitoring. A common objective with these insoles is to estimate ground reaction forces (GRFs). However, force estimates from insoles typically exhibit a magnitude bias-underestimating or overestimating GRFs-that can vary across individuals and contexts. Conventional force scaling approaches can correct for this bias, but they rely on ground truth force plate data for calibration. This is often impractical for remote or longitudinal data collection, particularly for individuals with lower-limb injuries or disabilities. Objective The purpose of this study was to introduce and evaluate a new force scaling method for pressure insoles to enable more accurate estimation of vertical GRFs without laboratory calibration or access to ground truth force plate data, and which could be applied to individuals with lower-limb injuries or disabilities. Methods The new method combines epoch-based and physics-based approaches to perform periodic and dynamic force scaling based on a user's body weight, in a way that is well-suited for use in real-world patient monitoring, and which does not require an individual to weight-bear on a single limb. This force scaling method was evaluated across different participants and activities representative of daily living and rehabilitation exercises. Results Compared to nominal (unscaled) insole force estimates, the new scaling method reduced GRF errors by an average of 54-72%, achieving average errors on the order of 0.11-0.16 body weights. The new method worked reliably for different individuals, both limbs, and a variety of tasks and exercises. Conclusions This method provides a practical, generalizable, and effective approach for improving vertical GRF estimation from pressure insoles during remote, longitudinal monitoring without in-lab calibration or force plates. This could improve GRF assessment outside clinical or laboratory settings and enable clinicians, researchers, and users to more accurately monitor musculoskeletal loading and other biomechanical metrics during rehabilitation, recovery, and physical activities in real-world environments.

abstract: Action selection in cluttered environments, where individuals must simultaneously pursue goals and avoid obstacles, presents a significant challenge for the brain. To understand the underlying mechanisms of action selection in such contexts, we propose a computational model that extends stochastic optimal control theory through a novel framework for obstacle avoidance. The model decomposes action selection into a weighted combination of individual control policies, each generated for either target approach or obstacle avoidance. By integrating value information from goals, obstacles, and actions into a unified measure of "relative desirability", the model dynamically determines the contribution of each policy to the overall action selection process. We evaluated the framework using simulated target-reaching tasks in cluttered environments based on previous human studies. The results showed that the model qualitatively captures key features of human motor behavior, including the influence of obstacle properties on movement trajectories and the transient tendency to initiate movements toward obstacles before avoidance. This work offers new insights into the dynamic interaction between approach and avoidance behaviors, providing a basis for future studies of action selection in more complex and naturalistic settings.

abstract: Background Evidence-informed health policymaking (EIPM) is essential for strengthening health systems and achieving equitable health outcomes. Despite policy commitments in Nepal, the translation of research evidence into policy and practice remains limited. This scoping review synthesizes the barriers and facilitators influencing EIPM across health policy domains in Nepal. Methods We conducted a scoping review following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025 that examined barriers and facilitators of EIPM in Nepal were identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Global Health. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and conducted descriptive and thematic analyses. Results Of 2,139 records identified, 26 studies met the inclusion criteria. The studies covered maternal and neonatal health, non-communicable diseases (NCDs), nutrition, emergency care, health systems governance, climate-health, public health regulation, and COVID-19 ethics. Barriers were grouped into five themes: systemic and governance challenges; capacity and resource constraints; evidence-related issues; contextual and cultural factors; and operational gaps. Common barriers included political interference, fragmented coordination, workforce shortages, inadequate funding, donor-driven agendas, poor dissemination of research, and limited implementation guidance. Facilitators clustered into four themes: institutional and structural enablers, political and leadership commitment, capacity building and stakeholder engagement, and global and donor support. Sector-specific differences were observed, with socio-cultural barriers more prominent in maternal and neonatal health, governance and coordination challenges particularly evident in NCD policies, and technical capacity and data limitations more pronounced in climate-health policy. Conclusions Nepal's EIPM landscape reflects strong commitment but uneven institutionalization. Strengthening governance, institutional capacity, evidence systems, and coordination across federal, provincial, and local institutions is essential to improve the translation of research into policy and practice. Institutionalizing EIPM requires not only producing evidence but also creating systems that routinely generate, translate, and use evidence for decision-making.

abstract: Animal movement data often contain multiple behavioural states that vary across space and time, but identifying these states in a biologically interpretable way remains challenging. We propose an ecologically guided framework for inferring individual behavioural states from movement trajectories using hidden Markov models with step selection functions (HMM-SSFs). The method combines a small set of a priori, biologically motivated state hypotheses with explicit ordering and distinctness criteria on movement signatures, together with model-adequacy diagnostics and a stable fitting strategy. Unlike fully unsupervised approaches, our framework is designed to select among a limited number of ecologically meaningful behavioural states rather than exhaustively search a large latent state space. Simulations show that the method can recover the intended state structure under different behavioural scenarios, and that inference is sensitive to the specification of control locations in the SSF component. An illustrative application to a plains zebra trajectory demonstrates how the framework can be used to infer and label behavioural states from movement data. Overall, the proposed workflow provides a practical and reproducible way to infer individual-level behavioural states while maintaining ecological interpretability.

abstract: Intracellular calcium waves in cardiac myocytes propagate through a fire-diffuse-fire mechanism in which calcium released from one RyR2 cluster diffuses to neighboring clusters and triggers their activation. Yet propagation faces a fundamental physical difficulty: the calcium signal must cross distances of 1-2 μm between Z-planes while being attenuated by cytosolic buffering and diffusion, and at the same time the release site depletes its local sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium store. How waves propagate efficiently despite these constraints has remained unclear. We developed a three-dimensional computational model of mouse ventricular myocytes at submicrometer resolution to address this question. Our central finding is that co-localization of calsequestrin2 (CASQ2) with RyR2 clusters is required for robust wave propagation. In a physiological model, where CASQ2 is concentrated at release sites as observed experimentally, calcium waves propagate reliably across the cell with velocities that match the experimental range. In contrast, when CASQ2 is distributed uniformly throughout the sarcoplasmic reticulum, keeping total CASQ2 unchanged, the wavefront stalls. These results identify CASQ2-RyR2 co-localization as a key structural requirement for effective calcium wave propagation in ventricular myocytes.

abstract: Claudin 18, a tight junction protein, has emerged as a therapeutic target in various gastrointestinal cancers, notably gastric adenocarcinoma. However, its prevalence and clinicopathological significance in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain incompletely understood. In the current single-center, retrospective, immunohistochemical study, the prevalence and prognostic value of Claudin-18 was investigated in CRC. Claudin-18 expression was detected in 15.9% (17/107) of CRC cases, with negative/weak expression in 84.1% (90/107). No significant associations were observed between Claudin-18 expression and age, sex, tumor site, T stage, lymph node status, distant metastasis, TNM stage, histological subtype, or lymphovascular invasion (all p > 0.05). No significant associations were identified between Claudin-18 expression and age, sex, tumor location, histological subtype, or TNM stage. Furthermore, Claudin-18 expression independently predicted survival outcomes in CRC where Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly worse overall survival (OS) in patients with strong/moderate Claudin-18 expression compared with Claudin-18 -negative/weak expression (log rank test, p = 0.024). Mean OS was markedly longer in Claudin-18 -negative/weak expression group (121.0 vs.76.6 months). Progression-free survival (PFS) analysis demonstrated a trend toward poorer outcomes among patients with increased Claudin-18 expression; however, the difference did not reach statistical significance (log-rank test, p = 0.066). Event-free survival (EFS) was also significantly reduced in patients with strong/moderate Claudin-18 expression (log-rank test, p = 0.022). Mean EFS was markedly longer in CLDN18 negative/weak expression (93.1 vs. 31.1 months). Multivariable binary logistic regression showed that the overall model was statistically significant (χ2(7) = 22.657, p = 0.002). However, none of the evaluated variables-including gender, age, lymphovascular invasion, tumor laterality, TNM stage, MSI status, histological type, and Claudin-18 expression-was independently associated with the outcome (all p > .05). Claudin-18 expression was not a significant predictor in the adjusted model (p = 0.931; OR = 0.63). In conclusion, despite its low prevalence in the current cohort, Claudin-18 expression was associated with poorer overall survival; however, its independent prognostic value was not established.

abstract: Background Psychological stress is highly prevalent among nursing students. The clinical exposure is a major factor contributing to psychological stress, but there is a lack of consistent evidence, particularly in the context of Middle Eastern countries. The aim of this study was to quantify the association between clinical exposure and perceived stress among nursing students, and to assess whether perceived social support moderates this relationship. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study among nursing students from King Saud University. The Perceived Stress Scale was used to measure psychological stress, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support was employed to measure perceived social support. The clinical exposure was quantified as the average number of hours spent per week. We employed multivariable linear regression to determine the association. The regression analysis was adjusted for age, gender, living arrangements, and employment status. Results Higher perceived social support was significantly associated with lower perceived stress (β = -0.05, 95% CI -0.09 to -0.01). Clinical exposure was not significantly associated with perceived stress. Students living alone had significantly lower levels of perceived stress (β = -0.37, 95% CI -0.63 to -0.11), as did students working part-time (β = -0.34, 95% CI -0.54 to -0.13). The interaction model revealed that perceived social support was inversely associated with perceived stress levels (β = -0.14, 95% CI -0.23 to -0.04). A statistically significant interaction was observed among students with less than 10 hours of clinical exposure per week. This exploratory finding suggests that the association between perceived social support and stress may differ among students with limited clinical exposure. However, the finding was based on a single statistically significant interaction and should be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating. Conclusions Higher perceived social support was associated with lower levels of perceived stress among nursing students. Interventions aimed at enhancing the social support system may be beneficial in reducing stress, especially during the early clinical exposure period.

abstract: With the emergence of antiretroviral therapy (ART), changes have occurred over time in the causes of death and pathological findings among people living with HIV, including an increasing contribution of serious non-AIDS-related diseases. Assessing concordance between ante-mortem clinical and post-mortem diagnoses remains an important approach for evaluating diagnostic performance and monitoring changes in causes of death in this population. This study aimed to evaluate the concordance between ante-mortem clinical diagnoses of the underlying cause of death and autopsy diagnoses among adults living with HIV who underwent autopsy at the Fundação de Medicina Tropical Doutor Heitor Vieira Dourado (FMT-HVD), Manaus, Brazil, between 2014 and 2019. This cross-sectional retrospective study included 101 autopsies. Class I discordances were identified in 48 of 101 cases (47.6%), predominantly involving infectious diseases (37/48; 77.1%), followed by undiagnosed neoplasms (8/48; 16.7%) and other conditions (3/48; 6.2%). Overall concordance for the underlying cause of death was 36.7%, and most deaths were attributable to AIDS-defining diseases. The absence of ART was associated with a higher frequency of class I discordances. The high frequency of major missed diagnoses may also reflect advanced disease at presentation, overlapping clinical manifestations of opportunistic infections, and limitations in the availability of specific diagnostic methods during the study period. Overall clinicopathological discordance was 63.3%, underscoring the continued value of autopsy for identifying missed diagnoses and highlighting the importance of timely clinical assessment and improved access to sensitive and specific diagnostic methods for adults living with HIV.
