abstract: We present a comparative analysis of six models belonging to Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Transformer, and Mamba families for automated eye disease classification from fundus images under identical experimental conditions. To the best of our knowledge, our work is the first to explore Mamba-based models for automated multi-class eye disease classification from color fundus images. Our analysis suggests that, when evaluated fairly, modern CNN, Transformer, and Mamba-based models provide similar performance for eye disease classification on the Eye Disease Image Dataset (EDID). Along with analyzing individual model performance, we further evaluate performance using a logit-level ensemble of the top three models. The ensemble results imply that these model families capture partially complementary visual features, resulting in a slight performance gain when combined. In both cases, class-wise performance examination indicates that diseases with distinctive structural characteristics are recognized more consistently, while categories with subtle or overlapping features remain challenging. Our implementation, including the training and evaluation pipelines as well as the data splits, is publicly available at https://github.com/ahanaf019/EyeDisease2026.

abstract: Crushing treatment is essential for improving reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) quality, but how different crushing mechanisms affect aggregate-scale properties remains poorly quantified. Four crushing methods, namely small mesh hammer crushing, hammer crushing, jaw crushing, and double roller crushing, were compared in terms of deagglomeration efficiency and aggregate property enhancement. The residual mass ratio and physical and mechanical properties, including water absorption, crushing value, abrasion value, and needle and flake particle content, were evaluated. The surface micromorphology and roughness of RAP aggregates were examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and 3D laser scanning. Small mesh hammer crushing achieved the highest deagglomeration efficiency, with residual mass ratios of 77.8%-96.6%. Hammer crushing reduced crushing and abrasion values by 6.14% and 23.87%, respectively. Water absorption increased by up to 32.86% in coarse fractions but remained within technical limits. Regression analysis confirmed strong correlations (R² > 0.7) between the residual mass ratio and aggregate properties. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for selecting crushing methods to optimize RAP quality for highway base applications.

abstract: An 18-month prospective, non-randomized comparative observational study evaluated the effects of different optical corrections on myopia progression, binocular vision, and visual performance in Spanish children. Forty-five myopic participants aged 9-14 years were allocated to single-vision lenses (SV), low-addition progressive addition lenses (PALs), or defocus-incorporated multiple segments lenses (DIMS). Assessments included spherical equivalent (SE) and axial length (AL), comprehensive accommodative function evaluated by measuring amplitude of accommodation, positive and negative relative accommodation, accommodative facility, and accommodative response, and binocular function evaluated by measuring phorias, fusional vergences, and stereopsis. In addition, contrast sensitivity (CS), visual disturbance index (VDI), and subjective visual quality were assessed at baseline and at 6, 12, and 18 months. After 18 months, SE progression was -0.59 D for SV, -0.51 D for PALs, and -0.30 D for DIMS, corresponding to a 49% reduction with DIMS compared to SV. AL increased by 0.24, 0.27, and 0.23 millimeters, respectively, although inter-group differences were not significant for AL. Accommodative and binocular functions, visual acuity, CS, and VDI remained stable, while distance stereopsis improved in the DIMS group. These findings suggest an association between DIMS lens wear and reduced myopia progression compared with SV lenses in this cohort, without clinically relevant differences in accommodative or binocular function, visual acuity, or subjective visual quality.

abstract: Introduction In Thailand, the Emergency Severity Index (ESI) and Ministry of Public Health Emergency Department triage system (MOPH) are commonly used, whereas the Thai Rapid Initial Assessment and Grading for Emergency (TRIAGE) system has been newly proposed. Comparative evidence is limited. We compared correct triage as the primary outcome, with under-triage, over-triage, and completion time as secondary outcomes. Methods We conducted a randomized three-period crossover simulation study at the Lampang Medical Education Center from October 2025 to January 2026. Fifth- and sixth-year medical students without recent standardized triage reinforcement classified 50 standardized patient cards per system in one of six sequences, with a one-week washout between periods. Multilevel mixed-effects models were used to estimate between-system differences, with adjustment for period, sequence, and academic year. Results Sixty students completed all periods. No significant overall differences were detected in correct triage across TRIAGE, ESI, and MOPH (63.2%, 64.5%, and 61.8%, respectively), or in under-triage (19.6%, 20.0%, and 18.8%). Among sixth-year students, correct triage differed significantly across systems (global P = 0.004), with higher adjusted probabilities for ESI and TRIAGE than MOPH. Over-triage differed across systems and was highest with MOPH (7.0%), followed by TRIAGE (5.7%) and ESI (4.9%). Completion time was longest with TRIAGE (32.8 minutes), compared with ESI (24.3 minutes) and MOPH (23.2 minutes). Conclusion No significant overall differences in correct or under-triage were detected, but the study was not powered to establish equivalence. MOPH showed higher over-triage, Completion time was longest with TRIAGE. Generalizability to experienced clinicians requires further study. abstract: Early social experience is critical for the maturation of social behavior, and its disruption during juvenile development may confer long-term psychiatric vulnerability. Juvenile social isolation (j-SI) after weaning is widely used as a model of early social deprivation; however, its developmental and sex-specific effects on spontaneous social interaction remain unclear. We examined the behavioral consequences of post-weaning social isolation in male and female C57BL/6J mice (Mus musculus). Mice were individually housed from postnatal day (P)21, and spontaneous social interaction was assessed longitudinally at P35, P49, and P63 during prolonged cage-based sessions using an augmented reality-based behavioral monitoring system. Locomotor activity, inter-mouse distance, mean contact duration per initiated encounter, and interaction dynamics were quantified during the light and dark phases. Juvenile social isolation was associated with greater inter-mouse distance across most developmental stages and sex-phase combinations, whereas reductions in mean contact duration per initiated encounter varied by sex, developmental stage, and light/dark phase. Locomotor activity varied by developmental stage and sex, with late-emerging increases particularly evident during the dark phase in isolated mice. In contrast, lower interaction-partner switching in isolated males was detected only at the earliest stage (P35) during the light phase. An important design feature is that isolated mice were reunited at testing with cage mates from which they had been separated for more than two weeks and were therefore effectively unfamiliar, whereas group-housed mice were tested with continuously familiar cage mates; the reported effects therefore reflect social isolation together with its intrinsic reduction in social familiarity. These findings indicate that continued post-weaning social isolation is associated with persistent, sex-specific alterations in sociability and social interaction dynamics. Our results further suggest that juvenile social experience may shape the developmental maturation and temporal organization of social interaction across adolescence and early adulthood.

abstract: Background On June 12, 2026, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved capivasertib (Truqap; AstraZeneca) in combination with abiraterone and prednisone for adult patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naive or -sensitive (mAPMN/S) prostate cancer, corresponding clinically to metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), that is PTEN-deficient as detected by an FDA-authorized test. The pivotal CAPItello-281 trial demonstrated a statistically significant radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) benefit (hazard ratio [HR] 0.81; p = 0.034) but a nonsignificant and immature overall survival (OS) benefit (HR 0.90; p = 0.401). Capivasertib carries a publicly available list price of approximately $23,762 per 28-day cycle. Objective To estimate the incremental cost-effectiveness of capivasertib plus abiraterone and prednisone versus abiraterone and prednisone alone, both with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), from the perspective of a US third-party payer. Methods A three-state partitioned survival model (PSM) was developed with a lifetime horizon (40 years), 4-week cycle length, and 3% annual discount rate. Individual patient-level survival data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves via the Guyot algorithm. Given OS immaturity and AIC differences of less than 1 point across six parametric families, a preregistered proportional hazards (PH) base case was applied: the trial OS HR of 0.90 was applied to the placebo parametric fit. Generic abiraterone, ADT, companion diagnostic, and monitoring costs used National Average Drug Acquisition Cost (NADAC) or Medicare reimbursement schedules; capivasertib used a publicly available list-price proxy, and the OS hazard ratio was sampled lognormally in PSA. Uncertainty was characterized via one-way sensitivity analysis, eight pre-specified OS extrapolation scenarios, four scenario analyses, and probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA; n = 10,000). Reporting followed CHEERS 2022 standards. Results Capivasertib accrued 4.103 discounted QALYs at a total discounted cost of $1,455,507, versus 3.703 QALYs at $207,230 for abiraterone alone. Incremental cost was $1,248,277 and incremental QALYs 0.400, yielding an ICER of $3,120,720 per QALY. The probability of cost-effectiveness was 0% at willingness-to-pay thresholds of $100,000, $150,000, $200,000, and $500,000 per QALY. The most favorable OS extrapolation scenario (log-normal) yielded an ICER of $1,359,445 per QALY. The ratio of mean incremental cost to mean incremental QALY across PSA iterations was $3,148,744 per QALY; because a minority of iterations (13.54%) yielded a negative incremental QALY, the distribution of individual iteration ICERs is uninformative, and uncertainty was characterized using the cost-effectiveness acceptability curve and plane. Conclusions At current list pricing, capivasertib plus abiraterone is not cost-effective for PTEN-deficient mHSPC from a US payer perspective. The result is structurally driven by high incremental drug acquisition cost and small incremental QALY gain under immature and nonsignificant OS data. Mature OS data and a major net-price reduction would likely be required for cost-effectiveness.

abstract: Cross shareholders have become a common phenomenon in capital markets, which increasingly draw the attention of scholars. This paper examines the effect of cross shareholders on corporate cash holdings in Chinese capital market and finds cross shareholders increase corporate cash holdings. Further mechanism analyses find suggestive evidence that this increase is correlated with reductions in overinvestment and improvements in total asset turnover. Additional results show the effect of cross shareholders has heterogeneous significance given the conditions of different external environment and firm characteristics. Moreover, cross shareholders reinforce the positive effect of cash holdings on firm productivity. Overall, this paper's findings provide insight for understanding the role of cross shareholders in corporate cash holding decision in China.

abstract: Background We aimed to establish thresholds for assessing clinically meaningful pain improvement after spinal injections using numerical rating scale (NRS) and patient-reported relative reduction (PRR) of pain. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 1,828 patients who received spinal injections at our spinal intervention center and completed a 2-week follow-up telephone interview in 2017. NRS absolute and relative reductions were calculated using the NRS scores before injection and at follow-up. The PRR and 5-point global perceived effect (GPE; 1, completely recovered; 2, much improved; 3, slightly improved; 4, no change; and 5, worsened) were recorded. The mean ± standard deviation (SD) of NRS absolute reduction, NRS relative reduction, and PRR in the GPE 2 and 3 subgroups were calculated. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis was used to determine the cutoffs for NRS absolute and relative reduction and PRR in predicting the substantial clinically important difference (SCID, GPE 1-2) and minimal clinically important difference (MCID, GPE 1-3). Results The mean ± SD of NRS absolute and relative reduction, and PRR in the GPE 2 and GPE 3 were 4.5 ± 1.8, 65.4% ± 21.1%, and 67.7% ± 14.8% and 2.4 ± 1.4, 36.8% ± 22.5%, and 35.7% ± 16.1%, respectively. The cutoffs for predicting SCID and MCID were NRS absolute reduction of ≥3 and ≥1, NRS relative reduction of ≥50% and ≥10%, and PRR of ≥50% and ≥20%, respectively. Conclusions The NRS absolute and relative reduction and PRR thresholds were established to differentiate SCID and MCID in terms of pain improvement after spinal injections.

abstract: Background Older adults with diabetes are prone to frailty and increased mortality. Aim In this longitudinal study, we examined the association between depressive symptoms and the incidence of frailty in older people with cardiometabolic diseases. We also investigated whether comorbidities modified the association between depressive symptoms and incident frailty in this patient population. Methods We analyzed longitudinal data from 431 outpatients aged 65 years or older with cardiometabolic diseases who visited a frailty clinic from 2015 to 2023. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS)-15. The outcome during follow-up (median, 2.9 years) was incident frailty, as defined by the modified Cardiovascular Health Study (mCHS) criteria or the Kihon Checklist (KCL). Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for incident frailty were estimated using multivariable Cox regression models. Results Depressive symptoms (GDS-15 ≥ 5) were independently associated with incident mCHS- and KCL-defined frailty across all models. The fully adjusted HRs for incident mCHS- and KCL-defined frailty were 1.92 and 2.05, respectively. Stratified analyses demonstrated consistent associations between depressive symptoms and incident frailty in participants with diabetes and hyperglycemia. Significant interactions between depressive symptoms and diabetes were observed for both mCHS- and KCL-defined frailty, whereas no significant interactions were observed for cognitive impairment or physical inactivity. Conclusion Depressive symptoms were independently associated with incident frailty, as defined by both the mCHS and KCL criteria, in older outpatients attending a frailty clinic for cardiometabolic diseases. A significant interaction between depressive symptoms and diabetes was observed, suggesting that patients with coexisting depressive symptoms and diabetes may represent a high-risk group for incident frailty. Further studies are needed to determine whether interventions targeting depressive symptoms and diabetes management can reduce the risk of incident frailty.

abstract: One important purpose of back support exoskeletons (BSEs) is to reduce the stress to the lumbar spine and alleviate the low back pain. However, most previous studies introducing BSEs have argued for their effectiveness based only on easily measurable physiological outcomes such as muscle activation. Motivated by this gap, we examined whether the muscle activation of the back muscle during load handling with a passive BSE can faithfully reflect the estimated L5-S1 joint reaction forces and subjective perceptions. Experiments involving 12 healthy young adults revealed that the BSE significantly reduced average thoracic erector spinae muscle activation during both lifting and lowering the load, and lumbar erector spinae muscle activation during lowering. The BSE also reduced integrated thoracic erector spinae muscle activation during lowering. L5-S1 joint reaction forces were also significantly reduced by the BSE (p < 0.001). Participants reported a lower rate of perceived exertion (p < 0.05). However, the lack of associations among all metrics suggests that inferring one measure from another remains limited when evaluating the efficacy of a BSE.

title: Does low confidence drive reliance on AI, or does reliance erode confidence? A four-wave RI-CLPM study of chinese language and literature undergraduates.

author_details.name: Xinran Du

abstract: Generative AI tools are now routinely used by Chinese Language and Literature majors for tasks once considered the province of individual literary craft: drafting verse, shaping narrative prose, revising fiction. Two competing accounts describe what this means for students' confidence in their own creative writing. A cognitive-offloading account holds that repeated reliance on AI displaces the mastery experiences through which writing self-efficacy is built, so reliance erodes confidence over time. A compensatory-use account holds the reverse: students whose confidence is already low turn to AI to avoid the discomfort of unassisted composition, so low confidence drives reliance. Cross-sectional and standard cross-lagged designs cannot separate these accounts because they confound stable between-person differences with genuine within-person change. We addressed this using a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) across four waves spanning one academic year among Chinese Language and Literature undergraduates (N = 390 recruited; N = 387 analyzed under full-information maximum likelihood, of whom 298 supplied complete four-wave data). Generative AI writing reliance (GAWR) and literary creative writing self-efficacy (LCWSE) were assessed at each wave. The trait-level association between the two constructs was negative and could not be distinguished from zero (r = -.342, Δχ²(1) = 2.26, p = .133). At the within-person level, declines in self-efficacy predicted subsequent increases in reliance (β = -.276, p < .001). The reverse path, from reliance to subsequent self-efficacy, was smaller and fell short of the conventional threshold (β = -.085, p = .072). We state explicitly that this second result is not interpretable as evidence against erosion: a Monte Carlo power analysis put this design's power to detect an effect of that magnitude at 53.2%, close to a coin flip, so the erosion pathway is undetermined in these data and this null supplies no basis for concluding that erosion does not operate. A direct comparison of the two cross-lagged paths favored compensation (Δχ²(1) = 8.83, p = .003; bootstrap 95% CI for the difference [.020, .218] across 5,000 resamples), with the qualification that this comparison sets an adequately powered estimate against an underpowered one and therefore describes what this design was able to detect. Compensation is the pathway this study establishes; whether reliance also erodes confidence over a longer horizon is an open question. We discuss implications for writing pedagogy in Chinese Language and Literature programs and for how underpowered null results should be interpreted in AI-in-education panel research.

abstract: Maggot therapy uses necrophagous dipteran larvae to remove necrotic tissue, requiring strict aseptic protocols. The disruption of egg masses is a crucial step to ensure uniform disinfection; however, chemical agents can cause sublethal effects. This study investigated the impact of three disrupting compounds on the post-embryonic development of Chrysomya megacephala and Chrysomya putoria. Egg masses were subjected for 10 minutes to the following treatments: papain (0.5%), sodium hydroxide (NaOH 1%), potassium hydroxide (KOH 2%), and a control (distilled water). After hatching, 40 larvae per replicate (n = 640 per species) were monitored for viability, stage duration, feeding cessation rate, larval weight (L3), sex ratio, and morphological normality. Data normality was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test; comparisons between treatments were performed using nonparametric Kruskal-Wallis tests followed by Dunn's post hoc tests, while categorical variables were analyzed using chi-square tests and Fisher's exact test, with a significance level of p < 0.05. The results revealed species-specific responses. In Chrysomya megacephala, there was no significant reduction in viability (57% to 70%) or changes in the pupation rate among the groups. However, NaOH significantly reduced larval weight (67.5 mg) compared to the control (69.9 mg), while papain did not differ significantly from the control (68.5 mg). Chrysomya putoria, on the other hand, showed greater sensitivity to alkaline compounds; treatments with NaOH and KOH reduced total viability to 68% (compared to 88-91% in the control and papain groups) and delayed the feeding cessation rate. In both species, papain preserved larval weight gain and maintained developmental stability. The total duration of the life cycle (10-11 days) and the morphological normality of adults were not significantly affected by the treatments. It is concluded that C. megacephala exhibits greater physiological resilience to chemical stress in early life stages. Among the agents tested, 0.5% papain emerged as the most promising option for maggot therapy protocols, as it combines efficient dissociation with the maintenance of larval biological quality.

abstract: Olive mill wastewater (OMW) is a major environmental concern in olive-producing regions because of its high organic load and phytotoxic phenolic content, which limit its safe discharge or reuse. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an integrated electrocoagulation-adsorption (ECAD) treatment using olive pomace (OP) biochar and to determine how electrode material influences the performance and cost of the combined process. Specifically, the study characterized OP biochar produced by pyrolysis and evaluated its adsorption behavior toward total phenols (TPh) and soluble chemical oxygen demand (CODsoluble), compared Al- and Fe-based EC and their integrated ECAD performance, and theoretically determined biochar dosages and estimated the operational cost of both configurations. The produced biochar exhibited a BET surface area of 135.23 m2/g, a mesoporous structure with an average pore width of 21.95 Å, a negative zeta potential of -29.89 mV, and a carbon content of 67.21%, confirming the formation of a carbon-rich and porous adsorbent. Isotherm analysis showed that TPh adsorption was best described by the Langmuir model, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 84.74 mg/g, whereas CODsoluble was best fitted by the Dubinin-Radushkevich (D-R) model. Standalone EC achieved comparable TPh and CODsoluble removal using Al and Fe electrodes (about 52-55%). However, the integrated systems showed a strong electrode-dependent response. The Al-ECAD system achieved maximum removals of 70.69% TPh and 71.39% CODsoluble, while the Fe-ECAD system reached 67.40% and 66.33%, respectively, at the lowest biochar dosage, with removal declining at higher dosages. The estimated operational costs were 4.25 and 5.30 US$/m3 for Al- and Fe-based systems, respectively. The novelty of this work lies in demonstrating that the effectiveness of biochar-assisted EC is strongly dependent on electrode-biochar compatibility, identifying electrode selection as a key design factor for ECAD treatment of OMW.

abstract: This study examined the effects of elevation gradients on on soil and plant stoichiometry and heavy metals distribution in Mixed Coniferous Forests (MCF) and Oak Forests (OF). Soil organic carbon (SOC), total nitrogen (TN), and total phosphorus (TP) were significantly higher at the 10 cm soil depth at elevation EL-2, followed by EL-3, in both forests; whereas the lowest values were observed at EL-1. MCF exhibited significantly higher SOC, TN, and TP concentrations than OF. Similarly, leaf carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus concentrations were highest EL-2. In oak forests, leaf carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus concentrations reached 458.4 mg kg - ¹, 4.42 mg kg - ¹, and 2.54 mg kg - ¹, respectively. The Corresponding values in MCF were 472 mg kg - ¹, 16.1 mg kg - ¹, and 1.9 mg kg - ¹, respectively, indicating greater nutrient accumulation at the mid-elevation site (EL-2). The leaf C:N ratio was significantly higher at EL-2, whereas the C:P and N:P ratios did not differ significantly among elevations. A similar pattern was observed in branches, bark, and litter. At EL-2 site, soil nickel (Ni), lead (Pb), cadmium (Cd), copper (Cu), and iron (Fe) concentrations at the 10 cm soil depth were significantly lower in MCF than in OF. Conversely, plant tissues in MCF exhibited higher concentrations of Ni, Pb, zinc (Zn), Cd, Cu, and Fe than those in OF at EL-1. Soil and plant stoichiometry are fundamental components of ecosystem functioning and nutrient cycling, and elevation gradients also play a critical role in regulating these processes. These findings offer valuable insights for developing sustainable forest management strategies that aim to mitigate heavy metal pollution in high-altitude ecosystems.

abstract: Pigeons and quail contribute to poultry production, nutrition, and livelihoods in Bangladesh; however, their role in avian influenza virus (AIV) circulation remains poorly understood. These poultry species are widely reared and traded alongside chickens and ducks in household farms, commercial systems, and live bird markets, where inadequate biosecurity may create an overlooked ecological niche for AIV circulation, reassortment, and potential zoonotic spillover. Between November 2021 and April 2022, we conducted a cross-sectional study in Chattogram, Bangladesh, to estimate the prevalence and subtype-specific distribution of AIV and to identify factors associated with AIV positivity in pigeons and quail. A total of 300 birds (108 pigeons and 192 quail) were sampled from households, commercial farms, and live bird markets. Oropharyngeal and cloacal swabs were collected from each bird and tested for the AIV matrix gene using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, followed by subtype-specific detection of H5, H7, and H9. Data collected from bird owners and traders included bird demographic characteristics, bird source, and health status using a structured questionnaire. The overall prevalence of AIV was 14.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 10.6-18.8). Quail had a higher prevalence (18.2%, 95% CI: 13.0-24.4) than pigeons (7.4%, 95% CI: 3.3-14.1). Among detected subtypes, H9 was most prevalent (11.3%, 95% CI: 7.9-15.4), followed by hemagglutinin (HA)-untyped (2.7%, 95% CI: 1.2-5.1) and H5 (0.3%, 95% CI: 0.001-1.8), while H7 was not detected. Quail had higher odds of AIV positivity than pigeons (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 4.1, 95% CI: 1.8-10.6); clinically sick birds (aOR = 2.9, 95% CI: 1.4-6.2) and birds sampled from household farms (aOR = 2.8, 95% CI: 1.2-6.5) also had higher odds of AIV positivity. These findings indicate that pigeons and quails, which are understudied poultry species, may contribute to the maintenance and transmission of AIV within mixed poultry production and marketing systems in Bangladesh. Integrating these species into routine AIV surveillance is therefore necessary to strengthen early detection, inform control strategies, and reduce the risk of zoonotic spillover.

abstract: Background Typhoid fever, caused by the bacterium Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi (S. Typhi), remains a major global threat despite substantial declines over the past three decades. In 2021, an estimated 7.1 million (5.6 to 9.2 million) cases occurred worldwide. Following the WHO's recommendation, ten countries (excluding Indonesia) have introduced the typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV). To inform decision-making for the potential introduction of TCV into Indonesia's National Immunisation Program, we estimated the direct and indirect costs of typhoid fever in Indonesia. Methods We conducted a multisite, incidence-based cost-of-illness study using a patient-level bottom-up costing approach in 23 hospitals and primary health centres (PHCs) across six provinces. Children (6 months to 17 years) and adults (≥18 years) hospitalised with ICD-10 A01 typhoid fever hospitalised with at least one positive typhoid serodiagnostic result during 2019-2023 (retrospective) and 2022-2023 (prospective), without other major infectious or chronic comorbidities, were identified from facility records. Direct medical costs were obtained retrospectively from hospital/PHC bills and clinical records, while direct non-medical and indirect (productivity loss) costs were collected prospectively through interviewer-administered household questionnaires. Sensitivity analyses re-estimated costs after excluding component-wise outliers and imputing missing income values using the provincial minimum wage. Results We collected 2,069 records (1,538 retrospective [891 children; 647 adults] and 531 prospective [329 children; 202 adults]) across six provinces. The weighted mean direct medical costs were US$177.0 ± 101.9 for children and US$199.8 ± 119.8 for adults, while the corresponding direct non-medical costs were US$43.7 ± 16.3 and US$39.0 ± 10.9, respectively. Indirect costs were US$23.9. ± 5.6 (children) and US$17.9 ± 5.5 (adults). Private hospitals had the highest total direct medical cost (US$254.4), while PHCs had the lowest (US$47.8). Costs varied substantially by provinces (BPJS tariff regions). Conclusion Hospitalised typhoid fever imposes a substantial economic burden in Indonesia. These setting- and region-specific cost estimates can inform cost projections and cost-effectiveness analyses for the introduction of the typhoid conjugate vaccine in Indonesia.

abstract: Background Inflammation is a common pathological feature underlying type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk and progression. Determining the roles of fatty acids and bioactive lipid oxylipin inflammatory mediators could inform T2D preventative efforts and therapeutic targets. Methods Leveraging the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos (HCHS/SOL), we evaluated cross-sectional and prospective associations of 81 oxylipins and polyunsaturated, monounsaturated, and saturated fatty acids with T2D. We assessed whether fatty acid levels differed at visit 2 by visit 1-prevalent T2D status and prioritized likely causal metabolites using Bayesian model averaging Mendelian randomization (MR-BMA). Results Fifty-four fatty acids and oxylipins were associated with prevalent T2D at visit 1 (15,138 participants; 2,962 T2D cases), four of which (adrenic, dihomo-gamma-linolenic, tricosanoic, and lignoceric acids) were also associated with incident T2D by visit 2 (8,548 participants; 1,376 T2D events), though effects were attenuated for adrenic and dihomo-gamma-linolenic acids upon further adjustment for impaired glucose tolerance. Sixteen out of 28 fatty acids were significantly different at visit 2 between those with and without prevalent T2D at visit 1 (9,115 participants; 2,151 T2D cases), holding visit 1-measured fatty acid levels constant. MR-BMA prioritized one diHETrE oxylipin as a likely causal risk factor for T2D. Conclusions Fatty acids and oxylipins showed complex patterns of association with T2D, including more associations likely reflecting overt disease processes in prevalent T2D, than incident risk-enhancing associations.

abstract: Background Maternal mortality has declined in Ethiopia, yet rural areas still struggle with access to care. Mobile phone-based gain or loss-framed messaging-hold promise for improving maternal health outcomes. Evidence on the comparative impact of these framing strategies in low-resource rural settings remains limited. This study evaluated the effectiveness of gain- versus loss-framed SMS messages in improving maternal health service utilization in Jimma Zone, Ethiopia. Methods A three-arm cluster-randomized controlled trial was conducted across 21 clusters, with clusters allocated to gain-framed messaging, loss-framed messaging, or control (usual care). A total of 588 pregnant women (16-20 GA) were recruited in March 2023 and followed from May to December 2023, with endline assessment in February 2024. Participants received 39 messages over a 6-8 month period, aligned with gestational age and postnatal timeline. Primary outcomes were at least one ANC, SBA, and PNC within 7 days. Secondary outcomes included knowledge, attitudes, self-efficacy, and self-reported morbidity. Analyses used generalized and linear mixed models with cluster-level adjustments. Result Both framing strategies improved service utilization compared to control. Gain-framed messages increased odds of ANC attendance (OR 5.40, 97.5% CI 1.95-14.94), SBA (OR 7.53, 97.5% CI 2.20-25.79), and PNC (OR 4.83, 97.5% CI 1.71-13.67). Loss-framed messages also improved ANC attendance (OR 7.14, 97.5% CI 2.40-21.26), Skilled Birth Attendance (SBA) (OR 7.31, 97.5% CI 2.13-25.09), and PNC (OR 4.07, 97.5% CI 1.46-11.39). Knowledge improved in both arms, attitudes improved only in the gain-framed arm, and self-efficacy showed no significant change. Self-reported maternal morbidity decreased in both intervention arms. Conclusion Both gain- and loss-framed mobile messages led to increased maternal health service utilization. Loss-framed messages were more effective for ANC attendance, knowledge, and morbidity reduction, while gain-framed messages showed greater impact on SBA, PNC, and attitudes. abstract: The Hawaiian Islands, an isolated oceanic archipelago in the Pacific, had one of the world's most spectacular land snail radiations. Unfortunately, only 35% of the 759 Hawaiian snail species remain, with >100 species threatened with imminent extinction. Though many extant Hawaiian snails are arboreal and are known to eat microbes on the surface of plants, our current understanding of which microbes compose arboreal Hawaiian snails' diets remains rudimentary. Here, we examined microbial assemblages (bacterial and fungal) on plants previously identified as preferred and avoided by a diverse assemblage of arboreal snails at three sites in wet and mesic forests on O'ahu, Hawai'i, USA, to identify microbes that may form the foundation of Hawaiian arboreal snails' diets. At Mt. Ka'ala, we also investigated if microbial assemblages change across years. Across sites, microbial assemblages differed on preferred and avoided plants. While differences across sites can complicate the process of identifying key microbes, microbes with elevated abundances on preferred plants across sites are likely important food resources. Using this approach, we identified bacterial and fungal OTUs that we hypothesize form important components of Hawaiian arboreal snails' diets. While we found that microbial assemblages differed among years at Mt. Ka'ala, differences between preferred and avoided plants remained consistent across years. Expanding a snail plant preference-microbiome framework across multiple forest types is a crucial step in understanding arboreal snail diets as microbial taxa enriched on preferred plants across sites may be meaningful components of snail-associated microbial resources. Microbial taxa enriched on preferred plants are not presented here as confirmed dietary components, but as experimentally tractable candidates that should be further evaluated in laboratory trials. This information is foundational to improving captive rearing of critically endangered snails and informing habitat quality assessments for the many threatened Hawaiian snails.

abstract: Currently, there are still no reliable pre-treatment biomarkers for vedolizumab in ulcerative colitis. To investigate baseline mucosal signals, we reconstructed the discovery cohort from GSE73661 and evaluated the derived panel in the blood samples from GSE191328 and the independent mucosal RNA-seq cohorts from E-MTAB-7845. The reconstructed cohort comprised 24 baseline samples, including 14 composite responders and 10 non-responders. Through repeated LASSO variable selection, the study identified an exploratory gene set consisting of ZNF689, TPRXL, ZC3H10, and MRPL55. The selection procedure yielded a mean held-out AUC of 0.611 across 18 complete nested-validation repetitions; this does not independently validate the final gene set. When the fixed gene set was projected exploratorily, the AUC for 17 blood samples was 0.458 (95% CI 0.162-0.755), and the AUC for 27 independent UC mucosal samples was 0.534 (95% CI 0.293-0.775). The apparent AUC of this gene set on the discovery set was 1.000, and 500 full-process bootstrap analyses indicated that gene selection was unstable. Among the three targeted inflammatory panels, interferon-γ showed a directional difference that was not statistically significant (mean GSVA score difference -0.425; nominal P = 0.066; adjusted P = 0.197). Expression scales and clinical endpoints differed across cohorts. The above results describe post-selection separation within the discovery cohort and do not establish reproducible predictive performance, tissue specificity, or a definitive four-gene signature.

abstract: Understanding how environmental stressors affect pollinator behavior is essential for assessing ecosystem health. Automated flower and robotic feeder systems (AFRFSs) have transformed studies of pollinator foraging and learning, yet most remain reward-centric and cannot probe aversive learning under field conditions. Here, we present FloBuzz, a modular AFRFS that combines automated reward delivery with computer vision visit detection to trigger closed-loop electric shock stimulation in free-flying honey bees (Apis mellifera). The system consists of a 3D-printed feeder with a shock grid, a syringe pump with fluid level feedback, and a computer vision based shock module. In a replicated field proof-of-concept experiment, mean bee occupancy decreased with increasing stimulus voltage, demonstrating a measurable voltage-dependent deterrent response. These results validate the ability of FloBuzz to deliver automated, programmable aversive stimulation under outdoor conditions. Its modular architecture provides a flexible platform for future studies requiring controlled integration of appetitive and aversive stimuli in freely foraging bees.

abstract: Understanding the segmental anatomy of the human spinal cord remains challenging due to its interindividual variability and the lack of standardized definition of a spinal cord segment. In this human cadaveric study, we dissected 40 spinal cords, identified and measured the length, thickness and width of each segment comprised between C2 to S5. This extensive dataset enabled us to characterize the distribution and variability of the measurements, as well as to conduct ratio and correlation analyses. By converting segment length measurements into an original coordinate system, and thickness and width values into scaled data relative to easily identified anatomical features, we showed that L4 and C6 can be considered relevant landmarks of the cadaveric SC. We also divided the sample into three subgroups according to the total SC length: a short group (n = 9), an intermediate group (n = 15), and a long group (n = 16). This distinction revealed unexpected morphological features regarding the transverse dimensions, showing that variations in total SC length did not result in proportional changes in average segment thickness or width. Overall, these new morphometric findings highlight the gross morphological complexity of a generally oversimplified structure and provide additional anatomical landmarks, improving our understanding of SC cadaveric anatomy.

abstract: This longitudinal study examines how preschool children's phonological awareness and emergent literacy skills relate to their early writing performance in first grade. Conducted within the context of a transparent Turkish orthography, the study aims to identify early cognitive-linguistic correlates of subsequent writing development. A total of 97 children (aged 66-77 months) from preschools in a socioeconomically diverse Turkish district were followed over two academic years. In the first year, participants were assessed using the LAP-3 Early Literacy Subtest and the Phonological Awareness Test to measure their emergent literacy and phonological skills. One year later, their writing performance was evaluated using a validated sentence construction assessment. Non-parametric statistical tests and correlation analyses were conducted to examine developmental variations and relationships among the variables. Results revealed statistically significant correlations between early writing performance and both phonological awareness (r = .46, p < .01) and emergent literacy (r = .32, p < .01). Specific sub-skills such as syllable segmentation, rhyming awareness, and letter-sound correspondence showed the strongest associations with writing performance. These skills did not differ significantly by age or gender. The findings highlight the foundational role of preschool phonological and emergent literacy skills in early writing development. This study contributes empirical data from a transparent orthography. Given the correlational design, these findings should be interpreted as evidence consistent with developmental literacy theories rather than as confirmation of causal or predictive mechanisms; they emphasize the importance of early identification and instructional support in preschool settings to promote future writing success.

abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is a central regulator of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol metabolism, yet the functional consequences of many clinically observed PCSK9 variants remain unknown. To establish a rigorous system for quantitative variant assessment, we generated a PCSK9 knockout (KO) HepG2 cell line through CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of exons 2-8, effectively removing both the prodomain and catalytic regions required for PCSK9 function. This null background enabled systematic functional mapping of wild-type (WT) PCSK9 and multiple clinically relevant variants representing well-characterized, recurrent, and previously understudied alleles. Functional assays revealed pronounced heterogeneity among variant activities. The classical gain-of-function (GOF) variants D374Y and R496W exhibited robust suppression of LDL uptake, whereas A443T-an infrequently reported and previously uncharacterized variant-demonstrated a loss-of-function (LOF)-like phenotype with significantly enhanced LDL uptake. Additional poorly characterized variants, including V4I, R104C/V114A, and R496W/N425S, displayed varied functional profiles, providing novel mechanistic insights. Surface LDL receptor (LDLR) levels generally correlated with LDL uptake but revealed unique patterns for specific variants. This KO-based rescue system provides a high-resolution framework for mechanistic classification of both established and poorly characterized PCSK9 variants, bridging the gap between genetic discovery and functional interpretation while supporting precision lipid-lowering strategies.

abstract: The democratization of sequencing has led to a wealth of high-quality genome assemblies from across the Tree of Life. One pattern that has emerged is that chromosomes within a genome can vary drastically in their gene density (e.g., human chromosomes 13 and 19, with gene densities of 17.5 and 60.5 genes per megabase, respectively). To our knowledge, the cause of this variation in gene density has not been explored. In this study, we leveraged genome assemblies of 262 vertebrate species to examine the range of within-genome variation in gene density. We combined gene density data with repeat landscape analyses in each species. We predicted that genomes with more recently expanded repeat families should show greater variation in gene density, because repetitive elements accumulate unevenly across the genome, while chromosomal rearrangements such as fusions, fissions, insertions, deletions, and inversions homogenize gene density over time. Our empirical analysis reveals a significant yet variable effect of repeat expansions, with additional processes likely contributing to variation in gene density.

abstract: GAPO syndrome is characterised by a core combination of phenotypes: growth retardation, alopecia, pseudoanodontia and ocular atrophy, and to date has only been reported in humans. It is a rare autosomal recessive condition caused by pathogenic variants in the Anthrax Toxin Receptor 1 (ANTXR1) gene. This study reports a canine form of the disease observed in a litter of Segugio Italiano dogs. Affected dogs, examined at 21 months old, presented with the core GAPO phenotype, short limbs, craniofacial abnormalities, alopecia, pseudoanodontia, and ocular abnormalities that included glaucoma. Whole genome sequence analysis of two affected puppies and the dam identified a nonsense variant c.505C > T in ANTXR1 which introduces an early stop codon in exon 7, predicted to truncate the protein by 395 amino acids. Comparative quantification of ANTXR1 gene expression in corneal, retinal and optic nerve tissues of a GAPO-affected dog were markedly reduced compared to control samples. Evaluation of protein expression through Western blot analysis using retinal and optic nerve tissue showed absence of ANTXR1 in the affected dog. Access to canine ocular tissues, rarely available in human GAPO patients, provides insight into tissue-specific effects of ANTXR1 loss. Our findings establish this canine disorder as a model of human GAPO syndrome and has facilitated the development of a DNA test that can identify carriers of the disease variant and prevent production of affected litters with this life limiting disease.

abstract: Upon ligand binding, the kinase domain of EGFR phosphorylates multiple tyrosine residues on the receptor cytoplasmic tail through a trans-autophosphorylation process. Phosphotyrosine sites on activated receptors recruit Grb2, which further recruits SOS to initiate downstream signaling by activating Ras. Multivalent binding between SOS and Grb2, as well as direct Grb2:Grb2 interactions, contribute to formation of a protein condensate of activated EGFR. The condensed state of EGFR facilitates autoinhibition release in SOS and exerts regulatory control over signal propagation from activated EGFR to Ras. While kinase activity of EGFR is an essential driver of this signaling process, phosphorylation at residue Y160 on Grb2 blocks Grb2:Grb2 binding and can interfere with EGFR condensation. Here, using a reconstituted system, we examine how titrating kinase activity in the EGFR system can both promote and inhibit signal output to Ras. The results reveal how effects of tyrosine kinase inhibition can, under some circumstances, promote Ras activation by inhibiting negative feedback through Grb2 phosphorylation and disruption of a Grb2 SH2/SH3 dimer interface.

abstract: Online handwriting provides a low-burden source of cognitive-motor measurements, but small datasets can yield optimistic results when preprocessing, task selection, or explanation is not separated from evaluation. We evaluated eight classifiers on the DARWIN dataset (174 participants; 25 tasks; 450 predictors) using ten repetitions of 5-outer/3-inner-fold nested stratified cross-validation. All preprocessing, hyperparameter selection, and calibration were restricted to outer training data. We added a training-derived operating point, fully nested seven-task selection, cross-model subset transfer, foldwise SHAP analysis, and an all-feature SHAP sensitivity analysis. Random Forest had the highest descriptive ROC-AUC (0.938 ± 0.033 across 50 held-out folds). The Friedman omnibus test indicated model differences (p < 0.001), but no one of 28 paired comparisons remained significant after Holm correction. Training-derived thresholds (median 0.461) yielded held-out sensitivity 0.869 and specificity 0.831; these are exploratory operating characteristics, not a clinical cutoff. Nested seven-task selection achieved AUC 0.916 ± 0.037, compared with 0.956 ± 0.030 for all 25 tasks, and selected subsets were unstable (mean Jaccard 0.195). Cross-validated SHAP emphasized temporal variables, although an all-450-feature sensitivity analysis showed that individual ranks depend partly on ANOVA preselection. The study contributes an integrated, leakage-controlled evaluation rather than a new classifier or a validated diagnostic instrument; external prospective validation remains necessary.

abstract: Long COVID is associated with persistent physical and emotional symptoms that may substantially impair health-related quality of life, with growing evidence suggesting that these outcomes differ between women and men. This cross-sectional study examined sex differences in health-related quality of life, lifestyle habits, and symptom severity in long COVID, and explored factors associated with health-related quality of life in women and men. A total of 342 adults with long COVID (mean age = 51.20 years, SD = 10.49; 265 women and 77 men) completed a battery of questionnaires during a single, face-to-face individual assessment session. The questionnaires assessed health-related quality of life, smoking behaviour, physical activity, dyspnoea, fatigue, and anxiety and depressive symptoms. Controlling for age and months since diagnosis, women reported lower quality of life and greater dyspnoea severity than men, whereas no sex differences were observed in smoking behaviour, fatigue severity, or anxiety and depressive symptoms. In sex-stratified exploratory analyses, poorer quality of life was associated with greater dyspnoea, fatigue, and emotional symptom severity in women, whereas in men it was associated with greater fatigue. However, interactions between sex and these factors were not statistically significant. These findings indicate sex differences in health-related quality of life and dyspnoea severity among individuals with long COVID. Larger, adequately powered studies are needed to determine whether the factors associated with health-related quality of life differ by sex.

abstract: Reliably capturing transient animal behavior in the field and laboratory remains a logistical and financial challenge, especially for small ectotherms. Here, we evaluate home security cameras as affordable, accessible and suitable alternatives for monitoring small, cold-blooded animals historically overlooked by commercial camera traps. These cameras are often lightweight, weather-resistant, operate offline or online, store data continuously for up to four weeks and can use phone notifications over local Wi-Fi to alert users to behaviorally relevant events. We first benchmark a representative home security camera against an established trail camera under matched laboratory conditions in both continuous and motion-triggered modes, comparing event detection, recording duration, and missed-event rates. We then validate the system during a 1.5-month deployment in a tropical primary rainforest, assessing weather durability, sensitivity-versus-data-volume trade-offs, and whether behavioral measurements obtained in the laboratory are reproducible under natural conditions. We discuss the relative affordability of our system for researchers in the Global South, home to the largest ectotherm diversity.

abstract: Arterial cannulation for cardiopulmonary bypass in small dogs is challenging because small vessel diameters may preclude use of appropriately sized pediatric arterial cannulas. Although off-label use of 14-gauge hemodialysis catheters has been reported, their pressure-flow characteristics under small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass conditions remain unclear. This in vitro study evaluated one 8-French pediatric arterial cannula and six 14-gauge hemodialysis catheter specimens-separate side-hole and sealed specimens at effective lengths of 25, 32, and 38 mm-in a closed-loop mock circuit for a 3-kg small dog. A 34% (w/w) glycerol-water solution (viscosity 2.8 cP at 28°C) served as an approximate Newtonian blood analogue. The Stockert S5 pump flow-rate setting was increased from 50 to 350 mL/min; 50-300 mL/min was prespecified as the primary analysis range and 350 mL/min as exploratory. The reported outlet pressure was recorded 1,000 mm upstream of the test device, while inlet pressure was monitored 300 mm downstream and regulated to 60 mmHg; six technical runs per condition were conducted using the same physical device and circuit setup. Within the primary analysis range, outlet pressure was approximately 136-137 mmHg at 300 mL/min; mean differences for the 14-G specimens versus the 8-French cannula were +0.33 to +0.67 mmHg, with 95% confidence intervals from -1.33 to +2.15 mmHg. At 350 mL/min, outlet pressures were higher for all three side-hole 14-gauge specimens than for the 8-French cannula. At 300 mL/min, outlet pressure was approximately 2-3 mmHg lower for the side-hole specimens than for the sealed specimens across all catheter lengths. Together, these findings indicate small observed circuit-level differences in outlet pressure among tested devices within this standardized mock small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit, but do not establish formal equivalence, device-to-device interchangeability, or clinical validity.

abstract: Background In the context of museum and cultural heritage protection, rapid and accurate identification of Coleopteran pests is crucial for museum and cultural heritage protection. This study evaluated the effectiveness of MALDI-TOF MS in identifying Coleopteran species collected in the field. Materials and methods Seven species of Coleoptera collected between 2014 and 2023 from 17 French cultural sites. MALDI-TOF MS spectra were compared against two reference databases: one composed of laboratory-reared specimens and a second expanded with spectra from field-collected specimens. In parallel, three specimens per species and storing mode were submitted to molecular identification using COI and 16S markers. Results A total of 273 specimens (205 field-collected and 68 laboratory-reared) were analysed. Correct identification at the species were obtained for MS spectra query against DB1 for species which possess homolog in the database. However, the spectra reaching threshold for relevant identification were coming from essentially laboratory-reared Coleoptera. An upgrading of the reference MS database (i.e., BD2), improved identification performance for field specimens, although limitations remained for species with MS spectra of low peak diversity like Pentarthrum huttoni. Molecular identification of field-collected specimens showed a sequencing success rate below 10%. Conclusion MALDI-TOF MS is a promising tool for the identification of Coleopteran pests in cultural heritage contexts, especially when reference spectra matched both species and preservation mode.

abstract: Purpose Immune checkpoint inhibitors, a type of immunotherapy, show promise in treating triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Although TNBC is more prevalent among Black and Hispanic women, they are less likely than non-Hispanic White women to be treated with immunotherapy. To date, no studies have explored the reasons underlying these disparities in the use of immunotherapy. This information is crucial for the development of targeted interventions that mitigate these disparities and accordingly address TNBC-related inequities among Black and Hispanic women. The aim of this study is to qualitatively identify medical oncologists' perspectives of barriers to immunotherapy access among patients with TNBC. Methods Using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research, between May 29, 2020 and September 23, 2022, we conducted semi-structured interviews until thematic saturation with 15 medical oncologists treating New York City metropolitan area patients with breast cancer. We used inductive content analysis to examine the interviews and identify themes corresponding to barriers to access to TNBC immunotherapy. Results The following five overarching themes emerged: (1) Mixed public perceptions about immunotherapy safety and efficacy, (2) Two-tier systems of care, (3) Timely initiation of immunotherapy, (4) Lack of dissemination of best practice guidelines leads to lack of adoption of standard of care, and (5) Side effect profile impacts use and continuation of immunotherapy. Conclusion Large-scale studies quantifying the effect of these barriers on access to TNBC immunotherapy are needed to determine cause and inform effective interventions promoting equal access to all patients with TNBC.

abstract: Introduction The opioid epidemic in the United States poses a major public health challenge, with postoperative prescribing recognized as a significant source of initial opioid exposure. Midwestern states, including Iowa, have experienced substantial opioid-related morbidity and mortality, reflecting broader national trends of opioid misuse, diversion, and overdose. Excess postoperative opioid prescribing increases the availability of unused medications, which are often retained in households and pose ongoing risks for diversion and nonmedical use. These challenges highlight the need for effective, scalable strategies to reduce opioid exposure at surgical discharge. Accordingly, this study investigated the impact of a broadly targeted Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathway on opioid prescribing at discharge for hysterectomy patients compared to other gynecologic procedures. Methods A retrospective chart review was conducted across six Iowa hospitals implementing the "Billion Pill Pledge" ERAS pathway. Two groups of patients underwent surgery between November 3, 2022 and April 4, 2024: those undergoing hysterectomy (n = 63) and those undergoing other gynecologic surgeries (n = 30), including cervical hysteroscopy, cesarean section, endometriosis excision or ablation, and sterilization procedures. Pre-ERAS and post-ERAS implementation data from the postoperative period were analyzed between the two groups in terms of average opioid pill counts prescribed, percent reduction in pill counts prescribed after ERAS implementation, and percent of prescribed pills remaining unused. Results Pre-ERAS data showed no significant difference in mean opioid pill counts prescribed at discharge between hysterectomies and other gynecologic surgeries (p = 0.3). Post-ERAS data displayed significantly higher mean pill counts for hysterectomies (23 pills) versus other gynecologic surgeries (16 pills) (p < 0.001). Patient-reported post-ERAS prescription quantities were significantly lower than surgeon-estimated pre-ERAS prescribing quantities for both hysterectomies (27 pills versus 23 pills) (p < 0.001) and other gynecologic surgeries (29 pills versus 16 pills) (p < 0.001). The hysterectomy group had a significantly smaller percent reduction in prescribed pill counts than the other gynecologic group (14% versus 40%) (p < 0.001). There was no significant difference in the proportion of prescribed pills left unused between the hysterectomy group (55%) and the other gynecologic group (65%) (p = 0.08). No prescription refills were reported within 30 days postoperatively. Conclusion Patient-reported opioid prescription quantities prescribed at discharge following implementation of the Billion Pill Pledge ERAS pathway were significantly lower than surgeon-estimated pre-ERAS prescribing quantities across gynecologic surgeries, with a larger difference observed among non-hysterectomy procedures. Despite lower post-ERAS prescription quantities, over half of prescribed pills on average remained unused, highlighting the need for ongoing efforts to optimize postoperative opioid disposal practices. These findings suggest that broadly targeted ERAS pathways may be associated with lower postoperative opioid prescribing in gynecologic surgery.

abstract: Chlorous acid water is a type of chlorine-based disinfectant with chemical properties distinct from those of sodium hypochlorite solution, which is in common use. In this study, we evaluated the inactivation efficacy of chlorous acid water against avian influenza virus deposited on material surfaces, in comparison with sodium hypochlorite solution. First, the intrinsic antiviral activity of both disinfectants was examined under conditions free of amino acids and proteins. The results demonstrated that the 99% (IC99), 99.9% (IC99.9), and 99.99% inhibitory concentrations (IC99.99) were all approximately half those of sodium hypochlorite solution, indicating that chlorous acid water possesses slightly stronger inactivation activity. Next, the efficacy against protein-containing virus deposited on material surfaces (stainless steel, plastic, and rubber) was evaluated under conditions simulating a poultry house environment. At room temperature, both disinfectants exhibited equivalent inactivation capacity; however, a marked difference was observed under low-temperature conditions. Specifically, the efficacy of chlorous acid water was maintained or enhanced, whereas that of sodium hypochlorite solution declined, with the required concentration increasing approximately 2- to 3-fold. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that chlorous acid water exhibits antiviral activity comparable to or exceeding that of sodium hypochlorite solution, while retaining its efficacy even at low temperatures and in the presence of proteins. These properties suggest that chlorous acid water may be a particularly useful disinfectant in real-world settings such as poultry houses operating under low-temperature conditions.

abstract: Extracellular acidification can alter the structure and function of ion channels by neutralizing acidic residues exposed to the extracellular space. However, the relationship between protonation states and alterations in the structural dynamics of the channel is difficult to investigate by experiments. Here, we used atomistic simulations and graph-based algorithms to predict the H-bond pattern of the mouse hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN2) channel, whose gating is facilitated by extracellular acidification. Our simulations revealed that E212 - a residue exposed to the extracellular space absent in human HCN channels - participates in a complex hydrogen-bond network with the transmembrane domain. These networks are partially disrupted at acidic pH levels, affecting the molecular interactions of the S4 helix in the channel's voltage-sensing domain. On the basis of our findings, we suggest that hydrogen-bond network alterations under acidic extracellular conditions can affect channel's gating.

abstract: This study proposes a design semiotics-driven, integrated innovation method for designing furniture based on Chinese regular script (Kaishu), aiming to overcome the fragmented and practice-detached approaches prevalent in current research. First, furniture-related words were collected, high-frequency terms were identified, and extensible semantic analysis was performed to select Chinese characters based on semantic flexibility. Second, the KJ method was applied to gather and analyze user needs, clarify their vector relationships, and construct a direct reachability matrix to derive a reachable matrix, resulting in structured user need analysis. User needs were then translated into functional and design requirements using Axiomatic Design (AD) theory. Third, design requirements (prioritized) were guided by shape grammar to reconstruct regular script symbols and finalize the reconstruction plan. Finally, iterative integration of product design elements achieved the commercialization of the reconstruction plan. The feasibility of this process was validated through the design example of the regular script " (Diligence)" bookshelf, offering a novel method for expanding Chinese character furniture shapes.

abstract: This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the pharmacological and computational potential of the methanolic extract of Combretum indicum. Mineral profiling by ICP-AES confirmed the presence of essential elements, including K (5.92 ppm), Mg (4.94 ppm), Fe (1.92 ppm), and Zn (1.13 ppm), with no detectable toxic heavy metals. The extract exhibited strong antioxidant activity with 95.48% inhibition of H2O2 and an IC50 of 0.82 µg/mL. Significant thrombolytic activity was observed, achieving 82.71% clot lysis, exceeding streptokinase. Anti-inflammatory activity showed 95.27% inhibition in vitro and 65% edema reduction in vivo. Anti-arthritic activity reached 85.6% inhibition in vitro and 87.50% in vivo, surpassing indomethacin. Analgesic activity demonstrated up to 70.15% inhibition of writhing. Cytotoxicity (LC50 = 30.19 µg/mL) and strong anthelmintic effects further supported bioactivity. Molecular docking revealed high binding affinities (up to -10.6 kcal/mol), while ADME and drug-likeness analyses indicated favorable pharmacokinetic profiles. DFT analysis confirmed chemical stability and reactivity. Overall, C. indicum demonstrated promising multi-target therapeutic potential, warranting further investigation for drug development.

abstract: This study examined the influence of older age and race (White/Black/Arab) on stereotypes of women. To evaluate whether age and race shape stereotype content for an intersectional group relative to its superordinate racial or superordinate older age identities, 525 Amazon Mechanical Turk participants were asked to list up to five words or short phrases that most people associated with these target groups. Overall, the study found stronger support for a distinctiveness hypothesis, whereby the most distinct identity of an individual's intersectional identity influenced their associated characteristics. For example, because being White is common in the United States, old White women had more stereotypes in common with their old superordinate identity than their White identity. This suggests that the nation's population characteristics may be predictive of the stereotypes associated with different intersectional groups. Overall, this research reveals the complex interplay between stereotypes of age and race for women, underscoring the need to acknowledge intersectional identities and cultural norms. Such insights can enhance our pursuit of inclusive and accurate societal perceptions.

abstract: Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) is an early mediator of ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), however, the evidence on its role in orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT), particularly with donation after circulatory death (DCD) grafts is limited. Given its key regulatory function, this study investigated the effects of IRI on graft injury and assessed whether the use of ISO-1, a small-molecule MIF-inhibitor, affect IRI in a rat DCD-OLT model. 196 male Lewis rats were randomized into DBD control, DCD-30 min, DCD-60 min, DCD-30 + ISO-1, and DCD-30 + vehicle groups (n = 7/group/time-point). ISO-1 was administered before controlled cardiac arrest (0-60 min) and 3 h cold preservation before arterialized OLT. Animals were sacrificed at 1, 3, 24, and 168 h post-reperfusion. DCD grafts showed marked injury, with the DCD-60 group exhibiting lethal IRI. ISO-1 significantly reduced early hepatocellular injury compared with vehicle (AST:294 ± 63 vs 867 ± 211 IU/L, p = 0.017) and resulted in values comparable to DBD controls. Serum HMGB-1 (11 ± 2.8 vs 26 ± 6.2 pg/mL, p = 0.045) and MIF (45 ± 5.3 vs 144 ± 27.5 ng/mL, p = 0.034) levels were similarly decreased following ISO-1 application. ISO-1 improved graft microcirculation at 24 h, attenuated histological injury, and was associated with an altered time course of CD163 + macrophage infiltration. ISO-1 pre-treatment attenuated hepatocellular injury and was associated with improved graft microcirculation and reduced DAMP release, supporting further mechanistic and translational evaluation in DCD liver transplantation.

abstract: Purpose We assessed the safety and efficacy of magnetic resonance (MR)-guided microwave ablation for treating hepatic malignancies. Methods This retrospective single-center review evaluated patients who underwent MR-guided microwave ablation for hepatic malignancies between 02/15/2017-04/22/2020. Complications were classified following CIRSE guidelines. Local tumor progression (LTP), local tumor recurrence (LTR), non-target progression (NTP), progression-free survival (PFS) and time to progression (TTP) were assessed, with data presented as mean ± standard deviation. Results Sixteen patients (60.75 ± 14.4 years; 9 males, 7 females) underwent 17 MR-guided microwave ablation for 21 hepatic malignancies (17 (81.0%) hepatocellular carcinoma, 1 (4.8%) cholangiocarcinoma, 2 (9.5%) metastases, and 1 (4.8%) suspicious lesion in a patient with primary sclerosing cholangitis). Lesion size was 12.2 ± 4.8 mm and total procedure time 138 ± 53 minutes. Complications included fever (N = 2), abdominal pain (N = 2), biloma (N = 1), and reactive cholecystitis (N = 1). These resolved with pain medication for one patient and antibiotics for another. No tumor recurrence was observed at ablation sites (LTP and LTR = 0%) at 36.7 ± 28.2 months. NTP occurred in 11 patients (68.8%) with a TTP of 14.8 ± 11.4 months. PFS was 44 months (95% CI: 10-85 months). Three patients died during follow-up - one from complications after liver transplantation and two from disease progression. Post-ablation liver transplantation was performed in two patients. Conclusion MR-guided microwave ablation for hepatic malignancies is safe and effective, with no local tumor recurrences noted over a follow-up period of 36.7 ± 28.2 months. Clinical significance MR-guided microwave ablation is a promising minimally invasive treatment for hepatic malignancies, demonstrating no LTR at 36.7 ± 28.2 months. Precise, radiation-free needle placement in real-time and effective targeting of small tumors may further improve future patient care.

abstract: An increase in metabolomics research over the last decade has expanded species-specific knowledge of biological processes, but has primarily focused upon humans, domesticated and model animal species. Recent advances, particularly around data management pipelines for untargeted studies, make the field more accessible to disciplines outside those embedded in analytical chemistry, including wildlife conservation. To establish the breadth of existing wild vertebrate animal metabolomic research, specifically utilising non-invasive sampling, this scoping review establishes: (1) general trends in publication numbers; (2) coverage of wildlife taxonomic groups and species; (3) subject numbers and sample size; (4) non-invasive sample types; (5) metabolomic techniques utilised; (6) the context of current literature and (7) conservation implications. This scoping review was conducted following the JBI methodology and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR; searches were conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and supplemented with Google Scholar; following screening, 83 peer-reviewed original research papers were identified using predefined criteria and data extracted. The most popular areas of research were physiology and reproduction (30%) and diet and nutrition (27%). Although most publications focused on a single species, there were 11 multi-species publications, resulting in metabolomics data for 93 species. A large proportion of which, 72%, were mammalian, and of these, 52% are currently listed at risk of extinction on the IUCN Red List. With over 60% of all publications published between 2022-2025, non-invasive vertebrate wildlife metabolomics appears to be gaining traction as a tool in wildlife physiology research. However, future research would benefit from alignment with model animal metabolome research experimental design, as few studies included the consideration of metabolite extraction optimisation, storage conditions, the use of integrated omics platforms beyond microbiome analysis and consideration of statistical power, particularly in respect to intra-individual variation and the characterisation of species-specific metabolomes.

abstract: Phosphorus (P) is a vital macronutrient for grapevine (Vitis vinifera L.); however, the physiological and biochemical mechanisms governing grapevine adaptation across varying P supply levels-from deficiency to toxicity-require further clarification. This study evaluated the morphophysiological, nutritional, and biochemical adaptations of two contrasting grapevine cultivars, 'Khalili' and 'Perlette', to varying P levels: 0 mM (deficiency), 2.5 mM (sufficiency), and 5 mM (excess/toxicity). Results demonstrated that vegetative growth parameters-including stem length, stem diameter, lateral shoot number, and shoot dry weight-peaked under P sufficiency (2.5 mM), whereas severe P deficiency and P excess significantly impaired shoot development. In contrast, root dry weight remained comparable between 2.5 and 5 mM P, resulting in a higher root-to-shoot ratio under P excess. Nutrient profiling revealed distinct tissue-specific partitioning: P supply promoted foliar P and N accumulation while altering root macronutrient status (N, P, K, Ca, Mg), but sharply reduced foliar Fe and Zn concentrations. In roots, elevated P suppressed Fe, Mn, and Cu accumulation while enhancing Zn uptake. Both P deficiency and excess triggered oxidative stress, evidenced by up-regulated activities of antioxidant enzymes (catalase, guaiacol peroxidase, and ascorbate peroxidase) in leaves and roots. Cultivar-specific responses were prominent: P deficiency induced substantial anthocyanin accumulation and higher leaf starch content in 'Khalili', whereas 'Perlette' maintained more stable ionic homeostasis under P excess. Overall, 2.5 mM P represents the physiological optimum for grapevine vegetative development, while both extreme deficiency and excess impair growth via distinct mineral imbalances and oxidative stress cascades.

abstract: In response to the accuracy loss caused by lightweight networks on edge devices and the difficulty in accurately detecting small defect targets, this paper studies the lightweight You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) transmission line insulator defect detection algorithm based on Three-Branch Attention Mechanism (TBAM) and Enhanced Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Network (EMSFFN), which can perform high-precision detection on edge intelligent devices of unmanned aerial vehicles. Aiming at the problem of significant differences in the number of image categories in the current aerial insulator defect dataset, the dataset was expanded through image data augmentation to generate more minority class samples, balance the number of samples in each category. Experiments show that compared with YOLOv7, YOLOv8, YOLOv9, Detection Transformer (DETR) and Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN), the model parameters and computational complexity of TBAM-YOLOv8-EMSFFN are relatively low. Its AP reaches 99.2% and the mAP reaches 98.7%. Therefore, the TBAM-YOLOv8-EMSFFN model is suitable for unmanned aerial vehicles carrying edge intelligent devices to achieve power inspection.

abstract: Background Achieving the 2030 target of 90% human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage among girls by age 15 requires effectively reaching out-of-school (OOS) girls, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where most vaccine delivery occurs in school settings. This study explored country definitions of OOS girls and strategies for estimating the size of this population. Methods Between May and September 2024, we conducted semi-structured in-depth interviews with 32 HPV vaccine program stakeholders across six African and Asian LMICs with established HPV vaccination programs: Cambodia, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, and Uganda. Using hybrid inductive-deductive thematic analyses, we identified country approaches to defining OOS girls and to enumerating or estimating population size. Results Administratively, countries commonly defined OOS girls as those not enrolled in schools under the Ministry of Education's purview, but in practice, definitions varied across contexts. National-level data (e.g., census, school enrollment rates) and household-level approaches (e.g., headcounts) were commonly used to enumerate in-school and OOS girls. However, the distinction between in-school and OOS girls was often blurred during HPV vaccination implementation and evaluation, limiting the operational utility of these methods. To address these challenges, some countries adopted alternative approaches, including proxy-based population estimates using historical or approximate data and the prioritization of areas perceived to have a higher presence of OOS girls. These alternative approaches were perceived as pragmatic compromises between accuracy, feasibility, and resource constraints. Conclusion Accurate enumeration of OOS girls is important for HPV vaccination but may not be feasible in resource-limited settings. Pragmatic, context-specific estimation methods can offer a feasible way to identify and reach OOS girls more effectively with HPV vaccination services.
