abstract: Infertility is a global health challenge, and impaired endometrial receptivity remains an important contributor to treatment failure. Endometrial dysbiosis, characterized by a low proportion of Lactobacillus in the endometrial microbiota, has been proposed as a potentially modifiable factor that may affect endometrial receptivity and fertility, and treatment with Lactobacillus-containing probiotics is emerging as a promising therapeutic approach. However, the optimal route of Lactobacillus supplementation remains unclear. We compared oral versus vaginal supplementation using the same Lactobacillus-containing formulation as an adjunct to standardized doxycycline/metronidazole therapy and continued oral lactoferrin in patients with baseline endometrial Lactobacillus <10%, based on paired microbiome profiling of endometrial samples (aspirated intrauterine fluid and endometrial tissue). In this single-center retrospective cohort study, thirty-two patients underwent paired endometrial microbiome testing before and after 30 days of supplementation (oral, n = 18; vaginal, n = 14). In the vaginal group, the median endometrial Lactobacillus proportion increased from 0.05% [0.00-0.20] to 99.15% [70.45-100.00] (p = 0.001), whereas in the oral group it increased from 0.00% [0.00-0.18] to 0.30% [0.03-66.33] (p = 0.005). The median change was greater with vaginal versus oral supplementation (+98.90% [70.45-99.80] vs + 0.25% [0.03-66.33], p < 0.001). Post-treatment Lactobacillus ≥80%, used as an exploratory marker of marked microbiota improvement, was observed in 9/14 patients (64%) in the vaginal group and 3/18 (17%) in the oral group (p = 0.010). Exploratory reproductive outcomes were limited by the small sample size and did not define a reliable clinical threshold. These findings suggest that, within this combined treatment regimen, vaginal Lactobacillus supplementation may provide a greater route-associated additional improvement in endometrial microbiota profiles than oral administration.

abstract: Background Outdoor risky play and its relationship with children's health, development and well-being have garnered significant attention in recent years. Objective This systematic review synthesised existing evidence on associations between children's outdoor risky play and health outcomes. Methods A systematic search of five electronic databases (SportDiscus, MEDLINE, PsychInfo, ERIC, and CINAHL) was initially conducted in December 2023 and updated three times (April 2024, March 2025, May 2026) during the review development. Studies were eligible if they examined outdoor risky play in children aged 3-12 years and assessed a health outcome. Studies that did not use empirical data or did not have an accessible full-text were excluded. Five reviewers independently screened all articles and two separate reviewers resolved discrepancies. Quantitative narrative synthesis and qualitative framework synthesis were completed, and a mixed-methods synthesis occurred using a Pillar Integration Process. Results A total of 74 studies met the eligibility criteria for inclusion (48 quantitative; 19 qualitative; 7 mixed-methods). Six health domains (physical health, mental health and well-being, aggression, social, cognitive, and risk competence and injury) and four risky play exposures were identified: general risky play (n = 13 studies); environments that support risky play (n = 21); independent mobility (n = 19); and rough-and-tumble play (n = 21). General risky play and risky play supportive environments were positively associated with health outcomes across physical, mental health and well-being, social, cognitive, and risk competence domains. Independent mobility was positively associated with physical activity, with insufficient evidence to determine associations for other domains. Evidence for rough-and-tumble play was inconsistent across all domains, except for a negative association with aggression (i.e., increased aggression). The overall quality of evidence was low-to-moderate. Conclusion Outdoor risky play shows promising associations with children's health outcomes. The low number of studies in some health domains and need for higher quality evidence preclude firm conclusions and provide direction for further research in this field. Registration International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (No. CRD42023488023).

abstract: Poly (ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG) is the main enzyme responsible for degrading poly (ADP-ribose) (PAR), which is synthesized by PARP family proteins during the poly ADP-ribosylation cycle. We previously reported that the PARG inhibitor PDD00017273 suppressed osteoclast differentiation through PAR accumulation in RANKL-stimulated RAW264 cells. However, the molecular mechanisms of osteoclast differentiation under PARG inhibition remain unclear, and elucidation of the regulatory mechanisms may contribute to the development of novel therapeutic strategies for metabolic bone diseases associated with excessive activation of osteoclasts. In the present study, we investigated the molecular mechanisms whereby PDD00017273 suppresses osteoclast differentiation. RNA-seq and pathway analyses revealed enrichment of oxidative stress- and redox regulation-related pathways, and an ATAC-seq analysis identified enrichment of the NRF2-binding motif in PDD00017273-treated RAW264 cells compared with DMSO-treated control cells. Pharmacological inhibition of NRF2 partially restored the osteoclast formation suppressed by PDD00017273. Under these conditions, the expression levels of NRF2-regulated genes were suppressed, while the expression levels of osteoclast marker genes were upregulated. Taken together, the present findings suggest that PAR accumulation via PARG inhibition suppresses osteoclast differentiation through NRF2 activation, indicating that PAR metabolism plays an important role in osteoclast differentiation.

abstract: Purpose To evaluate patient satisfaction and preferences for portable versus table-mounted visual field (VF) devices in a rural telemedicine setting and identify influencing factors. Methods We conducted a sequential explanatory mixed methods study at three Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) within the Alabama Screening and Intervention for Glaucoma and eye Health through Telemedicine (AL-SIGHT) study. Participants completed VF testing with table-mounted Humphrey Field Analyzer (HFA), tablet-based Melbourne Rapid Fields (MRF), and virtual reality (VR)-based VisuALL perimeters. Participants rated satisfaction, comfort, ease of use, and future testing preference. Chi-square tests assessed differences in device preferences. Twelve participants completed semi-structured interviews to explore reasons underlying preferences. Qualitative data were analyzed in NVivo 14 using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Among 271 respondents (mean age 60.4 years; 62.4% women), 50.6% preferred VR-based, 35.1% tablet-based, and 14.4% table-mounted for future testing (χ2 (2) = 53.52, p < 0.001, Cramér's V = 0.31). Satisfaction was highest for VR-based (56.9% very satisfied), followed by tablet-based (49.4%), and HFA (38.0%). VR-based perimeter was most frequently selected as the most comfortable (55.7%; χ2 (2) = 63.33, p < 0.001, V = 0.34) and easiest to use (54.6%; χ2 (2) = 71.96, p < 0.001, V = 0.36). Preferences did not vary significantly across demographic variables (all p > 0.05). Qualitative themes identified four key drivers: comfort and physical experience, visual experience, ease of use and interaction, and psychological and motivational factors. Portability and community suitability were valued. Conclusion Rural underserved patients strongly preferred portable visual field devices, particularly VR-based, over table-mounted HFA. Comfort, ergonomic flexibility, immersive visual experience, and simplicity of interaction were central determinants of preference. Portable perimetry may enhance patient-centered glaucoma monitoring within telemedicine programs and access in resource-limited settings.

abstract: Background Extreme risk protection orders (ERPOs) temporarily prohibit the purchase and possession of firearms by people at high risk of harming themselves or others. This study drew on the experiences of ERPO respondents to learn about the perceived short- and long-term consequences of the law. Methods For this qualitative descriptive study, we conducted 24 semi-structured interviews between March and November 2024 with respondents to ERPOs issued in California between 2016 and 2020. We purposively sampled 250 respondents for whom we had previously abstracted ERPO court case data to ensure adequate representation across domains of interest (e.g., demographics, location) and invited respondents to participate in the study by mail. All interviews were recorded, double coded, and thematically analyzed. Results Our diverse participants described heterogeneous consequences across 4 domains: violence risk, legal/economic outcomes, opinions/attitudes, and social/emotional wellbeing. Two participants believed their ERPOs prevented violence and 1 was unsure; the rest believed that they would not have committed violence irrespective of the ERPO. Some perceived the ERPO to have had negligible effects on their lives, while others described both positive consequences, including self-reflection and behavior change, and negative consequences, including employment or housing difficulties, stigmatization, damaged relationships, loss of trust in legal institutions, and perceived exacerbation of violence risk. Participants reported that they were not connected to mental health care or other supportive services through the ERPO process. Conclusions Participants perceived ERPOs to have varied and mixed consequences. These accounts identify outcomes that warrant consideration in ERPO research, policy, and implementation. Future research should assess the prevalence and distribution of these consequences and evaluate whether policy refinements can reduce adverse experiences without compromising the public health benefits of these laws.

abstract: This retrospective study examined the historical progression of Olympic swimming performance across 24 Olympic Games from Paris 1924 to Paris 2024. Finalist race data for 1553 women and 1641 men were extracted from the official World Aquatics database, including final times, reaction times, and calculated swimming speeds across all strokes (freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly) and Olympic distances (50-1500 m). Across all strokes and distances, final times demonstrated substantial reductions over the century, with the most pronounced improvements observed in freestyle and long-distance events. The largest percentage improvements in performance were observed during specific Olympic cycles, including 1956, 1972, and 2008, which coincided with major developments in pool engineering, competition regulations, training methodologies, and swimsuit technology. Swimming speeds increased consistently in all events, while reaction-time analyses revealed significant improvements across Olympic Games during the period in which reaction-time data were recorded. Overall, these findings demonstrate substantial long-term improvements in Olympic swimming performance and provide a comprehensive historical overview of performance changes across strokes, distances, and sexes. The periods associated with the largest performance improvements coincided with major technological, biomechanical, and regulatory developments in the sport. The results may serve as valuable benchmarks for coaches, athletes, and sports scientists to evaluate long-term performance trends and prepare for future international competitions.

abstract: Large river ecosystems are complex and difficult to study. Spatial and temporal variability in managed river ecosystems is further complicated by structural alterations such as channelization, dams, and hydroelectric power stations. The increasing frequency and intensity of harmful algal blooms in lotic systems challenges the convention that productivity in these systems is low. A substantial algal bloom in the Ohio River in the fall of 2015 with a lesser bloom in the fall of 2019 demonstrated the need for research in this area. To characterize algal dynamics in managed rivers, and specifically the Ohio River, high frequency sensors were deployed on lock structures of the Robert C. Byrd and Greenup Dams bracketing the 100-km Greenup pool and providing continuous monitoring of pool conditions. Depth profiles at transect sampling locations were conducted through the pool's entirety to profile spatial variability. Parameters measured included light, turbidity, chlorophyll-a, phycocyanin, specific conductance, temperature, pH and dissolved oxygen. These data are combined with USGS discharge data and nutrient data from multiple sources to examine temporal and spatial conditions in the pool as they pertain to algal growth and productivity. High turbidity and subsequent light limitation constrain algal growth throughout most of the year. Lower flow conditions in the late summer months demonstrated higher light penetration and limited thermal stratification and were associated with higher algal biomass as conditions approach those of a lentic system. Chlorophyll-a, indicating green algae or diatoms, dominated the late summer and fall algal communities during this investigation. Cyanobacteria, indicated by phycocyanin measurements, showed peaks in winter months with cooler temperatures and reduced pool retention, possibly indicating tributary sources. These data will support the development of models to advance harmful algal bloom (HAB) predictions and evaluation of management options. Results may be relavent to other managed river systems.

abstract: Objective To determine the prevalence of sarcopenia and identify clinical and functional factors independently associated with confirmed sarcopenia in individuals with stroke undergoing rehabilitation. Methods This cross-sectional study enrolled 209 adults with stroke admitted for neurological rehabilitation. Sarcopenia was defined according to the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 (EWGSOP2) algorithm, using SARC-CalF, handgrip strength, five-times sit-to-stand test, physical performance measures and appendicular skeletal muscle mass by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify factors independently associated with confirmed sarcopenia. Results Confirmed sarcopenia was identified in 55 of 209 participants (26.3%; 95% CI: 20.6% to 32.8%). Participants with sarcopenia were older and had lower body mass index (BMI), poorer physical performance, and greater motor impairment than those without sarcopenia. In the multivariable model, lower BMI (OR = 0.70; 95% CI: 0.59 to 0.83), positive SARC-CalF screening (OR = 6.37; 95% CI: 2.03 to 20.05), and lower Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores (OR = 0.83; 95% CI: 0.69 to 0.99) remained independently associated with sarcopenia. Motor impairment severity, assessed using Fugl-Meyer motor categories, was also independently associated with sarcopenia. Conclusion DXA-confirmed post-stroke sarcopenia affected approximately one in four individuals undergoing rehabilitation and was independently associated with lower BMI, poorer physical performance, and greater motor impairment. These findings indicate that sarcopenia is closely linked to functional impairment after stroke and reinforce the importance of integrating muscle health and functional assessment during rehabilitation. Early identification of individuals at risk may support more individualized rehabilitation strategies and improve clinical decision-making.

abstract: Background Osteosarcopenia - the concurrent presence of sarcopenia and low bone mass, including osteopenia or osteoporosis - is emerging as a significant health issue in aging populations. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of osteosarcopenia and identify factors associated with prevalent osteosarcopenia among older Vietnamese outpatients. Materials and methods A cross-sectional study was conducted on 389 outpatients aged ≥60 years at Can Tho University of Medicine and Pharmacy Hospital from 01/202511/2025. Osteosarcopenia was defined by coexistent low bone mass (osteopenia/osteoporosis via DXA) and sarcopenia defined according to AWGS 2019 as low muscle mass accompanied by low muscle strength, low physical performance or both. Logistic regression analyses were used to assess factors associated with osteosarcopenia. All data were analysed using R version 4.5.5. Results The overall prevalence of osteosarcopenia was 26.7% (95% CI 22.6-31.3%). Prevalence was similar in women and men (26.3% vs 28.6%, p = 0.68). On multivariable analysis, older age (per 1-year increase; OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02-1.10), lower BMI (per 1 kg/m2 increase; OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.50-0.65), coronary artery disease (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.09-3.95), and diabetes (OR 2.48, 95% CI 1.35-4.56) were independently associated with osteosarcopenia. Conclusion Osteosarcopenia affected about one in four older outpatients in this Vietnamese cohort. Older age, lower body mass index, coronary artery disease, and diabetes were independently associated with osteosarcopenia. These findings highlight the importance of early screening and integrated management of bone and muscle health in older adults.

abstract: Image ciphers are usually proposed with a fixed battery of statistical indicators, and the numbers reported for competing designs are almost never produced under the same conditions, on the same pictures, with the same code. We address that gap for one family of designs and propose a cipher whose components come from provable combinatorics and standardised cryptography rather than a chaotic map. The scheme, RAPID-Gray, builds three keyed switching networks on the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak Ramanujan graph X(29,41), restricts them to the image domain by cycle walking, interleaves them with two Cauchy maximum-distance-separable layers over GF(28), applies a two-pass nonlinear feedback diffusion, and closes with AES-CTR whitening and an HMAC-SHA-256 tag over a fresh 96-bit nonce. Five recent designs were re-implemented without algorithmic alteration and evaluated with identical code on three medical and three general 256 × 256 grayscale images. All six recovered every plaintext exactly. Beyond that, the spread is wide: cipher entropy ranges from 6.9320 to 7.9976 bits, one collapses to an NPCR of 0.0015%, two produce unchanged ciphertexts under the tested one-bit key perturbation, and only the proposed scheme rejects tampered ciphertexts. Agreement on entropy and correlation says little; plaintext sensitivity, key sensitivity and integrity are where these designs actually separate. Three of the five reference designs left a step of their published description underdetermined; in each case a fixed, reversible resolution was adopted and is documented, so the comparison is between faithful re-implementations rather than between the published texts themselves.

abstract: Standard cell-culture ware is mass-produced in fixed designs, whereas many tissue-engineering workflows require custom inserts, lids, chambers, or patterned substrates, especially during early-stage research and method development. Conventional fabrication methods for cell culture accessories involve injection molding and machining, which are too costly and time-consuming to implement for producing custom designs in small batches, and/or while testing the usefulness of a new design before mass production. Here, we propose polycarbonate (PC) thermoforming as a solution for creating customized transparent and autoclavable accessories. We demonstrate that optimized preheating of PC overcomes issues with bubbling during thermoforming. The use of high heat deflection temperature (HDT) resins allows these PC devices to be thermoformed off molds created by Digital Light Processing (DLP) 3D prints, enabling rapid prototyping of the PC. Using this approach, we fabricated custom PC well plate inserts, staining chambers and other custom accessories. We next validated the cytocompatibility of these devices by demonstrating culture and cardiomyocyte differentiation of human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC). Finally, we demonstrated the utility of thermoformed PC for creating 3D engineered tissues (cardiospheres). These results establish DLP-assisted PC thermoforming as a rapid, low-cost workflow for fabricating transparent, autoclavable, user-defined cell-culture accessories during prototyping and small-batch bioengineering applications.

abstract: Background Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality globally, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention is the standard treatment for ST-elevation myocardial infarction, a life-threatening acute coronary syndrome requiring urgent revascularization. Despite increasing access to this intervention in sub-Saharan Africa, evidence on patients' lived experiences of recovery remains limited. This study explored patients' experiences of recovery and quality of life following primary percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-elevation myocardial infarction in Tanzania. Methods An interpretive descriptive qualitative design was employed. Fourteen patients who had undergone primary percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-elevation myocardial infarction were purposively sampled at a national referral cardiac centre and interviewed within three months after PCI. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Participants perceived quality of life after PCI as an evolving experience closely linked to their recovery, with improvements in one aspect often accompanied by ongoing challenges in others. Six interrelated themes emerged: physical symptoms, functional capacity and daily activities, emotional responses, coping and illness perceptions, social support and relationships, and health system interactions and communication. Although participants generally reported symptom improvement and gradual functional recovery, persistent fatigue, activity limitations, emotional uncertainty, and unmet informational needs continued to influence their quality of life. Family support and adaptive coping helped participants adjust to life after PCI, while healthcare communication shaped their confidence in managing recovery. Conclusion Recovery after primary percutaneous coronary intervention extends beyond survival to include physical, emotional, and social dimensions. Holistic, patient-centred post-intervention care is needed to support long-term recovery in resource-limited settings.

abstract: Objective This study proposes a refined approach to anatomy-based fitting (rfABF) that aims to reduce interaural place mismatch in bilateral cochlear implant (CI) users with asymmetric electrode array insertions between ears, a condition frequently associated with incomplete cochlear coverage. Design Prospective monocenter proof-of-concept study comparing rfABF with conventional clinically based fitting (CBF). ABF maps were prepared using two algorithmically derived methods: one scaling inter-electrode spectral spacing (zipped), and another transposing the ratio between clinical and tonotopic frequencies (transposed). These maps were then refined based on user feedback until a natural sound quality was achieved. Assessments consisted of speech perception in quiet and noise, sound localization, subjective sound quality ratings (HISQUI19), and listening effort assessed using pupillometry. Study sample Nine experienced adult bilateral CI users with interaural asymmetry in electrode array insertion depth and/or electrode array type. Results Bilateral speech understanding improved significantly with rfABF in quiet (CBF: 77.5% ± 8.1%; rfABF: 83.1% ± 8.0%; p = 0.025) and in noise under both S0N0 (signal and noise from front) and S0Ncontra (signal from front, noise from contralateral ear) configurations. Interaural place-of-stimulation mismatch was substantially reduced from a mean of 33.8° ± 27.3° to 6.4° ± 4.2° with rfABF. Exploratory, descriptive pupillometry indicated reduced listening effort in a subset of participants, reflected by lower event-related pupil dilation (ERPD) amplitudes, particularly in cases where speech intelligibility was preserved or improved. Conclusions rfABF shows clinical potential to improve speech understanding and facilitate access to binaural cues in bilateral CI users with asymmetric electrode array insertions, with preliminary evidence for reduced listening effort.

abstract: Candida auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen and a major global health threat, highlighting the urgent need for new therapeutics. We screened ~2,600 FDA-approved drugs and clinical compounds and identified darapladib (DAL), a phospholipase A2 inhibitor, as a potent antifungal agent against multidrug-resistant C. auris. DAL exhibited antifungal activity against all tested C. auris isolates and showed broad-spectrum activity against other tested clinically important fungal pathogens, including other Candida, Cryptococcus, and mucormycosis-associated species, with minimum inhibitory concentrations of 4-16 μg/mL. DAL also displayed rapid fungicidal activity against C. auris and synergized with amphotericin B against C. auris and filamentous fungal pathogens. More importantly, serial exposure of C. auris to subinhibitory concentrations of DAL for 16 passages did not result in detectable resistance. Mechanistic studies indicated that DAL acts through an ergosterol-dependent membrane targeting mechanism, as exogenous ergosterol attenuated its activity and ergosterol-related haploinsufficient mutants showed reduced susceptibility. Consistent with this mechanism, DAL increased membrane permeability, nucleic acid leakage, and reactive oxygen species. In a Caenorhabditis elegans-C. auris infection model, DAL reduced the C. auris burden to below the limit of detection. Together, these findings support further investigation of DAL as a repurposed antifungal candidate against drug-resistant fungal infections.

abstract: Long-term disposal and management of nuclear waste is one of the major hurdles for nuclear energy. Deep geological disposal, an idea originating in the 1970s, is currently the preferred path being followed in many countries. However, acceptance of this approach is hindered by societal concerns around the safety of the "one-million years" geological disposal and passing the waste burden to future generations. iMAGINE, an integrated nuclear system based on molten salt fast reactor technology with self-sustained iso-breeding, online clean-up and reverse reprocessing, has been proposed as an innovative way to eliminate the demand for a long-term high-level waste disposal. In this work, we investigate the use of iMAGINE as a technological approach for reimagining high-level nuclear waste management by overcoming the challenges of classical partitioning and transmutation (P&T). After discussing the current status and limitations of P&T along with an overview of the nuclear waste classification and management framework existing in major nuclear power producing countries, we demonstrate the potential impact of iMAGINE in simplifying the disposal of high-level waste. The results indicate that among the key long-lived radionuclides, many lie well below the criteria for requiring deep geological disposal. Besides Finland, India and Russia where most (or all) of the important long-lived fission products exceed current high-level waste thresholds, only two to three fission products (generally with half-lives from 30 to 100 years) exceed the national limits in Canada, China, France, Germany, Japan, and South Korea, while concrete conclusions can't be drawn for the UK and US based on available information. The results presented here do not aim to make inflated claims but should be seen as the scientific basis for deeper discussions amongst all nuclear waste disposal stakeholders to explore a novel technological solution for rethinking high-level waste management and possibly eliminating the need for a "one-million years" geological disposal.

abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a respiratory disease with a high degree of cellular heterogeneity and molecular complexity, characterized pathologically by persistent airflow limitation and an inflammatory-tissue remodeling cascade involving multiple cell types. Traditional transcriptomics lack the resolution to precisely define cell subpopulation roles in COPD. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) overcomes this limitation by enabling high-resolution analysis of cell-type-specific mechanisms in COPD. A total of 101,009 cells from three scRNA-seq datasets were integrated to profile COPD-related molecular features and cell interactions at single-cell resolution. Analysis identified four major cell types and 17 distinct cell subtypes. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed a significant reduction in signaling activity of macrophages and fibroblasts, whereas certain immune cells exhibited enhanced signaling, suggesting that immune dysregulation plays a pivotal role in COPD pathogenesis. Further analysis focused on macrophage-dominant myeloid cells and fibroblasts, uncovering their critical roles in inflammation modulation and fibrosis progression. Meanwhile, this study also identified 19 chemicals that may influence COPD progression by modulating cellular gene expression. This study provides an important molecular basis for unraveling the cell-cell interaction network of COPD and elucidating the mechanism of each cell subpopulation in the disease process.

abstract: Background Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health challenge, with rapidly rising incidence in low- and middle-income countries, including Ethiopia. Survival outcomes are compromised by late-stage presentation, limited therapeutic capacity, and weak post-treatment follow-up. Although survival analysis is critical for characterizing CRC prognosis, insufficient attention has been given to the performance and validity of commonly applied survival models in Ethiopian populations, particularly when statistical assumptions are violated. Objective To identify key clinical and treatment-related prognostic factors influencing overall survival among Ethiopian CRC patients and to assess the robustness and interpretability of Cox proportional hazard model (Cox PH model), stratified Cox proportional hazard model, frailty model, and Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) models, focusing on model adequacy under assumption violations. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 161 colorectal cancer patients diagnosed between 2012 and 2016. Survival probabilities were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, with group comparisons via log-rank tests. Multivariable modeling employed Cox proportional hazards, stratified Cox proportional hazard model, frailty, and accelerated failure time models. Model adequacy was evaluated through Akaike Information Criterion, concordance indices, and the Global Schoenfeld test for proportional hazards assessment. Results The Cox proportional hazard model violated the proportional hazards assumption (global p = 0.043), primarily due to histological subtype effects, indicating that the standard Cox proportional hazard model was not appropriate for this dataset. Assumption violations were mitigated using the stratified Cox proportional hazard model (global p = 0.122). Among accelerated failure time models, the log-logistic distribution provided superior model fit (AIC = 649.88; concordance = 0.724). Time-ratio (TR) interpretation showed that surgery extended survival by approximately 2.4-fold, whereas elevated baseline carcinoembryonic antigen levels and metastatic disease reduced survival duration by nearly half. Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen, distant metastasis, vascular invasion, and squamous cell histology were consistently associated with poorer prognosis, while surgery and chemotherapy remained protective across models. Conclusion Rigorous model checking indicates that the conventional Cox proportional hazards model is inappropriate for this cohort due to proportional hazard assumption violations. Accelerated failure time modeling, particularly the log-logistic form, offered improved fit and clearer time-based interpretation of covariate effects. These findings underscore the importance of model validation in CRC survival research and highlight the need for improved early detection, surgical access, and targeted management of aggressive tumor subtypes to enhance patient outcomes in Ethiopia.

abstract: Studying limited datasets derived from complex interacting systems, such as neural population activity, represents an important and challenging task. The level of detail in recorded activities is highly influenced by the temporal resolution at which the activities are studied. However, does more detail always lead to a correct assessment of the system? This study examines how temporal resolution influences the inference of higher-order statistical dependencies and information representation in population-level neuronal activity. Using a minimally biased data-driven statistical inference framework, minimally complex models, we studied grid cell populations in the medial entorhinal cortex across a broad range of temporal resolutions. Results based on 23 grid cell recordings including different animals and behavioral states show that at an intermediate temporal resolution (𝒪(102)  ms), the inferred model captures significant higher order dependencies alongside efficient information representations, whereas the finest and the coarsest temporal resolutions lead to poor information representation. The informative temporal resolution can be identified by two criteria: the bin size at which the inferred interaction structure is most consistent across population sizes, and the peak of the model's information representations, which agree closely across recordings. These findings indicate that temporal resolution is a critical factor in the inference of higher order neural structure and highlight that resolution-aware modeling is crucial for accurate analysis and characterization of collective dynamics in complex neuronal systems.

abstract: The global rise of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens has increased interest in bee-derived natural products as sources of novel antimicrobials. While most research has focused on European honey bee (Apis mellifera) products, the 550 species of stingless bees found globally also produce honey and other hive products, representing a largely unexplored source of novel bioactives. This study investigates the antimicrobial activity of propolis extracts and honey from the Australian stingless bee Tetragonula carbonaria against 16 clinically significant bacterial and fungal pathogens, using broth microdilution methodology. T. carbonaria propolis and honey exhibited distinct antimicrobial profiles: propolis showed selective activity against a subset of bacteria and certain filamentous fungi, while honey showed broad-spectrum activity against all tested bacteria and selective activity against dermatophyte fungi. The level of H2O2 production in T. carbonaria honey was only moderately correlated with its antimicrobial activity, and the total phenolic content of propolis did not correlate significantly with its antimicrobial activity, suggesting other bee- or plant-derived compounds are important contributors. These findings highlight T. carbonaria propolis and honey as promising antimicrobials and potential sources of novel bioactive compounds.

abstract: Background E-cigarette use, also known as vaping, has rapidly increased in recent years, often marketed as a safer alternative to traditional smoking. While the cardiovascular risks of vaping are increasingly being recognized, its relationship with dyslipidemia remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between e-cigarette use and serum lipid levels, specifically total cholesterol (TC), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL), and triglycerides (TG). Methods A search of PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, CENTRAL, CINAHL, medRxiv, and Google Scholar was conducted up to May 31,2025. Eligible studies included adult populations and assessed the association between exclusive e-cigarette use and lipids. Study quality was assessed using the Methodological Standards for Epidemiological Research (MASTER) scale. Meta-analysis of adjusted odds ratios (aOR) for dyslipidemia and unadjusted weighted mean differences (uWMD) for each lipid was conducted using a bias-adjusted inverse-variance heterogeneity method. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic, and publication bias using Doi plots and the LFK index, with the LFK index used as the primary quantitative criterion. Planned subgroup analyses by age group and sex could not be performed due to insufficient stratified reporting in included studies. The overall quality of evidence for each lipid outcome was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Results Of 4,160 identified data sources, seven observational studies from the U.S.A., South Korea, Romania, and Iraq with a total of 25,690 participants met the inclusion criteria. Meta-analysis showed that vaping was associated with higher odds of hypertriglyceridemia (aOR 3.10, 95% CI 1.18 to 8.16, I2 = 80.1%, LFK = 1.34), and higher odds of low HDL (aOR 3.26, 95% CI 2.28 to 4.65, I2 = 3.1%, LFK = 1.41). In studies with unadjusted mean lipid levels, the primary quality-effects model showed no statistically significant difference in TC (unadjusted weighted mean difference (uWMD) +3.66 mg/dL, 95% CI -13.89 to 21.20, I2 = 86.9%, LFK = 9.44) but showed higher LDL (uWMD +12.40 mg/dL, 95% CI 7.91 to 16.88, I2 = 29.1%, LFK = 1.05), and VLDL (uWMD +3.23 mg/dL, 95% CI 1.43 to 5.02, I2 = 0.0%, publication bias not assessed). For all outcomes, the GRADE certainty of evidence was very low. Conclusion This synthesis suggests that e-cigarette use may be associated with adverse lipid profiles, but the evidence remains observational and of very low certainty, limiting causal inference. Further well-designed longitudinal studies, using validated smoking-status assessment, detailed vaping exposure measures, fasting lipid panels, repeated lipid measurements, and adjustment for key cardiometabolic confounders, are needed to clarify these associations.

abstract: Background Optimal mucosal visualization is essential for high-quality esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), particularly for the detection of subtle upper gastrointestinal lesions. Oral simethicone and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) are commonly used to improve mucosal cleanliness, whereas lidocaine ice popsicles provide effective topical pharyngeal anesthesia for unsedated EGD. We evaluated whether incorporating simethicone and NAC into a lidocaine ice popsicle could improve mucosal visibility while maintaining patient comfort. Methods This single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial enrolled 374 adults undergoing unsedated diagnostic EGD between December 2024 and June 2025. Participants were randomized (1:1) to receive either a lidocaine ice popsicle containing simethicone (100 mg) and NAC (600 mg) or a conventional lidocaine ice popsicle. The primary outcome was mucosal visibility assessed using a modified Total Visibility Score (TVS). Secondary outcomes included procedure time, water volume required for mucosal cleansing, additional simethicone use, endoscopist satisfaction, ease of esophageal instrumentation, gag reflex, patient satisfaction, discomfort, pain, and adverse events. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Results All 374 randomized participants (187 per group) completed the study and were analyzed according to their assigned groups. Baseline characteristics were descriptively similar between groups. The intervention group had a significantly lower TVS than the control group (6.19 ± 0.51 vs. 10.39 ± 2.22; mean difference, -4.20; 95% CI, -4.53 to -3.88; P < 0.001), indicating better mucosal visibility. Exploratory segment-specific analyses showed lower visibility scores in all six gastrointestinal segments. The intervention group also had higher endoscopist satisfaction, shorter procedure time (10.87 ± 1.44 vs. 12.75 ± 0.96 min; P < 0.001), lower water requirements for mucosal cleansing, and less frequent use of additional diluted simethicone during EGD (12.8% vs. 96.8%; P < 0.001). Exploratory analyses showed statistically significant differences in gag reflex and pain scores, although the absolute differences were small. Patient satisfaction, discomfort, and ease of esophageal instrumentation did not differ significantly between groups. No adverse events were observed during the defined observation period. Conclusions The combined formulation of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine incorporated into a lidocaine ice popsicle improved mucosal visibility compared with a lidocaine ice popsicle alone during unsedated EGD and was associated with improved procedural efficiency. This integrated formulation may provide a practical approach to pre-endoscopic preparation by combining topical anesthesia with mucosal cleansing. Further multicenter studies are warranted to confirm its effectiveness, generalizability, and safety with longer follow-up. Trial registration Thai Clinical Trials Registry TCTR20240606004.

abstract: The preschool years are a critical period for the rapid development of executive function in children. While executive function in preschool children is influenced by multiple factors, existing research has been limited by its theoretical and empirical perspectives, resulting in singular pathways for promoting executive function. To address this, the study adopted a systems theory perspective to explore the configurational pathways through which subsystems of gross motor skills are associated with higher levels of executive function in preschoolers. The study included test data from 67 children aged 3-6 years. Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), six subsystems of gross motor skills (running, jumping, throwing, catching, kicking, and striking) were treated as antecedent conditions to explore the configurational associations of gross motor skill subsystems with executive function. Necessary condition analysis indicated that no single gross motor skill subsystem constituted a necessary condition for higher executive function in preschool children. Subsequent configurational analysis identified three distinct pathways that are associated with higher levels of executive function (with a total consistency of 0.906 and an overall coverage of 0.496). The development of executive function in preschool children is not associated with single gross motor actions in a linear manner but rather with multiple concurrent combinations of gross motor skill subsystems characterized by "multiple concurrent pathways leading to the same goal." This is reflected in the three configurational pathways: "a combination of jumping, throwing, and striking actions," "a combination of running, kicking, and striking actions," and "a combination of running, throwing, and catching actions." These findings provide preliminary insights and hypothesis-generating evidence for future research on gross motor skill activities and executive function development in preschool children.

abstract: Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma (UPS) is a genetically complex type of soft tissue sarcoma (STS) and there are few therapeutic options for advanced disease. Immune checkpoint blockade therapy may be of benefit to a subset of UPS patients, particularly those with elevated tumoral Programmed Cell Death Ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression and an inflamed tumour microenvironment. From transcriptomic analyses we previously identified Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 1 (STAT1) expression, a key mediator of interferon-γ (IFN-γ) signaling, as enriched in a cohort of UPS cases with elevated PD-L1 levels that were observed to have an improved clinical outcome. This led us to investigate the role of STAT1 in UPS biology. We examined the effects of STAT1 loss, and overexpression of either wild type or tyrosine phosphorylation-deficient STAT1 in primary human UPS cell lines. We observed that IFN-γ treatment decreased cell counts, increased cell death, and induced the secretion of CXCR3 ligands in a STAT1-dependent manner. Overexpression of wild type STAT1, but not a tyrosine to phenylalanine phospho-mutant (Y701F), restored IFN-γ-mediated cell death and cytokine secretion, highlighting the importance of Y701 phosphorylation in STAT1-associated antitumour functions. STAT1 Y701 phosphorylation status was associated with gene expression changes that were cell line specific. Together, these findings shed light on the central role of STAT1, and specifically the Y701 phosphorylation, in mediating IFN-γ signaling and related phenotypes. This study underscores the need for further exploration of the role of STAT1 phosphorylation in tumor-immune interactions within UPS.

abstract: Southeast Asia is home to 22 endemic raptors, and almost all are classified as "Endangered" or higher by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN). The limited range and fragmented distribution of some Southeast Asian raptors from the genus Nisaetus hinder the characterization of these endangered birds. This study presents the mitochondrial sequences of the Pinsker's Hawk-eagle (Nisaetus pinskeri) and Changeable Hawk-eagle (Nisaetus cirrhatus) and conducts a comparative mitogenome analysis across Accipitriformes. The partial mitogenome lengths of N. pinskeri and N. cirrhatus are 18,654 bp and 17,874 bp, with a GC content of 46.4% and 47.4%, respectively. An extra cytosine at position 174 of the nad3 gene was present in both mitogenomes, which was not previously observed in other Nisaetus species. Phylogenetic analysis recapitulated the topology of the order Accipitriformes. It showed that N. pinskeri and N. cirrhatus are closely related to each other and sister to the rest of the Nisaetus representatives. Moreover, the trees based on concatenated mitochondrial protein-coding genes were closer to the latest reported phylogenies than single-gene trees using conventional mitochondrial markers. The selection pressure analysis showed that all protein-coding genes experienced purifying selection, with the highest in atp8 and the lowest in cox1. As the first report of the near-complete mitogenomes of these raptors, this study expands the available genomic resources for these understudied raptors and provides a foundation for future population genetic research.

abstract: Forecasts of whether marine species can evolve fast enough to survive climate change rely largely on single-stage tolerance assays, tacitly assuming that tolerance measured at one developmental stage reflects adaptive capacity across the organism's life cycle. We test this assumption in a common marine bivalve (Mercenaria mercenaria) and find that it fails in sign, not degree: larval and post-metamorphic tolerance to end-century ocean acidification are strongly negatively correlated (r = -0.53, 95% CI [-0.69, -0.33]) across family-level, pedigree-conditioned and animal model estimates, with pervasive rank reversals among the top performers of each stage. A multivariate analysis of the among-family covariance matrix G shows why: under acidification, 57% of the among-family variance collapses onto a single dominant axis that loads positively on every larval trait and negatively on every post-metamorphic trait, whereas under ambient conditions the same families show no cross-stage covariance at all. Acidification therefore does not merely depress performance-it reorganizes the genetic architecture into a cross-stage conflict. Under ramping RCP 8.5 forcing this conflict geometry dictates the direction-not merely the magnitude-of adaptation: only balanced multi-stage selection preserves family diversity, whereas single-stage selection systematically erodes the opposite axis. In complex life cycles, resilience is a geometric property of ontogeny that forecasts cannot compress into a single-stage without inverting the sign of the answer.

abstract: Functional vision loss at any stage affects quality of life even before clinically quantified to be moderate or severe. Eye care providers as the gatekeepers to vision rehabilitation services often underestimate how small variations in functional vision loss can have a significant impact in a patient's life. Greater provider-patient communication about vision loss is an opportunity to build trust and increase access to vision rehabilitation services to improve quality of life. Tertiary eye care centers serve the greatest number of visually impaired patients. The purpose of this study was to find what factors influenced eye care providers with vision rehabilitation service referral decision-making at a tertiary medical center. We also further studied whether decision making was influenced by the eye care provider's specialty, volume of practice, years of practice, number of practicing locations, gender and continuing education status. Our survey found that about 77% of respondents were early (<10 years) in their career and 75% of posterior segment specialists agreed that people with any functional vision complaint should be referred to services regardless of visual acuity. Fifty-two percent of all respondents indicated the reason for low referrals to services was due to a lack of inquiry from patients. Inquiry about driving status by patients was an important factor for referral to services for 35% of respondents. Forty-five percent of respondents reported lack of vision rehabilitation providers and long wait times as a barrier to referrals. However, only 61% of respondents reported "never" to "sometimes" referring to community services. Posterior specialists attended more continuing education courses related to low vision/ vision rehabilitation than anterior segment specialists. By understanding influencers on eye care providers decision making, we will be able to make more targeted recommendations on workflow changes, continuing education and quality improvement processes to increase access to vision rehabilitation services.

abstract: Beech leaf disease, caused by the invasive foliar nematode Litylenchus crenatae, is an emerging threat to Fagus grandifolia across North America. Since its initial detection in 2012, the disease has spread to a total of 16 U.S. states and the Canadian Province of Ontario; however, the mechanisms underlying nematode dispersal remain poorly understood. This study evaluated multiple potential dispersal pathways across two forest sites in central Pennsylvania through integrated field surveys, environmental monitoring, and experimental validation. Weekly sampling was conducted to characterize nematode population dynamics in relation to temperature, precipitation, wind, and humidity. Long distance water-mediated dispersal was assessed through creek sampling, while biotic dispersal was investigated through field sampling from migratory bird feet during high-moisture events and a controlled greenhouse transmission experiment. Wind dispersal was further examined in a pilot study using unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted rainwater collection during precipitation events. Nematode presence was detected across all investigated pathways, supporting dispersal via water flow, rain splash, and biotic vectors. Funnel-based sampling recovered Litylenchus crenatae up to 90 m from infected trees, demonstrating movement beyond the immediate canopy area. Confirmed downstream transport of nematodes suggests waterways may facilitate long-distance dispersal across forested landscapes. Litylenchus crenatae was recovered from the feet of migratory birds, and greenhouse experiments confirmed that bird-associated nematodes could infect healthy beech seedlings, providing evidence for avian-mediated transmission. Desiccation assays demonstrated that live Litylenchus crenatae specimens could survive up to 10 days in the absence of available moisture, indicating that the nematodes may remain viable during transport on bird feet or exposed surfaces. In addition, unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted rainwater sampling detected Litylenchus crenatae within canopy-associated precipitation samples, providing additional evidence for short-distance aerial dispersal during wind and rain events. Together, these findings demonstrate that beech leaf disease spread is driven by multiple interacting abiotic and biotic dispersal mechanisms operating across spatial scales.

abstract: Root growth must continuously adjust to fluctuating nutrient availability, yet the mechanisms that quantitatively integrate environmental signals into developmental responses remain poorly understood. Distinct nutrient stresses, including ammonium toxicity and phosphate deficiency, inhibit primary root growth through iron-dependent processes, suggesting that iron acts as a central regulatory node. Here, we show that plants use an antagonistic module composed of CYBDOM ferrireductases and LPR ferroxidases to regulate apoplastic iron homeostasis and control root growth in a graded manner. Genetic perturbation of this module demonstrates that root growth inhibition scales quantitatively with iron accumulation, supporting a proportional control mechanism rather than a binary response. Loss of CYBDOM function causes excessive iron accumulation, elevated reactive oxygen species, and impaired meristem activity, whereas increased CYBDOM activity buffers iron deposition and confers resistance to stress. Mechanistically, iron-induced oxidative stress promotes HYP1 expression, which in turn limits further iron accumulation. Transcriptomic analyses distinguish ammonium-specific responses from Fe-associated transcriptional changes enriched in redox buffering and cell-wall remodeling. Finally, we show that this regulatory module is redeployed in distinct tissues under phosphate deficiency, indicating that plants reuse a conserved iron-based mechanism to coordinate growth across environmental contexts. Together, our findings establish genetically controlled Fe accumulation as a key determinant of developmental plasticity under nutrient stress.

abstract: The historical chronology of Mesopotamia offers a key chronological bridge to connect the Near East and eastern Mediterranean during the second millennium BCE. It is unusually rich in written records, including king lists, administrative documents, royal inscriptions, and astronomical observations. The latter offer a number of alternate possible absolute anchor points, resulting in competing high, middle, low, and ultra-low temporal frameworks. Establishing which of these is correct has consequences far beyond Mesopotamia. Tree-ring sequences from preserved timbers at archaeological sites in Anatolia, linked directly to Mesopotamia via the Old Assyrian trade network, could provide the answer. However, attempts have been limited by the lack of calendar secured dendrochronological dating for these timbers. Here we develop transferable methodologies in single-year radiocarbon analysis, utilizing patterns of 14 C preserved in single tree rings from Anatolian timbers to anchor their combined chronology 2072 BCE-744 BCE. This provides a calendrically-secured reference chronology for wood samples from Anatolian sites during this period as well as an annually resolved paleoclimatic record. Tree-ring dates are combined with archaeological and high-resolution ice-core evidence to evaluate the competing chronological frameworks for Mesopotamia between 2000 and 1500 BCE. Remaining dating uncertainties are constrained in strong support of the middle-low chronology.

abstract: OpenAI's disproof of the Erdős unit distance conjecture marks a milestone in AI for mathematical research. However, the result relied on an internal model with undisclosed test-time compute, hindering independent reproduction and analysis by the community. Here we present a simple autonomous agent built on the publicly available GPT-5.5 Pro. The agent uses a problem-agnostic three-stage prompting pipeline: brainstorm, execute, and review. We ran eight independent trials with web search disabled. In each trial, the agent produced a correct or essentially correct disproof of the conjecture. The resulting proofs are diverse and do not merely reproduce earlier AI-generated proofs. Since GPT-5.5 Pro was released nearly a month before OpenAI published its disproof, our evaluation is free from data contamination. The system operates efficiently, using an average of 106.7 k reasoning tokens per trial. We release our code and all outputs, providing a publicly accessible AI agent to resolve this conjecture autonomously.

abstract: Sleep is a fundamental behavioral state found across the animal kingdom, yet most of what we know about sleep is heavily vertebrate-biased. Studies are scarce or nonexistent in all but a few invertebrate lineages. A recent study of an REM sleep-like behavior in a jumping spider has reported unexpected parallels to sleep expression in vertebrates. So far, experimental evidence that these behavioral indicators truly represent sleep was lacking in spiders. Here, we present a comprehensive investigation into sleep behavior in the spider Portia fimbriata (Salticidae). We demonstrate diurnal activity, a free-running circadian rhythm, robust sleep architecture, regularly occurring REM-like behaviors, elevated arousal thresholds during those REM-like states, as well as rebound effects following sleep disruption. We conclude that the behavior we observe in spiders is behavioral sleep, providing evidence for an REM-like sleep substate in a terrestrial invertebrate. These results contribute to fundamental questions about the evolution and function of sleep across animals.

abstract: Spending time outdoors provides opportunities for physical activity, exposure to natural light, and social contact. Although young people's time use has changed substantially in recent decades, little is known about long-term trends in adolescents' outdoor engagement. This question is especially important because adolescence is a period of major life transitions and the development of lasting behavioral habits. This study examines 20-y trends in time spent outdoors among American adolescents using time-diary data from 14,235 individuals aged 15 to 19 in the 2003-2023 American Time Use Survey, a nationally representative survey of the US population. We describe trends in outdoor exposure and examine associations between outdoor time and leisure behaviors, including computer use for leisure, indoor physical activity, and time spent with friends. We find that outdoor engagement among boys has declined sharply, erasing a long-standing male advantage and causing boys' participation levels to converge with girls' at similarly low rates. Greater time spent in computer-based leisure was associated with less outdoor time, particularly among boys, whereas time spent with friends was positively associated with outdoor engagement for both sexes. Indoor physical activity did not change over the observation period and did not offset declines in outdoor time. These findings suggest that broader changes in leisure activities may be reshaping how young people engage with outdoor environments. Further research is needed to better understand the factors underlying these trends and their potential long-term implications.

abstract: As climate impacts worsen, decision-makers, researchers, and public sector institutions increasingly need reliable, relevant, and appropriate information about emerging weather and climate anomalies. However, with the ever-expanding choice of datasets based on ground observations, satellite data, and models, it is critical to not only use the best dataset for a specific decision-making need but to avoid misinforming and even derailing decision-making due to dataset selection. The main objective of this perspective is to illustrate the importance of understanding datasets used to translate climate data into actionable knowledge, supporting the next generation of science- and data-driven climate risk management instruments, projects, and global initiatives. Through the lens of three use cases, we illustrate what data quality means for different applications, the implications of choosing, aggregating, and combining different climate datasets, and the potential consequences of dataset and baseline choice on decision-making. Choosing different datasets often leads to trade-offs that decision-makers need to be aware of, for instance, between the spatial resolution of a dataset and length of the data record. Here, we discuss the implications of selecting the appropriate time step, resolution, and dataset and provide examples of how these choices affect the identification of societally relevant anomalies.

abstract: Projections of future population are important for a myriad of reasons. Large cities, states, and countries routinely produce near- and mid-range population projections. In the context of climate change, the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) framework is used at global and national scales to project long-term population to inform future emissions scenarios and understand future climate-related exposures and impacts. Much less consideration has been given to long-term projections at smaller scales, even though climate impacts are place based and cities now host most of the world's population. Cities and their metropolitan regions are complex, heterogeneous in terms of population, environmental, and built features. Thus, using global or national-scale approaches overlooks important aspects of urban futures. Cities are diverse, fluid population centers home to migrants, with employment opportunities yet substantial inequality. These quintessential city-centric features are ignored in global/national-scale population projection methods, including long-term ones consistent with the SSPs. Leveraging state-level SSP-based projections, here we extend that approach for New York City, currently home to 8.8 million persons. Combining multistate and multiregional demographic projection and spatial downscaling models, we project county-level population by racial/ethnic groups and age-sex to 2100 and downscale to 100 m. Such projections allow for an equity lens to inform assessments of future vulnerabilities to climate hazards. Four of the five SSPs project that the population of New York City will be smaller and much older at the end of the century, though these futures are dependent on demographic assumptions about fertility and especially migration.

abstract: References to nonexistent studies are well documented in biomedical research, but evidence outside biomedicine is limited. We analyzed a stratified random sample of 500,000 peer-reviewed journal papers in chemistry, physics, materials science, engineering, and computer science published from January 2023 through March 31, 2026, using OpenAlex, a large open index of scholarly works and citations. Our automated pipeline classified 1,135 references across 619 papers as fabricated, with 85.8% precision on masked expert review; fabricated is an operational label for a claimed title that could not be located in any of seven bibliographic and open-web sources. Affected-paper prevalence rose from 1 in 1,600 (6.3 per 10,000) in 2023 to 1 in 435 (23.0 per 10,000) in the first quarter of 2026, and full-period rates differed roughly sixfold across fields, from 25.6 per 10,000 papers in physics to 4.3 in chemistry. Most affected papers contained one or two fabricated references, but the 27 papers containing five or more accounted for more than a third of all fabricated references identified. Applying each field's rate to the approximately 7 million OpenAlex papers indexed in these fields gives an estimated 8,500 papers carrying at least one fabricated reference. Routine automated reference verification at submission, together with retrospective screening of the published literature, can detect fabricated references before and after they enter the scientific record.

abstract: Relapse remains a major challenge in opioid addiction treatment. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has emerged as a potential therapeutic strategy for addiction, yet results had been mixed due to empirically selected stimulation targets and limited knowledge of neural circuit engagement. Here, we used a focal rat TMS platform to test whether high-density theta-burst stimulation (hdTBS) of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), a corticostriatal node implicated in opioid relapse by prior causal and longitudinal functional MRI studies, decreases relapse-like oxycodone seeking and associated circuit dysfunction. Male rats self-administered oxycodone intravenously for 14 d and then underwent 13 d of electric barrier-induced abstinence, a procedure that suppresses drug taking while preserving drug availability and drug-associated context. During abstinence, the rats received seven daily sessions of sham stimulation or ACC-targeted hdTBS, with relapse tests and longitudinal functional MRI acquired during early and late abstinence to assess the behavioral and circuit-level effects of stimulation. Sham-treated rats showed a time-dependent increase (incubation) in oxycodone seeking and reduced ACC connectivity with dorsal and ventral striatum. In contrast, ACC-targeted hdTBS prevented incubation of oxycodone seeking and reversed abstinence-associated ACC-striatal connectivity reductions. Stimulation-sensitive functional circuits showed spatial correspondence with tracer-defined ACC projection patterns, suggesting that anatomical connectivity is critical to the circuit-level effects of focal stimulation. These findings support ACC-centered corticostriatal circuits as mechanistically informed targets for neuromodulation in opioid addiction and introduce a preclinical framework for linking stimulation, behavior, and longitudinal circuit remodeling.

abstract: Surface dust poses a fundamental challenge to extraterrestrial human exploration, a reality demonstrated by the operational hazards encountered during Apollo lunar missions. On Mars, this challenge is compounded by regional and global dust cycles that coat sensitive hardware. While previous Mars missions have constrained the bulk geochemistry of coarser particulates (≳3 µm), the properties of the fine (≲2.5 µm) and ultrafine (≲0.1 µm) fractions remain largely uncharacterized. This knowledge gap is critical as these respirable particles, defined by their ability to bypass upper respiratory defenses, possess the mobility to penetrate deep into the alveolar regions of biological systems, presenting a systemic toxicity risk to future crews. Here, we report on direct examination of these fine and ultrafine Martian dust fractions using X-ray fluorescence through the analysis and modeling of data acquired by the Perseverance rover. We observe particulates measuring as small as 100 to 200 nm on spacesuit samples and calibration targets. Compositionally, this dust is a phosphorus-, iron-, and sulfur-enriched mafic silicate accumulating on materials analogous to the planned external layers of potential crew systems. Our results emphasize the importance of a thorough characterization of Martian dust properties in terrestrial laboratories to better prepare future crews and crew support systems destined for the surface of Mars.

abstract: Microbial anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) regulates the flux of methane (CH 4 ) released from anoxic marine sediments into the ocean. However, variations in AOM rates, especially at dynamic environments such as cold seeps, are difficult to constrain, hindering robust projections of marine CH 4 flux in a changing climate. Here, we quantify AOM rates at global marine cold seeps based on isotope bonding in methane-derived authigenic carbonates. We show through model simulations that 13 C- 18 O bond abundance in these carbonates quantitatively records AOM rates at marine cold seeps and validate this proxy using compiled datasets of seep carbonate isotope compositions and independent AOM rate measurements. Accordingly, we estimate a mean AOM rate of [Formula: see text] mol·m -2 ·yr -1 and a consumption of [Formula: see text] Tg·yr -1 CH 4 at modern global cold seeps, but potentially [Formula: see text] times as high an AOM rate and CH 4 sink over the last ~100 kyr. Our results highlight the important role of cold seeps in the global marine CH 4 cycle despite their relatively minuscule footprint.

abstract: In the past decade, the public in Europe has become more concerned about climate change and expresses stronger proenvironmental policy preferences. Based on data from the European Social Survey (2012-2022, 25 countries), we show that the increased exposure to temperature extremes has contributed to the observed changes in climate change attitudes and electoral support for environmentalist policy platforms. For each additional degree of excess temperature experienced during warm spells measured over the previous 12 mo, we find that the probabilities of being worried about climate change, of feeling responsible for climate change, and of voting for Green parties and Green coalitions increase by 4.0 [CI95: 2.5, 5.5], 2.5 [CI95: 1.1, 3.9], and 2.8 [CI95: 0.9, 3.7] percentage points respectively. We also document significant heterogeneity across individuals, based on gender and education, particularly between highly educated women and low-educated men. While the latter group consistently exhibits the lowest proenvironmental attitudes and voting, it is this group that shows the strongest increases when exposed to temperature extremes, converging toward the levels of their more educated counterparts. Further regional heterogeneity analyses reveal that the effects of warm temperature extremes are smaller in less prosperous or economically disadvantaged regions, as well as in regions with greenhouse gas emission levels above the median. The findings suggest a nuanced interplay between individual factors and contextual influences in shaping climate attitudes of European citizens and their motivations or reservations toward greater climate action.

title: Human organ trafficking and missing persons in China.

author_details.name: Xuebo Wang
author_details.affiliation: Independent Researcher, Shanghai 200000, China.

affiliation_resolution.input: Independent Researcher, Shanghai 200000, China.

abstract: The persistent shortage of human organs for transplantation has long been a global challenge. The prospect of substantial profit creates strong incentives for illegal organ trafficking, including murder for organ harvesting, yet empirical evidence remains scarce. This study addresses this gap by exploiting a unique quasi-natural experiment created by China's organ policy reform. From 1984 to 2014, executed prisoners were the primary source of transplant organs in China. In 2015, the Chinese government abolished the use of organs from executed prisoners, sharply exacerbating the organ shortage. Following this policy change, the number of missing persons rose notably nationwide. Employing difference-in-differences and triple-difference strategies, we show that, compared to cases unrelated to organ trafficking (e.g., voluntary disappearances), the number and incidence of involuntary missing persons plausibly related to organ trafficking increased significantly after 2015. The effects are especially pronounced among individuals with mental illness and in regions with higher transplant demand and greater transplant capacity. Although we do not directly observe organ trafficking, the spatial, temporal, and demographic patterns we document are consistent with the hypothesis that increased organ scarcity intensified incentives for illicit organ procurement. More broadly, the findings suggest that severe organ shortages may generate unintended and highly harmful consequences, even in a low-crime setting such as China. These results underscore the importance of accounting for behavioral responses and illicit-market incentives when designing policies that restrict the supply of scarce, high-value goods such as transplant organs.

abstract: Climate change is increasing the occurrence of dangerous heat events globally with immediate health consequences, particularly in the Global South. In this paper, we spatially integrate Demographic and Healt 9 h surveys with a high-resolution, blended remotely sensed and station-derived dataset of humid-heat events spanning 1983-2016 to examine the effect of humid-heat exposure on fertility in Nigeria, one of the largest and most climate-vulnerable countries in the world. We use discrete-time models to examine the relationship between humid-heat exposure and conception probability and linear probability models to examine the relationship between humid-heat exposure and pregnancy termination (spontaneous and induced). We find that a 1 ° C increase in the current maximum wet bulb globe temperature decreases conceptions (0.2 conceptions per 1,000 woman-months, 95% CI: 0.03 to 0.4), but exposure to hotter temperatures 1 to 2 mo prior increases conception probability. Exposure to hot-humid temperatures during pregnancy increases probability of pregnancy termination (1.73 terminations per 100 pregnancies, 95% CI: 0.7 to 2.7). The net effect is an increase in births, but the timing may be shifted. Subgroup analyses reveal that effects of humid-heat on conception were larger for women residing in rural areas or in northern districts, or who are Muslim or have lower educational attainment, while the association between humid-heat and pregnancy termination was larger for women in southern areas, older women, and Christian women. Differences in how humid-heat affects populations may exacerbate existing inequalities. Overall, our analysis contributes to a better understanding of how humid-heat exposure affects fertility and reproductive health among women in the Global South.

abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) regulate gene expression by binding to specific genomic loci determined by DNA sequence. Their sequence specificity is commonly summarized by a consensus binding motif. However, eukaryotic genomes contain billions of low-affinity DNA sequences to which TFs associate with a sequence-dependent binding energy. We currently lack insight into how the genomic sequence defines this spectrum of binding energies and the resulting pattern of TF localization. Here, we set out to obtain a quantitative understanding of sequence-dependent TF binding to both motif and nonmotif sequences. We achieve this by first pursuing accurate measurements of physical binding energies of human TF Krüppel-like factor 4 (Klf4) to a library of short DNA sequences in a fluorescence-anisotropy-based bulk competitive binding assay. Second, we show that the highly nonlinear sequence dependence of Klf4 binding energies can be captured by combining a linear model of binding energies with an Ising model of the coupled recognition of nucleotides by a TF. In this model, nucleotide-TF interfaces collectively switch between two states, weak binding and strong nucleotide-specific binding, and the states of neighboring interfaces are coupled with [Formula: see text]. We find that this statistical mechanics model parameterized by our in vitro measurements captures Klf4 binding patterns on an individual long DNA molecule stretched in the optical tweezer, and is predictive for Klf4 occupancy across the entire human genome without additional fit parameters.

abstract: Mumia vera aegyptiaca was a mummy-derived medicinal substance widely used in medieval and early modern medicine, yet its material composition and biological activity remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate Egyptological and pharmaceutical-historical analysis of 41 textual sources with LC-MS/MS-based metabolomics, molecular networking, machine-learning-assisted annotation, and bioactivity testing to investigate ancient Egyptian embalming materials and historical Mumia vera samples. We analyzed 24 objects from university and pharmacy museum collections, including historical Mumia vera products, mummified body parts, embalming residues, bandages, and two mummified skulls. Comparative metabolomics revealed substantial heterogeneity among materials labeled as Mumia vera , but also recurrent molecular signatures consistent with aged conifer resins, including oxidized abietane-type diterpenoids. Several samples contained Aloe -associated metabolites, including aloeresin A/D- and aloin-related compounds. These data reveal Aloe -associated metabolites in ancient Egyptian embalming-related materials and support the presence of Aloe spp.-derived exudates in selected samples. The convergence of molecular and textual evidence further raises the possibility that a previously unresolved Egyptian term from the 2nd millennium BC may refer to Aloe sp. or an Aloe -derived product. Comparative metabolomics also linked an inconspicuous powder sample to a specific mummified head, although their curatorial association had not been securely documented. Finally, a historical Mumia vera aegyptiaca extract modestly protected MDCK cells from influenza virus-induced cytopathic effects, whereas the isolated major compound 7-oxodehydroabietic acid was inactive on its own. Together, these findings show how integrating textual scholarship, pharmaceutical history, and molecular analysis can refine the interpretation of ancient Egyptian embalming practices, museum objects, and historical medicines.

abstract: As the natural environment continues to change, there is a shared sense among researchers, policymakers, and health practitioners that we need to better understand the impacts of those changes on health and health behaviors for individuals and populations. "Big" social media data, including large datasets from platforms like X (formerly Twitter), Reddit, Facebook, TikTok, and YouTube, provide access to previously hard-to-reach populations. These data are posed to revolutionize the data landscape in climate change research; however, there are limitations and ethical concerns with data from these platforms, such as ethical questions, biases, noise, and a distinct underrepresentation of marginalized groups. These issues could hamper the adoption of social media data in research on climate change and health. In this commentary, we propose leveraging and augmenting a "human-in-the-loop" approach that uses humans in data extraction, quality assurances, and model testing to ensure data quality and overcome known limitations of social media data. Using examples from health data, we propose new horizons in climate change health research made possible with qualitative research methods.
